SIGNED, so the furthest right a sprite can be placed is +255. A unit the
widened guest now emits at screen x = 296 is written as 296 and the renderer
reads it back as `296 - 512 = -216` — off the LEFT of the extended view, still
invisible. Nothing in OAM can express "x = 296".

`src/kol_obj_cull.cpp` therefore also installs `g_ws_obj_x_provider`, the
framework's existing "per-game interpretation of the 9-bit OBJ X field in
expanded-view rendering". It reinterprets a wrapped value as its unsigned
reading, and it is **safe by construction rather than by heuristic**: it only
ever touches a sprite whose DEFAULT decoding puts it entirely outside the
visible region, so it can add a sprite that would otherwise be invisible and
can never move a visible one. The two readings are 512 apart and the widest
view is 480, so at most one of them is on screen.

```
if (raw_x < 0x100)            keep;   // no wrap, the default decoding is right
if (raw_x >= 240 + extra_right) keep; // unsigned reading is not visible either
if (raw_x - 0x200 >= -extra_left) keep;  // signed reading IS visible
use raw_x;
```

The guest's own cull is what keeps the third test from ever being close: it
emits nothing left of `-(32 + extra_left)`, whose wrapped value is always
greater than the view's right edge.

**Corrected 2026-09-24: "at most one of them is on screen" was wrong at 480.**
The claim counts sprite POSITIONS, not extents, and it forgets the cull's right
slack. The widened cull emits units up to `x = 272 + extra_right` = 392 at 480
wide. The signed reading of 392 is -120, exactly the left edge, and a 16-wide
sprite there is visible. The rule then keeps the visible, wrong reading. Units
standing just off the RIGHT edge were drawn in the leftmost 8 columns,
floating in the sky (`states/AX_units_left_margin.state`: Alphonse, Flauros
and Stella). This is the recurring report of units at the far left. No rule
over a 9-bit field can be exact here: 480 + 32 > 512.

**The fix reads the answer instead of guessing it**, the same way Y does. The
guest's slot list records every unit sprite's true 16-bit X, and
`kol_obj_attr_x` looks it up (`obj_true_x`) by the sprite's (OAM X, OAM Y)
pair, in the table `on_obj_y` already builds once a frame. The rule above is
now only the fallback for sprites the guest did not record (the cursor, HUD
and effects).

Verified: on AX only the 444 wrapped pixels in columns 0-7 change. Scrolling
right until the camera reaches the units, they appear at the right edge,
identical to the old build. `AO_obj_sides`, `AP_obj_right` and
`AS_scroll_flash` are byte-identical. Both render invariants are unchanged.
AU at 480x270, three alternating runs: 6.36 vs 6.36 ms/frame.

#### Half three: OAM's Y field is 8 bits, and it wraps too

Widening the vertical window put two unit heads in the BOTTOM margin, floating
over open water below the map (`states/AQ_bottom_margin.state`), and later a
unit near the bottom edge refused to appear at all
(`states/AR_rictor_bottom.state` — Rictor, anchor y = 196).

OAM's Y is 8 bits and the renderer decodes it with the hardware rule — 160 or
more means negative — which is exact only while every sprite row lies in
`[-96, 159]`. A unit's two 16x16 halves sit at `[anchor - 32, anchor)`, so an
anchor of -68 puts the top half at y = -100, written as OAM Y **156**, which
decodes POSITIVE and draws the head at row 156. Dumping OAM from a run with
the widened cull actually in force (the TCP rig cannot show this — it never
runs the frame hook, so it only ever sees the stock window) made it
unambiguous: twelve entries added, six units of two halves, and precisely the
two whose OAM Y came out 156 were the floating sprites.

**The X trick does not transfer.** There the wrong reading was always the
invisible one, so preferring the visible reading was safe by construction.
Here it is the opposite: the true position (-100, off the top) is invisible
and the mis-decode (+156) is visible, so that rule picks the artifact every
time.

Worse, it is not a rule that can exist. One byte addresses 256 rows and
sprites span `192 + extra_top + extra_bottom`:

| size | margins | span | fits in 256? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 320x180 | 10 + 10 | 212 | yes |
| 384x216 | 28 + 28 | 248 | yes |
| 480x270 | 55 + 55 | **302** | **no** |

At 480x270 both readings of a single byte can land on screen, so **nothing
computed from OAM alone can separate them.** Capping the top slack at 64 and
refusing to widen the bottom removes the artifact, but it is a trade: it gives
up the bottom margin entirely, which is what hid Rictor.

**The way out is that the guest never truncated anything.** Before OAM it
records each sprite in its own slot list — IWRAM `0x03004150`, stride `0x20` —
and there the screen position is a full 16-bit pair at `[slot+0x1C]` X and
`[slot+0x1E]` Y. That list survives to the frame boundary. Verified against
the projection on `AR_rictor_bottom`: 164, 100, 100, 132, 108, 124, 84, 108,
each matching a computed anchor exactly.

So `src/kol_obj_cull.cpp` installs `g_ws_obj_attr_y_provider` (added to
gbarecomp for this, the vertical twin of `g_ws_obj_x_provider`) and answers
from that list instead of guessing. Each live slot predicts two entries,
`(scrX - 8, scrY - 32)` and `(scrX - 8, scrY - 16)`; a lookup matches the OAM
entry's **pair**, which is what makes it exact — two sprites 256 rows apart
share a Y byte, but not an X as well. Anything the guest did not record — the
HUD, the cursor, effects — finds no match and falls through to hardware
behaviour, so it fails closed. With the true row recoverable, both vertical
bounds simply follow the margins again and there is no trade to make.

It is indexed by the Y byte because the renderer calls it for every OBJ on
every scanline, about 35k times a frame; a linear scan would be ~9M
comparisons a frame. The index is a **counting sort with no per-row cap**,
and that is not an optimisation detail: an earlier version used fixed-width
buckets of four and DECLINED when one overflowed. Units in this game stand on
isometric rows, so four or more sharing a screen row is ordinary — measured
on a 16-step scroll over `states/AS_scroll_flash.state`, three frames hit
exactly four — and on those frames every sprite in that row fell through to
hardware decoding at once. That is the second flash: top-of-field sprites at
the bottom edge, a few frames at a time, while the camera moves.

**The table is sampled ONCE per frame, and that is load-bearing.** Rebuilding
it per scanline sweep — the obvious thing — tears it: the guest rebuilds its
slot list during the visible period, while the renderer is still composing
the frame from the OAM it wrote back in VBlank, so a mid-frame read picks up
the NEXT frame's positions and every lookup misses. That is visible as
top-of-field sprites flashing at the bottom edge while the camera scrolls,
exactly where they sat before any of this was fixed. The frame hook marks the
table dirty, so the first lookup of a frame samples the list that produced
the OAM now being drawn. `KOL_OBJY_STATS=1` reports per-frame fall-throughs;
over a 16-step scroll on `states/AS_scroll_flash.state` this took them from
spikes of 26,730 to **zero**, and the rebuild count from 34,290 a frame to 1.

**Scrolling in view mode: no exact match exists (fixed 2026-09-25).**
Reported as units flashing all over, mostly in the sky, while scrolling left
in view mode (`states/BE_scroll_left.state`, 480x270, Left held). The slot
list moves 8 px between samples, and the OAM being drawn sits halfway: 4 px
from the current sample and 4 from the previous. The measured example is a
unit at X 64 in the previous sample and 72 in the current, drawn at 68.

So no exact pair matched. Every unit below the view fell through to
hardware decoding, and its wrapped Y put it at the top, in the sky.
`KOL_OBJY_STATS` showed up to 2,430 declines a frame across the scroll.

The lookup now keeps the previous frame's sample too, and runs in three
steps:
1. An exact pair match in the current sample, then in the previous.
2. Failing that, a recorded sprite within 16 px in either sample picks the
   READING of the raw value nearest to it: raw, raw−256, or raw+256 for Y;
   ±512 for X.
3. Candidates that disagree decline.

The readings are 256 apart, so a unit 16 px away cannot suggest the wrong
one. Only the wrap is chosen; the position drawn stays the raw one.
Answers are cached per raw pair per frame, so the near search runs about
once per sprite, not once per scanline.

Only a 16x16 sprite is matched near: the square size-1 shape of both halves
of every unit. The roster panel's 8x8 selection brackets sit within 16 px of
units standing on the deployment tiles behind the panel. They were taken for
those units, kept their native X, and showed over the map during the
portrait animation (`states/BF_panel_brackets.state`, frame 40). With the
size test they move with the panel again, and the scroll frames are
byte-identical to before it.

**Inside the roster panel's footprint only an exact match counts.** The
panel's portraits are 16x16 too. Near-matched to units standing on the
deployment tiles behind the panel, they kept their native X and floated
over the map with an empty slot left behind: Deneb in
`states/BH_deneb_floating.state`, and a second-row portrait in
`BF_panel_brackets`. `obj_true_x(…, near = false)` is used there. Units in
the footprint still keep their true X (they match exactly when the camera is
still). `AD_user_charsel` and `BD_units_invisible` are unchanged.

**And only the panel's interface goes with it (2026-10-06).** Reported on
the Thor (`states/FP_slot1_dragon_cut_stick.state`, the user's slot 1,
battle preparation): with the right stick moved, the dragon on the
deployment tiles was cut and pieces came loose from the units around it. The
dragon is 32 wide, four 16x16 pieces at the slot's X - 16 and X; the slot
list predicts 16-wide units (X - 8), so its left pieces, under the panel's
native footprint, matched nothing exactly and went off with the panel. Its
square in the sprite atlas lost them too (no sprite left in the scene there:
code `0x50`), and under the perspective its horns hung loose to the left.
Every sprite of the panel itself is priority 0 (portraits, brackets, arrows:
BD, BF, BH, BP, FP, by `KOL_OAM_DEBUG`); unit parts are 1 or 2. Now a
priority 1-3 sprite in the footprint is world: it takes its true X like any
other sprite, and only priority 0 moves with the panel.

Verified, A/B dumps of 40 presents at 384x216 and 480x270, anchoring on: FP
changes (the dragon whole, at its place); BP, AI and BI byte-identical; BD,
BF and BH differ only in rain drops (2x2 specks, repeated 160 rows apart in
the margins): a drop falling through the panel's old footprint used to jump
to the left edge with the panel and now keeps falling where it is. No
portrait, bracket or unit moved.

**Then sprites still came apart under the stick.** Parts of units stayed
behind on the map while the units moved: a hat tip, a column of a unit's
edge, a speck. `claim_unit_sprites` works out which OAM entry drew each
pixel by drawing the latched OAM itself, and an entry no unit's frame takes
(the interface) was placed by its OAM fields. But KoL's own providers move
some of them: the roster panel's portraits and brackets are drawn 72 px left
of their OAM place at 384 wide (with the panel), a menu's hand with its box.
Placed by OAM, the dragon's portrait and a bracket lay over unit 9 and,
priority 0, took the top of its pixels there; those were never lifted and
stayed in the scene. gbarecomp now records where the wide compositor drew
each OAM entry (`GbaPpu::latched_obj_drawn`, latched with the OAM under
`g_ppu_record_obj`), and an entry no unit takes is placed there. Found with
temporary dumps: the atlas squares (magenta where empty), the ground filled
under lifted pixels, and per-pixel layer code, OAM entry, owner and lift.
Verified, A/B dumps of 40 presents with the stick held (-0.7, 0.4) at
384x216 and 480x270: FP loses its loose pieces; CH loses a dark wedge cut
into the unit under where the menu's hand sits in OAM; BH and BD lose a
loose copy of a unit's edge by the panel; BV, CB, EM and FO byte-identical.

After the change the scroll has no sky units. The declines left are one
sprite on a few frames, with nothing visible. Seven margin-sprite states
(`AO`, `AP`, `AQ`, `AR`, `AS`, `AX`, `BE`) render byte-identical at 480x270
with no input; exact matches exist whenever nothing scrolls. Both render
invariants are unchanged.

That also paid for itself: with the per-scanline rebuild the whole widening
cost 32.2 s against 29.7 s over 600 frames at 480x270, about 8%. Sampling
once a frame brings it to 29.7 s, which is the baseline.

**A counter that returns early cannot see the case it should be catching.**
The first version of that instrument bailed out on a saturated bucket before
reaching the counter, so it reported a clean zero across the very scroll that
was still flashing. Count the fall-through at the single point where the
lookup gives up, not per reason.

**Counting fall-throughs needs one exclusion.** Parked sprites sit at
`(y=168, x=248)`, and 168 is inside the wrapped band, so they never match and
never can. Left in, ~100 parked entries times 270 scanlines buried the real
signal under 26k a frame and made a clean run look broken.

**Verified.** A/B against `KOL_NO_OBJ_CULL_WIDEN=1` on both repro states at
all three extended sizes. `states/AP_obj_right.state` is the right-margin
repro (a knight on the top-right plateau, absent until the camera reached it):

| state | 320x180 | 384x216 | 480x270 | inside centre 240x160 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AO_obj_sides` (left)    |  184 px | 1299 px | 1891 px | **0** |
| `AP_obj_right` (right)   |    0 px |  193 px |  314 px | **0** |
| `AQ_bottom_margin` (top) |       - |       - |  365 px | **0** |
| `AR_rictor_bottom` (btm) |       - |       - |  401 px | **0** |

`AQ_bottom_margin` is the state that had the floating heads: 0 px in the
bottom margin now, because the Y provider resolves them to their true rows
above the screen rather than because anything was capped. `AR_rictor_bottom`
is 401 px, all of it in the bottom margin, at guest x 128..143 y 165..193 —
exactly where the projection puts Rictor's anchor of 196.

Every changed pixel is in a margin; the authentic 240x160 is untouched at
every size. AP gains nothing at 320 because that view only reaches x = 280 and
the unit is at x = 288 — correctly still outside. Both render invariants
re-run and byte-identical to the recorded references (240 `66e13ab2…`, 284
`84a95b05…`, and centre-240 identity 0 px on all four states at 480x270). On the device at 480x270,
`AO_obj_sides` shows six units with their END banners in the left margin,
composed with the terrain and correctly depth-ordered.

#### Dead ends, so they are not re-paid for

- **The `[rec+0x17] & 0x40` test** at `0x0805A84C`, in the 26-object loop that
  builds the draw list, looks exactly like a visibility flag and is not one.
  Dumped that array before and after the five taps: OAM active goes 21 -> 30
  while every unit's `0x40` bit is unchanged. The draw list is a fixed 9
  entries at both camera positions.
- **The park value** `(y=0xA8, x=0xF8)` is a CLEAR, not a per-unit reject —
  everything is parked every frame and only the visible few filled in.
- **`0x08144308`**, which the per-unit setup calls and skips the unit when it
  returns -1, picks the sprite VARIANT from flag bits and returns -1 for
  "this unit has no sprite". It never looks at a screen position.

#### Two tool limits this cost

- **An OAM entry being "active" does not mean it is visible.** Chasing the
  right-margin case, an OAM diff across the camera move turned up two 16x16
  entries at y = 220 and 236 and they looked like the answer. They are not:
  OBJ Y is 8-bit and only wraps when `y + height > 256`, so 220..236 is simply
  below a 160-row screen. Decode the wrap before believing a coordinate.
- **`GBARECOMP_READ_WATCH` is blind to IWRAM.** Generated code reaches IWRAM
  without going through the bus bridge, so a watch on the camera variable
  (`0x03000DDA`, found as the single cell in all of EWRAM+IWRAM tracking the
  scroll, stepping 0xD8 -> 0xA8 with BG0HOFS) returned zero hits. Only EWRAM,
  VRAM, OAM and ROM are visible to it.
- **The `bl.hi` address in a generated disassembly comment is an artifact**,
  not the call target — it ORs the high half-word's field over the current PC.
  Decode the BL pair from the ROM bytes instead. Several hours of this hunt
  were spent chasing functions at addresses that do not exist.
- And, still: `set_break_pc` plus `call_stack_dump` over TCP kills the
  session. The break unwinds into the runner, the step reports failure and the
  server exits. Use the read/write watches.

#### Still open on this

- The **vertical** widening is exercised by the table above, but only
  because `KOL_VIEW_SIZE=WxH` was added to `kol_widescreen.cpp` for it. The
  desktop runner has `--view-width` and no `--view-height`, and the real size
  comes from the Android menu, so without that test hook the vertical margins
  could not be A/B'd anywhere but on the device. It is ignored whenever a real
  menu choice exists.
- The emitter refuses past **128 slots** (`cmp r1,#0x7F` at `0x08076836`),
  which is the OAM limit. Widening the window means more candidates compete
  for those slots; 21-30 were in use here, so there is plenty of headroom on
  this map, but a crowded battle at 480 wide has not been measured.

### The terrain box was not top-aligned (2026-09-21)

At every extended size the terrain info anchored to the right edge but not to
the top, so it sat a margin's depth below the corner it belongs in. The
vertical corner test capped an anchorable box at `kVCornerTiles = 8` tile
rows; the terrain box is rows 0..8, which is nine. Raised to 9. It stays
under the roster's right-hand portrait column, which is 10 rows from row 0
and must NOT be swept into the margin — that exclusion is why the cap exists,
and `states/AI_prep_vertical.state` still renders the roster, MEMBER and the
unit box correctly.

**The three stranded element dots are fixed too, and by position.**
They are NOT sprites — there is no OAM entry anywhere near them, so the
OBJ-follows-BG machinery that the ARMS box needed does not apply here. They
are a BG component of their own. `KOL_WS_UI_DUMP=1` on
`states/AS_scroll_flash.state` shows why:

```
BG3  r03 <<<<<<<<<<..............=.>>>>
     r04 ........................=.>>>>
     r05 ........................=.>>.>
              ('=' occupied, not shifted; '>' shifted right)
```

The terrain panel is not one box. Its right part (cols 26..29) touches the
right edge, passes the edge test and anchors; the dots are a separate 1x3
component at **col 24**, two clear columns away, which touches nothing and so
stays put. Containment does not rescue them either — they are outside the
anchored component's bounding box, not inside it.

The choice was between a proximity rule — a component sharing rows with an
anchored corner element and sitting a column or two from it travels with it —
and recognising this furniture by position. Position won, because the game
already identifies that box that way: the second screen rasterises it from
exactly this rect (`kol_terrain_probe.cpp`, cols 23..29 x rows 0..8) and
`terrain_box_on_screen()` is the game's own test for whether the box is
really drawn there rather than a NAVI dialogue. A proximity rule would have
been a new heuristic applying to every screen; this one cannot affect
anything but this box, which matters because the anchoring heuristics are
where this project's HUD regressions have come from.

Every component lying entirely inside that rect now takes the same shift as
whichever part of it anchored. The box relocates to cols 15..21 with a NAVI
bar up and `terrain_box_on_screen()` is false then, so this correctly does
nothing there.

Verified at 480x270 on `AS_scroll_flash` and `AO_obj_sides`: the whole
cluster — STEP count, icon, both dot columns, their values and the
shield/sword figures — sits in the corner in the guest's own layout. The
battle-preparation screen (`AI_prep_vertical`) is **0 px** different from
before the change, and both render invariants are byte-identical.

### Equipment names that had no text (2026-09-21)

The second-screen panel drew one equipment slot as ordinary text ("Short
Sword") and the rest as small two-line images, which read as the panel
mimicking the game's own box for some names and not others.

They are not a style choice. **193 of the 489 pool strings begin with the
`0x81 NN` escape, which makes the whole entry a pre-rendered strip and leaves
no text form in the ROM at all** — `read_name` returned an empty string and a
bitmap id, so the panel had nothing to typeset. Checked across all 489: the
escape is ALWAYS the first byte, never after text, so nothing was being
dropped by the decode.

`kol_unit_data.cpp` now carries those names as a transcription table, keyed by
escape id, and `read_name` fills `text` and reports `bitmap = -1`. The Java
side needed no change at all: `-1` already means "this is text".

**How the table was made, because it is transcription and not derivation.**
The strips were rasterised straight out of `kEscPixels` and read. Two things
had to be got right first:

- `kEscTable`'s offset is in TILES, not cells — consecutive entries differ by
  `2 * cells`. Reading it as cells lands on a different name entirely and
  looks plausible, which cost a wrong "Ring of Flotation" for what is
  actually "Hard Leather".
- The strips are not all one shape. 105 of the 188 referenced are two 8px
  lines stacked in one 16px cell run; the other 83 are a single 16px line.
  The test is whether rows 7-8 are blank. Splitting a 16px line in half
  produces confident nonsense.

Whole words were read rather than glyphs matched. The font has 147 distinct
8px shapes with real ambiguity between I/l/1 and O/0/D, and only 23 of 2813
runs are merged pairs, so per-glyph OCR would have been 147 hand labels each
able to corrupt a name silently; English item names are self-correcting in
context and single glyphs are not.

**Nothing decodes pixels at runtime.** What ships is a `const char* const`
array and one bounds-checked index in `read_name` — the same cost as the
text path that was always there. The rasterising happened once, here.

**Treat a wrong name as a transcription error**, check the strip, and fix the
table — the lookup itself is a plain array. `tools/dump_name_strips.py` is
the tool that produced the sheets they were read from, kept precisely so a
suspect name can be checked against its own pixels:

```sh
python3 tools/dump_name_strips.py totkol.gba /tmp/strips
```

It prints the escape ids for each sheet in row order. An id with no entry
keeps the old behaviour and draws its strip, so this fails soft. Verified by
decoding units on three states: Short Sword, Hard Leather, Leather Hat,
Tower Shield, Transferring Stone, all previously `<strip>`.

### The second screen as the game's character sheet (2026-09-21)

The panel was a dark modern layout beside a game that draws a parchment
status sheet. It now follows that sheet: field over a diagonal hatch, a
blue-grey double border with corner studs, dark ink, slate header plates, and
EQUIP./TALENT as two cards underneath.

**The colours are sampled, not invented** — from a rendered frame of the
game's own status screen (`states/AT_status_sheet.state`): field `#FFFF8C`
over hatch `#DEE78C`, ink `#101818`, border `#63739C` with a `#84B5BD`
highlight, plates `#101008` lettered `#FFFFEF`, HP `#73BDFF`, MP `#FF4A10`.
The same values are in the ROM's own palette at `0x0861DF68` onward, which is
the better source if this is ever revisited.

**Since 2026-09-24 the top card is placed at the sheet's own coordinates**
(`StatsView.drawUnitPanel`). One game pixel is `card width / 240` across and
`card height / 80` down, starting from the sheet the game draws for
Alberich:
- name and class on the top line, with Lv./EXP stacked beside the name
  (raised from the game's spot at the user's request);
- the element icon in its bevelled square, with the alignment letter, under
  the name;
- HP and MP with their bars on the right, just under the class;
- STR/INT/AGI down the left, with ATK/DEF on the INT row and M.ATK/M.DEF on
  the AGI row, where the game puts them.

The portrait's slot is left as parchment, and Move is not drawn.

**It is the sheet's LAYOUT, not its artwork.** The portrait, the melee/magic
defence pair and Move are not in the record and are not captured, so they are
simply absent — a placeholder number on a panel of real ones is worse than a
gap. The one deliberate departure from the game: a stat equipment has moved
shows its base in brackets, because a figure that silently disagrees with the
record is worse than an extra one.

#### Can the artwork come from the ROM? YES — superseded 2026-09-24

The notes below record the dead end as it stood. The "bespoke codec" is the
game's own A7 archive format, and it is cracked: see "A7 archives" and "The
status sheet, from ROM" below. They are kept for how the question was
narrowed, not as the answer.


Asked and chased, so it is not re-chased:

- **Palettes: yes**, uncompressed, at the addresses above.
- **The frame tiles are in the ROM and are genuine.** The frame is BG0,
  palette bank 4, 25 distinct tiles; 22 of them appear in the ROM, each fully
  non-blank and occurring EXACTLY ONCE, around `0x086B7814` and `0x086FCD51`.
- **They are not a tileset.** Consecutive tiles sit at deltas of 0x20, 0x21,
  0x20, 0x21 — an extra byte every other tile, so a stream with interspersed
  control bytes. It is **not LZ77**: every 2-byte-aligned `0x10` block in the
  8 MiB image was decompressed (7,216 candidates, 0x200..0x40000) and
  searched for five distinct tile needles, with no hits. It is **not standard
  RLE** either. A bespoke codec.
- **No decompression SWI is involved.** The SWI log over a scene change shows
  only `0x0B`/`0x0C`: 784 copies into EWRAM, 440 into a small VRAM region,
  none into the char block. The block is staged in EWRAM and DMA'd — which is
  also why `GBARECOMP_WRITE_WATCH` sees nothing there, since DMA does not go
  through `bus_write_*`.
- Only 133 of 605 non-blank char-block tiles exist in the ROM at all; the
  rest are composed at runtime, which fits what this project already knows
  about names and class being dynamic tile runs.

#### Done: the frame IS read from the ROM

The offset-table route was taken and it needs only **twelve** tiles, not 22.
The sheet is a plain 9-slice on BG0 in palette bank 4 — four corners, four
edges, and a field of four hatched tiles laid 4 wide, shifting by two every
row — and all twelve are in the ROM:

```
corner TL/TR/BL/BR  0x086FCD51 0x086FCD71 0x086FCD92 0x086FCDB2
edge top/bot/L/R    0x086FCDD3 0x086FCDF3 0x086FCE14 0x086FCE34
field a/b/c/d       0x086B7834 0x086B7855 0x086B7875 0x086B7896
palette bank 4      0x0861DFE8
```

The three tiles that are NOT in the ROM turned out to be irrelevant: tiles
1-3 are used exactly once each, as the 2x2 weapon/element icon beside the
name, which is per-unit and composed. The frame never needed them.

`kol::sheet_frame_atlas()` reads those twelve plus the palette into a 96x8
atlas, `pushSheetArt` sends it once at startup, and `StatsView.sheetCardArt`
9-slices it.

**Give each tile its OWN bitmap; do not scale sub-rects of an atlas.** The
first version kept the 12 tiles in one 96x8 bitmap and drew each with a src
rect. Scaling a sub-rect lets the sampler reach the neighbouring tile's edge
column, which ruled a faint vertical seam down the panel at every tile
boundary. `setSheetArt` splits the atlas into twelve 8x8 bitmaps; a tile with
no neighbours cannot bleed.

**Derive the content inset from the FRAME.** The layout used a fixed 34px
inset against a border a whole tile thick, so every label, plate and bar was
drawn on top of the frame. It is `SHEET_TILE + 14` now, and the tile is 32
(4x) rather than 48: the game's border is 8px on a 160-line screen, so a
whole tile at 6x read far heavier here than it does there.

**Anchor the edges FLUSH to the far side, not on a grid from the near one.**
The first version laid tiles from the top-left at a fixed pitch, which only
lands on the far edge when the card is an exact multiple of the tile. At the
real panel size the top card is 1163 px for a 48 px tile, so the right border
was drawn 37 px past the card, the clip ate it, and every card had a dark gap
down its right side and a cut-off bottom. Since the edge and field tiles
repeat, clipping them mid-tile is invisible; only the four corners have to be
exact. **No capture and no codec work**: the art is there before the
sheet has ever been opened. Reproducing the field's 4-wide, shift-by-two run
rather than repeating one tile is what makes the hatch run diagonally instead
of striping. The drawn version stays as the fallback for when the art has not
arrived.

Verified by rebuilding the whole 30x20 frame from those twelve tiles and
comparing it against the frame the game draws, and on the Thor by
`screen2: sheet frame art 96x8 from ROM`.

The routes NOT taken, if the item icons or the portrait are ever wanted:
capture from VRAM while the sheet is open and cache it, as
`capture_unit_panel_frame` and friends already do for four other assets; or
trace whatever fills the EWRAM staging buffer and crack the codec.

### The interpreter was half the frame, and it did not have to be (2026-09-22)

**Every IWRAM PC the interpreter bridged was a byte-for-byte copy of ROM, so
all of them compile ahead of time.** This removed ~96-99.7% of interpreted
instructions and ~36% of the frame at 240, ~24% at 480.

This corrects a decision recorded in `game.toml` on 2026-09-17, which declined
to seed `0x03001110` with the reasoning:

> Code copied into RAM at runtime belongs to the self-heal RAM-dispatch tier
> ... never a game.toml extra_func — **there is no fixed ROM byte range to
> decode.**

There is, and the schema already had the mechanism: `[[code_copy]]` maps a
runtime RAM span to its ROM source and "keeps the runtime PC addresses while
reading opcodes from the source bytes", so PC-relative loads and the literal
pool resolve correctly by construction. The cost of that wrong call was ~3.5 ms
of every frame, at every view size, **forever on Android** — the self-heal
recompile tier cannot run there at all, because the platform blocks `dlopen` of
an app-written `.so`.

**Finding the blocks.** `GBARECOMP_IWRAM_DUMP=<path>` writes 32 KB of live
IWRAM at exit. Search the ROM for the bytes at each bridged PC, then extend the
match in both directions to bound the block:

| IWRAM | bytes | ROM source | resident at cold boot? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0x03001110` | 0x160 | `0x080000FC` | yes |
| `0x03001270` | 0x060 | `0x0806E208` | yes |
| `0x030035D8` | 0x380 | `0x0815B8BC` | yes |
| `0x03005240` | 0x2818 | `0x087D4D58` | **no** — zeros until audio starts |

**Four traps this cost:**

1. **`[[code_copy]]` creates no functions.** It declares the byte mapping only.
   Nothing in ROM branches to these addresses — the callers go through function
   pointers — so discovery cannot find them either. Each entry point needs its
   own `[[extra_func]]` with `source_addr`.
2. **Adjacent in IWRAM does not mean adjacent in ROM.** `0x03001110` and
   `0x03001270` sit back to back in RAM but come from ROM addresses 6 MiB
   apart. When the bridge reported `0x03001270` with the *same* call count one
   byte past the first block, the fix was a second `[[code_copy]]`, not a
   larger size.
3. **It is whack-a-mole until you stop playing it.** The sound driver produced
   a new interior PC on every pass — `0x030061C8`, then `0x03005B24`, then
   `0x03005AC0` — each appearing only once the previous went native. These are
   asynchronous IRQ returns landing past the end of a function the finder
   bounded short (`static_resume_all` covers interior PCs of *emitted* bodies
   only). One `[[resume_range]]` over the driver ended it in a single step.
4. **Zeros match zeros.** The leading bytes of the sound-driver range are
   padding that is zero in both ROM and IWRAM, so a naive "is it identical"
   check passes trivially there. Bound the block by its real content.

**Evidence that the ranges are real, not coincidence:** each was compared
byte-for-byte against its ROM source in five independent IWRAM dumps — four
in-play states (`AF_world_map`, `AS_scroll_flash`, `AT_status_sheet`,
`S_move_highlight`) plus a 400-frame cold boot. The sound driver's 64-byte
signature occurs **exactly once** in the 8 MiB ROM, so there is a single fixed
source and it is not bank-switched between drivers.

**Result**, 600-frame battle run: `interpreted_insns` 15,383,255 -> 51,750, and
`AF_world_map` now reports `self_heal_coverage=FULLY_STATIC dispatch_misses=0
interpreted_insns=0`. The remaining bridged PCs are all ROM addresses
(`0x08007698`, `0x080079D0`, `0x080124BC`, `0x08076524`) and are pre-existing,
unrelated to this change.

**Verified.** Both render invariants byte-identical (240 `66e13ab2…`, 284
`84a95b05…`, centre-240 identity 0/160 rows). And because this changes how four
blocks of guest code actually execute, the old and new binaries were A/B'd
directly: byte-identical BMP dumps on `S_move_highlight`, `AF_world_map`,
`AT_status_sheet` and `AS_scroll_flash` at **600 and 1800 frames each**, plus a
cold boot at 1200 and 4000 frames — the case that matters for the sound driver,
which is copied in mid-run.

### Two more IWRAM copies, found by a sweep (2026-10-06)

Asked: how much really goes through the interpreter while playing, and can
self-heal run on Android? Self-heal stays off there (no compiler on the
device, and its result is a library file the app wrote), so whatever the
static build misses is interpreted on the Thor for good. Two sources:

- **The Mac's self-heal cache** (`recomp_cache/`): 1,886 PCs healed since
  09-17 in development play. Today's dispatch table has 1,727 of them; the
  159 left are all ROM, in 21 places, mostly interior targets (jump-table
  cases: `0x0806E456` alone has 37). Not reviewed yet.
- **A sweep of all 170 saved states**, 600 frames each, self-heal off
  (`GBARECOMP_MISS_FRAG` / `GBARECOMP_COVERAGE_JSON` per state): 27 fully
  static; 130 have the same 4 ROM PCs at ~117 interpreted instructions a
  frame; 14 distinct PCs in all. `AA_unit_setup` aborts at load (not looked
  into).

The one that cost real time was IWRAM **`0x030012D0`**: rarely entered (103
times on EX, 8 on BL) but ~30,000 interpreted instructions each time, about
4 ms on the Mac. It is a copy of ROM: `0x030012D0..0x03001550` is ROM
`0x08025FE4` byte for byte (it starts exactly where `iwram_thumb_1270`
ends), and the next block, `0x03001550..0x03001750` (the Training path's
other IWRAM miss), is ROM `0x08022438`. In `GBARECOMP_IWRAM_DUMP`s of all
169 loadable states at 200 frames and a 400-frame cold boot, both ranges
were byte-identical to ROM in all 170: resident from startup, never
replaced. Both start with `push {r4-r7, lr}`. Now two `[[code_copy]]` plus
two `[[extra_func]]` with `source_addr` in `game.toml`; 49,672 -> 49,702
functions (the finder followed their branches).

Other ROM-copied runs in IWRAM, left alone: `0x03002B70` (256 bytes from
`0x08006474`), `0x03002CA0` (64 from `0x08006434`), `0x03007CBF` (73, odd
address): never missed in the sweep or the cache, so most likely tables.

**Result** (600 frames): EX 3,065,484 interpreted instructions -> 6,471,
BL_enemy_turn 342,602 -> 61,434, FF 207,571 -> 66,887; no IWRAM misses.
On EX nearly all of it fell in the scene's first 600 frames (3.07 M of 3.08 M
over 1,800), and its first 200 frames now take 0.92 s instead of 1.26 s on
the Mac; the steady frame is unchanged (4.07 -> 4.05 ms). So it was a
stutter while a scene loads, not a slower frame.

**Verified.** Old binary against new, `GBARECOMP_COMPOSE_HASH` (every
composed frame) and the final picture, at 600 and 1,800 frames on EX, BL,
FF, EM, AF, EV, CI, EU: all 16 identical; a 2,400-frame cold boot
identical. Both invariants (240 `66e13ab2`, anchor-off 284 `9054c456`,
centre 0/160).

**Then the rest: every saved state fully static (same day).** The 159 ROM
PCs from the cache were classified by the code at each: 53 are function
entries placed right after a literal pool or a return, reached only through
pointers (25 start with a push, the rest are short leaves; among them the
four that ran every frame in battle: `0x08007698`, `0x080124BC` push,
`0x080079D0` a 5-instruction leaf, `0x08076524` a lone `bx lr`). Each is an
`[[extra_func]]`. The 105 interior PCs were not listed one by one: after
regenerating, the dispatch table was checked for every one of the 159, and
the new bodies' resume entries covered all but four. Three of those were a
switch the finder's auto_jt did not size (`mov pc, r0` at `0x08073596`, the
table's address loaded from the pool): a `[[jump_table]]` of 129 abs32 Thumb
targets at `0x080735A0`. The last, `0x08000808`, was recorded in ARM mode
in Thumb code during the 09-17 bring-up and is left out. Running BL past
600 frames then found 49 more PCs in the enemy's turn (none new: the old
build had them too, behind the others); two entries, `0x080AF61C` and
`0x081096A0`, covered all 49. 50,042 -> 50,591 functions.

After: **all 169 loadable states fully static** at 600 frames (27 before),
BL at 3,600 frames fully static (412,055 interpreted instructions before);
old against new byte-identical on 17 runs (EX, BL, FF, EM, AF, EV, CI, EU at
600 and 1,800, BL at 3,600) and a 2,400-frame cold boot; both invariants.
Left: the cold boot interprets three IWRAM PCs near `0x03007DC0` (22,144
instructions over the boot, not looked into), and the recompiler's
pre-existing warning about an auto table at `0x08610BC8`.

**The Thor records its misses (same day).** gbarecomp: each miss also counts
its interpreted instructions (`insns` per PC in the coverage JSON), and
`GBARECOMP_MISS_FLUSH_FRAMES=N` rewrites the coverage JSON every N frames
once anything was bridged and the counts moved, from the guest thread beside
the save flush (present hook, outer loop, and the headless hook). Off by
default; byte-identical on and off. `main_android.cpp` points it at
`files/misses/coverage_<date>_<time>.json`, one file per launch, every 600
frames (the app is killed, not exited, so the exit-time write never
happened). Pull them with
`adb exec-out "run-as com.koldecomp.game tar c files/misses" | tar x`.
Tested on the Mac by killing a run (SIGALRM): the file was there, the
per-PC counts summing to the total.

**Compiled code against the interpreter** (measured the same day, Mac, EM
headless at 240, `GBARECOMP_FORCE_INTERP=1`): the frame 3.9 -> 13.9 ms;
the CPU emulation ~2.7 -> ~12.8 ms (the drawing, ~1.1-1.2 ms, the same in
both); the instructions themselves ~0.2 ms against ~7.8 ms. The forced
mode copies the CPU state in and out and checks for a mod hook on every
instruction (~30% of its samples), so ~40x is an upper bound; ~20x is
likelier for the bridge.

### The sky flashed beside a black screen after a scene load (2026-10-19)

Reported on the Thor from slot 3 (states/HV: the burning town, map 99, to the
smoke scene, map 100): the sky flashed for a frame or two. One frame, the
first after the game's 26-frame load hold: the native picture black, the far
left of the left margin the game's blue sky gradient. Not the perspective
(the flat view showed it too), not a fade (BLDY 0 then), not a window (none
enabled), not map_source (KOL_WS_NO_MAP_SOURCE=1 made it bigger). The game's
map layers were still cleared and a black curtain sat on its HUD layers,
which the margins leave out, so they showed the backdrop. Fixed in gbarecomp
(ENHANCEMENTS "A black native picture keeps black margins"): a frame whose
native 240x160 is black from edge to edge has black margins. A first try,
waiting a second verified frame before map_source re-arms, changed nothing
and was reverted. Over the 140 presents of the transition with the Thor's
settings: 0 flashes (was 1). Both invariants unchanged.

### Re-verifying

```sh
# faithful path unchanged (expect identical md5s vs a pre-change build)
./build/KnightOfLodisRecomp --rom totkol.gba --bios ../gbarecomp/bios/gba_bios.bin \
    --no-window --quiet --load-state states/B_rictor_highlighted_map.state \
    --frames 4 --dump-bmp out240.bmp

# The 284 reference 84a95b05 is the anchor-OFF dump (the command below). With
# anchoring and pinning on, 284 is 22896dfb, on the old and new builds alike.
# Since 2026-09-24 that state's rain is repeated into the margins, so the
# anchor-off 284 dump is 9054c456; add KOL_WS_NO_WEATHER_REPEAT=1 to get
# 84a95b05 back byte for byte. Centre-240 identity is 0/160 either way.
# centre-240 identity at any wider width: crop the middle 240 columns of the
# widened dump and compare byte-for-byte with out240.bmp. HUD anchoring moves
# pixels inside that region ON PURPOSE, so this check runs with it disabled.
KOL_WS_NO_HUD_ANCHOR=1 KOL_WS_NO_PANEL_PIN=1 \
    ./build/KnightOfLodisRecomp ... --view-width 284 --dump-bmp out284.bmp
```

## kol_focus.cpp and kol_perspective.cpp refactored (2026-11-02)

The user asked for the two very large files to be searched for repeated
code, unoptimised functions and anything else worth refactoring, and for a
careful refactor. Done in two steps. First, seven
read-only surveys of slices of the two files gave a list of candidates. Then
seven batches, one after another, applied them. Every batch had to leave the
pictures byte-identical; whatever could not be proven identical was left
out (listed below). The legacy `KOL_*` A/B switches all stay (the user's
choice).

**Where things are now.** kol_focus.cpp (15,234 lines) is split by subject:

| File | Lines | What |
|---|---|---|
| kol_focus.cpp | 3,347 | the capture, `build_scene_now` and its `SceneBuild` phases, the terrain pass, the debug arc |
| kol_focus_internal.h | 1,765 | what the focus files share: the guest addresses, the capture, the per-pixel buffers (inline variables with their comments), small per-pixel helpers, cross-file declarations (`// (file)` names the file that defines each one) |
| kol_focus_tables.h | 1,045 | the per-map tables (kMapSuns, kDarkMaps, kMapWindows, the record lists, ...) |
| kol_focus_queries.cpp | 409 | the guest-state queries in kol_focus.h (cursor, acting unit, target, damage numbers, talents) |
| kol_focus_sprites.cpp | 1,115 | `Unit`, the draw order, `claim_unit_sprites` (now `OamClaim` and its phases) |
| kol_focus_atlas.cpp | 1,339 | the sprite atlas, lifted props and walls, flame cards, `grow_over_sprite` |
| kol_focus_cutouts.cpp | 1,456 | the props passes: prop_base, cut-outs, BG1 shapes (map 102), spread |
| kol_focus_roofs.cpp | 688 | the editor's roofs, awnings and boxes, with their cache |
| kol_focus_models.cpp | 974 | the map models, `model_occluder`, the model shadow and the model pass |
| kol_focus_lamps.cpp | 725 | map lamps, chandeliers, door lights, `lamp_and_window_light` |
| kol_focus_windows.cpp | 964 | window light (beams, haze, cones, the moon), map 71's shutter |
| kol_focus_shadows.cpp | 1,096 | the sun, the shadow map, unit and prop shadows (sun, windows, lamps) |
| kol_focus_present.cpp | 1,095 | `focus_provider` and `kol::scene_pixels` with the masks they hand over |
| kol_workers.{h,cpp} | 201 | the row pool and the worker's section timer |

kol_perspective.cpp (5,781 -> 6,044) stays one file. `warp_provider` is
70 lines now, made of named phases (`WarpFrame`, the `warp_*` steps,
`fill_card` and its pieces). `apply_lighting` runs its steps per 16-row run
instead of one full-frame pass each. Shared small headers: `kol_env.h`
(`env_true`, `env_num_or`, `env_items`, ...: 89 copied getenv lambdas
replaced), `kol_hash.h` (`fnv_mix`, `fnv_ints`, `fnv_bytes`: ~55
hand-written key mixes), `kol_oam.h` (the OAM size tables, which had four
copies, and the texel fetch). Altogether the code is ~5% longer than before:
the split adds function headers and declarations. The goal was structure and
speed, not fewer lines.

**Faster.** The present worker's mean per picture on the Mac (pl/worker_time.sh,
all effects on, 384x216, 600 pictures), pre-refactor binary vs now, run
back to back:

| State | Before | After | |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0050 (map 71, shutter + window light) | 7.358 ms | 5.967 ms | -19% |
| B_rictor (rain battle) | 6.665 | 6.384 | -4% |
| HQ (map 99 fire) | 6.890 | 6.310 | -8% |
| GN (rain, overcast) | 8.997 | 8.202 | -9% |

The cuts: the lighting steps fused per run (`par_runs`), the strips-behind
merge, window shadows' buffers, per-frame memos of cell heights and record
rules in `build_scene_now` (`CellHeights`), the sun read once per build,
env switches read once instead of every call or pixel. Thor not measured.

**Checked.** After every group of edits: the 52-render list
(pl/refactor_check.sh) byte-identical to the pre-refactor baseline, and
both invariants (66e13ab2, 9054c456). Each batch also ran its own A/B
against the old binary, over 300 renders in all, covering the areas it
touched. They included spells, ice, water, wet rain, fire, map 51's slime
during a pan, roofs, models, the moon, Tile Info and the cache self-checks
(`KOL_PASS/ROOF/BG1_CACHE_CHECK`: 0 mismatches). For the guest-state
queries, the `KOL_SHEET_PROBE` logs were compared instead. Finally, on the
final tree: the 52 renders, the invariants and the APK build. A few renders
(map 51's pan replay, EU's story scene, 0039) can come out differently when
three run at once, on the old binary too. Rendered one at a time they always
match: the input replay is keyed to absolute guest frames.

**Left out, because it would change pictures or was not worth it:**
- Two suspected bugs, left for the user and then fixed: see "Two bugs the
  refactor turned up" below.
- Floating-point helpers (scene projection, smoothstep, colour packing):
  the order of operations and FMA contraction differ from site to site, so
  sharing them is not provably identical.
- A cache for window unit shadows (`cast_window_shadows`, 0.18 ms on map
  71): no key covers what it reads. The same goes for a band-only copy for
  the roof cache.
- `build_scene_now`'s biggest phases were not split further (cutouts 905
  lines, the model pass 624, roofs 478, terrain 459).

**Rules for the next change in these files:**
- A function that runs per pixel and is called from another focus file
  belongs `inline` in kol_focus_internal.h. A plain cross-file call cost
  0.2-0.3 ms a picture before this was done.
- kol_focus_internal.h is wrapped in `#pragma GCC visibility push(hidden)`.
  Without it, the shared inline variables go through the GOT on the Mac
  and the PLT on Android.
- The shared namespace is the global `kol_focus_detail` (with a
  using-directive), not `kol::`. Inside `kol::`, a name like
  `glow_strength`, which exists in both, would silently bind to the
  `kol::` one.
- Inside `SceneBuild` and `OamClaim`, an unqualified name that matches a
  member is the member. Grep the phases before adding one.
- An env switch read by several members is a lazy static, not a
  namespace-scope dynamic initialiser. main_android.cpp sets files/env.cfg
  with SDL_setenv after static initialisation.
- The sun queries in `build_scene_now` run on the build thread. Never call
  them from a pool callback: `t_present` is thread_local, so a pool thread
  would read the guest's live sun.
- `cell_height` is memoised per frame. Anything that writes `drawn[]` after
  the memo is made would leave it stale.

### Two bugs the refactor turned up (fixed 2026-11-02)

The user asked to look into the two bugs. Both are older than the refactor.

**Unit shadows on walls turned away from their light** (since 9b5a1d9,
2026-10-01). `card_shadow` leaves out a wall turned away from the light,
since that wall is in its own shadow already. The lamp light skips such a
wall too (`facing <= 0` in `lamp_and_window_light`), so a unit's shadow
there only darkened light from other sources. The test was meant to ask
whether `g_face` is scene-sized, but it compared `g_face` with
`g_cast_mark`, the sun pass's mark, which is sized only after the sun
pass's shadows are cast. That left two holes:
- the faces were not tested on a session's first sun frame, or after a size
  change;
- on a dark map (lamps, windows) they were tested only if a lit map at the
  same view size came first.

Shadows are cached per unit and view, so a still unit kept that first
frame's shadow until it or the camera moved. Now `g_face` is compared with
w*h. 10 of the 52 check renders change, by 2-468 pixels each, all lighter
(+3 to +11 per channel): map 63's tent edge facing away from the campfire,
a map 51 wall facing away from the pots, map 62's raised-floor edges, and
maps 55, 67, 89, 97 and 102. `KOL_CAST_FACE_BY_MARK=1`: as before.

**A flying unit's blob stood with its unit** (since 9553112, 2026-10-05).
In `OamClaim::pixel_owners`, a misplaced brace put the pass that lays a
blob drawn apart from its unit's frame (`g_blob_of`) on the ground inside
the loop over priority-0 entries. With no cursor, hand or menu on screen
it never ran. It now runs after that loop. Nothing seen changes: no check
render, and no frame of 14 states logged (200 frames each, FF and BL 900),
had a blob without a priority-0 entry. `KOL_BLOB_NEEDS_IFACE=1`: as
before.

Both switches together give the old pictures byte for byte, and both
invariants hold (66e13ab2, 9054c456).

## Rumble (2026-10-19)

Asked for: the groundwork for rumble, as a menu option, with the thunder as
the first test.

**The option.** Options > Rumble, under the controls: Off / Light / Medium
(the default) / Strong, saved as `rumble=` (strength 0, 0.4, 0.7, 1.0).
Changing it plays a short pulse at the new strength.

**What plays it.** The Thor's built-in controller has no motors of its own
(`dumpsys input`: no vibrator on the input device, `mVibrateInputDevices=
false`), but the device has a vibrator (id 0) with amplitude control
(`dumpsys vibrator_manager`). SDL2 has no controller rumble on Android
(`ANDROID_JoystickRumble` returns unsupported), and its haptic layer plays
one strength for a time only. So:
- Android: `Rumble.java` drives the device's vibrator with
  `VibrationEffect.createWaveform(timings, amplitudes)`: an effect plays as
  its waveform, step by step (a one-shot where there is no amplitude
  control). main_android.cpp binds `Rumble.play(int[] ms, int[] levels)` on
  SDLThread and sets it as kol_rumble's backend; `android.permission.
  VIBRATE` in the manifest.
- Desktop: gbarecomp's new seam `gbarecomp_host_rumble(low, high, ms)`
  (runtime.h; SDL_GameControllerRumble on the open controller, any thread,
  0 when nothing took it), stepped through the waveform on the wall clock
  from the frame hook (`kol::rumble_frame`).

**Effects.** `src/kol_rumble.{h,cpp}`: an effect is a list of steps
(duration, strength 0..1), scaled by the option. Started by what the game
does, through declining hooks. The first: sound effects, by a
`[[mod_function_hook]]` on MP2K's `m4aSongNumStart` 0x0815C4E8 (the game's
sound routine calls it for music and effects alike; r0 the song number),
with a table of the songs that rumble. The thunder is song 205 (player 3),
found by a ROM read watch over the song table (0x08167BB8 + 8 n:
`GBARECOMP_READ_WATCH=0x08167BB8,0x081683B8,4000`) across HW's thunder:
read at frame ~17895 (the first lightning, a palette flash) and ~18448 (the
white flash). Its rumble: a crack, then a roll that swells once and dies
away (1.2 s: 30 ms 1.0, 50 0.5, 80 0.85, 120 0.6, 150 0.7, 200 0.45, 250
0.3, 300 0.15). `KOL_RUMBLE_LOG=1` logs each effect, its strength and its
player, headless too: HW plays it at both thunderclaps, HT (the rain
battle) twice in 1500 frames. To add an effect for another sound: find its
number the same way and add a row to `kSoundRumbles`; for anything else,
call `kol::rumble_play` from the hook that sees it.

Not yet felt on the Thor. Both invariants hold (66e13ab2, 9054c456); the
hook declines every call, so the guest is untouched. `game.toml` changed:
regenerate `generated/`.

### Shaher's death (2026-11-12)

The user asked for rumble wherever it fits in the whole death sequence
(Thor state 0247, states/final_battle_won_route_b.state: map 57,
story scene 179). `KOL_SONG_LOG=1` now prints each sound with the frame of
the last present; read with the picture and the blend registers per frame
(TCP rig, A every 60 frames), counted from the state:

| Frames | What the game shows | Rumble |
|---|---|---|
| 232, 314, 337 | three white flashes, each with sound 418 | a jolt each (40 ms 1.0, 60 0.55, 100 0.3, 80 0.12) |
| 464-664 | his rays (BLDCNT 0x334C, EVA 0 -> 16 -> 0) | 0.15 + 0.35 x EVA/16 |
| 959-1066 | the demon (BG1) fading away (BLDCNT 0x3142) | 0.30 rising to 0.70 |
| 1079-1136 | brightened to white (BLDCNT 0x00BF, BLDY 0 -> 16) | 0.70 rising to 1.0 |
| 1136 | full white | a burst (250 ms 1.0, 200 0.6, 250 0.3, 300 0.12) |
| after | white held, back from white on Shaher as a man, his words | none |

The text's blip (sound 180, every 2 frames while a line types) does not
rumble. The steady parts are sent from the frame hook (`rumble_scene_frame`,
the frame's I/O) as 140 ms steps, again when the level moves by 0.05 or every
100 ms: Android's vibrator plays only the newest effect. The fading is by
time: its weights are written partway through each frame (BLDALPHA reads
0x1000 at the frame's start, and in the game's shadow 0x03000E1C; 0x10 ->
0x1000 only by the frame's end). All of it only on map 57 in scene 179 while
a story event runs; sound 418 elsewhere does nothing. `KOL_RUMBLE_LOG=1`
prints each step with its level and frame. `KOL_NO_DEATH_RUMBLE=1` off. Not
felt on the Thor; the strengths are my picks.

### A blow landing (2026-11-13)

Asked for: rumble when an attack lands. Every blow that lands brings up
a damage number (0x0202AFCC), whatever the weapon or the spell; the sounds
differ (BV's sword 410 + 376, IE's arrow 194 then 189). So a new number
rumbles (kol_rumble `hit_frame`, every guest frame), when it is damage, not a
heal: an attack writes the hit unit's HP about 2 s before its number, so a
battle record's HP dropping is a blow waiting for its number (a counterattack:
two drops, two numbers); a talent writes after its numbers, so by its result
list (`talent_results`: the unit's entry, not a heal). Drops while a number is
up or within 90 frames after are a talent's late write; a drop no number takes
in 600 frames is forgotten. Short punch (40 ms 0.9, 60 0.45, 70 0.15); a blow
taking the unit to 0 HP the heavier kill (60 1.0, 90 0.6, 120 0.3, 120 0.1).
Checked with `KOL_RUMBLE_LOG=1`: BV, HZ, IE and BL's enemy blow rumble on the
frame of the impact sound (BV 105 / 106, HZ 77 / 78, BL 220774 / 220775); IB's
heal does not; ID's Ice Javelin once, IF's Crag Crush four times, one a unit;
an idle map never. `KOL_NO_HIT_RUMBLE=1` off.

### Every rumble a little late (2026-11-13)

Asked for every rumble to start 80 ms late (still ending at the same time), then
cut to 40 ms: `rumble_play` turns each waveform's first 40 ms
into stillness (steps inside it dropped, the one it ends in shortened), so it starts 40 ms
later and ends when it did: a hit (40 0.9, 60 0.45, 70 0.15) is now 40 still, 60 0.45, 70 0.15.
Only from stillness: an effect sent while one still plays carries on at once (Shaher's death
refreshes a 140 ms step every ~100 ms; delayed each time it would come apart into pulses). An
effect no longer than the delay is not felt. Android without amplitude control plays the
waveform on/off (it played one buzz the whole length, the pause lost). `KOL_RUMBLE_DELAY=<ms>`
(0: none).

Then about 20 ms longer for hits and everything else battle-related: the battle's two (the blow, the kill) have the first part still felt after
the 40 ms 20 ms longer, and end 20 ms later: hit 40 0.9, 80 0.45, 70 0.15 (40 still, 80 0.45,
70 0.15 as felt); kill 80 1.0, 90 0.6, 120 0.3, 120 0.1 (40 of the 1.0 felt, was 20). Blocks
and misses bring up no damage (no HP lost, no talent damage) and do not rumble.

Then Thor state 0260 (map 52): the counterattack did not rumble. Rictor's attack on a 999-HP
unit took nothing (a 0) and the counter took his HP, both written at the action's start; the
numbers were matched to the drops by order, so the attack's 0 took the counter's drop (and
rumbled) and the counter's number found none. Each number now takes the drop of the unit it
stands over (its map object's record, +0x00 of the object `damage_number_unit` finds), kept per
unit; a number over a unit that lost nothing (a 0, a block) does not rumble; with no unit found
there, the drop that has waited longest. Drops while a number is up count (a counter's can be
written then); only the 90 frames after a number has gone are a talent's late write.
`KOL_RUMBLE_LOG=1` also logs each number's unit slot (0260: the attack over slot 1, nothing
lost; the counter over slot 8, Rictor). BV, HZ, IE, BL, IB, ID, IF rumble as before.

## Sound

Asked for on 2026-09-29: a sound engine rewrite so the game sounds better.
Two parts shipped, both in gbarecomp (ENHANCEMENTS.md §5 has
the mechanism and the traps); this section is what is specific to KoL.

**What the game's sound is.** MP2K (m4a), SoundInfo at `0x02002B30`: 6 voices
mixed at 15768 Hz into 8-bit bytes, DMA period 6 frames, no reverb in any song
checked. The driver runs in **mono mode**: SOUNDCNT_H `0x030E` routes FIFO A to
both sides and leaves B off, and each voice's gain is `env*(volR+volL) >> 9` —
yet the songs carry real pan (volR/volL), which the driver throws away. The PSG
voices are routed per side by SOUNDCNT_L `0x5677`: square 1 left, square 2
right, wave both. They carry more energy than the sampled instruments.

**1. The mixer (accuracy, always on).** Stereo output, the PSG at mGBA's level
(it was ~3.9 dB hot), PSG edges band-limited. Checked: the capture ring's raw
PSG and FIFO taps are byte-identical to the pre-change build; per-side loudness
matches mGBA's formula (3396 vs 3404 RMS on battle); a state saved by the new
build reloads byte-identically; old states load.

**2. The high-quality music (Options > Sound…).** "Original (hardware mix)",
"High quality, mono", "High quality, stereo" (default). Persisted as `sound=`
in enhancements.cfg. The music voices are re-rendered in float from the
driver's state, and every tick is checked byte for byte against the buffer the
game's driver wrote; a tick that differs plays the hardware mix and logs
`DEGRADED`. On the desktop it is off unless `GBARECOMP_AUDIO_SHADOW=1` (or
`mono`), so the invariants and headless runs are unaffected.

Measured: every tick verified on AU (battle), AF (world map), AG (title), BL
(enemy turn), CS, CN, BW, AK and a 9000-frame cold boot (only the BIOS chime,
whose driver uses reverb, plays canon). Coverage 99.0-99.7% after a state
load: the first ~50 ms anchor. Thor: +0.12M guest cycles/frame (+0.4%),
59.8 fps either way. The Thor's audio track is stereo (channel mask 0x3).

Listening files (loudness as heard, 20 s each): `shots/sound_ab/engine/`
`{battle,worldmap,title}_{1_before,2_mixer_fix,3_hq_mono,4_hq_stereo}.wav`.
The earlier offline mock-ups are beside them in `shots/sound_ab/`. The offline
tools (TCP capture of SoundInfo + channels + buffer, the Python driver model,
spectrograms) are in `tools/mockup/sound/`; they need numpy/scipy.

**HD instruments (2026-10-18).** Options > Sound is Original / HQ / HD, saved
as `music_quality=` 0/1/2 (HQ mono is gone; an older `sound=` reads 0 as
Original, 1 or 2 as HQ). HD's instruments are from the FluidR3_GM soundfont
by Frank Wen and Toby Smithe (MIT licence).

- *What the music is made of* (ROM parse, all 32 songs on one voicegroup
  `0x081669E8`): 14 PCM samples (9 melodic, a pitched drum `0x0818B914`, 4
  drums), all at 15.7 kHz; ~57% of the music's notes are PSG (squares: 3 duties
  x 8 envelopes; wave: 5 tables). No keysplits, no DPCM, no noise channel.
- *The mapping* is `tools/hd_audio/kol_hd_map.json` (one source): sample ->
  instrument with its pitch offset (KoL's samples are not C at key 60:
  `0x0816987C` sounds +3.97, `0x081792FC` +8, `0x08176318` +20, measured from
  the harmonics two ways), drums -> Orchestra Kit keys (the looped snare roll
  `0x08190C54` = the same snare rolled at 16 strokes/s, accents 0.7: the
  original's loop pulses at 8 Hz), and per song the PSG: battle (song 4)
  squares String Ensemble, wave Pizzicato; world map (10) Flute / Oboe (the
  user's pick over Clarinet) / String drone; song 6 French Horns / Pizzicato;
  title (song 28) French Horns on both squares / String Ensemble on the
  pulse-wave low part (the user's call, after trying Choir Aahs and Cello);
  battle preparation (song 9) English Horn melody (picked from nine winds:
  the Piccolo of version B sounded like it could be a brass instrument)
  / String Ensemble / Pizzicato; the opening (song 24: the boat, the
  archers' town) Flute on square 1 / Oboe a fifth under on square 2 /
  String Ensemble drone on the wave (the user's pick C of six, 2026-10-19);
  the battle theme song 1 (state AN) String Ensemble on both squares /
  Pizzicato bass on the wave (pick B of six); song 2 (state CB) String Ensemble /
  Flute on the fast high part / Pizzicato bass (pick B of six); song 3
  (state BD) String Ensemble / Orchestral Harp / Flute melody on the wave
  (pick D of six); song 5 (state FF) Flute / Piccolo / String drone (pick
  B of six); the castle battle, song 7 (state EM), French Horns on both
  squares / Cello on the wave (pick B of six); the ruins battle, song 13

  user asked for English Horns, pick G of four); the fortune teller, song
  22 (state FC), String Ensemble / English Horn / Harp on the wave's quick

  on both squares' fast runs / String Ensemble on the wave (pick C of six);

  songs plays every voice HD.
  The bell
  sample
  `0x0816B198` (songs 7, 11, 17, 21, 29) is Tubular Bells, the user's pick of
  six bells (`KOL_HD_SAMPLE_MAP`, the sample rows' trial switch) over the
  matcher's unauditioned Electric Piano.
  **2026-11-11:** the bells in the playing song were reported slightly off key
  (Thor state 225, song 29): the row played them at the matcher's +4.1
  semitones (a bell's partials fooled it). Recorded from the game, effects muted,
  at +4.1 / +4 / 0 / -8 against the game's own bell: the user took 0, then 4 dB
  down (first a bit quieter, then -4 dB on all of them). The game with the built row is
  byte-identical to that recording. Songs 7, 11, 17, 21, 29.
  Mock-ups from a state taken mid-fight are recorded with
  `GBARECOMP_AUDIO_MIX=100,0` (effects muted).
  The Orchestra Kit plays at 80% (-1.94 dB) in every song (asked with the
  opening, to apply everywhere); the timpani are not part of the kit and keep
  their level.
  The wave channel's one-cycle tables sound an octave below the key
  (transpose -12). Songs not listed keep the chip on the PSG; their PCM
  samples are HD everywhere. Picks marked "unauditioned" in the JSON came
  from a spectral matcher, not from listening.
- *Build:* `tools/hd_audio/get_soundfont.sh` (FluidR3 from Debian, sha256
  checked), `build_bank.py --atten-factor 1.0` -> `build/hd_instruments.bank`
  (29.5 MB, 13 instruments; 1.0 = the attenuation the approved mock-ups used),
  `gen_map.py` -> `src/kol_hd_map.inc`. The APK packs the bank as a stored
  asset; desktop finds it next to the binary or via `KOL_HD_BANK`. It is
  loaded only when HD is chosen. `KOL_MUSIC_QUALITY=0|1|2` sets the choice
  headless; `KOL_HD_PSG=0` leaves the PSG to the chip (A/B).
- *Mock-ups first:* the offline renderer (capture.py + hd.py, session
  scratchpad, gone) was A/B'd with the user: the Standard kit's drums were
  rejected, the Orchestra Kit with the
  snare roll accepted (mock-up 9); Clarinet rejected for Oboe.
- *Mock-ups from the game itself (2026-10-19, song 24 on):* the opening runs
  the sound driver twice in some frames (the driver's pcmDmaCounter skips a
  step about 20 times a minute), so the offline renderer, which takes one
  tick per frame, drifts off the game there (2-4% of its bytes matched where
  battle preparation matches 100%). Instead the game renders the candidates:
  `KOL_HD_PSG_MAP=<file>` (desktop) reads trial PSG rows, one per line,
  `song channel bank prog transpose gain_db` (song in hex), each replacing
  the built-in row for its song and channel; a trial bank holds the
  candidate instruments (`build_bank.py --map trial.json --out trial.bank`,
  `KOL_HD_BANK=trial.bank`); `GBARECOMP_AUDIO_RAW` records 65536 Hz stereo.
  *Clicks between notes (fixed 2026-10-19, song 15's reported clicks on the right
  channel):* between an HD channel's notes the mixer fell back to the
  chip, and a silent chip channel holds its last output level, so an offset
  (about -2300 on song 15) stepped in when a note ended and out when the next
  began. Song 15 routes square 1 to the right only (SOUNDCNT_L 0x6777),
  hence the side. gbarecomp now keeps the chip out of a channel the playing
  song maps (HdPsg::owned) between its notes too. Every HD song had them:
  27-68 clicks a minute on songs 1, 2, 7, 8, 13, 14, 24 before, 0-8 after
  (song 3's remaining events are its plucked bass's attacks).
  *Clipping (fixed 2026-10-19, song 30):* song 30's reported clicks were the right
  side pinned at the DAC's clamp. Two causes, both in gbarecomp (ENHANCEMENTS
  "HD instruments"): a replacement's level was matched over the first 0.35 s,
  where String Ensemble 1 and the English Horn swell in, so held notes came
  out hot; now over 1 s of a held note, loops played out. And real
  instruments at a square wave's RMS peak far higher: an HD-only limiter now
  sits under the clamp. Measured over all 28 HD songs from the same start:
  0 clamped samples (was up to ~2000 a minute), HD 0.3-3.6 dB over HQ (median
  ~+1.2), HQ bit-identical.
  What the user hears is then exactly what ships: the opening built from
  the JSON recorded byte-identical to the approved mock-up.
- *Any song, from any state (desktop only, 2026-10-19):* `KOL_PLAY_SONG=n`
  starts song n on the third frame through MP2K's m4aSongNumStart
  `0x0815C4E8` (song table `0x08167BB8`, 8 bytes a song; the game's own
  sound routine `0x0814506C` calls it once its sound bit is set), from the
  hook on `0x080020B8` that the menu sound uses. `KOL_MP2K_DUMP=path` writes
  the driver's state every frame (SoundInfo and its channels, the CGB
  channels, IO 0x60-0x8F), what capture.py reads over TCP, so a song's parts
  can be listed without the TCP rig (which runs none of KoL's hooks). Both
  are compiled out of Android. Survey of the 19 songs no state reached:
  11 (16 s) and 12 (8 s) are jingles, the rest play past 60 s; song 30 has
  no wave part.
- *Found on the way, fixed for every mode:* after a state load the wave
  channel was silent (wave RAM is not in the snapshot and the driver never
  rewrites a table it thinks is loaded): the battle theme had no bass after
  any slot load. gbarecomp now restores the driver's last table (ENHANCEMENTS
  "Wave RAM after a state load"). The mock-ups were captured from states, so
  their wave-channel level had been matched to that silence.
- *Verified* (headless, three songs, `GBARECOMP_AUDIO_RAW`): every tick still
  verified (99.7%+, as HQ); HQ bit-identical before and after; HD within
  ~1-4 dB of the approved mock-ups per octave band (the battle's deepest bass
  ~4 dB under: the game now follows the chip's real wave level). Both render
  invariants hold.
- *On the Thor* (2026-10-19): the user played it and approved. Cost,
  HQ/HD/HQ/HD on GN (rain battle, song 9 with every voice HD; 384x216, all
  effects), restart + slot load per leg, `simpleperf stat --per-thread` 10 s:
  guest thread 27.04 / 27.38 / 26.65 / 27.33 M cycles a frame, so HD costs
  ~0.5 M (~2%) on the guest thread, where the mixer runs; the audio threads
  unchanged (0.34 + 0.16 M), fps unchanged (56.4-56.6; the scene's own cost,
  the present worker at ~27 M, sets that). **Open (the user, 10-19):** find
  why GN holds ~56.5 fps and get it to ~60. Neither thread is saturated
  (each ~55% of a core), and EM ran 59.3-59.8 fps on 10-14 with more CPU
  work, so look at the GPU (rain, depth of field) and the worker hand-off
  before cutting CPU.

**3. Music and effects apart, effects placed, soft tones (2026-09-29, later).**
The shadow now knows every voice's owner: the driver's players are linked
from SoundInfo +0x24, the last is player 0 (the music: 8 tracks at
`0x02029B00` in the states checked), the others play effects; each PCM and
PSG voice names its track. So, in the high-quality modes:

- Options > "Music volume…" and "Effects volume…" (0-100%, persisted as
  `music_volume=` / `effects_volume=`). Checked: music-only plus effects-only
  equals the full mix exactly.
- "Sound effects come from where they happen" (a toggle, on by default,
  `effects_placed=`): `kol_sound.cpp` names a place every real frame — the map
  cursor while it is out, the unit being hit while a damage number is up
  (the game's highlighted unit, `0x02028960`), otherwise the acting unit
  (`0x0202A5F0`) — from its sprite slot's screen position (+0x1C/+0x1E). Pan:
  full at 96 hardware pixels from the middle, capped at 0.9; up to 20% quieter
  toward the top (farther). The mixer folds the effects to one voice and pans
  them (equal power), smoothed over ~30 ms. Measured: **the camera keeps the
  action near the middle** (the enemy turn follows its unit at x = 120; in BV
  attacker and target stand 16 px apart), so fights are placed subtly; the
  cursor's sounds sweep -0.6..+0.6 as it crosses the map.
  `KOL_SOUND_LOG=1` prints the source when it moves. The TCP rig does not run
  KoL's frame hook, so test this with `--load-state` and
  `GBARECOMP_INPUT_REPLAY` (absolute frames: B_rictor starts at 28213).
- "Soft tone channels" (a toggle, off by default, `soft_tones=`; works in every
  mode): a 2-pole low-pass at 5.5 kHz on the square/wave/noise channels. On
  the enemy turn's PSG: -5 dB at 5-10 kHz, -16 dB above 10 kHz, fundamentals
  untouched.

**More voices (asked, measured, not done).** Voices taken while still sounding,
counted per tick by the shadow: none by an effect, in attacks, spells, the
enemy turn and targeting (1800 frames each with A pressed every 1.5 s); only
5 music-over-music in 30 s of battle music. The 6 voices are not a bottleneck,
so the game's voice count was left alone. The counters are in the status line
(`steals mus<-mus … cuts mus … fx …`).

**4. Tempo rushing and crackle in menus and while units move (2026-09-29,
night).** Reported on the Thor with the hardware mix too, whatever the
graphics settings. The audio probe showed no underrun at all: emulation ran
FAST, 1.03-1.34x real time, and the bridge dropped the surplus (overflow drops
climbing, buffer pinned near 290 ms). Cause, in gbarecomp's runner: the frame
pacer waited once per present, but the present hook runs only at the guest's
yield points, and menus / unit movement run stretches of several emulated
frames without one, so those frames were never paced — the game's own music
sequencer (one tick per frame) rushed with them. Fix: the pacer waits for
every emulated frame a present covers (`FramePacer::wait_for_next_frame(n)`,
up to 120; state loads and rewinds already re-base the frame count). A first
cap of 8 frames still let bursts through (speed 1.09, 180 frames caught);
at 120 the first minute on the Thor read speed ~1.000 and no drops. The
user then heard the opposite (lag, audio late) — see below.

The pacer also threw time away: it resynced as soon as it was one frame
late and never paid back a late wake, and with every frame now paced those
losses added up to 5-7% in busy scenes (the game lagged, the bridge ran dry
and concealed, and concealment turned into lasting latency). It now keeps an
absolute timeline: lateness under 100 ms is caught up by the following
frames, only a longer stall resyncs.

Two audio-bridge changes finished it (gbarecomp `recomp_audio_drc.h`,
`runtime.cpp`):
- **Audio is handed over as the guest makes it** (a `GbaAudio` drain hook,
  every 512 frames), not only at presents: a stretch of frames without a
  present used to deliver its audio in one late lump, which a small buffer
  could not ride out.
- **Latency trim:** concealment never moved the read cursor, so each stall it
  hid became permanent delay, and the 0.5% rate servo drained 5 ms/s. The
  bridge now skips surplus one matched waveform period at a time (4 ms
  crossfade, pitch unchanged) — only surplus: the LOWEST fill over each 250 ms
  must exceed target + 30 ms. A first version trimmed on momentary peaks, cut
  0.85% of the audio and starved the ring (crackle every second).

Result on the Thor, 95 s of menus and moving units: no underrun, no
concealment, no drops, no resync; fill 58 ms average (target 60, low 35);
trims only in the first 1.4 s (the boot pre-roll). The user found it nearly perfect.
`tests/runtime/audio_drc_test.cpp` covers the trim and a bursty producer.

**5. Clicks heard afterwards (2026-09-29, late).** The pipeline stayed clean
(445 s: no gap, fill, drop). Measured on BV with A pressed, the re-rendered
voices alone: 16 hard note starts in 20 s, each also in the hardware mix at
the same sample (a sample starting at a non-zero value: 0 -> 6912). The HQ
render now fades a new note in over 64 samples (~1 ms): 16 -> 2 mild. What
remains is the tone channels: the two squares play 80-90% of the time, and
their edges are ~5600 steep steps in 20 s, the same in every mode; "Soft tone
channels" cuts the mix's steep steps by 94% (8955 -> 528). Also: a tick that
fails its check now crossfades with the hardware mix over 128 samples at both
edges (looking ahead in the verified timeline), so a fallback cannot click;
and `GBARECOMP_AUDIO_HQ_DUMP` records only real model mismatches (the BIOS
chime's reverb ticks used up all eight files before).

Probe on the Thor: `files/env.cfg` (KEY=VALUE lines, read by
`main_android.cpp` at start) holds `GBARECOMP_AUDIO_PROBE=1`; every 2 s the
`[gba-audio-probe]` line in logcat (tag KoL) gives `speed=` (audio produced
per wall second), `overflow_drops=`, `fill_ms=`, `paced_extra_frames=` and
`unpaced=` (gaps over the cap; one ~2000-frame gap appears ~5 s after launch,
not yet identified — a jump, correctly left unpaced).

**Verify:**

```sh
GBARECOMP_AUDIO_SHADOW=1 GBARECOMP_AUDIO_HQ_LOG=600 ./build/KnightOfLodisRecomp \
    --rom totkol.gba --bios ../gbarecomp/bios/gba_bios.bin --no-window --quiet \
    --load-state states/BL_enemy_turn.state --frames 1200 2>&1 | grep "MP2K HQ"
# expect degraded=0 and covered ~99%. GBARECOMP_AUDIO_HQ_DUMP=dir saves failing ticks.
```

**Failed approaches, kept so they are not retried:**

- The shadow already in gbarecomp (a JRickey port) armed on KoL but never
  substituted: its tick hook was a sample counter that needed SoundInfo.ident
  mid-tick at a random moment, and its verifier assumed stereo A/B. Rewritten.
- Offline, comparing a model against the FIFO stream topped out at 95.5%
  byte-exact: the 65536 Hz grid hides the FIFO phase. Comparing against the
  driver's own PCM buffer segment made it 100%.
- A "stereo driver" verdict left over from the BIOS chime broke every game
  tick until it was reset on a new SoundInfo.
- Following each segment's measured start chased emulated-FIFO jitter in heavy
  scenes and lost the anchor; the timeline now stays on ideal frames.
- "An interpolated one-shot too short for the tick is dropped" (the first tail
  rule) was wrong: what drops a voice unmixed is the sequencer stopping its
  track that tick (`MusicPlayerTrack.flags` bit 7 down). Attacks and spells
  showed interpolated one-shots mixed to their end.

The crash that blocked real play is fixed, so the milestones it was
blocking are now reachable:

1. DONE (2026-09-21): menu navigation and a save/load round-trip against
   the Flash 64KB chip are confirmed on the Thor — see "Saving failed, and
   the save never reached disk". Starting a NEW GAME and playing it through
