### Save and Load on the bar, on the world map (2026-10-01)

Asked for (`states/EA_slot1_save_icon.state`: the world map's system menu,
Save highlighted, Load beside it): those two on the bottom bar, world map
only. The bar shows Save and Load (icons 17 and 18 of the R bar's archive
`0x086DA2E4`) left of the Option button, 4 px apart (8 at first; the user
asked for closer), while the world map's
layout is up and the options menu closed (JNI `menuWorld`); each has the
pushed-in look and plays the game's confirm sound.

**Greyed while the game's save or load screen is up** (asked for; elsewhere
off the world map, and with the options menu open, they stay hidden). The
phase is the command menu's: from its queueing 7 or 6 (states 15/16 with
`0x02029C54` = 7 or 6, or 7/6 themselves) until it is back at a pad (1 or
3), whether the screen came from the bar or from the game's own submenu
(`kol::action_file_screen_open`). Greyed buttons take no touch; their frame
is the bar's colours by brightness and the icons their colours' brightness
x 0.6. The ROM's OBJ banks 12-15 are not the menu's dimmed copies (the
menu's 0xC + bank is filled at run time): read from ROM they drew Save red
and Load yellow. The second-screen thread redraws the bar when the mode
(none / on / greyed) changes (`SecondScreen.barChanged`), since nothing else
on that screen changes when the save screen opens.

Each icon tile has its own OBJ palette bank, as the menu draws them
(`0x08127F7C`): a nibble a tile in the table just before the archive
(`0x086DA294` + 4, low nibble first). Save's tiles are bank 1 (its arrow red,
`0x0432`), Load's and Option's bank 0. Drawn first with bank 0 for all, the
Save arrow came out blue (reported); kol_menu now loads all 16 OBJ banks and
that table.

A tap opens the game's own screen the way its system submenu does. The
submenu is the command menu's state 3 (`wm+0x27` = 1, cursor `wm+0x21`); its
A (`0x081285A4`, table `0x081285D0`) queues by item: Save 7, Load 6,
Pumpkin 8 (each behind the fade-out, 15), Option 9 directly, Return to title
a message (4). The flow is the profile flow's (`kol_actions.cpp`):

- From roaming: the R branch (start the menu, suspend roaming); at the menu's
  first pad call the hook sets `wm+0x27` = 1 and `wm+0x21` to the item, then
  queues 7 or 6 and enters 15. The menu's draw stays off all the way.
- The game's screen runs: "Select a save space", "Overwrite data?" (hand on
  No), "Data has been saved", back to the slots; or "Please select the data
  you want to load", "Data has been loaded". The menu waits in 14, fades in
  (17, 18) and returns to the submenu (3), as after its own Save.
- From roaming the hook then gives it B twice (submenu to main menu, main
  menu to roaming; one B when the story has no main menu yet, flag 0x6E), the
  two cancel sounds dropped. With the menu already open it stays on the
  submenu, Save or Load highlighted.
- The screens wait on the player, so the flow has no time limit there; it
  ends when the menu's task stops running (`g_command_seen_ms`, 1 s), e.g.
  after a load, so the menu's draw can never stay hidden.
- Without `wm+0x27`/`wm+0x21` set first, a Save queued from the open main
  menu came back to state 3 drawing the main menu's icons (DW).

Checked headless (the save file written next to a scratch copy of the ROM):
DO Save then B (back to roaming), DO Save on slot 1 with Yes (saved, back to
the slots), DO Load of slot 1 (loaded, roaming at Scabellum, and R then opens
the menu with its icons drawn), DW Save then B (the submenu, Save lit).
`KOL_LIST_TAP="f:save"` / `"f:load"` presses the buttons headless.

### Ambient occlusion on the perspective battlefield (2026-10-01)

Asked for: ambient occlusion on the perspective battlefields. Options >
Ambient Occl.: OFF / Half Tile / Full Tile (`ambient_occlusion=` 0-2 in
enhancements.cfg), strength 0.5 (the user picked 0.7 from mockups at 0.5
and 0.7, then lowered it to 0.5 to go with shadows, below), and asked for the two reaches (`shots/ambient_occlusion/`, gitignored:
`*_full.png`, `*_zoom.png`, `*_reach.png` on the rainy cliffs, the snowfield
and the pillar ruins).

- **Where.** kol_focus's terrain pass rasterises every cell's top face and
  walls itself (back to front), so each pixel it draws knows its cell, its
  face and where in the face it lies. A top-face pixel `(c, r)` from the
  cell's back corner is `a = 2 (r - sy) + c`, `b = 2 (r - sy) - c` world
  units along X and Z (0..32), from the projection.
- **The shade.** Each of the eight neighbours standing higher (in world units,
  16 a step) shades the side or corner next to it, `min(1, rise / 32) * (1 -
  distance / reach)`, the shades combined as independent ones (`1 - prod(1 -
  t)`); a wall darkens toward its foot, `0.6 * (1 - height above its floor /
  reach)`. Reach 16 (half a tile) or 32 (full). The pixel keeps `1 - 0.7 *
  occlusion` of its colour (0.5 since the shadows) (`g_ao`, 255 open).
- **Applied** in the warp provider to the scene before the mesh samples it,
  on the map layers' pixels (BG0/BG1) and the ground under lifted units; not
  on sprites or interface. So it moves and shrinks with the perspective. Only
  with the perspective on.
- **Props keep their own colour** (EK = the user's slot 1, the snowfield's
  trees under the cursor took the dark band of the wall behind them): a
  prop's BG1 art stands over cells the pass shaded, so the pixels the prop
  pass claims (seeded and spread) are reset to no occlusion, shadow or
  torchlight. Checked on EK: after the fix the only shaded pixels around the
  cluster are the wall's foot behind it.
- Not done: props (trees) cast nothing of their own; units get no contact
  shadow (the game draws theirs); the church keeps its model.
- Cost: a few multiplies (eight neighbour shades) per terrain pixel. Not
  measured on the Thor yet (the desktop window runs are paced at 60 fps).
- Tests: `KOL_PERSP_AO=<strength>` and `KOL_PERSP_AO_R=<reach>` override the
  setting. Both render invariants hold (the setting off changes nothing).

**Shadows (2026-10-01, on the Thor for trying).** Asked for: shadows, with
the light always from an imaginary top-right. Options > Shadows: OFF /
High Sun (45 degrees above the ground) / Low Sun (30) / Side Sun (below) /
Low Side Sun (20), `shadows=` 0-4,
strength 0.35, the AO beside it at 0.5. **Since 2026-10-11 the angle is not a
menu pick** (asked: one default shadow angle for every map without an override,
and no sun angle choice in the menu): Shadows is ON / OFF, and a map in `kMapSuns` or with an editor
`sun` line keeps its own. The default sun is the one the user had on the
Thor, on map 9 (BN), read from its log: `KOL_PERSP_SHADOW_ELEV=36.0
KOL_PERSP_SHADOW_DIR=0.585,-0.811` (36 degrees up, to the right and toward
the far side). It is not the former Low Sun (30 from (-1, -3)): the user had
moved the sun with L2, and the saved pick did not say so. A saved
`shadows=1..4` reads as on; `KOL_SHADOWS=<n>`, n != 0, is on. Debug > L2
Moves Sun stays: it is how a map's own sun is set, and it moves from the new
default.

**The sun sinks a degree a turn (2026-10-12, asked for the sun to sink
about 1 degree per turn).** kol_focus
`sun_turn_drop`: the sun's height, the default's or a map's own, less 1
degree for every turn after the first, never below 5 (the arc's lowest).
- **The turn is the game's**, the u16 at `0x020021CC`. Found with the TCP rig:
  6,000 frames of `BL_enemy_turn` sampled every 20; when the enemy phase ends
  (frame 3920, the acting unit `0x0202A5F0` goes to 0) it goes 1 -> 2, and so
  does `0x020021BC` (2 -> 3). Across the 190 saved states only `21CC`
  follows turns: 1 in battle preparation (`AB`, `AA`) and on first turns, 3
  in `CN`, 5 in `CO`-`CT` (one battle, map 40); `21BC` does not. The story
  scenes (map 89) read 1; one after a battle has not been seen.
- **Checked:** BN (turn 1) byte-identical to before; CO (turn 5) default
  byte-identical to an explicit `KOL_PERSP_SHADOW_ELEV=32` on the default
  direction, and with `KOL_SUN_DROP=0` to 36; both invariants unchanged.
  `shots/sun_per_turn/CO_turn1_turn5_turn20.png` is CO at 36 / 32 / 17
  degrees.
- An explicit `KOL_PERSP_SHADOW_ELEV` is taken as it is. `KOL_SUN_DROP=<deg>`
  sets the step (0 off), `KOL_SUN_TURN=<n>` stands in for the game's turn.
- The editor's SET SUN saves the first turn's height (the drop added back),
  so a sun set late in a battle still starts where it was set.
- The terrain's shadows are worked out again once a turn (keyed on the
  height), not every frame.

**Higher at first, sinking faster; shadows by the sun's height and the
weather; evening light (2026-10-12).** Asked: a higher sun on turn 1
that sinks faster, 2 or 3 degrees per turn; darker shadows with a high sun and
softer ones with a low sun; much less shadow contrast in bad weather and snow;
and, before, light turning gradually more orange as turns pass (strength 1.0, the user's pick from `shots/evening/`).
- **The sun:** 60 degrees on turn 1 (`kShadowSunDegrees`), 2.5 a turn
  (`sun_turn_drop`): 37.5 at turn 10, 12.5 at turn 20, the floor of 5 at
  turn 23. Maps' own suns sink at the same rate.
- **The shadows' strength by the height:** `0.5 * sqrt(sin h / sin 36)`,
  0.15..0.65: 0.61 at 60, 0.5 at 36 (where 0.5 was picked), 0.30 at 12.5.
  The sun on level ground goes with the sine of its height while the sky's
  light in the shade does not, so a low sun's shadows are paler. Units' and
  the terrain's alike. `KOL_SHADOW_BY_HEIGHT=0` keeps 0.5.
  **Lifted at the low end (2026-10-14):** asked for more visible
  shadows at the lowest sun, the sine curve not dropping as low. Below 36 degrees the curve is remapped to reach 0.28 at the
  lowest sun (5 degrees) instead of 0.19: 10 degrees 0.34, 20 0.42, 30
  0.47; from 36 up as before (the user's pick of 0.28 / 0.35,
  `shots/low_sun_strength/sheet.png`, the sun at 8 on BN and GM).
  `KOL_SHADOW_LOWEST=<strength>`, negative: as before. Checked: BN at 8
  degrees equals the mockup, GM at turn 1 (60) unchanged, both invariants.
- **Rain and snow:** while the game's weather particles (`0x0202A0F8`, as
  for the wide weather) are live, and 240 frames past the last, the strength
  is x0.35 (`kWeatherShadow`). Latched per capture: the strength is a key of
  the shadow map's cache, and the drops' count changes every frame.
  `KOL_WEATHER=0/1` forces it. Checked: BN (dry), AW (rain, map 9), CI
  (snow, map 40) each equal the forced flag they should.
- **Evening:** kol_focus `evening_amount`, none through turn 6, then an
  ease-in curve (the square of the way along) to 1.0 at turn 21: 0.11 at
  turn 11, 0.44 at 16 (asked to start at turn 6 and follow a curve rather
  than a line; it first rose evenly from turn 1). `KOL_EVENING`,
  `KOL_EVENING_START`, `KOL_EVENING_TURNS`; with Shadows on;
  kol_perspective `evening_tint` (red up, blue down, pulled toward the
  pixel's brightness in orange, like the torchlight) on every
  non-interface pixel in `apply_lighting` and on the atlas's texels. The sky
  backdrop takes it too.
- **Checked:** both invariants; turn 1 with `KOL_EVENING=0` was
  byte-identical before the sun changes. Stills:
  `shots/sun_height/BN_before_now_by_turn.png`,
  `shots/weather_shadows/rain_snow_dry_vs_now.png`.
- **The evening tint in rain or snow** is x0.3 (`kWeatherEvening`; asked
  for less orange in the rain), on the same latch.
- **Only under a grey sky (2026-10-14).** Map 6 rains under its blue sky
  too (GO = the user's slot 3) and under a grey sky with a darker palette
  (GN = slot 2); asked: in GO normal shadows and sun colour, GN as it
  was. The game keeps no overcast flag: its
  weather block after the drops (`0x0202A1C0`) holds the drops' count
  (+0xC8, +0xC9) and an intensity 0..2 (+0xCE), and map 6's heavier rain
  (V, level 2) is under the blue sky. The grey is the palette the battle
  loaded, so the drops count only while the backdrop in the game's own
  palette buffer (`0x02002400`, entry 0) is a near-neutral grey, its 5-bit
  components within 4 (GN, BX 5,7,7; H, B_rictor 5,6,7); a near-black one
  (a fade) keeps the last verdict. Not grey: GO and the other blue skies
  (the snowfield's 0,21,31, so its snow now keeps the normal light), DF's
  pale blue (16,23,27), FU's green. The latched palette's entry 0 is no use
  for this: the sky is a gradient changed line by line, and it holds the
  last line's colour (GO: light cyan 0x7FAB). `KOL_WEATHER_ANY_SKY=1`: as
  before. Checked: GN identical to before, GO identical to `KOL_WEATHER=0`;
  both invariants.
- Not changed by the weather: the occlusion, the godrays. **Darker since 2026-10-10: 0.5**
(asked for slightly darker shadows; the user picked 0.5 from
`shots/shadow_strength/`, 0.35 / 0.5 / 0.65 / 0.8 on B_rictor, BN, EM and
EU; 0.8 turned the castle's shaded walls near black). Units cast and take
shade at the same strength.
- **The light.** Screen top-right is world `(X, Z) = (-1, -3)` (screen right
  is `X - Z`, up is `-(X + Z)`), so shadows fall toward the camera, down-left,
  onto the ground in front of steps and cliffs: the part the camera sees.
- **The map.** Every cell top is split into 8 x 8 spots; from each spot a ray
  climbs toward the sun (`tan(elevation)` units a unit, 2-unit steps) and the
  spot is shadowed when a cell's height (16 a step) is above the ray. Worked
  out only when the heights or the sun change (hashed), not per frame.
- **Applied** as a factor on top-face pixels in the same `g_ao` byte.
- **Walls (asked on EI = the user's slot 1: the gate wall stayed bright over
  its shadowed water).** The map now stores, per spot, the height below which
  a point over it is in shade (the highest terrain toward the sun above the
  ray), so a wall pixel asks it with its own height over the spot in front
  of it. A wall turned away from the sun is in its own shadow.
- **The sun's side.** The art lights the walls facing down-right (+X) and
  darkens those facing down-left (+Z). The first sun, (-1, -3), is behind
  the scene: every visible wall faces away from it, so with walls shaded all
  of them darkened. Hence a fourth choice, **Side Sun**: low (30), world
  (2, -1), to the right of the battlefield and a little toward the camera;
  shadows fall left and slightly back. Tried first on the Thor: (1, -2) read
  as coming from the back right, and (1, -1) (straight from the screen's
  right) still as too far back. Stills `5_side_sun_closer_*.png` ((1, -1) / (2, -1) on EI).
  **Low Side Sun** (asked for after): the same direction at 20 degrees,
  shadows ~1.6x longer (`shadows=4`; still `6_low_side_sun.png`, 30 / 20 on
  EI).
- **Units take the shadow over them** (asked: shadows falling over
  units, not behind them). The map's value is a shade HEIGHT, so a unit is
  read as a card standing at its place: its feet at height `y - 8` on row
  `(x + z) / 4 - (y - 8) / 2 + ky`, a row up 2 units higher. Rows below
  `feet - (shade - foot) / 2` darken by the shadow strength: in a low
  shade the boots only, under a cliff's the whole unit. Applied where the
  atlas is written, the sprite tables' texels in build_sprite_atlas and the
  frame-copied ones in kol_perspective (each write once a frame, so it does
  not compound). Checked on EK with an 8-degree sun: shade 14 over the feet
  darkened the bottom rows, the body stayed lit.
- **Units cast shadows, and lose the game's blob** (asked, with
  enthusiasm, for units to cast shadows, replacing the black blob). With
  Shadows on and Options > Unit Shadows on (`unit_shadows=`, on by default:
  it acts only with the shadows or the occlusion, which start off). Off, the
  game's blob is back and there is neither this nor the contact occlusion
  below.
  - The blob is painted into the unit's frames (Alphonse is two 16x16
    pieces, no separate sprite): colour 1, the outline's, in the rows from
    feet - 7 down (EK, EI; the legs' outline stops above). Those texels are
    left out of the atlas, so the ground the game drew under the unit shows.
    Not checked on monsters (32 wide) yet.
  - The shadow: the unit stands as a card turned to FACE THE SUN (turned to
    the camera, the side sun would see it edge on and cast a sliver). A
    scene point is in it when the line from it toward the sun meets the
    card on a solid texel (a column is sqrt 2 units across the sun, a row 2
    up). Exact and gap-free; falls over steps, walls and water alike. Not
    on walls turned away from the sun (their own shadow already), not on
    props, not where the terrain's shadow is; darkens g_ao by the shadow
    strength, once however many units overlap.
  - Region: within half the card across the sun, out along it as far as a
    ray from the card's top reaches the lowest ground under it (cell
    heights, two steps); each row only the columns that strip can reach.
  - Cost (Mac, B_rictor, 9 units, Low Side Sun): 0.62 ms a frame with a
    +-48-row margin, 0.37 with the margin from the cell heights, 0.05 with
    each unit's shadow pixels kept until its place, sprite frame, the view,
    the sun or the heights change (re-applied every frame).
  - **The blob's top row (2026-10-20).** The user's slot 3
    (`states/IH_slot3_fairy_blob_lines.state`, AO off, shadows on): two
    small lines, one vertical and one horizontal, under the fairy.
    The blob is one oval in every unit's lower 16x16 (IH: the same bytes in
    all six units), colour 1, rows feet - 8 to feet - 2; its top row is 8
    wide, feet x - 4 to + 3. The rule above took colour 1 from feet - 7 down
    only, so the top row stayed on the card: a dark line under the feet,
    and, lifted, a one-pixel dark column under it (IH: the fairy's row 137
    x 220-228 and x 221 rows 138-143). On most units the legs hid it; the
    fairy's short legs did not. Now that row goes too, within the oval's
    width only (colour 1 is also outline: the fairy's dress edge).
    `KOL_BLOB_NO_TOP=1` leaves it. A/B: IH 32 pixels, EI 14, CJ 43, FF 43,
    every change that row and its column; EK none. Both invariants.
- **Contact occlusion under units** (asked for a little AO around
  units to ground them). With Ambient Occl. and Unit Shadows on, shadows or not: the ground's top
  within 18 units of a unit's place, at its height, darkens toward the
  feet, `min(0.7, 1.4 * AO strength * (1 - r / 18)^0.7)` (flat near the
  feet, which the sprite mostly covers, so the ring around them carries
  it). Trap: a unit's `y` is the ground it stands on; the `y - 8` the
  sprite code uses is the sprite's anchor, 4 rows under the ground row (the
  blob's). Compared with it, nothing was ground.
- Not done: trees, pots and the church cast nothing; edges step every 4
  world units (~2 px); a unit's shadow is not blocked by terrain between
  it and the ground it lands on.
- **Trap paid for:** the first mockup set showed "no shadows" because those
  runs never had them on (25 px different from AO alone). Before judging a
  mockup, count its differing pixels against the baseline. A
  `KOL_PERSP_SHADOW=1` render (shadowed ground black) shows where the map
  lands.
- Mockups: `shots/ambient_occlusion/*_shadows_{full,zoom}.png` (AO 0.5 /
  +45 / +30), `4_side_sun_{full,zoom}.png` (EI: AO only / (1, -2) / (1, -1)). `KOL_PERSP_SHADOW=<strength>`, `KOL_PERSP_SHADOW_ELEV=<deg>`
  override the setting.
- **Moving the sun by hand (2026-10-01, asked for a debug option where
  holding L2 and moving the right stick left/right moves the sun, then for it
  to change only the sun's height, along an arc over the field from left to
  right, not its angle).**
  Options > Debug > L2 Moves Sun (`debug_sun_stick=`, off by default). With
  the perspective on and L2 (gbarecomp's new `g_host_pad_left_trigger`) past
  half, the right stick's x moves the sun along an arc over the battlefield,
  toward the side pushed, 45 degrees a second at full tilt. The arc stands
  in the vertical plane of the Shadows pick's direction (Side Sun (2, -1):
  screen right to left): from that side's horizon (5 degrees) over the top
  to the other's (175); the sun starts at the pick's height, and past 90 it
  shines from the opposite side (the direction flips, the height is
  `180 - arc`, at most 89 overhead). The look lets go of the stick
  meanwhile. It holds while the option is on (not saved); off, the sun is
  the pick again. When the stick is let go the log gives it as
  `KOL_PERSP_SHADOW_ELEV=d KOL_PERSP_SHADOW_DIR=x,z`, so one found by hand
  can become a choice. It reaches the present worker through the capture
  (`Capture::sun_arc`). Every frame it moves, the shadow map and the unit
  shadows are worked out again (keyed on the height and direction). Two
  first versions were wrong: turning the direction around the field, then
  only raising the sun in place. L2 is also
  gbarecomp's default Rewind: KoL keeps no rewind history, and gbarecomp no
  longer logs "rewind history is not ready yet" when there is none.
- **What moving the sun cost, and the fix (2026-10-04, asked to look at
  the cost of moving the shadow).** The shadow map (256 x 256
  spots, a ray each, stepped 2 units toward the sun until nothing higher is
  left) is built again every frame the sun moves. Measured on the Mac's
  present worker with `KOL_PERSP_SUN_SPIN=0.75` (below): 13.4 ms a frame on
  EK, 18.0 on ER, and **160 ms on EZ with the user's map-6 roofs** (every
  step asked every roof, all over the map); the terrain pass beside it is
  ~1 ms. A low sun walks a long way: 120-170 steps a spot.
  Now a ray only looks at the first step into each cell it crosses (off a
  roof that step stands highest of the cell's: the same height, the
  shortest way, and the sun's rise is always positive), and the cells a
  ray crosses, with the step entering each, are the same for every ray
  leaving the same place inside its own cell: worked out once per
  sun for the 8 x 8 places. Under a roof every step still counts, the
  roof's height changing across the cell. EK 13.4 -> 1.2 ms, ER 18.0 ->
  1.6, EZ 160 -> 2.5. Byte-identical to the stepped march: 12 presents
  each on EK, ER and EZ (with the Thor's drawn_heights.cfg) while the sun
  spins, both invariants, pass cache check 0. Tried first and dropped:
  skipping to just short of each cell's edge inside the step loop, which
  cut the steps 4x and saved nothing (each step got dearer).
  `KOL_PERSP_SUN_SPIN=<degrees a frame>` swings the sun back and forth
  for headless timing; it needs `KOL_SETTINGS_ON=debug_sun_stick` (without
  the option the sun is reset to the pick every frame).

### Torchlight (2026-10-01)

Asked for, as an experiment (EJ = the user's slot 1, the cursor on a torch on
the ruins by the water): could the torches cast a glowing orange light?
Options > Torchlight (`torchlight=`, off by default), strength 1.0, the
user's pick from the stills `shots/torch_glow/EJ_*.png` (off / 0.6 / 1.0).
`KOL_PERSP_GLOW=<strength>`, `KOL_PERSP_GLOW_R=<reach>` (default 128 world
units) override it.
- **The lights.** Every cell whose terrain record is 70 (the torch) is a
  light at its centre, 8 units under its top (EJ: three torches, tops 6, 6
  and 16). Each flickers on its own (two slow sines, +-10%).
- **Per terrain pixel** (kol_focus's pass, which knows each pixel's world
  point and face): `(1 - d / reach) * (0.35 + 0.65 * facing)`, summed over
  the lights; nothing where a cell other than the pixel's and the torch's
  stands above the line between them, or where the face turns away.
- **The water** is not modelled (height 0, no unit may enter it), so the
  pass never drew it; for the light only, map pixels it left are taken as
  ground at height 0 where the screen puts them.
- **Applied** in kol_perspective after the AO, map pixels only: partly a
  brightening by an orange light, partly a pull toward the pixel's own
  brightness in orange. Multiplication alone turned the green stone yellow.
- **Cost (the user liked the look but found it slowed the game).** The
  first version lit every pixel the pass drew (overdraw included) and walked
  each lit pixel's line to every torch through `cell_height` (records, prop
  rules) every frame. Now: the heights are read once a frame into an array;
  the light is worked out after the pass on the pixels that stayed, inside
  each torch's screen box; whether the terrain hides a torch is kept per
  4-unit cube around it (filled as asked, kept until the heights or torches
  change); and the light itself is kept until the view moves, the flicker
  applied per pixel's main torch in kol_perspective. Mac, EJ, whole scene
  build: 2.24 ms off, 2.90 with the per-frame light, 2.25-2.28 with the view
  still; scrolling frames pay the ~0.65 ms again. The old version was not
  timed before it was replaced. Pictures: within 3 levels of the per-frame
  version (flicker rounding).
- **Traps:** a squared falloff over 96 units left the water six steps below
  the flames at almost nothing (linear over 128 now). A debug paint
  (light set = magenta) found that, not guessing.
- **The blue flame (2026-10-01, asked on EN = the user's slot 1, the castle
  map's statue in the sunken pit, asking for a blue glow from it).**
  The statue is terrain record 86 (map byte 0x0A there, height 15; its
  record's +1 is 0x01, not an obstacle), the only one on that map. It is a
  lamp like the torches (same reach, falloff, flicker), tinted blue
  (`kTint`/`kHue` row 1 in kol_perspective); a pixel takes the colour of the
  lamp most of its light comes from. Strength 1.0, the same as the torches,
  the user's pick from `shots/blue_torch/EN_{zoom,full}.png` (off / 0.6 /
  1.0 / 1.6; `KOL_PERSP_GLOW_BLUE=<strength>` scales the blue alone). On EN
  it lights the pit's back wall, its floor and the ledge above (8,484
  pixels at 1.0); blue on the blue-purple stone reads subtler than the
  orange. Other maps' record-86 cells are not checked.
  `KOL_PERSP_CELL_LOG=1` logs the cursor's cell (map byte, record, height)
  and the other cells with that record: how the statue was found.

### The menu button: pushed in, the game's sound, the hand (2026-10-01)

Asked for (09-30, the user's choices): the button looks pressed in while a
finger is on it, a press plays the game's own sound, and while the menu is
open the game's hand bobs beside the button. No gold, no vibration.

- **Pressed look.** `menu_zone_render(argb, h, pressed)`: the button's
  window darkened (first the bar's darkest grey; since the yellow came back,
  a brightness decrease of 4/16) and the System icon a pixel down and right.
  StatsView keeps both zone bitmaps and draws the pressed one while the
  finger that went down on the button is still inside it.
- **The hand.** `menu_hand_render` (the OPTION menu's pointing hand, ROM
  tiles `0x086D7F61`), JNI `menuHand()`. StatsView draws it left of the
  button, centred on it, still, while the menu is open. **The hand inside
  the menu bobs** (the user moved the bob there, 10-01): toward its row, 0,
  1, 2, 1 pixels, a step every 133 ms (a 32-frame cycle); `menu_take_dirty`
  reports a new step so the second-screen thread (33 ms tick) sends the
  picture again. The bob is a choice, not the game's: the game's OPTION hand
  does not move (its pixels were constant over 150 frames, B_rictor > R >
  System > Option).
- **The sound.** Opening plays `0xAD` (the game's confirm), closing `0xB0`
  (its cancel), through the game's routine `0x0814506C(id)`, which starts
  the effect only when the game's sound is on (`0x02002B20` bit 1). It runs
  in the VBlank handler right after the game's tasks: `0x080020B8`, called
  at `0x080005F4`, only flips the byte `0x030032B8`; with a sound pending
  the hook flips it itself and sets `r15` to the sound routine, which
  returns to the handler with the handler's own `r14`. Checked on B_rictor
  with the menu opened: the routine runs once (read watch on `0x02002B20`,
  `lr` `0x080005F9`) and MP2K's `MPlayStart` writes the effect's player
  (`0x0815CC36`, `0x0815CCA8`), which a run without the press does not.
- **Failed first, and why it is gone.** The first version tail-called the
  sound routine with `0x080020B8`'s own entry as the return, to restore
  r0-r3 and `lr` there and let the function run. The game then hung in
  MP2K's channel walk at `0x0815C0EA` (r4 `0xD1EED1EE`), 300 frames never
  finishing. Called from SoundMain's entry it hung the same way. Returning
  into a hooked entry is what changed; replacing the one-instruction
  function instead does not hang (300 frames in 35 s).
- Both render invariants hold (66e13ab2 / 9054c456).

### The camera from a unit that was not drawn (2026-09-30)

Reported on the Thor (`states/DU_persp_broken.state`, the user's slot 1,
battle preparation on the lava map, MEMBER 0/8, the cursor in the list):
the perspective was completely broken. Only a triangle of the map was placed, in
the wrong spot; the rest had no place and was drawn flat as background.

- **Cause.** The camera is voted for by unit slots (screen place minus the
  projected world place) and by the map cursor. Here the only voter was the
  unit to be deployed: slot at the screen's centre (120, 100), world place
  (16, 280, 16) on the map's back corner (height 18), drawing nothing. The
  map cursor was not out. Its one vote put the map far from where it is.
- **Fix.** A unit votes only where the frame's OAM (latched) has an entry
  over its slot's screen place, the 16x32 above its feet. Without a record
  of the frame's sprites (the first frame after a load) no unit votes; the
  record is on whenever the perspective or the depth of field is.
- With no believable voter the scene is not built and the plain picture is
  shown; the map cursor or a drawn unit brings the perspective back.
- Checked: DU plain, no warp. BK at frame 30 differs by 2,210 px (the
  camera's height ease starts a frame later), at frame 200 by 16 (snow).
  BT 75 and CG 6 (noise), BU 0. Every BK unit still votes.
- **The cursor off screen too** (`states/DV_r_then_b.state`, the user's
  slot 1: R then B sometimes brought the bug back). With the R
  menu up, the map cursor's slot keeps its world place but its screen place
  goes to (-24, -300); its votes (weight 8) put the map 96 columns and 156
  rows off. In 200 frames it voted 52 times against 148 for the true place;
  with the menu up long enough it won and the map broke on closing it
  (reproduced with B 450 frames after R). The cursor now votes only while
  its slot is on screen, within the same bounds as the units.

### Torches stand like the rocks: the game's own terrain records (2026-09-30)

Asked for on the Thor (`states/DN_torch_prop.state`, the user's slot 2, the
cursor on a torch in the ruins by the water): the torch should be a prop
like the rock in the water below it. This is the long-open `CA_torch` (same
map, same cell).

- **The game's records.** A cell's byte +0 is the map's own number. The
  map's table (u16 per number, in ROM, pointer at `0x020042E4`, read by
  `0x08028774(x, y)`) gives the record in the terrain table `0x0861CA5C`.
  The terrain box uses these records (the probe saw 70 for the torch, 61 for
  the wall beside it). The same byte means different things on different
  maps:

  | Map | 0x07 | 0x08 | 0x09 | 0x0A |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | DN / BO / CA (ruins by the water) | 70 torch | 40 | 50 rock | 61 wall |
  | BK (snowfield) | 41 tree | 30 | 0 | 42 snow rock |
  | CZ (fire pots) | 9 | 61 | 54 | 76 fire pot |
  | BY (ruins blocks) | 66 block top | 45 | 66 | 66 |

  So the prop rules, keyed on the byte (`is_prop`: 0x07, 0x08, 0x09, 0x0A),
  hold by coincidence on some maps. Records +0 = 1, +1 = 0x7F are the
  impassable obstacles (30, 40, 41, 42, 45, 50, 54, 60, 70, 73, 76). But
  that is not "prop" either: 60 is the ruins' 22-high border pillars (kept
  as terrain on purpose, CV) and 71 is BT's church (a building).
- **The torch.** Its byte, 0x07, is the trees' byte there. The trees' rule
  took its highest neighbour, the wall at 13, as its ground, so the torch
  cell was not a prop: it stood as a block 6 high with the torch art moving
  with the wall behind it.
- **Change.** A cell whose record is 70 (torch) goes by the rocks' cut-out
  rule (ground from the two front neighbours: 3 here), whatever its byte.
  `KOL_PERSP_NO_TORCH_PROPS=1` leaves it to its byte. Maps without record 70
  are byte-identical (BK, CZ, BT, stick down).
- **Not perfect yet.** With the stick down a one-row seam opens along the
  left of the torch's base, where the cut-out's bottom meets the ground now
  drawn at 3 (22 -> 89 unplaced interior pixels on DN); a few flat pixels of
  the old pedestal top stay beside the brazier. At rest there are fewer
  holes than before (716 -> 615).
- **Then (same day): props must be obstacles.** Reported on the Thor
  (`states/DP_cursor_not_terrain.state`, the user's slot 1, cursor at cell
  (11,1)): it did not seem to be treated as terrain. The cell's byte is
  0x0A, the fire pots' byte on CZ, but here it is record 1, plain ground: a
  raised grassy block stood as broken prop fragments with holes. Now a cell
  is a prop only if its byte says so AND its record is an obstacle (+1 ==
  0x7F), or it is a torch. Nothing new becomes a prop (the pillars, 60, and
  the church, 71, have no prop byte). `KOL_PERSP_BYTE_PROPS=1` goes by the
  bytes alone again.
  - DP: the block is terrain, a clean top and walls.
  - BY: two record-66 block tops stop being props; the broken block that
    showed slivers of sky through its top is whole (7,583 px).
  - CZ: 1,809 px around its spires and pots, which stay props.
  - BK, BT, CB, CK, DN: byte-identical (stick down).
- **Then: props by record lists** (`states/DQ_rock_prop.state`, slot 1,
  cursor on a rock at (3,2)): the rocks on that map are byte 0x05, no prop
  byte, but record 50, the same record as the water rock by the torches.
  Two lists of records now make props wherever the bytes miss them, and
  choose the rule over the byte: cut-out (rocks, pots, the torch) 33, 42,
  50, 51, 53, 54, 70, 76; the trees' rule (trees, bushes) 30, 40, 41, 45,
  47, 55. They are the records the byte rules already treated right on the
  maps we have. `KOL_PERSP_NO_RECORD_PROPS=1` (or the older
  `KOL_PERSP_NO_TORCH_PROPS=1`) turns the lists off.
  - The cut-out rule's "rise 2 over the front unless above all four" guard
    was for BY's block tops, byte 0x0A but record 66, which the obstacle
    check now excludes. It only applies with `KOL_PERSP_BYTE_PROPS=1`, so a
    low rock (DQ, 1 over its front) stands.
  - Against the bytes alone (mesh view, stick down): BK 0 px; new props on
    BT (snow rocks 42 and bushes 30 standing as props instead of little
    blocks), BY (record 33 rubble), DQ (the rocks), BO/DN (torches, the
    water rock); small changes on CB, CK, CZ. CK's byte-0x0A cells are
    record 41 (a tree) and now take the trees' rule.
  - **A desktop trap:** the invisible present renders (SDL software
    renderer) showed 1-px cyan lines at some new props' bases (BT, a bush).
    The strips' triangles, rebuilt from a dump and tested exactly, cover
    every one of those pixels: it is the software rasteriser's rounding on
    long, thin triangles. The Thor draws them on its GPU. Judge seams on
    the device, not in these renders.
- **Open: a bare tree's tile stands up with it** (`states/DS_tree_tile.state`,
  the snowfield's corner tree at (0,12), record 40): the tree's BG1 art
  carries a mound of snow over the top of the cell behind, and the trees'
  rule claims it. Tried and removed the same day: laying claimed pixels
  that land on the tops of the tree's cell and the cells behind back on the
  ground, trunk kept. On all trees it flattened the snowfield firs' (41)
  lower halves; on record 40 only it flattened BT's bushes (also record 40:
  `states/DT_tree_cutout.state`, the user's slot 3) down to a 3-px trunk.
  A BG1-against-BG0 colour test, full 8x8 tiles and tile ids shared with
  BG0 do not separate a ground piece from leaves either.
- **To report another one:** save a state with the cursor on it and say
  which it should be like (a rock or torch: stands as a cut-out; a tree or

### The unit being placed tore the ground beside it (2026-09-30)

Reported on the Thor with the perspective on, placing a unit in battle
preparation (camera pushed down with the stick): the terrain left of the unit
being placed was deforming. Reproduced from `DM_prep_warning` (Up, A
on the list, then Right) with `KOL_PERSP_LOOK=0,1`: the water left of the
unit was repeated in a band a few rows high, and the mesh view showed a
false ledge across the flat ground on those rows.

- **Cause.** The unit being placed is the blinking unit the game draws at
  50% (`kol_ghost.cpp`, OBJ mode 1 at BLDALPHA 8/8). Units are drawn from
  their own sprites and lifted out of the frame (`build_sprite_atlas`), but
  a semi-transparent one was left in the frame, since only opaque blends
  (16/0) were taken. Its pixels stayed in the scene as an upright thing at
  the unit's place (the mesh view painted it dark red, like a prop), and the
  mesh tore the rows beside it. The unit was claimed correctly: its two
  entries are unit 5's, and its feet match.
- **Fix.** Semi-transparent units are rebuilt like the rest. Their visible
  texels take the frame's colours, which are already the blend with the
  ground. A hidden texel (under another sprite) is blended with the ground
  the compositor recorded under it (`latched_scene_under`) at BLDALPHA's
  weights.
- **The core: a strip fanned to a pulled corner.** The ground's places
  were right (old against new, only the unit's own 315 pixels differ). The
  band came from the mesh. A corner is placed by the frontmost pixel
  touching it, so where an upright thing stands, the corners it touches are
  pulled to it (here 6 px up). Each pixel row's strip is zipped between the
  kept corners of its top and bottom edges. At the unit's edge the top edge
  kept corners 232 and 233 (233 pulled up), the bottom edge only 0 and 233,
  so the zipper made the triangle (top 232, top 233, bottom 0): a wedge
  from the unit to the row's far end that painted the row's texture over
  the rows above it, tapering away. Anything upright can pull a corner, so
  this was not the ghost's alone.
- **Fix for the core** (`kol_perspective.cpp`, after `keep_row`): a corner
  kept in one corner row is kept in the rows either side too, where they
  place one. Both edges of every strip then have a corner at each column
  either edge keeps, and a pulled corner's triangles stay one pixel wide.
  Every strip sharing a corner row still uses that row's one set, so no
  T-junctions. With the ghost put back in the frame (a temporary switch),
  this alone removes the band. `KOL_PERSP_NO_KEEP_SPREAD=1` turns it off.
  - It also cleans older artifacts: bright ice-edge specks along the cliffs
    of CK_chevrons_ice and faint row smears in BK's water, both the same
    wedge at a smaller scale.
  - Cost: 8-24% more triangles (CK 178,908 -> 215,280 indices, BK 110,226
    -> 136,197, CV 337,416 -> 366,573, DM placing 59,916 -> 70,500), and one
    pass over the corner flags.
  - The teal line at DM (300,134) shrinks from 24 to 11 pixels; the rest of
    it is a real gap, still open.
- **Checked** (invisible presents, see "Streaks in the sky"): the band and
  the ledge are gone; the unit is still half transparent. BK and CG, stick
  at rest and down: byte-identical. BT (a unit being placed by the church):
  2507 pixels, the mesh's rows no longer cut around the unit. The same build
  twice differs by 116 there. BU differs only in raindrops, 22 pixels
  between two runs of one build too.

### Streaks in the sky beside the preparation list (2026-09-30)

Reported on the Thor with the perspective on (`states/DM_prep_warning.state`,
battle preparation): the side bar left streaks in the background at the top of
the field, thin dark and green lines across the sky from the list's
edge.

- **Cause.** Where the far side shrinks, the perspective's backdrop fills
  what the map uncovers with the last sky pixel to the left on the same row
  (`kol_perspective.cpp`, step 1). A pixel counted as sky when nothing was
  placed from it. The preparation list lies over the map's left edge. The
  scene leaves the HUD out, so under the list it has the map, and nothing is
  placed from there because the frame shows the list. So that map art (the
  outline, the grass) was the "sky" carried along those rows.
- **Fix.** A pixel is no sky source if an interface sprite is there, or if
  a HUD layer (`g_ppu_scene_exclude_layers`) is on top with map art (BG0 or
  BG1) under it. Sky under a HUD panel (code `0x53`, BG3 over the backdrop)
  stays sky. The first try left out every HUD pixel and lost that sky.
- **Checked** with presents rendered invisibly (`SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy
  SDL_RENDER_DRIVER=software`, `--window`, `GBARECOMP_PRESENT_DUMP`): no
  window opens on the Mac, and the software renderer draws the warp mesh
  through SDL geometry. DM: the streaks are gone (336 pixels).
  CG_alphonse_stretch: byte-identical. BK_tree_glass_cage and CW_sky_streaks:
  5 and 8 pixels, the stair of a cliff edge next to the bottom bar. They show
  sky now, as the same edge already does on rows with no HUD beside them.
- **Still there, not this:** a one-pixel teal line in DM at (300,134), where
  the mesh leaves a row of the cliff face at the map's right corner
  uncovered. It predates this change (see "The unit being placed tore the
  ground beside it": now shorter, still open).

### The opening scenes on the second screen (2026-09-30)

During the opening's panning mountain and on the title screen (through PUSH
START and its menu), the second screen carries the scene on below the top
screen. The strip starts at the first row under the presented picture (160
plus the view's extra rows: 55 at the Thor's 480x270) and moves with the
scene. It spans the game's 240 columns inside a 248-wide strip (1240 px at
5x), black outside them, because the top screen pillarboxes both scenes.
The zone and the menu button lie over its foot, and touches elsewhere do
nothing there.

| Scene | Frames (cold boot) | Layout | What continues |
|---|---|---|---|
| Opening | 682-2045 | mode 0, BG0CNT `0x990B`, BG1CNT `0x9B08` | the mountain and chasm (BG0, 256x512, panned by VOFS) and the fire (BG1), blended as the game does: BLDCNT `0x3D42`, BLDALPHA 8/8 |
| Title | from 2103 | mode 0, BG0CNT `0x1D03`, BG1CNT `0x1E02`, BG2CNT `0x1F01` | the clouds (BG0) only |

- **Title: BG0 only.** The title's emblem and logo layers repeat every 256
  rows; below the screen they would show a second logo
  (`shots/intro_two_screens.png`, an early mockup).
- **Opening: no sprites.** Its narration is sprites and never reaches below
  the screen. Under the chasm the picture is black, so the bottom screen
  shows mostly the fire sinking out of the top one
  (`shots/opening_two_screens.png`).
- **Recognising the scenes.** Each is recognised by its layer layout. The
  task pointers near `0x02002BE4` are shared slots that change under them.
  No other state of 46 sampled (battles, roster, menus, world map,
  cutscenes) matches.
- **The rows below the screen use the registers of the presented frame's
  last scanline**, exactly as gbarecomp's own margin rows do. The fire's
  wobble is per-scanline scrolling, so below the screen it holds still, as
  it does in the top screen's own extra rows. gbarecomp gained
  `GbaPpu::latched_io()` for this: IO `0x00-0x5F` as of that line.
- **The options zone is hidden during the opening** (and its loop after
  the title), so nothing sits over the scene. It comes back on the title.
  The strip's push carries the scene (1 the opening, 2 the title).
- **The title's veil continues.** The title's BG1 is an opaque near-black
  field: one solid tile, the map's most common entry, bank 3. The emblem
  and text are transparent holes in it, and the game blends it over the
  clouds at BLDALPHA 15/5. It covers only lines 0-159, so the clouds were
  bright below it: in the top screen's own extra rows as well as on the
  second screen. Past lines 0-159, BG1 now samples one pixel of that field:
  the X and Y providers in kol_widescreen.cpp for the top screen (BG1 joins
  the Y provider's mask only while the title is up), and the same in the
  strip. No row is field alone, and some columns never are, hence one pixel
  rather than a row.
- **The fire keeps deforming.** Its wobble is an HBlank DMA (DMA2 into
  BG1HOFS/VOFS; DMA0 does BG0) from a 161-line table that `0x0800CAEC`
  fills each frame, during VBlank, double-buffered: HOFS = base (`+0`) +
  (`sin(phase) >> +0xA`) on lines [`+4`, `+6`), the phase starting at `+8`
  and stepping by `+9` per line, with the sine table read by `0x08007EF0`.
  A record-only hook (`[[mod_function_hook]]` in game.toml) keeps a copy of
  each fill's parameters with its frame number. Rows past 160 run the same
  rule on, and a range ending at 160 counts as open: it ends there only
  because the screen does. The frame a table is drawn in comes after its
  fill, so each frame uses the last fill stamped before it. gbarecomp's
  `latched_frame()` supplies that frame, and `latched_io()` (now 0x00-0xDF)
  supplies the DMA source.
- **The fire waves from the scene's first frame (2026-11-16).** Reported from
  the Thor: at boot the circle on the bottom screen did not wave for a
  couple of frames. The game sets its raster effects up 31 frames into the
  opening: no HBlank DMA and no fill before then, and the fire's parameter
  block (`0x0202BDF4`, its two tables right after it) is zero until its first
  fill. On a GBA the fire is far below the screen at that point; below the
  screen it stood as a still circle for half a second, then snapped into the
  wave. Until the game's first fill, BG1 past line 160 now runs the wave the
  game's own would have been (`fire_preroll`: step 10 a line, sine >> 5, 2 a
  frame, phase 0 thirty frames after the layout first shows), so the frame
  the game takes over on carries straight on: phases 252, 254, 0, then the
  game's 2, 4, 6 (cold boot with `--skip-bios-intro`, scene from frame 412,
  first fill 442). Nothing to read early: the block is zero, so the three
  figures are constants measured from the first fills. BG0's haze is left to
  start with the game's, as it shows on the game's own lines 152-159. The
  game's 240x160 frame is byte-identical with and without at frames 430 and
  460. `KOL_NO_FIRE_PREROLL=1` off; `KOL_STRIP_LOG=1` prints each composed
  frame's waves and each fill. Not checked: the opening's replay after the
  title (the same lead is assumed), the full invariant suite.
- **Colour effects** use gbarecomp's arithmetic in the GBA's domain: a
  sixth green bit (palette bit 15), blends rounded to nearest, darkening
  rounded with +7. A first version blended on 5-bit values and was one step
  off on 2568 fire pixels.
- **Checked** against gbarecomp's own extra rows (rows 160-214, the game's
  240 columns, frames 700, 1000, 1300, 1600 and 2300): 0 of 13,200 pixels
  differ at each. After the veil and the wave, the same comparison at frames
  800, 1000, 1300, 1600 and 2300 again gives 0: the strip and the top
  screen's rows now run the same rules. 91 saved states set neither scene
  off.
- Code `src/kol_scene_strip.cpp`, JNI `pushSceneStrip`, desktop
  `KOL_STRIP_DUMP=<ppm, %d = frame>`. Still:
  `shots/title_clouds_two_screens.png`.

### The hand-drawn panel is gone (2026-09-30)

At boot the second screen still showed the first panel this project built
("waiting for a selected unit…", terrain box, captured glyphs). That panel
is removed. Every page is now a native picture (sheet, unit list, menu), and
before there is one the page is black, with the framed zone and the menu
button below it.

- **Java:** StatsView keeps the sheet and its swipe, the list and the card,
  the menu, the zone and auto-win.
- **Native:** the screen2 loop no longer reads or captures anything for that
  panel. Every 33 ms it used to send stats and name strings, the terrain id,
  and captures of the panel frame, font atlas, stat labels, name tiles and
  terrain box. `pushSheetImage` is now the method the bind requires.
- The capture helpers stay in kol_terrain_probe, whose desktop dumps use
  them. `sheet_frame_atlas` and `name_bitmap` (kol_unit_data) have no
  callers left.

### Switching units on the EMBLEM page broke the lower cards (2026-09-30)

Reported on the Thor (`states/DK_status_equip_broken.state`): Right to the
game's EMBLEM page, then the unit button, a few times over, and the EQUIP
card was drawn twice, shifted. The switch restarts the roster task, which
rebuilds the window, but not the fields the window's open routine
(`0x0803A5E0`) sets. The lower page `+0x61D6` stayed 1, while the page
toggle (`0x080362F8`) keeps per-page fields in step (`+0x5830`/`+0x61D3`,
`+0x61BC`/`+0x61D4`, `+0x5838`/`+0x5834`) and slides the map buffers
(`0x0803F7E4`). Each Right after that landed further off.

Fix: the switch also writes `+0x61D6` = 0 and `+0x5838` = 0, as the open
routine does, so the new unit starts like a freshly opened window, on the
EQUIP page. Repro and check: AY, Right / Next three times
(`GBARECOMP_INPUT_REPLAY` + `KOL_NEXT_UNIT_AT=120,320,520`). Every page is
now clean. The roster switch (AZ) is unchanged.

### The unit buttons are the game's Shortcut A and B (2026-09-30)

On the battle map the unit buttons now do whatever the OPTION window's
Shortcut A and B are set to. The game runs these in its hold-L mode (L, then
A or B). The options are EWRAM `0x02001330` / `0x02001331` (option block
`0x0200132C` + 4 / + 5), with 0 Next, 1 Reverse, 2 Element, 3 Wounded,
4 Level Up, and they are the argument of `0x08074338`.

- **Which buttons:** with the pad remap on, the shoulders (the right one is
  Shortcut A); with it off, the north and west face buttons (north is A),
  since the shoulders are then the GBA's R and L. In the status window the
  same buttons are still Next / Previous unit.
- **Next / Reverse:** one step per press, as before (the hook's own index).
- **Element / Wounded / Level Up:** the game's state 5 calls
  `0x08074338(option)` every frame while A is held. That recolours matching
  units (object `+0x65` = 0x0C-0x0F: by element; HP at most 50%, or 25%;
  close to a level) and blinks them through the counter `ctl+0x75A`. On
  release it restores each `+0x65` from `ctl+0x740` and calls
  `0x0806D970(2)`. The hook does the same: the selection each frame while
  the button is held, then the restore and that call.
- **Checked** on DJ: Element while held recolours the units. After the
  release, frames 100 and 150 are byte-identical to a run with no press
  (Element, Wounded and Level Up alike). Wounded marks nothing there,
  because no unit is at 50% HP or less.
- **Test hooks:** `KOL_SHORTCUT_AT="b:n1-n2"` holds button b over those hook
  calls; `KOL_SHORTCUT_FORCE=c` overrides the option.

## Next unit, inside the status window (2026-09-25)

The second screen now has **Previous unit** beside **Next unit**. On the
battle map both buttons move the cursor, as above (`0x08074338(1)` for
previous). With a status window open, in the army roster or in battle, they
show the neighbouring unit **inside the window**. The game has no such
thing: its window shows one unit until it is closed.

**Order.** The army's 32 record slots from `0x02000030` (stride `0x68`),
skipping empty ones (class byte `+0x4F` == 0). This is the roster grid's
order: the "NO." the window prints is record byte `+0x51`, and it rises with
the slot (1, 2 … 15, 17, 24 in the endgame save). In battle, the eight
records of the unit's own side from `0x02001420`, skipping units off the map
(`+0x4E` or HP zero). Both wrap.

**Who draws the window.** Not the status task `0x0803A0D0`. Restarting that
task blacks the screen (the old `KOL_STATUS_SWITCH` experiment, now removed).
The contents come from the **roster task `0x08034498`**, in the roster AND in
battle. It is in the menu task table at `0x0860D77C` (44 records of 16 bytes:
task, second routine, flags, data). None of that table's 23 routines was in
the static build, so the whole window ran interpreted before this; see
game.toml "The menu screens' task table". Its state byte (r1) is 3 while the
window is up (4 is the roster grid). The control block (`[0x02002B1C]`) holds
the unit at `+0x5854`, the battle entry at `+0x5860` (0 in the roster), and a
sub-state at `+0x61A4` that is 1 while the window is idle.

**The switch**, a reviewed hook on `0x08034498` (`src/kol_actions.cpp`,
`on_roster_task`). With a tap pending, state 3 and sub-state 1:
1. It writes the neighbour into `+0x5854` (and its entry into `+0x5860`).
2. It sets the task's state byte to 0, then declines. The task's own init
   redraws everything: number, name, portrait, stats, items and talents.
3. **Battle only:** the picture there is the unit's map sprite, a sprite
   object the init does not touch. It kept showing the first unit.
   `0x0802EBD8(i, 0)` re-points window sprite `i` at the control block's unit
   (`0x08012418(obj, sprite, palette, …)`, no allocation). The game wraps that
   as `0x0803A964(i)`, which a menu at `0x0802D1F0` uses. So on the next idle
   call the hook tail-calls `0x0803A964([ctl+0x5ED2])` in place of that one
   task call. The task's epilogue returns nothing, so the scheduler cannot
   notice the skipped call.

How the picture was traced: its OBJ tiles (0 and 4) are filled every frame
by a persistent VBlank DMA node (`0x080008EC`) from `ctl+0x62C8`. That buffer
is fed from the sprite object at `ctl+0x61DC[i]`, which `0x0802EBD8` stores.
Not the way to it: `0x0802EA2C`, the per-frame animator that also targets
`0x06010000`, and the sheet at `ctl+0x4164`. Both are shared by every unit.
The roster init also refreshes the sprite itself, but only when
`ctl+0x61A5 == 0x21`; faking that byte was not tried.

**The roster's list position (fixed 2026-09-25).** Reported as: after Next
unit, class change showed Alphonse. In the roster the window's unit is not
only the pointer. `0x0803AA8C(i, mode)` derives it from a position
`ctl+0x5ECB` in the grid's list of record indices at `ctl+0x58FC` (0-15,
20, then 0xFF). It stores the record index at `ctl+0x5ED2`, then sets
`+0x5854 = [ctl+0x584C] + index * 0x68`. The window's menus call it again
(mode 2), so class change (and Item, Spellbook, Dismiss) re-derived the unit
from the stale position 0: Alphonse. The hook now steps through that list
and writes the position and the record index along with the pointer. The
battle window has no list there (`0x0803AA8C` returns early when
`ctl+0x6194` has bit 5 and not the low nibble 7), so battle still walks its
side as below.

The menu opens with the R shoulder button from the idle window. Repro:
`states/BA_equip_cursor.state`, then B, B, B to the idle window (Flauros),
Next (Lechies), R, Right, Right, A. The class-change screen reads "NO. 4",
AGI 311 (Lechies); before the fix it read NO. 1, Alphonse's AGI 383. B backs
out to Lechies' menu. Item opens on Lechies. That save was taken after a
Next on the old build, so its position is already stale: without a Next,
class change still shows Alphonse there.

**The battle window's colours (fixed 2026-09-25).** After Next in battle,
the new unit wore the first unit's colours: Alphonse's leader palette on
Allos and Lechies. The window's palette comes from `0x0802A7A0(0)`, which
the window runs when it opens. It calls `0x08143378(unit,
0x0804041C(unit))`, which copies the unit's palette into the OBJ palette
shadow (`0x02002600`) and stores its id at `ctl+0x591C`. It loads every
unit of the list in the roster (`ctl+0x6194` bit 4), which is why the
roster never showed this, but only the current unit in battle.

After the task init, the hook now uses two idle calls:
1. It tail-calls `0x0802A7A0(0)` for the new unit.
2. It tail-calls the sprite refresh `0x0803A964`.

Checked from `BG_gauge_palette`:
- Next to Lechies matches her window opened fresh (green), where it was
  blue before.
- Previous then Next to Allos is green, as on the map.

Not the way to it:
- **The sprite object's palette selector** (`+4`, the unit's `+0x50`,
  set only by the creator `0x08011C50`): writing it changes nothing, and
  nothing reads it after creation.
- **Freeing and recreating the object** (`0x0802EBD8(i, 1)`): same colours.
- **The window's fixed palettes** (`0x0861E288`, 8 banks into
  `ctl+0x5B7C`): the same for every unit.

The same dispatch misses occur with and without a Next.

**Verified** headlessly:
- `states/AZ_alphonse_mismatch.state` (roster). Next gives "NO. 2" Allos with
  his portrait. Previous from NO. 1 wraps to NO. 24 Cybil. After a Next,
  Previous and Next, B closes to the grid. The grid cursor stays on the unit

- `states/AY_kamui_talents.state` (battle). Seven Nexts walk the whole side
  (Allos, Stella, Alphonse with his LEADER tag, Flauros, Alberich, Ivanna,
  Winter), each with its own sprite. Kamui → Allos → Kamui matches the
  untouched window except for 245 pixels, all inside the 16x32 sprite (the

- Render invariants unchanged, with the switch on and with it off: 240
  `66e13ab2`, 284 anchor-off `9054c456`, centre-240 0/160.
- On the Thor, Screen-2 shows both buttons (captured with the physical
  display id).

Not covered: a window opened on an ENEMY unit. `neighbour()` walks the enemy
side the same way, but no repro state has one.

Kill switch: `KOL_NO_STATUS_SWITCH=1` (or `KOL_NO_ACTIONS=1` for every
button). Trace: `KOL_STATUS_TRACE=1` prints both tasks' state changes, and
`KOL_NEXT_UNIT_AT` taps as before.

**Measurement trap, hit this session.** Desktop runs that load the self-heal

## Item descriptions on the second screen (2026-09-25)

When the status window's cursor is on a piece of equipment, the second
screen's top card shows that item's description in place of the unit. This
is the text the game's HELP box shows on SELECT, drawn in the game's font.
The same goes for talents, and for every row of SELECT's help cursor, in
the roster and in battle (see "Every HELP text on the second screen" below).
The EQUIP. and TALENT cards stay as they are. Everything is read from guest
RAM and ROM; nothing in the game changes.

**Which item.** The same one SELECT would describe, found the way the game
finds it. The control block is `[0x02002B1C]`.
- **Equipment list open** (sub-state `+0x61A4` == `0x1D`; the spellbook
  list is `0x1F`). The list object
  is `[ctl+0x582C]`. It is an item list when its kind `+0x19` is 0, 2 or 4
  (1 and 3 are talent lists). The tab is `L[0x30 + L[0x1A]]`, the row is
  `L[0x20+tab] + L[0x28+tab]` (scroll plus cursor), and the item is byte 0
  of the entry at `[L+0x1C] + 4 * L[0x38+row]`. These are the routines
  `0x08046C20`, `0x08046EB0`, `0x08046F04` and `0x08046F78`.
- **Otherwise, the cursor row.** Twelve bytes at `[ctl+0x6188] + 12 *
  u16[ctl+0x618E]`. Its `(id, kind)` is what the help builder `0x0802ABE0`
  switches on. Kind 5 is the equipped slot named by the row index; kind 6 is
  the slot named by the id. The slot cursor after the list (sub-state
  `0x1C`, rows `0x0860E448`) is kind 5. The window's plain cursor rows
  (`0x0860E568`) have no equipment.
- `L[0x13]` stays set after the list closes, so the sub-state, not the list,
  says the list is open.

**Which text.** The help id is the item accessor's field 2 (`0x081438B8`):
u16 `+0x04` of the item's ROM record, or of a made item's base record. The
made items' bases (ids 17-22) all say `0x3A`. `0x0801C004` replaces that
with an id chosen by the item's type (field 15), from `0x2A3` to `0x2AD`.
The id indexes one of two banks: `0x0874B6DC` for ids up to `0x1FF`, and
`0x0875976C` for ids from `0x200` (index less `0x200`). An entry is at
`bank + u16[bank + 2*i]`: two header bytes, then text in the name-pool
encoding.

Text codes: digits `0x34`-`0x3D`, `.` `0x40`, `,` `0x41`, `'` `0x46`, `(`
`0x47`, `)` `0x48`, `+` `0x4B`, `-` `0x4C`. `0x88` ends a line, `0x8E 0x8A`
ends a page (the box shows two lines), and `0x8D 0x8A 0xFF` ends the text.
`0x87 NN` is character NN's name (`0x086254D8`; "The witch Deneb's"). `0x80
NN` is a figure the game fills in at run time; it appears in item text only
in the generic made-item text, and is left out.

**Layout.** A description floats over the sheet as a card of its own, as
tall as the text needs, always at the top. The unit, EQUIP. and TALENT
cards stay drawn beneath it, dimmed to 9/16 so the card stands out. All
its pages show at once, every line 16 px from the next as the game sets
them. A page break gets 4 px more only where the page ends a sentence, i.e.
its last character (past any spaces) is a period (**changed 2026-09-25**,
the user's rule). A sentence often runs across a page, and a gap there read
as awkward: `states/BJ_help_spacing.state`, the Support/Fear text. There,
"affects" ends page 1 with no gap; the element text gaps only after "water.",
"restrictions." and "N-neutral.". A two-line text is a 7-row card. The
longest (up to 11 lines) drop the gaps, then close the lines up until they
fit the sheet. Nothing turns.

**Verified** from `states/BA_equip_cursor.state` (the user's slot 1:
Flauros, the armour list open on Hard Leather):
- List on Hard Leather: "Animal hide. PHYS DEF 9, / Spell DEF 5. PHYS
  RES+3.", word for word the game's own SELECT box.
- Down gives the Robe (two pages).
- B moves to the slot cursor: Cloak of Oath (three pages). Down
  gives the Armlet of Wisdom.
- B to the menu brings the unit card back.
- The normal sheet is byte-identical to the previous build (AZ and AY).
- Render invariants unchanged.
- On the Thor, Screen-2 shows Hard Leather's text with slot 1 loaded.

### Talents (2026-09-25)

A talent's help id is u16 `+0x06` of its record (`0x0861A8F0 + 64 * id`).
The talent is found the same two ways.
- **Cursor rows:** kind 7 is the talent at `unit[0x64 + row index]`
  (`0x0802AFD4`). Kind 8 is the one at `unit[0x64 + row id]` (`0x0802B00C`).
  The talent-slot cursor (menu, the spellbook icon) uses the 4-row kind-7
  table at `0x0860E49C`. The kind-8 tables are at `0x0860E514`, `0x0860E67C`
  and `0x0860E7C0`.
- **Talent lists:** list kind 1 or 3. The list help routine `0x08046C20`
  jumps (table `0x08046C68`) to `0x08046D00` for these. That case skips an
  entry of `0xFF` and reads `+0x06` of the talent record.
- An empty slot (`0xFF`) brings the unit card back.

**Verified** from `states/BA_equip_cursor.state`: B, B, Right, A (the
spellbook icon), then A to close NAVI.
- Acid Vapor: "Missile (Earth). 6 MP, RNG 7, / AOE 1. Vapor that corrodes
  target."
- Down gives Crag Crush (three pages). The game's own SELECT box
  reads "Area-Effect (Earth). 12 MP, / RNG 6, AOE 1-5. Damages foes", the
  card's first page word for word.
- Down gives Fiend's Grip. Down again reaches the empty slot, and the unit
  card comes back.
- The spellbook list is sub-state `0x1F`, not the equipment list's `0x1D`,
  so at first it showed nothing. Its list object is the same (kind 3). Repro
  `states/BB_spell_change.state` (the user's slot 1, Ivanna): Down walks
  Heal, Cleanse, Lightning Bow, Faith. On Heal the card reads "Support
  (Virtue). 8 MP, RNG 7, / AOE 1. Recovers HP (not undead).", word for word
  the game's SELECT box.
- Render invariants unchanged: 240 `66e13ab2`, 284 anchor-off `9054c456`,
  centre-240 0/160.

**Class change** (sub-state `0x21`). The card follows the class-change
grid's cursor without SELECT. The highlighted class is `ctl+0x58C3` (and
`+0x58C4`); outside that screen the byte holds the unit's own class. The
text is class `+0x30`, as for the window's class row. The female classes
(even ids) have 0 there and fall back through `+0x09` to the male ones, as
the game's accessor does. The grid runs in columns: Soldier, Archer, Cleric,
Swordmaster on top; Ninja, Wizard, Knight, Dragoon below. It was found by
diffing EWRAM snapshots taken before and after cursor moves. Repro
`states/BC_class_change.state` (the user's slot 1, Shiven): Soldier, then
Archer (Right), then Wizard (Down). On Soldier the card reads "The basic
class where all / characters begin.", word for word the game's SELECT box.

### Every HELP text on the second screen (2026-09-25)

The user asked for any help text, in battle as well. In the status window,
SELECT gives a help cursor. It walks the whole window: No., birthday,
element, level, EXP, support, class, HP, MP, the stats, the two MOVE icons,
equipment and talents. A opens the game's HELP box for the row under it. The
card now shows that row's text as the cursor moves, without A.

**When.** `ctl+0x61A6` is 1 while SELECT's cursor is up and 3 while a box
(HELP or NAVI) is up. B sets it back to 0. The row index `+0x618E` stays
behind when help mode ends, so rows other than the slot cursors count only
while `+0x61A6` is nonzero. The slot cursors (sub-state `0x1C` equipment,
`0x1E` talents) and the list (`0x1D`) describe as they move, as before.
Before SELECT the battle window's rows point at "No.", which is why the flag
matters.

**The rows.** Battle uses the 27-row table at `0x0860E6AC`; the roster's
window uses the same layout at `0x0860E568`. The help builder `0x0802ABE0`
switches on the row's kind (jump table `0x0802AC30`, kind - 1). Every kind
outside 1-17 is the default: the row id is the help id.

| kind | row | help id |
|---|---|---|
| 0, 3, 4 | labels, level, HP | the row id (id 0 is "dummy": nothing) |
| 1 | No. | 400; in battle (`ctl+0x6195` == 1) 503 if the entry's `+0x17` bit 0 (leader), else 504 if bit 1 (guest) |
| 2 | birthday | 434 + fortune, or 502 with no birthday |
| 5-8 | equipment, talents | as above |
| 11 | land-move icon | 414 + (type[0] - 1), + 5 if type[2] == 1 (snow) |
| 12 | water-move icon | 424 + (type[1] - 1) |
| 13 | class | class `+0x30` (u16, with the `+0x09` fallback) |
| 17 | element | 402, 496-499 (wind, fire, earth, water), 500 virtue, 501 bane |

The window's rows have no kinds 9, 10 or 14-16. Kind 9 is the army sort menu
(`0x0860E3F4`). The menu's own icons (`0x0860E418`, ids 470-473) are plain
rows, and they show while the icon's NAVI box is up.

**The unit accessor** `0x08143B70` (jump table `0x08143B90`) reads plain
record bytes for everything used here:
- `0x10` `+0x4E`, `0x11` `+0x4F` (class), `0x12` `+0x50` (second class);
- `0x16` `+0x54` (element), `0x17` `+0x55` (alignment);
- `0x18`/`0x19` `+0x56`/`+0x57` (birth month and day);
- `0x1A` `+0x58`, `0x1B` `+0x59`, **`0x1C` u16 `+0x5A`**, `0x1D` `+0x5C`;
- `0x1E` `+0x5D`, `0x1F` `+0x5E` (sex);
- `0x28`: the battle entry's signed `+3`, or 0 in the roster.

**Element** (`0x0802B068`). If class field `0x0D` (`+0x16`) is 0, the value
is the alignment: 1 becomes 5 (virtue), 3 becomes 6 (bane). Otherwise it is
the element. Then 0-6 index the ids above.

**Birthday** (`0x0802B160`). The text has three figures:
- `0x80 00`: the month's name, string `0x19E + month` of the table at
  `0x08623678` (five are `0x81` strips, "Sombra" to "Oceano");
- `0x80 01`: the day, in decimal;
- `0x80 02`: string `0x1AD + sex`, or "--" when the sex is 0.

The fortune is `0x081406AC`:
- day count D (`0x0813AEB4`) from the date at `0x0200118B`/`C` and the
  month lengths at `0x0861C8B4`;
- x = `(s16(u16 +0x5A + D) * 100 / +0x59) % 100` (`__divsi3`, `__modsi3`);
- band 0, 9, 18, 27, 0 for x up to 13, 36, 63, 86, and above;
- plus 3 or 6 for `+0x58` in 6-10 or above 10;
- plus 1 or 2 for `+0x5C` in 41-59 or above 59.

The phase `+0x5A` is a halfword. Read as a byte, it gave Kamui
"Dissatisfaction" where the game says "Stability". A read watch on the
record while the game built its box showed the `w=16` read.

**Movement type** (`0x08139B74`) is a walk in the table at `0x0861C8C4`
(8 bytes a type):
1. Start at class field `0x22` (`+0x2D`).
2. For each equipped item whose field `0x1D` (ROM `+0x20`; a made item's
   base, side 1 reading `0x02001C60`) is 1-4, move to entry byte `2 + t`.
3. If `+0x5D` bit 0 is set, the battle entry's `+3` moves it again.
4. A snowfield rule (`0x08020BF8`) moves it by +20 or +10: story flag
   `0x122` set and `0x119` clear (flags are bits of `0x020011CC`), a unit
   whose `+0x4E` is not 13 or 14, and IWRAM `0x03001029` clear.

**Verified** against the game's own HELP box (A), from
`states/AY_kamui_talents.state`, with SELECT and then the cursor:
- No.: "A character's number. Can be reassigned…".
- Birthday: "Born on Sombra 7. Sex: Male. / Fortune: Stability.".
- Class: "Highly trained spies who act / under a veil of secrecy. Ninjas".
- Land icon: "Acrobatic characters can climb / up to 3 steps up or 4 down.".
- Water icon: "These characters can move on / the water's surface with little".

The element, stats, HP/MP, equipment and talents walk as expected. B
leaves help mode and the unit card comes back. Before SELECT, both AY and
