### The battle's weapon and spell lists (2026-09-29)

After Attack or Magic the game lists the acting unit's weapons (ARMS) or
talents (TALENT). SELECT there shows the row's HELP text. The second screen
now shows that text on its own, the same card as in the status window, for
the row under the cursor. Asked for on the Thor, to match the other screens.

**How it was found.** An entry hook on the help text fetch `0x08015D50`
while SELECT was pressed:
- in `CO`'s weapon menu the caller is `0x0807B66B`, with help id `0x32`;
- in `CO`'s spell menu the caller is `0x0807C997`, with help id `0x10A`.

Both callers index the same list, in the battle's work block
`[0x0202B26C]`. That block moves between runs (`0x0202B740`, `0x0202B734`,
`0x0202B858`), which is why a fixed-address search for the item found
nothing.
- `+0x2047` is 3 while such a list is open. It is 5 in the command menu,
  the move choice and targeting.
- `+0x203C` is the acting record.
- `+0x1E94` holds the list's ids, 0-terminated:
  - `CO` ARMS: `09`, Balmung;
  - `CN` ARMS: `C8`, Kaukown;
  - `CO` TALENT: `24`, Heal;
  - `CN` TALENT: `17 57`, Ice Javelin and Atropos.
- The window object is at `+0x206C`:
  - u16 `+0x0E` is the title: `0x22F` ARMS, `0x255` TALENT;
  - the row is u16 `+0x16` plus u16 `+0x1A`, as `0x0807B4FC` and
    `0x0807C92C` compute it. Down in `CN`'s spell list moves `+0x1A` from 0
    to 1, and SELECT then shows Atropos's text.
- The help ids are the ones the game passes: the item's ROM `+0x04`
  (Balmung `0x32`, via `0x081437AC(item, 2)`) and the talent's `+0x06`
  (Heal `0x10A`).

**Not handled:** a `0xFF` row, which the weapon path (`0x0807B52C`)
resolves through the class instead, and lists with other titles (the item
bag was not tried). `kol::battle_list_row` in `kol_unit_data.cpp`.

**Verified:** `CO` weapon menu shows Balmung, both pages. `CN`'s spell list
shows Ice Javelin, then Atropos after Down, and its weapon menu shows
Kaukown. Both render invariants are unchanged.

### The move prompt goes to the second screen (2026-09-29)

Asked for on the Thor: starting a move always put up the NAVI prompt "Choose
where you want to move this character.", and it needed an A before the D-pad
did anything. Now the prompt closes at once. The second screen shows its text
as a card on the moving unit's sheet, and hides it when the cursor leaves
the unit.

**The prompt.** Traced by hooking the text fetch `0x08015D50`, backing out
of `CN`'s command menu into the move choice:
- The move-choice task opens the prompt at `0x080662C4`: NAVI bank
  `0x0875D99A`, entry `0x22`. It stores the box handle at `0x0202A5A8`,
  saves and clears the map-cursor flag `0x03000FD5` (which is why the D-pad
  is dead), and sets its state byte (task `+0x27E`) to 9.
- State 9 (`0x080662F0`) polls the text box through `0x0801670C` until that
  returns `0xFF` (A pressed). It then closes the box (`0x0806CD50`), clears
  `0x0202A5A8`, sets `0x03000FD5` to 1, and goes to state `0x0B`.

**The change** (a game change, a reviewed `[[mod_function_hook]]` on
`0x0801670C`; `kol_actions.cpp`):
- The hook answers `0xFF` only when the caller is that state-9 handler
  (return address `0x080662F4`), by setting `R0 = 0xFF` and `R15` to the
  return address, which is what the generated caller's `bl` expects.
- Every other dialogue that polls the same routine is declined and waits
  as before.
- The box never reaches the screen: frames 163-166 show no box, and at 240
  a Right already moved the cursor.
- `KOL_NO_SKIP_MOVE_NAVI=1` puts the prompt back, byte for byte the old
  frames.

**The second screen** (`kol::move_choice_on_actor`). A move is being chosen
when a unit takes its action, the map cursor is out, and the move-choice
task (`0x0202A5B0`, the `r7` of the handlers above) is in its
choose-a-destination state `0x0B` (`kol::move_choice_active`). The card goes
on the actor while the cursor's cell holds the acting unit.
- **Corrected 2026-09-29:** B cancels the move without moving the cursor,
  and the card stayed up. The first test (not targeting, `0x0202A753 == 0`)
  and then the painted move range (grid bit `0x40` on the actor's cell) both
  survive B unchanged, along with every other flag. The task's state goes
  17, 16, 18, 7, 5 (back on the map). `CN`, B at +200: the card goes at
  frame 204. `S_move_highlight` reads `0x0B`. `BU_freelook_blurry` and
  `AV_pre_range` read 5: they are map browsing on the unit's turn, not move
  choices, as they were earlier taken to be.

The acting unit's sheet then carries NAVI entry `0x22` as its HELP card, read
with the HELP decoder (`help_text_at`; the NAVI bank has the same layout).
The card shows once per move choice (the user's rule):
- it is shown from when it appears until **4 seconds** have passed or the
  cursor leaves the unit, whichever comes first;
- coming back to the unit does not bring it back; the next move choice does
  (`kol::move_choice_active`).

`CN`, B three times: the card appears at frame 165 and goes at 404 (239
frames, 4.0 s). With Right at +200 and Left at +240, it goes at 202 and
stays away at 242.

**"Can't move to that spot." (2026-09-29).** Asked for on the Thor
(`states/CT_cant_move_spot.state`: Elrik moving, cursor on Eleanor, A). The
user's rule is the same: not on the game screen; on the second screen for
4 seconds, gone when the cursor moves.
- The move choice's message state (`0x08066B28`) polls the same
  `0x0801670C` and, on `0xFF`, closes the box and returns to the state it
  came from.
- The message is bank `0x0875C8DE` entry `0x1D`, fetched from
  `0x0806657E`: "Can't move to that spot. Select a panel within range."
- The poll hook now answers that caller too (return address `0x08066B2C`).
- A second hook on the text fetch `0x08015D50` records each fetch's bank and
  entry and declines every call. So the second screen shows whatever
  message that state was given (`kol::move_message`).
- The card goes on the top unit's sheet, and the sheet stays single while
  it shows (the two-card sheet has no room for it). It goes after 4 s, when
  the cursor leaves the cell, or when the move choice ends (B). That cell is taken once the cursor is
  out again: for frames 12-18 the cursor is put away and its slot is stale.
- The text's leading `0x81 0xBF` escape is skipped by the decoder.
- `CT`: with A only, the card shows from frame 12 to 251. With A and then
  Right, it goes at 62, and the cursor moves at once.

**Open:** NAVI entry `0x08` is the same sentence. The caller that uses it
was not found. If pressing A on a unit at the start of its turn goes through
that one, the prompt will still appear there. A state saved just before that
A would settle it.

**Verified:** both render invariants unchanged, with and without
`KOL_NO_SKIP_MOVE_NAVI=1`.

## Controller: R and L on the face buttons, the shoulders switch units (2026-09-25)

**Removed 2026-11-17** (the user found it of little use, and it broke the game's
button prompts): R and L stay on the shoulders; the top and left
face buttons are the unit buttons (Shortcut A/B, Next/Previous), as they were
with the option off. `Setting::PadRemap` keeps its slot (retired, always off,
no label, so the BACK menu skips it); `pad_remap_set` is now `pad_install`.
Then Options > Gameplay > **Swap Face Buttons** (`swap_face`, off): the
game's A and B on each other's buttons (gbarecomp `g_host_pad_binds`), and the
unit buttons X and Y too (`kol::pad_swap_set`); the menus read the bound keys,
so they follow it.

The user asked for GBA R on the top face button in all situations, so the
shoulders can be **R: Next unit** and **L: Previous unit**. GBA L goes on the
left face button. The shoulders do exactly what the second screen's buttons
do: on the battle map they move the cursor, and in a status window they
switch the unit it shows.

**The seam** (gbarecomp, `runtime.h`):
- `g_host_pad_binds[10]` gives the controller button for each KEYINPUT bit.
  The defaults are the old fixed table.
- `g_host_pad_button_hook(button, down)` is called on every controller
  button edge. The shoulders are not reported while L3 is held, so the
  save-state combos (L3+R1 save, L3+L1 load) still save and load and switch
  no unit.
- The table is plain `int`s outside the SDL backend so the stub build links.
  A `static_assert` ties it to SDL's values.

**Which button is "top".** SDL names face buttons by Xbox position, but the
Thor's pad reports its Nintendo labels. Its key layout
(`/system/usr/keylayout/Vendor_2020_Product_0111.kl`) maps the kernel's
`BTN_NORTH` (0x133) to `BUTTON_X` and `BTN_WEST` (0x134) to `BUTTON_Y`, and
SDL passes those through. `getevent -l` confirmed the physical buttons. So
on the Thor, SDL X is the top button and SDL Y the left one. KoL binds R to
SDL X and L to SDL Y (`src/kol_actions.cpp`, `pad_install`). On a pad that
reports Xbox positions instead, the two would swap.

**A BACK-menu toggle**, "Shoulders switch units (R/L on X/Y)" (key
`pad_remap` in `enhancements.cfg`, on by default). It applies at once:
`kol::pad_remap_set()` rewrites the two bindings and sets or clears the
button hook. Off puts R and L back on the shoulders, and the shoulders then
switch nothing. The desktop runner has no menu and keeps the default.
`KOL_NO_PAD_REMAP=1` forces it off whatever the setting says. On start the log says
`pad: R on SDL X (top), L on SDL Y (left); shoulders = next/previous unit`.
Headless runs have no controller, so this can only be checked on the device.

## The left stick moves the hand (2026-10-13)

Asked for the left stick to move the hand cursor analogically: slow when
pressed softly, fast when pushed all the way, in all directions, snapping to
the nearest position when the stick is released.

**What the game does** (all from the ROM and a fingerprint trace of one
D-pad step, `GBARECOMP_INSN_TRACE=1` + TCP `fp_save`):

| what | where |
|---|---|
| the cursor | IWRAM `0x03000FA0`: +0x30 keys held, +0x2E repeat pulse, +0x35 mode (1 out, 4 gliding), +0x36 lock (0xFF), +0x3C x and +0x40 z (u16; +0x3E is something else), +0x44/+0x48 the cell before, +0x95 1 while the camera pans to it |
| its task | `0x08056E90`, once a frame: with a direction held, mode 1 and the step `0x08056F90`; L held is view mode; nothing while +0x95 is up |
| the step | one cell per pulse, onto a cell with flag `0x20` only (else it tries the diagonal neighbours); copies the old cell to +0x44/+0x48 |
| a cell | `[0x02029CCC] + (x + 32 z) * 4`: +1 height, +2 flags (`0x08028800` flags, `0x08028914` height); the map header `[0x02029CC0]` (in ROM) +6 width, +8 depth |
| the drawing | `cursor_draw` `0x08057768(x, z)`: world X = 32x + 16, Z = 32z + 16, Y = 16 height; the floating hand through `0x08002394(def, sx, sy)` (returns to `0x08057874`), then the corner pieces through `0x0807696C(0x08057AD5, cursor, X, Y, [sp] Z)` (returns to `0x08057900`) into the sprite emitter `0x08076810` |
| the projection | `0x080769D0`/`0x08076A28`: sx = `(X - Z) >> 1`, sy = `((X + Z) >> 2) - (Y >> 1)`, plus the camera |

The cursor has no position between cells: a D-pad step moves the cell and the
sprite jumps.

**What KoL does** (`src/kol_stick_cursor.cpp`, three reviewed hooks in
`game.toml`):
- **The task (declines).** The stick (radial dead zone 0.2, full at 0.95,
  speed = 5 screen px a frame times the push squared) moves a point P in
  screen directions: stick right is right on the screen, so up crosses cells
  diagonally. Screen to world: dX = sx + 2 sy, dZ = 2 sy - sx. When P crosses
  into another cell the hook writes it as the step does (+0x44/+0x48, then
  +0x3C/+0x40); the camera, the terrain box, the move range's red hand and
  the second screen follow the game's cell as for the pad. A cell the step
  would refuse (no flag `0x20`, off the map) stops P on that axis, so it
  slides along walls. While +0x95 is up P moves on inside its cell. Let go,
  P eases to the cell's middle (30% a frame, there in ~9 frames). Only with
  the cursor out (mode 1, not locked) and no direction, A, Select, Start,
  L or R held (the pad's step path refuses on `0x30D`); the pad, a glide or
  a jump that moves the cell puts P back on it. (+0x51 is 1 in
  preparation's view mode, where the pad's step runs too: an early version
  stood aside on it, and the stick did nothing there; state GH.)
- **The two draw calls.** While P is off its cell's middle, each is made
  again with P's point (`R15` = the routine, LR kept, a one-shot pass for the
  repeat): the corner pieces get P's X, Y, Z, so the game projects and sorts
  them; the hand's screen x, y move by the same projected offset. The height
  drawn eases to the cell's (35% a frame) instead of jumping. Both check
  that `cursor_draw`'s arguments (`[sp+0x88]`, `[sp+0x8C]`) are the cell.
  Their return sites are static entries, so this stays fully static.
- With P on its middle (the stick never touched) all three decline.
- `kol_focus.cpp` reads the cursor's slot: the camera votes now use the
  game's shifts (identical on cell centres, exact between them), the cell is
  `X >> 5` (was `(X - 16) / 32`; the same on centres, half a cell apart
  only mid-glide), and the unit under the cursor compares the cell's middle.

gbarecomp: `g_host_pad_left_stick[2]` beside the right stick (`runtime.h`).
Options > **Analog Cursor** (key `analog_cursor`, on by default).
`KOL_NO_STICK_CURSOR=1` leaves the hooks out. Tests:
`KOL_STICK_TEST="a-b:x,y;..."` holds the stick from the task's a-th call after
a state load to its b-th; `KOL_STICK_TRACE=1` logs each frame.

**Checked (desktop, dummy-video window; the hooks need the frame hook):**
- DF (cursor on empty ground): right at full tilt crosses a cell every ~6
  frames along the map's z = 0 edge (sliding: z = -1 is off the map), the
  height eases 112 -> 96, the camera pans at the field's edge; let go, it
  settles in 9 frames. Zoomed frames: the hand and the corner pieces glide
  together, ~5 px a frame.
- The same with the perspective and depth of field on: the map does not
  shift while the hand moves (0, 0 by correlation over 30 frames), no
  artifacts at the hand.
- S_move_highlight (choosing a move): the cell, the terrain box and the
  game's red out-of-range hand follow.
- Stick idle, the hooks on vs `KOL_NO_STICK_CURSOR=1`: 40 presents
  byte-identical (DF, perspective, 480x270). Both invariants hold (240
  `66e13ab2`, anchor-off 284 `9054c456`). Coverage FULLY_STATIC.
- Not checked: the Thor's stick (whether Android reports it as the left
  axes, and its feel); the targeting cursor; holding the stick while the
  enemy acts.

### On the world map too (2026-10-13)

Asked for the same on the world map, snapping to a city that is very close
when the stick is released, as the d-pad already does.

**What the game does.** The world map's cursor is the sword, free on the
screen: the roaming task `0x08128D9C` in state 4 (its first argument's byte)
adds 3 px a frame for each direction held (keys at `0x03000820`) to the
control block's (`[0x02029C5C]`, IWRAM `0x03000EB0`) +0x1E x and +0x1F y,
kept to 8..232 and 8..152. Then `0x0812A268(&x, &y)` looks at the 24 places
(table `0x08621228`, stride 0x2C, +0x11/+0x12 the tile column and row): a
place whose 24 px box (from its tile corner, minus one) holds the sword pulls
it one pixel a frame on each axis toward its middle (corner + 11); once the
sword sits on a middle the place is chosen (+0x12) and its name shows. Then
`0x0812B0F0` draws the sword. So the pad snapping to a town is that
pull, every frame, held or not; the pad's 3 px outrun its 1.

**What KoL does.** A fourth hook on the roaming task (declining; the army
list's hook in kol_actions shares that entry): in state 4, with the stick
pushed and no direction held, the sword's place is the stick's, kept in
fractions of a pixel (up to 4 px a frame, the same dead zone and curve as
the battle map) and written before the task runs. The pull then moves it a
pixel at most toward a town (the stick's place is written again the next
frame), so a slow push leaves a town instead of being held. Let go, nothing
is written and the game's own pull takes the sword onto a town within its
box, as after the pad. No `game.toml` change: the roaming task was hooked
already.

**Checked** (DO_overworld, dummy-video window):
- A slow push (0.45 right, 0.45 px a frame) crosses the town at (147, 83)
  and goes on past it.
- Let go at (150, 86), inside that town's box: two frames later the sword is
  on Vespa and its name is up, as after the pad. Let go at (167, 86), in no
  box: it stays.
- Stick idle, the pad replayed (right, down, up): 150 presents
  byte-identical with the hooks on and with `KOL_NO_STICK_CURSOR=1`.
  FULLY_STATIC.

## Depth of field on the battle map (2026-09-25)

An optional present-time effect (BACK menu, off by default): the battle map is
blurred by its distance from the cursor, sharp around it and heaviest at the
screen's extremes. It is drawn at present, over the uploaded frame; the PPU
frame, frame hashes and both render invariants are unaffected (re-run with the
effect forced on: 240 `66e13ab2`, anchor-off 284 `9054c456`, centre-240 0/160).

### What the game gave us

| what | where | verified |
|---|---|---|
| **per-cell height** (the long-open "elevation") | EWRAM `0x02016440`, 32x32 cells, row-major, 4 bytes: +0 terrain id, +1 height, +2 flags (`0x80` on the map) | 37/37 cells on `H_terrain_info`, 43/43 on `AU`, against the terrain box's "N STEP" digit (BG3 sb10 col 23, tile `0x42+2d` over `0x43+2d`) |
| unit world positions | objects (u32 at `0x0202A238`, stride `0xD0`): +0x10 X, Y (up), Z; X = cell_x*32+16, Z = cell_y*32+16, Y = height*16 | 3 units against the grid |
| the projection | `sx = (X-Z)/2 + kx`, `sy = (X+Z)/4 - Y/2 + ky` | exact on 8 unit slots |
| the cursor | the sprite slot whose routine is `0x08057AD5` holds its world position, gliding; absent on the enemy turn and while a command menu is up | 3 states |
| the camera | `kx + BG0HOFS` and `ky + BG0VOFS` are constant per map, mod the BG size 512x256 | 3 maps, across an enemy-turn pan |

A prop's cell (tree `0x07`, rock `0x0A`, bush `0x08` on the snowfield) holds
the prop's TOP: +3, +2, +1 over its neighbours. Its ground is the highest
non-prop neighbour. Other maps may have prop ids not in that list.

### How it is drawn

KoL (`src/kol_focus.cpp`) rebuilds each pixel's place in the scene at present:
terrain rasterized back to front from the grid (tops and walls), props and
units as camera-facing cut-outs at the place of the cell they stand on. A prop's
pixels are BG1, or BG0 where no terrain was drawn (trees are partly on the
ground layer); a prop's place spreads through its connected pixels, up to
24 px, so tree art larger than its cell is covered. Sprites that are not units
(menu text, icons, cursor, weather) stay sharp.

Distance = rows apart (X+Z) plus height apart, one height step counting one
row (`KOL_FOCUS_HEIGHT`). Sharp within 1.5 rows (`KOL_FOCUS_NEAR`), then an even
ramp to full at the most distant terrain on screen on each side. The focus is
the cursor; with none, the unit that moved since the last frame; with neither,
the tile at the screen centre. It eases over a few frames.

gbarecomp draws it: four levels (sharp, 1/2, 1/4, 1/8), each pixel blending the
two either side of its position on that ladder. The heavy levels are built from
a CPU 1/4-size source that weights each pixel by its own blur, so in-focus
things and the HUD leave no halo on the background. BG2/BG3 (the battle HUD)
and sprites over them are forced sharp from the compositor's per-pixel layer
map (`gba::g_ppu_record_layers`, recorded only while asked for).

### What did not work, and why

- **Camera depth (X+Z+Y) as the distance.** Front and below cancel: a unit six
  rows in front and eight steps below the cursor came out two rows away and in
  focus. Rows and height now add.
- **Each prop cell as a solid column of its stored height.** It boxed every tree
  in a sharp "glass cage" of sky and terrain.
- **The camera from the first unit sprite slot.** The slot list keeps stale
  entries and trails the scroll during pans: terrain landed 40 px off on the
  enemy turn. Votes accumulated over frames, plus the frame's own BG0 scroll,
  fixed it. Taking Y mod 512 instead of the BG's 256 split one map's constant
  in two, and the wrong one won mid-turn.
- **One blur level faded in with alpha.** It hazes rather than blurs: sharp
  detail shows through to the end, so distance did not read as more blur.
- **Blurring the frame as uploaded.** In-focus trees and units smeared a blocky
  ghost of themselves over the background.
- **The screen's extremes including the sky.** The sky reads as the ground plane
  far beyond the map; letting it set the ramp left the whole map barely blurred.
- **RGBA render targets on the Thor (GLES2, Adreno).** Their alpha reads back 0,
  so every translucent draw of them was invisible while desktop Metal and
  OpenGL were fine. The levels are `RGB888` targets; per-pixel opacity rides
  on mesh vertex alpha or on CPU-uploaded textures.

### Tools

`GBARECOMP_PRESENT_DUMP=<file.bmp>` (+ `GBARECOMP_PRESENT_DUMP_AT=<n>`) saves
the window as the player sees it; `--dump-bmp` is the PPU frame and never shows
a present-time effect. `KOL_FOCUS_DUMP=<prefix>` (+ `KOL_FOCUS_DUMP_AT`) writes
one frame's layer map and blur, raw 1 byte per pixel.

### Open

- Menu text over a blurred unit takes the unit's blur (the unit's box claims
  the pixel); exact needs the compositor to record which sprite drew it.
- Snow and rain stay sharp (non-unit sprites).
- Only 16x32 unit sprites get their own place; larger monsters partly read as
  terrain.
- BG0 tree art in front of terrain takes the terrain's place.
- Cost on the Thor is not measured: the depth pass, the weighted 1/4 source and
  a full-frame overlay upload run every frame while it is on.

Repro states (local only): `BK_tree_glass_cage`, `BL_enemy_turn`,
`BM_tree_broken`, `BN_water_focus`, `BO_grimal_alphonse`.

## Perspective on the battle map (2026-09-26)

A BACK-menu toggle, "Perspective (farther is smaller)", off by default: the
battle map is drawn as a camera looking LEVEL at it would see it. The farther
a thing is, the smaller it is, and everything upright stays upright. Drawn at
present; the PPU frame, frame hashes and both render invariants are unchanged
(240 `66e13ab2`, anchor-off 284 `9054c456`, centre-240 0/160, also with the
perspective and the depth of field forced on).

This is NOT the keystone warp rejected on 2026-09-25. That one scaled each
screen ROW, so every wall leaned in; and it cut the HUD out and refilled it,
which left smudges. Here the scale follows the WORLD.

### How it works

- **Where every pixel is.** `kol_focus.cpp`'s scene rebuild (height grid,
  objects, camera; see "Depth of field" below) gives each pixel its depth D
  (X + Z), height Y, and whether it faces up (a cell top) or stands upright
  (walls, props, units, the grid cursor). It is shared: `kol::scene_pixels()`,
  built once per frame.
- **The projection.** A place at depth D is drawn at `s = K / (K + Dref - D)`
  times its size, toward the screen's middle column. Heights scale by s about
  Yref and depth offsets from Dref by s, then the game's own iso projection
  applies. That is a projective map of the world, so straight lines stay
  straight, and s does not change along a vertical line. Dref is the depth
  under the middle row, so the middle keeps its size. `K = 3600`
  (`KOL_PERSP_K`): the top of a 480x270 screen at 0.87, the bottom at 1.18.
  The user chose this from mockups labelled "0.9".
- **The HUD-free frame.** gbarecomp composes each frame a second time without
  BG2|BG3 (`gba::g_ppu_scene_exclude_layers`, `GbaPpu::latched_scene`), in the
  same pass: one more compare per layer per pixel. Interface sprites are then
  filled from their left neighbour, since they are drawn flat on top.
- **The mesh** (`g_present_warp_provider`). There is one vertex per pixel
  corner. It is placed by the FRONTMOST of the up to four pixels around it, so
  a near unit keeps its shape and the background stretches to its edge instead
  of leaving a hole. Each corner row is cut into straight pieces once
  (tolerance 0.1 frame px), and both strips sharing the row use the same cuts:
  no T-junctions, so no hairline gaps. Runs are split where the surface
  changes and drawn far to near. That is about 18k triangles.
- **The sky** is not in the mesh. It is the backdrop, drawn as it is. Where
  the map moves away, the backdrop has that row's sky colour. The map's dark
  outline (BG0|BG1 pixels up to 3 px outside the rebuilt cells) is attached to
  the map, or it stayed behind as dashes in the sky.
- **The HUD** (BG2|BG3, sprites over them, interface sprites) is drawn flat
  from the real frame, last.

`KOL_PERSP_HOLES=1` paints the backdrop under the map magenta, so any gap in
the mesh shows. On `BK`, `BO` and `BS`, magenta appears only along the
silhouette the map vacates. On the Mac it shows what SDL's software renderer
drew, not only the mesh: before 2026-10-02 that renderer dropped slivers it
took for rects, so a hairline there needs the mesh checked on its own
(dump it and rasterise in float) before the mesh is blamed ("Perspective:
drawn heights").

`KOL_PERSP_KIND=1` shows the mesh's geometry. The scene is painted by what
each pixel is, before the warp:
- green: flat ground; red: upright (walls, props, a unit's place);
- light and dark bands alternate every 8 units of depth, so **on level
  ground the bands must run parallel**;
- blue: an overlay; blue added: the floating hand (magenta on a wall); half
  blue: other interface;
- black: nothing placed.

Units drawn from their own sprites, the flat HUD and the moved hand keep
their colours. Render it with the stick (`KOL_PERSP_LOOK=x,y`) and look for
bands that bend, bunch or break on level ground. To measure, read the band
transitions per column in the present dump: on level ground every column
changes band on the same rows. It found the ice shear and the hand's ground
sheet (below). On the Thor it is the last BACK-menu toggle, "Debug:
perspective mesh (green flat, red upright)" (`debug_mesh=` in
enhancements.cfg, off by default); it shows only with the perspective on.

### The camera flipped on a blinking unit (fixed 2026-09-26)

Reported on the device as the perspective going wild in battle
preparation (`states/BT_persp_crazy.state`, one unit on a deployment square).
The scene rebuild finds the camera from votes: each unit's sprite slot implies
one. The unit on the square blinks (see "The blinking unit, half
transparent"), and on the frames it is not drawn, the sprite slot that held it
holds another sprite naming the same unit as its owner, at (56, 276) instead
of (120, 100): the slots are handed out in call order. That position implies
a camera 176 rows off. With one unit the two tied, the camera flipped every frame, and the

### Scene overscan: the far side reaches the edge (2026-09-26)

The far side shrinks inward, so the frame's edge used to show as a straight
cut against the sky. With the perspective on, gbarecomp composes the HUD-free
scene past the view (`g_ppu_scene_overscan`): at 480x270, 45 px each side and
32 rows on top, from K and the view size (`kol::perspective_overscan`). Beyond
the view only the scene is composed (BG2|BG3 are not drawn there) and the
providers are asked in view coordinates, so HUD anchoring is untouched; the
frame and its layer map are cut back to the view at latch. The guest's unit
cull is widened by the overscan. Mockup and throwaway patches:
`shots/perspective_edges/`. Both render invariants are unchanged, also with
the perspective forced on. Headless cost +1.1 ms a frame on the Mac (7.8 to
8.9). The batched HUD row path had a 512-px limit that fell back to per-pixel
work (+4.7 ms); it is 576 now. `KOL_PERSP_NO_OVERSCAN=1` turns it off. Without
GL (Metal) the overscanned warp draws without the layered blur.

**What it cost on the Thor, and the row trim (2026-09-27).** Measured A/B/A
with the user playing one battle map (480x270, perspective and depth of field
on, 88-96 °C): the overscan took the guest thread from 87-88% of a core to
97.7-98.7%, and fps from a median of ~56.5 to ~53-54. The desktop's headless
+1.1 ms had hidden half of it: headless never presents, and the warp provider,
the scene upload and the mesh all grow with the scene too (a windowed desktop
profile split the extra time about evenly between the compositor and present).
Android has no way to pass `KOL_PERSP_NO_OVERSCAN`, so the A/B was a throwaway
build.

Only the far rows need the side columns. A place at view row r and height Y
lies `4 (view_h/2 - r) + 2 (Yref - Y)` behind the reference and is drawn
`(view_w/2)(dref - D)/K` farther in than it is; nothing is below Y = 0, and
Yref moves at most 5% of the way a frame. So `kol::perspective_overscan_rows`
gives each row of the scene the side columns it can need (plus 8 of slack and
32 units of Yref drift), and gbarecomp composes only those
(`g_ppu_scene_overscan_rows`; the rest read as `gba::kLayerNotComposed` in the
scene's layer map, and the warp places nothing from them). Before the reference
is known, every row gets all of them.
- `KOL_PERSP_TRIM_CHECK=1` composes everything and counts the left-out corners
  the warp would draw inside the view. Panning across `BO` and `BT` (Yref from
  46 to 219) it found none; the nearest came 4.5 px from the edge.
- The presented picture: `BO` byte-identical to untrimmed at three points of a
  pan; `BT` differs in 53-152 scattered single pixels on flat water and sand.
  They are the mesh's row merge, which is greedy from the first corner of a
  span within 0.1 px, cutting at other places when a span starts at the trim.
- Both render invariants unchanged; the 480x270 frame with the perspective on
  is byte-identical to the plain one, headless and windowed.
- Cost. Desktop CPU a frame (200/800 difference, windowed): no overscan 14.0 ms,
  untrimmed 15.5, trimmed 15.2. Thor: 93.6-94.1% of a core, fps median ~54.5
  with almost no frame over 25 ms. What is left is the 32 top rows (needed full
  width) and KoL's per-pixel work over the whole scene. The build without the
  overscan also sat at 54-58 fps at 87%, so the Thor's shortfall from 60 is not
  the guest thread alone. `KOL_PERSP_NO_TRIM=1` composes all the side columns.

**The warp provider on worker threads (2026-09-27).** Timed per phase (a
throwaway timer build, logcat on the Thor), the provider is ~3 ms a frame on
the Mac and ~2.1 ms on the Thor, spread evenly over six per-pixel passes: the
scene rebuild, the outline flood, the vertices, the surface cuts, the row
merge and the triangle list, each 0.3-0.6 ms. Two rewrites of single passes
bought almost nothing (the vertex search as row pairs: 0.63 -> 0.56 ms;
skipping the slope bounds of corners that do not fit: nothing). They run at
~2.5 ns a pixel, bound by memory and branches, not arithmetic.
- The row passes (vertices with cuts, then the merge) and the triangle list
  now run on a small pool (`RowPool`): two workers plus the guest thread take
  chunks of 16 rows from an atomic counter, a chunk at a time, so a worker on a
  slower core just takes fewer. A claim carries the run's generation, so a
  worker that wakes late cannot touch a finished run. Each row is computed as
  it would be alone and the triangle chunks are joined in order: the presented
  frames are byte-identical with and without it (`KOL_PERSP_THREADS=0`).
- The row functions copy what they use into locals. Captured by reference,
  every byte store (`used`, `keep`) forced the compiler to reload the view
  size, the camera and the array pointers: the serial path was 30% slower
  until then.
- Mac: the provider 2.95 -> 2.0 ms. Thor: the guest thread did 42% of the
  chunks and waited 0.16 ms a frame at the ends of the regions, so it saves
  ~0.9 ms a frame there, ~5% of a core. The workers run at ~5% each. That is
  below the session-to-session noise of the fps/CPU scripts, which did not see
  it (97.5-98% of a core in that session, 94% in the one before).
- So the provider is not where the Thor's ~16 ms goes. The desktop profile
  puts ~5 ms in the compositor, which with the perspective on composes every
  pixel twice (the frame and the HUD-free scene), line by line at HBlank; it
  cannot simply be split across threads.

**Where the Thor's frame goes, and the mesh through GL (2026-09-27).** A
throwaway build timed each part of the guest thread's frame (wall and thread
CPU, logcat every 300 frames) while the user played a battle map, 480x270,
perspective and depth of field on. Per frame, thread CPU:

| | before | mesh through GL |
|---|---|---|
| whole frame | 17.0-18.0 ms | 16.8 |
| compositor (scanlines) | 6.6-7.1 | 6.9 |
| present | 4.9-5.8 | 4.1-4.6 |
| - the warp provider (KoL's mesh) | 2.0-2.25 | 2.0-2.2 |
| - the blur map (focus provider + upload) | | 0.8-0.95 |
| - the two mesh draws | most of ~2-3 | 0.12-0.13 |
| the game, hooks, the rest | ~4.5 | ~4.5 |

- The frame's CPU was over the 16.7 ms budget, so that session's missing fps
  was the guest thread; the swap barely waits (0.3 ms). On the Mac the split
  is the same shape. Without the perspective the compositor is 5.1 ms on the
  Mac and with it 5.7: the second picture is cheap; nearly all the compositor
  is the game's own 480x270 frame.
- `SDL_RenderGeometryRaw` expands every index into a vertex of its own on the
  CPU, and with the depth of field the mesh is drawn twice. gbarecomp now
  draws it through GL (`disc::mesh_upload` / `disc::mesh_draw`, see its
  commit): Mac 1.60 -> 0.09 ms, presented frames byte-identical, the user saw
  no change on the Thor. The first attempt differed in every map pixel by 1-4
  levels: SDL applies a texture's scale mode when it draws, and the GL texture
  itself was linear; the draw now sets the SDL texture's mode and puts it back.
- Left, in order: the compositor (~7 ms, mostly not the perspective), KoL's
  mesh (~2.1), the blur map (~0.9, the focus provider per scene pixel).
- The user hears the Thor's fan run loudly with the perspective and depth of
  field on, and not with everything off.

**The depth of field on the GPU (2026-09-27).** Thor GPU busy on one battle
map (`/sys/class/kgsl/kgsl-3d0/gpu_busy_percentage`, clock steady at 550 of
680 MHz): depth of field off 6-7%, on 29-30%; the guest thread 82.6% vs 94%.
- Where: a throwaway build cycled four variants 20 s each (logged, GPU sampled
  once a second in step): full 29.1%, no disc gather 9.4%, no gather and no
  blur-map target 8.1%, off 7.0%. So ~20 points are the gather itself; the
  window-sized render targets were not the cost (the first guess).
- Fewer taps for smaller discs (same density as the largest disc's 48): 27%,
  within noise, and a little grainier at mid radii: dropped. The spiral now
  turns by a constant rotation instead of a sin and cos a tap (same picture).
- The gather at half the window's size, composited back (gbarecomp
  `disc::kComposite`): GPU **18%**. Sharp pixels are the picture itself; a
  blurred one takes the four half-size results around it with bilinear
  weights, leaving out any whose centre is sharp. A plain bilinear upscale
  left a one-pixel dark ring round a unit in focus against the blurred sky.
  The user approved the look on the Thor. `GBARECOMP_DISC_FULL_SIZE=1` is the
  A/B.

### The combat camera (2026-09-27)

At the user's request: while an attack plays on the battle map, the camera
goes lower and closer, eased in and out over 14 frames. Only with the
perspective on; spells are left alone (their animation is a scene of its own,
pillarboxed, `states/BW_spell_confirm.state`).

- **The signal.** `0x08088912`, seen through the function-entry hook (the
  guest is not changed). A per-frame trace of every function entered, over
  900 frames after confirming an attack (`states/BV_attack_confirm.state`),
  found it called once a frame on all 299 frames from the strike's start to
  its "EXP earned" message, and never at rest, in menus, on the phase banner
  or in a spell. The strike code is shared, so enemy attacks trigger it too
  (the user wanted that). A strike holds 8 frames after its last call.
- **The camera.** Three things eased together by one `t`: the perspective's K
  down to 0.4 of itself; a pitch that draws depth at 0.75 of its rows about
  the reference while heights keep all of theirs (the ground flattens, walls
  and units stand as tall: a lower camera); and a zoom about the view's
  centre. The user's condition: never more overscan than at rest. The zoom is
  the larger of 1.45 and what K and the pitch need for that (sides:
  Z s(K) >= s(K0); top: Z >= (1 + 4H/K - 4H/K0)/f), 1.63 at 480x270. Eased
  alike, the need is largest at rest and falls from there; fully in, the
  sides need none. The overscan plans for the cameras two frames either way
  (each K with its own zoom). `KOL_PERSP_STRIKE_K`, `_PITCH`, `_ZOOM`,
  `KOL_PERSP_NO_STRIKE`, `KOL_PERSP_STRIKE_FORCE`.
- **Sprites belong to the action** while the camera is on. A unit claims only
  the sprite pixels in its 16x32 box, the rest being interface (flat). The
  zoom tore what crossed the box ("GUARD" on a counter-hit read "GUARL"). Now
  sprite shapes (pixels within 2 px of each other) are flooded: pixels a unit
  claimed keep it, and the rest take the place of the nearest claimed pixel,
  as `kSceneOverlay` (placed upright, winning shared corners, drawn last, kept
  sharp). A shape no unit touches takes the unit whose body is nearest.
  Failed on the way: giving a whole shape the front unit's place (Flauros and
  Alphonse side by side are one shape; his hood was drawn at Alphonse's depth
  and showed the wall), and interface pixels as plain upright (a torch's flame
  in front pulled a digit's corners; the depth of field blurred the digits).
- At rest nothing changes: `BO`, `BT`, `BK` byte-identical, both invariants.
- **Rain (fixed the same day).** Raindrops are sprites too, and at first a
  shape no unit touched joined the nearest unit wherever it was: every drop
  became an overlay at that unit's place and pulled the terrain corners around
  it (the user reported the rain interfering with the terrain). Now such a shape
  joins a unit only within 32 px either side of it and 64 above its feet
  (damage numbers, slashes); the rest stay flat as at rest.
- Built and taken out again at the user's request: rain and snow at random
  depths with the depth of field (for much later; notes in the session
  memory, not in the code).

#### A damage number over a lifted stone came apart (2026-10-19)

Reported: an enemy's coming damage number, 30, was broken up
(`states/HZ_slot2_damage_30_broken.state`, the user's slot 2, map 2 in the
rain, 384x216). Under the combat camera (presents 124-166) the 30's 3 was
a dash beside a whole 0; flat, or with Lifted Props off, it was whole.

**Why.** The 3 lies over the stone left of the target, a lifted prop. The
lifting takes the prop's pixels under interface too (so the stone's card
has no hole under a menu, FG/FX), and the 3's lower rows were lifted with
it. Then the combat camera made the number an overlay at the target's
place and cleared its interface flag. In the warp a lifted pixel is placed
at the ground behind its prop, and the interface-over-prop handling keys
on the interface flag: so those rows went behind the stone's card, the
card took the digit's colours, and the overlay (drawn last) had none.

**Fix** (kol_perspective, warp provider): a lifted pixel the combat camera
moved as an overlay (`moved_overlay`: lifted, `sp.kind` overlay)
- keeps the overlay's place and kind (not the ground behind the prop), so
  it is drawn with the overlays, last; not its prop's bucket either;
- counts as interface over the prop: the card takes the prop's own colour
  there (`under_rgb`), the scene keeps the digit's;
- is not filled as a hole under interface (its colour is its own);
- is not lit as the ground behind the prop (the lift map handed to the
  lighting leaves it out; it took the rain's grey there).
`KOL_PERSP_OVERLAY_LIFTED=1` = as before.

**Found by measuring, after two wrong guesses** (both left in as needed
parts of the fix, each verified): a per-pixel tally in kol_focus (lift,
kind, interface, layer under the digit's OAM pixels) showed the 3's rows
over the stone lifted; magenta painted on those pixels before the mesh
landed where the 3 is (so place and order were right); colour checkpoints
through the warp found the fill under interface (step 2) copying the stone
along each row into the pixels my first change had marked "interface over
a prop". Trap paid again: probes appended to real lines (`lt.lap(...)`)
were deleted with them by the `// TMP` line filter; restored from HEAD by
their neighbours.

**Verified.** HZ: the 30 whole on every present of the hit. 200 presents
old/new at 384x216, all effects: BV, FF, HX, GD, EM byte-identical; GC
(enemy hits Alphonse, map 2) differs on 57, all on the counter-hit's GUARD,
whose D lay over the same stone and lost its outline (fixed the same way).
Both render invariants unchanged (240 `66e13ab2`, anchor-off 284
`9054c456`).

**Then: the 30 tied to the ground behind it, and some raindrops
too** (HZ again; the user suggested looking with the perspective mesh). Under
the mesh paint the number was a blue overlay with green spikes of ground
at its edges, and so were the drops the combat camera gives a unit's place:
overlay pixels were pixels of the map's mesh, and an overlay wins every
corner it shares, so the ground around each was pulled to its place and
the two moved together. **Now each piece is a card** (kol_focus
`overlay_card`, `SpriteBlock::overlay`): squares of the atlas at the
piece's place, as units are drawn, its colours as the game drew them (no
light, no blur, kol_perspective's texel pass skips it), in a last bucket
after the units; its pixels in the scene go back to the ground under them
(`g_under_*`), which shows there. Over a lifted prop the prop keeps the
pixel (its card the prop's colour, `ScenePixels::ovl_card`) and the
overlay card takes the frame's colour from the scene; the mesh-side parts
of the first fix (place, bucket, hole fill, light) went with it.
`KOL_PERSP_OVERLAY_MESH=1` = mesh pixels as before. Verified: HZ's 30 whole
and the ground around it clean under the paint; 200 presents cards/mesh:
HX, EM, GD, BV byte-identical; GC (99) and FF (6) differ only on the
counter-hit's GUARD, whole now where the mesh tore it ("GUARP" on GC); both
render invariants unchanged (240 `66e13ab2`, anchor-off 284 `9054c456`).
Not done: a thin spike of the stone's art, left of the number, is taken as
flat ground (green under the paint) with or without this.

### Units in a spell keep their place (2026-10-20)

**Asked first:** only the affected units stay visible during a spell, all
others fading out. It was built (the card fade for every unit
neither the talent's user nor its target, and fully faded units left out of
the frame so Ice Javelin's blended frost left no ghosts of them), shown on
the Thor, and dropped by the user, who kept only what put
Lara on the right layer. What that was:

**Bodies at priority 0.** While a spell's effect plays the game puts some
units' bodies at OAM priority 0 (`IB`, Rictor's heal on Lara, present 600:
Rictor, Alphonse, Stan and three more at 0; Lara and two others stay at 1).
To the sprite claim priority 0 is interface (menus, the hand: `CH_menu_hand`),
so those bodies were drawn flat where the flat game puts them, which under
the perspective is not where their units stand: Stan in front of Lara and
lower, three units on her left not shown at all. Now, while the spell
camera plays (`cap.spell_camera`, kol_perspective's `0x080AC608`), a 16x16
or 32x32 priority-0 entry that fits a unit's frame is that unit's
(`spell_body` in `claim_unit_sprites`), and its pixels are not interface.
`KOL_NO_SPELL_BODIES=1` keeps them interface, as before.

Checked: IB at presents 600 and 700, every unit on its cell with Lara among
them (with the switch: Stan misplaced, three gone); outside a spell nothing
changes (gated on the spell camera). Both invariants (66e13ab2 / 9054c456).

Found on the way and kept for later: Ice Javelin (`GD`, A at 12) draws its
frost on an affine BG2 blended over BG0, BG1 and the sprites (BLDCNT
`3344`); its flat pixels already hold the units under it, so anything that
fades or moves a unit under it shows the unit's ghost in the blend.
### The right stick moves the camera (2026-09-28)

With the perspective on, the right stick (gbarecomp
`g_host_pad_right_stick`, 15% dead zone) leans and tilts the camera within a
range, eased 20% a frame toward the stick and back to exactly nothing when it
is let go. Down: K x exp(-0.4), pitch 0.75 (lower camera, as the combat
camera); up: K x1.49, pitch 1.25. Left/right: the perspective's centre moves
by up to 1.2 x half the view (at 0.35 the lean was barely visible). It
combines with the combat camera; the zoom is the least that keeps the
overscan within rest's, the sideways shift included (sides: C (1/(Z s) - 1) +
|dx| (1/s - 1) <= C (1/s0 - 1)), and the overscan plans for the cameras the
combat camera and the stick can reach in two frames. Stick centred is the
camera of before byte for byte (BO, BT, BK). `KOL_PERSP_LOOK=x,y` holds a
look for desktop tests, `KOL_PERSP_NO_LOOK=1` ignores the stick.

**The range grown (2026-10-05).** Asked to extend the range of the

### Monsters torn in two: a unit is not always 16 wide (fixed 2026-09-28)

Reported on the Thor as broken sprites (`states/CB_sprites_broken.state`,
the user's slot 1, view mode on a lava map). With the perspective on, a dragon
was split down the middle and a griffin's tail and hind legs sat apart from
it; under the stick the pieces scattered. The plain game draws them whole.

**Why.** The scene rebuild gave a unit the sprite pixels in a fixed box, 12 px
either side of its feet. A human is two 16x16 OAM parts, 16 px wide, from its
screen X - 8. A monster is four, 32 px wide, from X - 16 (read from the state:
units 1-4 and 7 on CB). Its outer 4 px columns were left as interface, flat,
so the perspective moved the body and not the edges.

**The fix: what the hardware drew** (`claim_unit_sprites` in `kol_focus.cpp`).
- An OAM entry belongs to the unit whose sprite frame (32 x 32 on its feet,
  2 px of slack) holds it whole. Where two frames do, the nearest unit by
  column wins, then the front one. X and Y are read in the wrap that fits the
  frame (9 and 8 bits; the wide view unwraps them).
- At every sprite pixel the entry on top is found as the hardware finds it:
  lower priority number, then lower OAM index, first opaque texel, over every
  entry. So a unit takes exactly what it drew there.
- A pixel whose top entry is no unit's keeps the box's answer. That covers
  menus, the cursor and the rain's margin copies.
- **The sprites the frame was drawn with.** The game rewrites OAM and streams
  each unit's animation into OBJ VRAM in VBlank, before the present. Read live,
  2% of the sprite pixels had no opaque texel under them at rest (a pose
  ahead), and 1,300-1,800 a frame while the camera panned on the enemy turn (a
  scroll step ahead; `BL_enemy_turn`). gbarecomp now keeps them with the
  latch: `g_ppu_record_obj` copies OAM, the OBJ tiles and DISPCNT as they
  stood at the frame's last composed line (`GbaPpu::latched_oam`,
  `latched_obj_tiles`, `latched_dispcnt`). KoL sets it with the layer map. A
  rectangle fallback remains (a sprite pixel with no texel goes to the unit
  part on top covering it); with the latched sprites it catches 0-4 pixels a
  frame.
- `KOL_FOCUS_BOX_ONLY=1` keeps the box alone. `KOL_FOCUS_OBJ_STATS=1` prints,
  a frame: the sprite pixels, those a unit drew, those found by rectangle
  only, those no entry accounts for, the ones the box had given elsewhere,
  and the time taken.

**Verified.**
- CB: both monsters whole, at rest and with `KOL_PERSP_LOOK=0,1`.
- The box was also wrong for humans, where it reached into a neighbour. On BO
  a red unit's leg went to the hooded unit in front (86 pixels); on BK the
  grey-helmeted unit's head edge went to the unit beside it (180). Both are
  their own now. BT is byte-identical.
- No sprite pixel is left unexplained on CB, BO, BT or BV_attack_confirm once
  the rain repeat is off (`KOL_WS_NO_WEATHER_REPEAT=1`); the rest are rain.
- Both render invariants unchanged, also with the perspective and the depth
  of field forced on: 240 `66e13ab2`, anchor-off 284 `9054c456`, centre-240
  0/160.
- Cost on the Mac: 24-72 us a frame, plus the 33 KB copy at the latch.

**Open.** For 4 frames of a camera pan on `BL_enemy_turn`, half the unit parts
fail the frame test (up to 684 pixels a frame fall back to the box). The
camera the scene rebuild uses is a scroll step off the drawn frame there. The
box inherits the same offset, so this is the camera's lag, and the terrain's
depth has it too. Not fixed.

### The cursor's hand broke and warped the ground (fixed 2026-09-28)

Reported on the Thor: when the camera moved, the hand cursor broke up and
warped its surroundings. Reproduced on `CB_sprites_broken` with `KOL_PERSP_LOOK` in
all four directions. The grid cursor's slot position is the centre of its
cell's top face, and the cursor draws two things there:
- **Corner pieces** lying on the face, 9 rows above that centre to 8 below.
  They were placed as if they stood upright at the centre, so under the stick
  the front piece broke up. Now they take the place of the face under them
  (flat, at the cursor's height) and stay on their cell.
- **A pointing hand** floating above it, 27-43 rows up. In the mesh, each
  pixel corner is one vertex shared by everything around it. The hand is in
  front of ground several rows farther back, so its corners dragged that
  ground along, and its top rows fell outside the cursor's old box and stayed
  behind. Now, with the perspective, the hand stays interface (out of the
  mesh) and is drawn flat and whole where its cell has gone: moved as the
  point at its middle moves, keeping its size. Where it was, the ground is a
  copy of the run of ground just left of it, so the texture goes on. (Filled
  with one colour, as under a menu, it read as a dark smear.) Under the depth
  of field that spot blurs like the ground around it.
- gbarecomp: `PresentWarpMesh::moved` / `moved_rgb`, pixels drawn with the
  flat ones (under them) from the provider's own colours.

On `BO` the hand used to become a blob on the head of the unit under the
cursor; it now floats above the head as in the plain game, the gap scaled by
the zoom. On `BT` the stretched hand is crisp. `BK` is byte-identical. Both
render invariants unchanged.

### Units drawn from their own sprites (2026-09-28)

Reported: moving the camera side to side with the stick made the two
red ghosts break each other up (`states/CF_ghosts_overlap.state`). Two
ghosts stand one cell apart in one screen column; the front one's sprite
covers the back one's lower half. Drawn from the frame, the back ghost has no
lower body, so when the lean pulled them apart the mesh stretched the two into
one warped figure.

**Now every unit is drawn whole, from its own OAM entries**
(`build_sprite_atlas`, kol_focus.cpp):
- **The atlas.** Each plain unit up to 32x32 is rebuilt into a square of a
  sprite atlas, from the latched OAM, OBJ tiles and palette. Texels the frame
  shows are copied from the frame; texels hidden by another sprite get the
  palette colour.
- **Hidden by priority stays hidden.** A texel the frame shows under a
  background layer stays out: the game hides a unit's lower part in water or
  behind a wall by priority.
- **The frame pixels are lifted.** The unit's own pixels in the frame are
  lifted out. The mesh places the scene without units there (snapshotted
  before units claim their pixels), and each pixel takes the ground from its
  nearer side, mirrored across the gap.
- **Drawing.** gbarecomp appends the atlas under the scene texture and under
  the depth of field's blur map (`PresentWarpMesh::atlas_*`). Each square
  has a fixed grid of corners (so the GL uv cache holds), placed as an
  upright thing at the unit's place. Its opaque runs are drawn after the
  whole map, back to front among units, with the combat camera's overlays
  still last. Each unit blurs at its own distance.
- **Colour effects.** The PPU latch now also keeps the palette, BLDCNT,
  BLDALPHA and BLDY. Brightness on sprites (a menu darkens every sprite 8/16
  in `BK_tree_glass_cage`) is applied to the palette texels as the PPU
  applies it. Mode-1 sprites at BLDALPHA 16/0 (every unit on that snowfield)
  are opaque and count as plain. Left in the frame as before: units blended
  at other weights (the deployment ghost at 8/8), alpha blending on sprites,
  window-gated effects, and sprites larger than 32x32.
  `KOL_PERSP_NO_SPRITES=1` draws units from the frame; `KOL_SPRITE_DEBUG=1`
  lists the squares and the time taken.

**Two things found on the way.**
- **Two units' parts on one rectangle.** The front ghost's upper half and the
  back ghost's lower half are OAM entries on exactly the same 16x16 (OAM 19
  and 32). The back one's went to the front one by column and depth. An
  entry that fits several units now takes the owner of the entry before or
  after it that it adjoins, since a unit's parts are emitted consecutively.
- **Depth order against the map hid units.** Sorted by depth among the map's
  runs (just in front of their own cell), whole groups of units vanished on
  `BO_grimal_alphonse`, at rest too. The height grid puts the upper castle
  higher and nearer than the walkway's units, so with the perspective it slid
  over them. The game never draws terrain over a sprite except by priority,
  and priority-hidden texels are already out of the atlas. So units are drawn
  after the map, as the game layers them. A unit does not go behind a wall
  under the stick; neither does it in the game.

**Verified.**
- `CF`: both ghosts whole at rest, leaning and lowered, with and without the
  depth of field. The back ghost's covered half is its own texels.
- `BO`, `CB`, `BK`, `BT` at rest and lowered: every unit present. BT's
  deployment ghost is in the frame as before (8/8).
- The strike in `BV_attack_confirm` (A replayed) shows the target whole
  behind the attacker, with the damage number over it.
- Both render invariants unchanged: 240 `66e13ab2`, anchor-off 284
  `9054c456`, also with the perspective and the depth of field forced on.
- The atlas costs ~80 us a frame on the Mac. The scene snapshot copies only
  sprite pixels.

User-approved on the Thor 2026-09-28.

### The ground under a unit, from the compositor (2026-09-28)

Where a unit's sprite leaves its place under the stick, the gap used to be
filled by mirroring the ground on either side. On `CB_sprites_broken` that
copied what lay beside the unit into the gap: the purple of a knight's sword
(a piece the fill counted as ground), and, where the griffin stood against a
cliff, the cliff's dark face mirrored into a figure. The wider-looking shadow
of the section above did not reproduce as such: at six stick positions no
exposed fill pixel took a shadow's colour. The dragon's shadow is part of its
own sprite and is lifted with it.

**The game's own ground.** The compositor already ranks every candidate
under a pixel. gbarecomp now keeps, beside the scene frame, the best
candidates over the scene's layers other than OBJ, and where the scene's top
is a sprite it writes that pixel as the game would show it with no sprite
there, its own blending and brightness applied (`g_ppu_scene_under_obj`,
`GbaPpu::latched_scene_under`). The lifted pixels take it. With the units
hidden, the map under them is the map: the cliff face runs on behind the
dragon, and the griffin's figure is gone.

**The scene's own top layer.** The frame's layer code is the top two
layers. The scene leaves out the HUD (BG2|BG3, drawn flat over it), so where
the HUD covers a unit, the scene shows the unit, but every sprite test read
the frame's top and saw HUD:
- `CB`: the "5 STEP" bubble lies over the knight's sword (code `4 << 4 | 3`).
  The sword stayed out of his atlas square and behind in the scene.
- `BK_tree_glass_cage`: the units in front stand under the unit bar, where
  BG2's text lies over BG3's frame over the sprite. The code names two HUD
  layers and cannot say a sprite is under them; whole bodies stayed behind.

gbarecomp now records the scene's own layer codes with the ground
(`GbaPpu::latched_scene_own_layers`), and every sprite test in
`kol_focus.cpp` reads `scene_top()`: those codes for the scene's layer map;
otherwise the frame's code, with the layer under an excluded one. Without the
perspective nothing is excluded, and nothing changes.

**Verified.**
- `CB` at rest and at six stick positions: the knight is whole with his sword
  (as drawn from the frame); no foreign colour in the gap.
- `CF`, `BO`, `BK` lowered, with the units hidden: the ground under them is
  clean. BK leaves no fragment under the bar (the old rule left bodies; the
  code rule alone left outlines).
- Both render invariants unchanged: 240 `66e13ab2`, anchor-off 284
  `9054c456`, also with the perspective and the depth of field forced on.
- Cost on the Mac at 480x270, perspective on, three alternating pairs:
  8.88 -> 9.01 ms a frame (+0.12, about 1.4%): the extra candidate pair in
  the compositor, plus 1.2 MB copied at the latch. Only while the
  perspective draws units from their sprites.
- `KOL_PERSP_MIRROR_FILL=1` fills from beside the unit as before and records
  nothing.

**A second Alphonse in the sky** (reported on the Thor,
`states/CG_alphonse_stretch.state`, the user's slot 1). Alphonse stands
against the sky at the top left. A copy of him hung in the sky above the map,
and his colours ran along those rows to the right, under the map. Present
since units were drawn from their own sprites, with either fill;
`KOL_PERSP_NO_SPRITES=1` did not show it.
- The warp's backdrop (the sky, and under the map each row's last sky
  colour) was built from the scene before the lifted unit pixels got their
  ground. Behind Alphonse the ground is sky, so those pixels counted as sky
  and the backdrop copied his colours. The units' atlas copy and ground now
  come first, before anything reads the scene.
- One row still carried the map's dark outline, which the game drew under
  his hair. Outline pixels within 3 px of placed map move with the map; the
  rule took only BG0/BG1 tops, and there the top was his sprite. A lifted
  pixel now counts as the layer under it (the scene's own codes, second).
- CG at rest, lowered and diagonal: the sky rows around him are the sky
  colour up to the map. Both invariants unchanged.

**Open.** The Thor's cost is not measured.

Reported on the Thor (`states/CH_menu_hand.state`, the user's slot 1): the
hand of the Attack/Cancel box was misplaced and also moved with the

**It moved with a unit under the perspective.** The hand is OAM 0, 16x8,

gave it to that unit (whose atlas square grew to 21 wide), and the box rule
then made its pixels the unit's, drawn under the unit's own sprite. Over

### Performance pass on the Thor (2026-09-28, evening)

The user reported heat and fan noise near the limit. The measurement was the
user's snowfield battle, `states/CI_thor_snow_perf.state`: guest thread 97.7%
of a core, on the prime core pinned at 3.19 GHz, and the committed build had
dropped to 56.7 fps. That was the most power per unit of work the SoC has.

**How it was measured.** The app is debuggable, so the Thor profiles with no
rebuild:
- `run-as com.koldecomp.game simpleperf record -g`, symbolised on the Mac
  with the unstripped `libmain.so`;
- `simpleperf stat` on the guest thread for **cycles per frame**. CPU% alone
  misled: the old build read 97.5% before AND after a real 6% saving,
  because it was dropping frames.

On the Mac the benchmark was the runtime's frame-phase CSV
(`GBARECOMP_FRAME_PHASE`, 480x270, perspective + DoF): guest/present
microseconds per frame, reproducible to 0.03 ms.

**Result** (all byte-identical: both invariants, plus present dumps of 6
states at 2 stick positions each):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| guest cycles per frame (Thor) | 48.8 M | 39.2 M |
| guest thread (Thor) | 97.7% | 82.6% |
| whole process (Thor) | 1.23 cores | 1.09 cores |
| fps (Thor) | 56.7-59.3 | 59.5-59.8 |
| work per frame (Mac) | 14.1 ms | 12.3 ms |

**What changed.**
- gbarecomp `gba_ppu.cpp`, the wide compositor:
  - a candidate is one u64 (key in the high half);
  - the per-row arrays are plain data, filled over `out_w`: six arrays
    default-constructed at full width were 5-9% of the frame;
  - `submit`/`resolve` are always inlined, and the pillarbox test is
    decided per row;
  - columns the row provider drops, and whole empty tiles, are skipped;
  - the HUD layers return before asking the row provider for rows they
    never draw, and ask it only for the clipped columns;
  - the scene's colour is copied from the frame's where the two stacks
    match.
- gbarecomp `host_window.cpp`:
  - the frame texture is uploaded only when something draws it
    (`frame_texture()`); the warp never did, and SDL converted RGB24 on
    the CPU each frame;
  - the warp's uv are converted once;
  - `warp_xy` is built only when the window pass uses it;
  - the backdrop is uploaded as BGR888.
- gbarecomp `host_platform.cpp`: **on Android the frame pacer sleeps.** Its
  1.2 ms `yield()` tail was ~7% of the guest thread once the thread had
  slack, spent on `sched_yield` and clock reads.
- KoL:
  - the OBJ attribute providers are memoised per OAM entry per frame
    (`kol::obj_attr_new_frame()`): the renderer asked all 128 entries on
    every scanline;
  - the warp's outline candidates are precomputed;
  - the focus loop keeps its reads in locals.

**Tried and dropped.**
- Reusing the warp mesh across frames: geometry and camera were identical
  in 3-44 frames of 700, since the reference height eases every frame.
- A per-tile fast path for opaque BG tiles: no gain.

**Left, by share of the Thor's guest thread:**
- **Emulation, 27%.** KoL's mainline task loop (the scheduler at
  `0x08000768`, spinning to VBlank) is 34% of guest cycles, about 1.5 ms a
  frame. Eliding it changes guest timing and needs recompiler eligibility
  work: the user's call.
- The compositor, 21%.
- The warp mesh, 16%, plus its two workers.
- `build_scene` 6%, focus 4%.

The prime core started to drop its clock at the end. To move off it
altogether, the thread probably needs to be under ~50% of an X3 core.

### The present pipeline: the warp and the focus a frame behind (2026-10-01)

Reported: with everything on at 480x270 (perspective, depth of field 1.5,
full-tile occlusion, Side Sun shadows, torchlight, HQ sound) the game is not
at full speed on the Thor: the music says so. The user's slot 1 (`EL`, then
`EM`: the castle map with some fifteen units on screen) read, with the user
playing, by `thor_stat.sh` / `thor_fps.sh`:

| | first reading | the state the user found worse |
|---|---|---|
| fps | 56.0 | 50.6 |
| guest-thread cycles a frame | 43.3 M | 47.6 M |
| guest thread, of a core | 97% | 95% |
| its cycle rate | 2.5 GHz | 2.5 GHz |
| GPU busy | 24% | 24% |

The guest thread is saturated (it sits on the prime core; the clock just is
not 3.19 GHz under that heat), and `simpleperf record` on it says where the
frame goes: the present-time work 47% (the warp provider 20%, the scene
build 15%, the focus map 4%, uploads and the swap the rest), the wide
compositor 26%, emulation 27%. The scene build had doubled its share since
the 09-28 pass: the lighting. On the Mac the three lighting effects cost
3 ms together and nothing one at a time (the terrain pass runs for any of
them); the warp's hottest single line was the index `push_back`.

**The fix is structural: the present-time providers run on a worker
thread, one frame behind.** Present N draws what the providers made of frame
N-1 (the mesh, the retouched scene, the blur map) while the worker builds
frame N, so the guest thread pays only the copies and the GL draw. The
picture is the same, one present later (16 ms, which the turn-based game
does not feel).

- gbarecomp (`host_window.cpp`): a `WarpJob` holds everything the providers
  are given, copied (the frame, its layer map, the scene and its layer map,
  the provider pointers and the blur settings as they were), and their
  answers. `present_job` joins the worker, draws the previous job
  (`warp_draw`, the old draw_warp over a job), then captures this frame and
  starts the worker on it (`warp_compute`: the warp, then the focus over
  the scene the mesh samples, or over the frame when the warp declined).
  The order matters: the mesh points into the provider's own buffers, which
  the next call overwrites, so a job starts only after the last picture is
  drawn. `g_present_pipeline` (runtime.h; `GBARECOMP_PRESENT_PIPELINE=0` to
  run inline as before) and `g_present_capture_hook`.
- KoL (`kol_focus.cpp`): the present path read live guest memory and the
  PPU's latched records; a frame later the guest has moved on. So
  `kol::present_capture()` (the hook, on the guest thread at present) copies
  all of EWRAM and IWRAM, the latched OAM, OBJ tiles and palette, the scene
  under sprites and its own layer codes, the blend registers, BG0's scroll,
  the frame hook's scroll and serial, the view, the excluded layers, the
  perspective's state and the camera (`kol::perspective_capture`: the combat
  camera's ease and the look). The present path reads only the capture.
  The guest-state queries at the end of the file (`cursor_on_map`...) serve
  the sheet and the sound too: on the present path (`kol::PresentScope`, a
  thread-local flag set by the providers) they answer from the capture,
  elsewhere from live memory. The reference height (`g_yref`) is written by
  the warp and read by the overscan rows on the guest thread: atomic now.
  The scene's own layer codes went by pointer identity with the latched
  scene layers; a copy has no identity, so it goes by size (without
  overscan the scene's layer map is the frame's own).
- About 2 MB is copied a frame (0.2-0.3 ms); the worker uses the row pool
  as before.

**Verified.** Both render invariants unchanged (240 `66e13ab2`, anchor-off
