### The worker's work cut: the terrain pass cached, the index build (2026-10-01, later)

Asked for (the worker option chosen): less work on the present worker, for
heat, byte-identical. The Thor profile of the worker ("present", with the
row-pool workers): the scene build 30%, the warp 55% (its row passes
included), the focus 7%. By line: the mesh index build's `push_back` (4%),
the `keep_row` division (4%, left alone: an exact division cannot be
replaced), the occlusion reach's `getenv` guard asked per pixel (1.4%), and
the terrain pass's lines.

- **The terrain pass is kept across frames** (`PassCache`, kol_focus.cpp).
  Everything the pass reads is hashed: the view and the camera, the grid's
  4 KB, the map's record table, the lighting strengths and reach, the sun,
  the shadow map's key, and the torchlight's flags. The same key twice means
  the camera is still: the pass's arrays (places, heights, covered, kind,
  the cell and face of each pixel, the torchlight's world coordinates, the
  occlusion) are kept, and from the third frame restored instead of
  rasterising every cell again. A scrolling frame pays nothing (no copy
  until a key repeats). `KOL_PASS_CACHE=0` turns it off;
  `KOL_PASS_CACHE_CHECK=1` runs the pass anyway and compares every array
  with what the cache restored, counting mismatches to stderr.
- **The index build writes through a pointer** into a buffer that keeps its
  size (`IdxPart`), bounded by six indices per corner column of a run.
- **`ao_reach()` is read once a frame**, not per pixel.

**Verified.** Both invariants unchanged. The new binary against the one
before it, both pipelined, presents 61-65 byte for byte: `EM`, `B_rictor`,
`CI_thor_snow_perf`, `BK_tree_glass_cage`, and `EM` with the stick and the
combat camera. The cache's self-check over 400 frames on `EM`, `BL`, `CI`,
`B_rictor`, `BK`: 1800 hit frames, 0 mismatches.

**Cost (Mac, the worker's own clock: `[present-pipeline]` at the end of a
GBARECOMP_FRAME_PHASE run):** a job 5.28 -> 4.17 ms on `EM`, 5.10 -> 4.07
on the snowfield (-21%); the guest thread unchanged.

**On the Thor** (installed 23:22, the user playing; `simpleperf stat`
per thread over 10 s at 59.5 fps): the guest thread 30.6 M cycles a frame
(unchanged, as meant), the worker 14.6 M and its two pool threads 3.8 M
each, 22.2 M in all against about 33 M before this pass; the worker's
share of the process's samples 51% -> 41%, the scene build 30% -> 12% of
it. GPU 27% -> 13% and the SoC 69-86 -> 58-82 degrees, though the scene
may not have been the same. 59.8 fps, no long frames.

**Found on the way, open: the Mac's software renderer is not
deterministic on `BL_enemy_turn`.** Comparing the new binary with the old
on that state failed about one run in six; then the old binary against
itself too, in the direct path as well, with or without the row pool, with
or without the column trim: 45 pixels along the map's outer outline, sky
where the outline is, two variants, the same variant for runs minutes
apart. Chased with `KOL_PERSP_HASH=1` (the capture, the scene build's
arrays, each pool pass, the backdrop, flat, atlas and indices) and
`GBARECOMP_WARP_HASH=1` (every buffer the draw uploads, the window xy, uv
and indices; `=2` reads the renderer back after each pass): in 12 loaded
runs with 2 outlying pictures, every hashed buffer was identical in all
12. So the divergence is in SDL's software triangle rasterisation or its
readback on the Mac, which the Thor (GLES) never runs. Recipe: scratchpad
`det14.sh` (CPU hogs, 12 runs, dumps at present 61). Compare pictures on
still states only until this is understood.

### The wide compositor's work cut (2026-10-05)

Asked to look into it (the compositor, 35% of the guest thread on the
Thor, kept on the TODO list since 10-01), then approved the
single-thread route. All of it is in gbarecomp's `render_scanline_wide`
(`gba_ppu.cpp`); the pictures are the same byte for byte.

**Where its time went** (macOS `sample`, `EM`, 480x270, every effect on, so
570x302 composed with the overscan): the background pixel loop 60%, the
row's last loop (blend, three pictures out) 17%, sprites 10%. No hot spot:
~12 cycles per layer pixel, spread over the whole loop.

**What changed.**
- *One stack instead of four per drawn pixel.* Every pixel a layer drew was
  inserted into four two-deep stacks (the frame, the scene, the ground
  under sprites, behind BG1), and three were mostly thrown away: the last
  two are read only where the scene's top is a sprite or BG1. A
  background's key is the same along a row, so a background pixel is now
  its colour in the layer's own row and one bit in `bg_mask`; sprites keep
  one two-deep stack. The row's last loop builds each pixel's top two from
  a 16-entry table (the front two layers for each set present) and merges
  the sprites in: the frame's, the scene's only where a left-out layer is
  present, the other two only where they are read. The native-screen
  overlay (another game's; KoL publishes none) keeps its rule: over every
  background, under every sprite.
- *A tile's columns together.* The loop did the whole per-pixel sequence
  (row provider, window, remap, margin test, cache key) for each column,
  and stepped over a tile whole only when it was empty. Now the first
  column of a tile does it, and the columns after it that sample the same
  tile (not remapped, same side of the margin boundary, no per-pixel Y
  provider on the layer) only pass their own two gates, the row provider's
  drop and the window. The length of that run is computed, not scanned,
  unless the row has a remapped column.
- A 16-colour tile row is decoded from one 32-bit read; a candidate is a
  per-row constant OR its colour; the front two are read without a branch
  (the backdrop and the empty slot are table entries with a row of zeros
  for colour: the branch on "is there a second layer" missed at every edge
  in the art); a row the provider mostly drops (the HUD layers) runs from
  its first kept column to its last.

**Measured on the Mac** (frame-phase CSV, medians of 700 frames, two runs
each, alternating builds):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| guest phase, `EM` | 7.87 ms | 6.72 ms |
| guest phase, `CI_thor_snow_perf` | 7.77 ms | 6.69 ms |
| compositor with its providers (`sample`, 8 s) | 1175 samples | 805 |

About 31% off the compositor, 1.1 ms a frame. Step by step on `EM`: the
stacks 7.87 -> 7.60, the tile runs 7.19, the run length and candidate
constants 6.79, the rest 6.72. **Not measured on the Thor yet.**

**Checked.** `GBARECOMP_COMPOSE_HASH=<path>` (new, kept) writes a line per
latched frame hashing everything the compositor wrote: the composed frame,
its layer codes, the scene, the ground under it, the scene's codes. Against
a build of the old compositor with the same hash: 600 frames of ten states
(EM, B_rictor, CI, S_move_highlight, AT_status_sheet, AS_scroll_flash,
AF_world_map, AG_title_return, BL_enemy_turn, EW_newgame_dialogue), each
with every effect on at 480x270 and plain at 284: all 20 identical. Both
invariants (240 `66e13ab2`, anchor-off 284 `9054c456`, centre 0/160).
`GBARECOMP_WS_TILE_CACHE_CHECK=1` and `KOL_BGX_ROW_CHECK=1` pass and hash
the same. The overlay path, which KoL never runs, with a made-up 64x64
overlay patched into both builds for the test: identical on four states.

**What did not work.** Finding a row's first and last kept column in the
same pass as the remap flag (one loop with a branch in it) cost 0.4 ms a
frame: it replaced a loop the compiler had vectorised, 690,000 iterations a
frame. Two scans that stop at the first kept column do it for nothing.

**Trap: windowed runs in parallel.** With several windowed (dummy video)
runs at once, `BL_enemy_turn` and once `CI_thor_snow_perf` gave other
compose hashes, on the old build as on the new: two whole frames differ
and the under buffer after them, and the number of latched frames changes.
One at a time, four runs of each build agreed every time. So what the
compositor is given depends on timing there (not looked into; it may bear
on the BL item above, though that one had identical buffers). Windowed
comparisons run one at a time.

**Left in the compositor:** the last loop (40% of what remains: ~16 cycles
a pixel for up to three pictures and two code maps), the tile's first
column (21%), sprites (13%, still texel by texel), and KoL's
`anchored_x_row` for the HUD layers (~2% of the thread; HUD anchoring, not
touched). The other route, rows composed on worker threads, was not taken:
KoL's providers read live guest memory and keep caches.

**On the Thor (2026-10-06, the user playing `EM`; APK of 10-05 23:50,
every effect on).** `simpleperf stat` on the guest thread, two 10 s
windows: 19.14 and 19.15 G cycles at 59.8 fps, **32.0 M cycles a frame**
(10-01: 30.6 M). A `simpleperf record` of the thread (8 s, 22,775
samples) puts `render_scanline_wide` and its lambdas at **28.3%** of it,
~9.1 M cycles a frame, against 35% of 30.4 M (~10.6 M) on 10-01: about
**15% less on the Thor** (31% on the Mac). The thread as a whole grew
~3 M a frame elsewhere, from what was added since 10-01 (not split out:
no A/B on the device). The rest of the thread: the runtime loop (yield
check, tick, dispatch, trace) 23.7%, KoL's row providers 5.9% (HUD
anchoring `anchored_x_row` 1.7%), bus and DMA 5.2%, the warp's draw call
2.9%; libc 5.4%, the GL driver 4.8%.

**`unw_getcontext` at 2.6% of the thread was the PLT.** Nothing unwinds:
there is no `throw` or backtrace in either tree. `unw_getcontext` is the
last named symbol in `.text`, and `.plt` follows it with no symbols, so the
symbolizer gave it every stub's samples (`report.py` calls the same samples
`@plt`). `libmain.so` is a shared library, and by default its own exported
functions are called through PLT stubs as if another library could replace
them: 25,023 stubs, every call from the recompiled code into the runtime
(`runtime_tick@plt` 0.61% of the thread, `runtime_should_yield@plt` 0.26%,
`irq_pending` 0.21%, `runtime_mem_cycles` 0.20%, the flag helpers, bus
reads, 0.23% to other generated functions): ~0.8 M cycles a frame, plus
what the extra jumps cost the branch predictor. The desktop build is an
executable and never had them. Fix: `-Wl,-Bsymbolic` on `main` in
`android/app/jni/CMakeLists.txt`; calls are direct `bl`s now, `.plt` is
304 entries (libc, libc++, SDL), `SDL_main` is still exported. Nothing
interposes: SDLActivity only `dlsym`s `SDL_main`, and overlays reach the
runtime through `GbaOverlayCallbacks`. To find PLT samples in a profile,
check whether an address lies in `.plt` (`llvm-readelf -S`) before
believing the symbol.

### Sprite pieces go by the order the game draws them (2026-09-28)

Three reports, one rule. KoL emits unit sprites **front to back** (by x + z +
y), each unit's pieces together. That is not slot order: slots are call
order. `claim_unit_sprites` now follows it:

- **The cockatrice and the white dragon split under the stick**
  (`states/CJ_cockatrice_split.state`). A monster's lower half also lies in
  the frame of the unit a cell in front, and "nearest column, then the front
  one" gave it that unit. An entry that fits several frames now goes on with
  the unit of the entry before it, when that unit is one of its own. Else it
  goes to the frontmost of its units not in front of that one, and only
  then, as before, nearest column then front.
- **The cursor's white chevrons moved over the purple dragon in front**
  (`states/CK_chevrons_ice.state`). They are the grid cursor's corner
  pieces: 8x8s, priority 1, sorted in among the units by the cursor's
  depth, so units took them. An 8x8 within the cursor slot's own screen
  place (its slot in the guest list, 9 rows above to 8 below) belongs to no
  unit. The existing cursor code then lays them on the cell's face.
- **The command menu was embedded in the units' sprites**
  (`states/CL_menu_embedded.state`). Its boxes and icons are priority 1 and
  come before the unit run. Two icons went to the units they lay over, and
  the selected Attack icon and its label were hidden entirely. The unit run
  is the longest front-to-back sequence of claimed entries. Everything before
  or after it is interface: flat, and on top.
- Under interface, the warp's scene now takes the ground the game drew there
  (`latched_scene_under`) instead of the colour to its left. That fill had
  carried a wing's dark grey across the menu, which showed as streaks past
  the menu's end when the camera leaned.

`KOL_OAM_DEBUG=1` lists every plain OAM entry: its owner, the units whose
frame it fits, and whether it was made interface.

### The spell menu's icon drawn over by a unit (2026-09-29)

Reported on the Thor: the cursor on the spell option had merged into
the sprite behind it (`states/CP_spell_hand_merged.state`,
Ivanna's command menu on Spell/Special). With the perspective on, the
highlighted staff icon (OAM 5, semi-transparent) showed pieces of the unit
standing behind the menu instead. Flat it was right.

**Cause.** The run of unit entries (previous section) started at OAM 0, the
menu's hand. It is drawn first and lies in Ivanna's frame, so it was claimed
as hers. The menu's text and icons after it (OAM 1-8, which fit no unit)
then fell inside the run and were never interface. Her texels under the
highlighted icon were rebuilt over it.

**Fix.** A unit's parts are emitted together. So an end of the run that is
cut off from the next member by entries that fit no unit is trimmed off,
repeatedly at both ends. OAM 0 is released, and OAM 1-8 are now outside the
run and interface.

**Verified.** At 480x270 with the perspective and anchoring on, `CP` changes
and its icon matches the flat render. These are byte-identical to before:
`CL_menu_embedded`, `CH_menu_hand`, `CJ_cockatrice_split`,
`CF_ghosts_overlap`, `CK_chevrons_ice`, `BK_tree_glass_cage` and
`BV_attack_confirm`. Both render invariants are unchanged.

Reported: the action menu stuck to Rictor on some frames, perhaps because

OAM 5 fits none but touches it, so the part join gave it to him too. The
two then started the units' run, cut off from his own parts (OAM 16-17) by
the raindrops (OAM 7-15, in no frame). The run already drops a first member
cut off like that ("The spell menu's hand"), but it tested only the gap
after the FIRST member: here the empty gap between the two icons. On the
good frames a raindrop fell in another unit's frame (unit 6 or 8) and the

frame. So it came and went with the rain, not with his animation.

**Fix** (kol_focus, the run): the cut test is applied to a GROUP at the
run's start too, the members of one unit consecutive in OAM, when that
unit's parts come again after the gap and interface is drawn just before
the group. A unit's parts are emitted together, never split by interface.

### Whose sprite is whose: the game's tile blocks (2026-10-20)

Reported again (the user's slot 2, `states/IG_slot2_menu_sticks_anim.state`,
A): the action menu stuck to units behind it during animations again; the
user asked why it keeps recurring and for a permanent fix.

**Why it kept happening.** The sprite claim decided which unit an OAM entry
belongs to by geometry: an entry lying in a unit's 32x32 frame on its feet
is the unit's, with rules on top for ties (draw order, the run pass, part
join, the run's group cut, blobs, sky units, ...). The command menu's icons
are ordinary priority-1 sprites (tiles `0x1D7`, `0x1DB`, `0x1DF`, `0x1EF`)
drawn just under the units, so whenever a unit's frame reaches them (IG: the
unit above the Item icon, as its idle frame dips; 103 of 450 frames), one
of those rules hands an icon to the unit, and its card carries the icon off
with the perspective and shades it. Each fix before (CL, CH, FH, HY) closed
one way geometry gets it wrong; the next animation, map or menu position
found another. FH's own case was still wrong on 449 of 450 frames of its
state, and raindrops (`0x165`) went to units in HY, IB, BW, HM.

**The game's own answer.** A unit's frames are drawn from a fixed block of
16 OBJ tiles: its actor's slot in the game's sprite pool (map object `+0x08`;
the pool at `[0x02026F08] + 0x2020`, `0x3C8` bytes a slot). Found in the ROM
(a subagent's trace): the pool's VRAM callback `0x08059000` (installed by
the battle setup `0x080592A0` through `0x08013374`), in its fixed-slot mode,
puts slot i (0-15) at `0x06010000 + i * 0x200`, i.e. tiles `i * 0x10` to
`+0x0F`; the slot routine `0x0805A130` turns that address into a base tile
(`(vram - 0x06010000) / 32`), and the OAM builder `0x03005758` adds each
piece's own offset (`+0`, `+4` for the two 16x16 halves; a monster's 32x32 is
the whole 16). The battle makes each object with its actor, both the first
free slot, so the slot is the object's index on all 1143 objects in
`states/`. Other modes: a ring over tiles `0x200-0x2FF` and slots 16-25 at
`0x06012000` (the scene actors drawn from tiles of their own), BG VRAM.

**The rule now** (`claim_unit_sprites`, a last pass over the frames'
answer):
- an entry in a battle unit's block (not at priority 0, which is the
  interface's, except a spell's bodies; not a blob) is that unit's;
- a unit whose frames are in its block this frame owns nothing outside it,
  except while an attack or a spell plays, when effects and the GUARD
  letters over it go with it on purpose;
- a scene actor with tiles of its own (the boat's flag and door, the
  sailors, the town's archers) and the bags keep the frames' answer, the
  only one there is.
`KOL_NO_TILE_OWNERS=1` is the frames' answer alone.

**Checked.** First the rule against the old claim's every owned entry over
26 sprite states (BO, CJ, CF, CQ, CP, CL, CH, CK, CB, BL, EM, B_rictor, DE,
CN, BW, DM, AB, HY, IB, FF, FH, HM, GY, HP, GD, IG), 450 frames each: no entry
below tile `0x100` was ever owned by a unit other than its block's (the
geometry got those right), and every disagreement was a unit owning a tile
outside its block. Then the ownership A/B (`KOL_OAM_DEBUG` owners, old vs
new, 300 frames): 18 states identical; the rest differ only by menu icons
released (IG 134, FH 299), raindrops released (HY 103, IB 19, BW 6, HM 6),
END's tiles released (IG 2), and unit parts given to their own unit (IB 4:
a walking unit's body went to Rictor for 2 frames; HM 1, HP 1). IG on
screen: the menu stays put and the unit above it whole. Both invariants
(66e13ab2 / 9054c456).

Open: the run, part-join and group-cut rules still run first; with this
pass they matter only for scene actors and bags, and could be retired for
battle units later.

**A menu icon among the units' entries (2026-11-02).** With the cursor
on Attack, the Standby icon flashed and part of it was taken by
the dragon (states/thor/0087, map 16, the command menu beside the
griffin). The icons were priority 1 here, not 0; the run released the
ones outside the units' span of entries (#1-#6), but Standby (#7, tile
0x1EF at 136,104) lay among them, under the griffin's lower left part
(#22), owned by no unit and not released, so its pixels kept the box's
answer: the griffin's place. It stood with the griffin's card, and as the
griffin bobbed its claw came over the icon's corner (15 versions of the
icon over 60 pictures). Now (`OamClaim::menu_icons_free`, last): an entry
from the menu's tiles (0x1D7-0x203) that no unit owns by its tile block is
released, interface. The icon stays whole over the claw (3 versions over
60 pictures, differing only above its frame). The 52 check renders and
both invariants unchanged. `KOL_MENU_ICONS_BOXED=1`: as before.
### A bag on the map came apart (2026-09-29)

Same save (`CP`): the bag between Radam and Elrik was partly
treated as interface. Under the stick, half of it was missing or
smeared.

**Cause.** Every sprite pixel starts as interface. Only pixels in a unit's
16x32 box, or claimed by a unit's entries, are cleared. The bag is not a
unit: it is not in the map object list, and its two 16x16s (OAM 19/20) fit
no unit's frame. So it stayed interface (flat, filled under), except for the
columns a neighbouring unit's box happened to cover. In the mesh view the
bag kept its colours, and a strip of it was interface in the layer dump.

**Where the game keeps it.** A sprite slot of its own:
- routine `0x0805AD9D` (`kBagSlotFn`), owner `0x0202A26C` (not a map
  object);
- world 496,40,304, with the slot's Y 8 below the object's as for units;
- screen 152,84, which is the bag's feet.

EWRAM `0x02034E50` also holds 496,48,304, but it is not used.

**Fix** (`kol_focus.cpp`, `claim_unit_sprites`).
- Bag slots follow the units in the array as "props" (up to 8, deduplicated
  by place).
- A prop is a candidate only for an entry that no unit's frame takes. The
  slot list keeps stale entries, and this way a stale bag slot can never
  take a unit's part, and without a sprite of its own it changes nothing.
- A claimed bag then goes through everything a unit does: the draw-order
  run, its depth, and the sprite atlas. It is drawn whole and upright at
  its place.

**Then: the bag stuck to Ivanna** (`states/CQ_bag_stuck_ivanna.state`).
Ivanna moved to a cell in front of the bag. The bag's lower half (OAM 19)
then lay in her frame as well. Since a bag only took entries no unit fits,
it went to her and moved with her under the stick. A bag that drew something
(it is the only fit of some entry, here OAM 18) now also competes for the
entries a unit fits. The draw-order rules settle those:
- OAM 19 adjoins OAM 18 and goes to the bag;
- Ivanna's own OAM 12, on exactly the same 16x16, adjoins her OAM 13 and
  stays hers.

A stale bag slot still never competes, because it is nobody's only fit.

### A shared corner sheared the ice (2026-09-28)

Reported from `CK_chevrons_ice` (cursor down 5, then the stick): ice beside
a raised block looked higher at the bottom than at the top, and a smeared
band sat by the cursor. The heights were right: every pixel of that plain is
height 2. Painting the scene by kind with depth-parity stripes showed
contours that were not parallel (the user saw it first). Every corner was
placed correctly, and with merging turned off the band vanished.

**Cause.** The nearer surface places a corner the two share (`front()`), and
a surface's edge runs diagonally: the raised block started at column 287 on
row 178, 285 on row 179, and 283 on row 180. So row 179's displaced corner
lay inside row 178's merged piece, and the zipper fanned from far along that
piece (column 151) to it. That sheared the strip, 7 px across 135 columns.

**Fix, in `keep_row`.**
- A corner row also breaks where the pixel rows beyond its two neighbours
  are cut (j-2 and j+1), so both edges of a strip have corners at every
  nearby boundary.
- A forced corner is fit-tested like any other; when it does not fit, the
  piece also ends at the corner before.

Corners are still chosen once per row and shared by both strips, so there
are no T-junctions. `KOL_PERSP_HOLES=1` on five states at three stick
positions shows no gap inside the map: 15-33 single pixels move on its
outline against the sky. Cost: +0.13 ms a frame on the Mac.

### The cursor's hand pulled the ground out at the bottom of its bob (2026-09-28)

Reported with the stick held bottom-left (`states/CM_hand_distorts.state`):
the hand cursor distorting the terrain, everywhere, and only while the
bobbing hand is low. Rendered across the bob (frames 60-88), a grey sheet of
ground reached out from the hand from frame 68 on. At 60-64, with the hand
high, there was none.

**Cause.** At the bottom of its bob the hand is within 32 rows of the feet of
the unit on the cursor's cell, i.e. inside that unit's box. The box gives
sprite pixels the unit's place, upright at its depth. The hand's pixels
became floating interface, and the ground filled in under them kept that
place: a patch of ground standing up at the unit's depth among ground lying
at its own, and the mesh stretched between them.

**Fix.**
- Under every interface pixel (the hand, a menu) the scene is ground, so it
  now takes the ground's own place: the terrain's `g_under_*`, saved before
  the units' boxes and claims.
- The warp fills under the floating hand from `latched_scene_under` as
  well, not from the run to its left.
- Whether a cursor pixel lies on the cell (a corner piece) or floats (the
  hand) is decided by the OAM entry that drew it (`g_cursor_piece`), not by
  its row. The row test is kept only when the latched OAM is missing.
- The command menu (CL) also lost a white wedge by its right end: the same
  cause.

Both invariants and every PPU frame are byte-identical; only present-time
geometry changed.

## The blinking unit, half transparent (2026-09-27)

In battle preparation the unit on a deployment square blinked. At the user's
request it is now drawn every frame at half opacity (chosen from a mockup at
65/50/35%, `shots/transparent_unit/`). The game does the drawing itself.

**How the blink works.** Every frame `0x080676EC(ctx)` flips bit `0x40` of
byte `+0x17` of the unit's record (`[[ctx+0x40]+4]`). The map's draw list
(`0x0805A77C`) takes an object only while that bit is set. Found by watching
the unit's sprite in the shadow OAM (`0x03000010`), then which objects the
draw loop took per frame (the function-entry hook), then the bit.

**The game's own transparency.** Object flag `0x100` (u16 at `+0x78`) makes
the sprite builder give every part OBJ mode 1 (`0x0805A702`, descriptor `+8`,
into attr0 at `0x030059B4`). Mode 1 blends only with BLDCNT's second targets,
by BLDALPHA, and battle preparation sets neither (`0000` / `0010`). The game
keeps copies of the display registers at `0x03000DD0` (DISPCNT) onward and
copies them to the hardware: BLDCNT at `0x03000E1A`, BLDALPHA at `0x03000E1C`.

**Two reviewed hooks** (`src/kol_ghost.cpp`, `game.toml`), both declining:
- at the flip: clear the bit so the flip always sets it, set the object's
  `0x100`, and, while the game blends nothing (BLDCNT's effect and first
  targets both 0), make BG0-3 and the backdrop second targets at 8/8.
- at the draw list: once the flip has stopped running, put back what was
  changed, where it still holds our value.

Verified on `BT_persp_crazy`: the unit's two sprites are mode 1 on every frame
and drawn at half opacity, with and without the perspective. Pressing A
(`GBARECOMP_INPUT_REPLAY`) ends the blink, the hook logs that it put things
back, and the frame after is byte-identical to the game without the hooks.
Both render invariants are unchanged. `KOL_NO_GHOST=1` keeps the blink.

Also found on the way: the emitter's sprite slots (`0x03004150`) are handed
out in call order, so a slot is not tied to one sprite across frames.

## Depth of field as lens discs (2026-09-26)

The user said the depth of field looked greasy, as if smeared on the screen.
It was the layered blur: the sharp frame crossfaded over 1/2, 1/4 and 1/8-size
copies, enlarged smoothly. That gives a double image plus a structureless
haze, not defocus. It is now a GPU shader in gbarecomp (`disc::` in
`host_window.cpp`). Each window pixel averages a disc of its OWN radius (48
taps on a golden-angle spiral), and a neighbour counts only as far as ITS disc
reaches (min of the two radii). So an in-focus unit does not bleed onto the
blurred ground behind it, and bright taps weigh a little more, as highlights
do through a lens. The per-pixel amount is the same `focus_provider` blur as
before.

- **Strength**: BACK, then Options, then "Depth of field strength". The
  choices are Subtle 1.0, Medium 1.5 (default), Strong 2.0 and Very strong
  2.5. The value is the disc radius, in frame pixels, of the most distant
  terrain, persisted as `dof_radius=`. `KOL_DOF_RADIUS` overrides it (0 = the
  layered blur). The user picked 1.5 from a mockup comparing the layered blur
  with discs of 1.0 and 1.75 (`shots/dof_mockup/`, gitignored, built by
  `tools/mockup/disc.c`).
- **With the perspective**, the picture and its blur map both go through the
  mesh into window-sized targets, and the disc pass reads those, so the blur
  moves with the picture.
- **Needs a GL renderer** (opengles2 on the Thor, opengl on a desktop with
  `SDL_RENDER_DRIVER=opengl`). With Metal (the Mac's default) the layered blur
  draws, at 0.5, or 0.35 with the perspective.
- **Cost**: GPU 27% busy on the Thor. The layered blur's ~2 ms of CPU work per
  frame is gone. The guest thread is the same 87%, at 58-59.5 fps.

Traps paid for, all in `host_window.cpp` comments:
- **SDL2's renderer has no custom shaders**, so the pass is raw GL. SDL's
  queue is flushed first, and the GL state SDL relies on is saved and put
  back around the one draw.
- **Desktop GL draws nothing unless generic attribute 0 carries the
  position** (compatibility rule). On GLES2 the pass uses slots 6 and 7,
  because SDL uses 0-4 there.
- **SDL does not reliably expose the GL texture behind a streaming texture.**
  On desktop GL the frame and the blur map returned the SAME id, and the
  picture came out as the blur map. The inputs are copied into render targets
  first.
- **On GLES2 SDL stores an RGB888 texture with red and blue swapped** and
  swaps them in its own shaders. The sky came out orange. The targets are
  BGR888, which is GL's own byte order.
- Measuring fps with a busy-wait loop on the device between samples dropped
  the game to 42 fps. Sleep instead: push `tools/thor_fps.sh` and
  `tools/thor_cpu.sh` to `/data/local/tmp` and run them there.

Open: where a blurred part of the map meets the sky, its outline stays
crisper than a lens would give. The sky has its own blur, but the min rule
keeps the two apart.

## Debug: win the battle (2026-09-29)

Options > Debug > **Instant Win** (`debug_auto_win`, off by default; it was
"R3 Wins Battle" until 2026-10-06, see the end of this section). With it on,
every battle is won at its first unit's turn, with no button.
`src/kol_auto_win.cpp`; `KOL_NO_AUTO_WIN=1` leaves the hooks out.

**How the game decides a battle.** Story variable `0xB4` picks one of five
outcome routines, dispatched by `0x08020E30`:

| `0xB4` | Routine | Seen in |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `0x08020230` | `A*`-`Z_` (38 states) |
| 1 | `0x08020AB4` | `BQ`-`BW`, `CH` |
| 2 | `0x0801FEA8` | `BK`-`BM`, `BX`, `CF`-`CT` |
| 3 | `0x0801FF74` | |
| 4 | `0x08020004` | |

- Every one of them asks `0x0801FBAC` whether the enemy side is out: all
  eight enemy records (battle slots 8-15) empty, fallen or gone. Nothing
  else calls it.
- A reviewed `[[mod_function_hook]]` on it answers 1 once, after R3. The
  routine then declares the win, and the game's own victory follows.
- In `CO`, R3 then Ivanna's attack on Mulinne: "Congratulations!", bonus
  money 200 Goth, war trophy "Mirror of the Gods", then the world map.

**When it happens: at the next defeated unit.** The outcome is checked only
after a unit falls: the battle task's states `0x14` -> `0x2F` (the check,
result at task `+0x259`) -> `0x31` (acts on it). The task is `0x0202A5B0`,
its state byte `+0x27E`. A move, Standby, an attack that does not kill and
the enemy's turn never reach it (`S_move_highlight`: Standby, then a whole
enemy phase with an attack, and no check). In single play `0x08021378` lets
only event 6 through. The link-play path `0x08021248` is gated on
`0x020012E0`.

- The request is answered once, then dropped. It is also dropped on a state
  load and in the next battle preparation, so it never carries into another
  battle. Each battle needs its own R3.
- While a request waits, the second screen shows "auto-win" in amber in its
  top-left corner, over the band above the sheet (`kol::auto_win_pending`,
  pushed to `SecondScreen.setAutoWin` when it changes). Seen on the Thor
  after an R3.
- Winning at the moment of R3 would mean pushing the battle task into
  `0x2F`/`0x31` from outside, with its two return stacks (`+0x26D`/`+0x26E`
  for `+0x26C`, `+0x27F`/`+0x280` for `+0x27E`). Not done.

**Checked:** both render invariants unchanged. Without a request, `CO`'s
kill gives the same frame at 700 as the build before the hook.
`KOL_AUTO_WIN_AT=<n>` asks for the win n frames into a headless run, and
`KOL_AUTO_WIN_ANY=1` skips the setting.

**Instant Win (2026-10-06).** The user: no R3, win at once when the option
is on. The battle task is `0x08060E54(task)`, a 69-way jump table on
`+0x27E` (table `0x08060E84`), every case ending at the shared epilogue
`0x08063756`. Before `0x14` the game pushes, at `0x0806250C`-`0x0806256A`,
two (sub-state, state) pairs on the task's return stacks, `(sub, 0x31)` then
`(sub, 0x30)` (sub-states `+0x26E[+0x26D++]` from `+0x26C`, states
`+0x280[+0x27F++]`); `0x14` sets `0x2F`; `0x2F` (`0x0806296C`) runs the
outcome routine through `0x080211D0(6)`, stores the result at `+0x259` and
pops `0x30`, which pops `0x31`; with a result, `0x31` (`0x08062AD4`) pushes
`0x3B`, calls `0x0811831C` (the battle's end) and goes to `0x00`. A unit's
turn starts at state `0x00` (the enemy turn's cycle in `BL`: `... 40 04 00
08 02 07 ...`).

A second reviewed hook, on `0x08060E54`'s entry (`game.toml`), with the
setting on and the task `0x0202A5B0` at `0x00`: pushes the same two pairs,
sets `0x2F`, starts the answer for `0x0801FBAC`, and declines, so the task
runs the game's own check at once. Once a battle (again after the next
preparation or a state load). Routine 2 (`0x0801FEA8`) returns 5 on "the
enemy side is out". `BL_enemy_turn`, the setting on: the next turn start
goes `00 2F 30 31 00 3B`, the units fade, "Congratulations!", 200 Goth, the
world map (Naja). With it off, both render invariants unchanged.

**Not every battle can be won so (FR, the user's slot 1, map 54).** On the
Thor the first unit's turn ended and the battle went on. The battle's
routine is 0 (`0x08020230`, story variable `0xB4` at `0x020012E0`): it
declares nothing while an enemy carries the flag at `+0x1E` bit `0x80`
(`0x0801F95C(1)`, most likely the leader): such a battle ends by its own
script when that unit falls. And a declared "all enemies out" is not the
result by itself: in `0x08020CE4(6)` the dispatcher maps code 5 to 2
(`0x08020FE0`), and then the map's victory script runs (event 3,
`0x0802105C(3, 1)`), whose return is the result `0x080211D0` gives the task.
On BL it wins; on FR, with the leader's gate answered "none" too, it
returned 0. Forcing the result to 2 was tried: the story battle faded to
black and stopped presenting. Both were removed.

What stays: with no result the game ends the unit's action (`0x31` ->
`0x3B`); the hook puts the task back to `0x00` instead and logs "this
battle's outcome routine (n) declared nothing; the turn goes on". On FR the
battle then plays on normally. Winning a leader battle would mean making
its units fall through the game's own death path (the task's fallen list at
`+0x1D4`, states `0x32`-`0x37`), not done.

**On the way: the hooks past 32 were never installed.** gbarecomp's
registry held 32 (`kMaxFunctionHooks`); Fast Loading's 13 made 37 declared,
and every hook registered after the 32nd failed: this one, the options
menu's sound, the second screen's game-options hook (SoundMain), the opening
scenes' raster hook (scene_strip). From the Fast Loading build (Thor, 14:59)
until this fix. The registry holds 128 now and logs a refusal ("REFUSED: the
registry is full").

  the camera.

  - this one: 51 pillars;
  - the rainy coast (`S_move_highlight`, `B_rictor`, ...): row 11, the strip
    of sea along the front edge, at height 2 with one cell at 5. It now
    moves with the map as well.

  perspective and the stick on. Both render invariants are unchanged.

## Perspective: streaks in the sky while the camera moves (2026-09-29)

Reported on the Thor on every map, set up in `states/CW_sky_streaks.state`:
press Up. For the few frames the camera scrolls, the sky right of the map
shows horizontal streaks in the map's colours.

**Cause: the scene was a scroll step ahead of the picture.**
- The scene rebuild (`kol_focus.cpp`) finds the map's camera by votes in
  BG0's own coordinates, then subtracts BG0's scroll. It took that scroll
  from the frame hook's live registers.
- The game writes the next frame's scroll in its VBlank handler, before
  the hook runs. So while scrolling, the scroll was one step ahead of the
  latched picture being presented. Up scrolls 4 px across and 2 rows down
  per frame here.
- The map's diagonal right edge then went unplaced by up to 30 px. The
  perspective left those pixels as backdrop, and the backdrop carried them
  along their rows under the moving map: the streaks.
- Confirmed by a throwaway run with the previous frame's scroll: no
  unplaced strip, no streaks.

**Fix.** gbarecomp's PPU latches BG0's scroll with the frame
(`GbaPpu::latched_bg0_scroll`, the last scanline's). The rebuild turns its
votes into the picture's camera with it. The votes themselves keep the live
scroll, which pairs with the sprite slot list they come from.
`KOL_PERSP_LIVE_SCROLL=1` restores the old reading.

**Checked:**
- `CW` with Up, perspective and depth of field on: no streaks on any frame
  of the move.
- Before the move the picture is identical. After it, an eased difference
  fades (3547 px at +10 frames, 110 at +74), and at frame 400 the picture is
  identical.
- `CN` and `BK` are byte-identical. Both render invariants are unchanged.

This is probably also the open "camera lags a scroll step for about 4 pan
frames on `BL_enemy_turn`". Not checked.

Tool: gbarecomp's `GBARECOMP_PRESENT_DUMP_COUNT=N` dumps N presents from
`_AT`, with a `%ld` in the path for the present number.

## Perspective: the church, modelled from its art (2026-09-29)

**Removed 2026-10-13.** The user tried the church (map 3; state GI = their
slot 3, view mode) with the editor's roof and box tools instead (it worked, and the user had the
church-specific code removed), so the model described below is
gone from kol_focus (~290 lines), with its switch `KOL_PERSP_NO_BUILDINGS`.
The church is the grid's cells (a stepped roof, the steeple a block) until
roofs and boxes are drawn on it. The cells' owners and faces, which the
switch also governed and the other passes read (water, pedestals, the
light), are now always built, as they were by default. Byte-identical on
GI (model off), DF and BL_enemy_turn (perspective and light, 40 presents).
This section is kept as the record of what was tried.


Asked on the Thor, `states/DA_church_roof.state` (slot 3), with
`states/DB_unit_on_roof.state` (a unit on the ridge, behind the steeple) to
measure against. The user called the church an important set-piece:
exceptions for it are welcome.

**The grid is where units walk, not the drawn shape.** Across the church it
reads 14, 17, 17, 17, 14, and 23 for the steeple, on ground of 8-10 (terrain
types `0x0D`-`0x12`, `0x0F`). The art laid over those steps bulged along the
ridge and blunted the steeple under the right stick. Overlaying outlines at
candidate heights on the flat frame gave the drawn shape:

| Part | Grid | Drawn | Rule used |
|---|---|---|---|
| ridge | 17 | 17 (the unit's feet are on it) | the highest cells' height, at their middle |
| eaves, at the outer wall | 14 over their cell | 11 | halfway between the eave cells and the ground beside the wall |
| steeple, stone top | 23 | 20 | the ridge + 3 |
| steeple, point | 23 | 24 | the tower's grid height + 1 |

The steeple's two rules are measured on this church only.

**The model** (`build_scene_now`, after the terrain pass).
- **Roof.** Two planes meeting at the ridge, which runs along the axis the
  heights do not change along. A plane stays a plane under the
  perspective, so the roof's edges stay straight.
- **Steeple.** A stone shaft up to its stone top, then a four-sided cap to
  its point.
- **Placing a pixel.** Each pixel goes where the ray through it meets its
  surface, solved exactly. A fixed-point walk diverged on the steep roof:
  6 steps over 80 units.
- **Pixels that change surface:**
  - An outer-wall pixel above the roof shows the roof beyond, since a
    gable end is drawn as a triangle.
  - On the side whose slope faces away, everything is the front gable wall
    and its outline.
  - The cap is claimed by its outline, overhang included (3 units), not by
    cell.
  - Sky inside the grid's blocks is sky, taken from the layer under
    sprites too: the unit by the steeple has sky under its head.
- **Unchanged:** the outer walls and the shaft stay upright, so the church
  keeps its full perspective. The terrain pass records which cell and face
  drew each pixel (`g_cell_owner`, `g_face`).

**Which cells.** The same types are walls elsewhere: castle walls (`AB`),
the ruins' border (`CU`), the fortress (`AU`), blocks on `BY` and `BP`.
Those are level with the terrain beside them. A connected group is a
building only when it stands free, its lowest cell at least 4 over the
highest cell around it. Only the church does, across the local states.

**Tried first, rejected:**
- The whole church as one cut-out. It kept its shape but did not recede
  (it looked uncanny on the Thor).
- Its BG1 half as a cut-out. It tore along the BG0/BG1 seam.
- A smooth height field over the grid. It still bulged: the grid is not the
  roof's shape.
- A gable through the eave cells' middles (grid 14). The pitch was too
  shallow, and it still bent.

**Checked:**
- `DA` at rest, with the stick left-down, right-down and up, and leaning
  both ways: straight roof, pointed steeple, no fringe or stray lines. The
  mesh view shows the roof as one plane and the cap as a pyramid.
- `DB`: the unit stays on the ridge, and the cap is whole beside it.
- `AB`, `AU`, `BQ`, `BY`, `CX` and `CH` are byte-identical with and
  without the rule. Both render invariants are unchanged.

`KOL_PERSP_NO_BUILDINGS=1` turned it off (removed with the model, 2026-10-13).

## Perspective: drawn heights (2026-10-02)

**The report** (`states/EN_slot1_gargoyle_pit`, the user's slot 1, the
castle): a gargoyle statue stands in a pool, and with the perspective the
pool read wrong. The 14 cells around the statue (x 7-9, z 6-10, the statue
at 8,8) are terrain record 77 and store height 11, their rim's height. The
art draws the water much lower. The mesh laid the pit's painted inner walls
and the statue's column flat on a floor at 11.

**The mechanism.** A table of drawn heights that differ from the stored
ones (`kDrawnCells`, `kDrawnRecords` in `kol_focus.cpp`), resolved once a
frame into a per-cell array that `cell_height` in `build_scene_now`
answers from first. Everything built on `cell_height` follows: the
terrain pass (walls down to the drawn floor), the shadow map, the
occlusion, the torchlight's visibility, and the units' cast shadows
(`g_cast_heights`). The game, the cursor and the units keep the game's
own heights; the prop and building rules keep reading the stored grid
(`raw_cell`). Two keys:
- **map + cells**, with the record the cells must hold (-1 any): one spot.
  The map is the u16 at `0x02029D40`, the number the map header parser
  `0x08021B68` reads (header = `0x085C55C4 + 2 + (n - 1) * 0x6A`; +0x1C is
  the record table's offset from `0x085E630C`). The castle is map 55.
- **record**, as steps added to the stored height: a shape that is the
  same on every map. Empty so far.

The terrain pass's cache key (`PassCache`) mixes a hash of the resolved
overrides: the grid's bytes do not name the map. The shadow and torchlight
keys follow from the heights they hash already.

**Why not by record 77.** Its terrain record is all zeros except +1 = 0x7F
(no unit enters): the game's plain blocked cell. It is in the record
tables of ten maps (53, 55, 56, 85-88, 109-111), next to fire pots and
statues on 109-111. Of the 147 local states only the castle's (EL, EM, EN)
have it on the grid, in these 14 cells. The other maps' grids are not
stored raw or as BIOS LZ77 in ROM, so they were not read. Map 55's header
fields (art, tables) are shared with no other map number.

**Measured, not guessed** (memory `kol-measure-drawn-shape`): outlines of
the pit's footprint at candidate heights over the flat 240x160 frame,
camera kx 88, ky 48 (`shots/drawn_heights/measure_flat_outlines_11_8_7.png`).
- The back-right inner wall (Z = 192) is the reliable one: its top edge lands
  on the rim's 11 within a quarter step. Its foot, per column, reads
  6.9-7.4 to solid water and 7.25-7.75 to where the wall's dither into the
  water starts. The tip where that foot meets the front rim's top edge is at
  x = 64 + 8h: seen at 119-120, h = 7.0.
- The back-left inner wall reads a step high from top to bottom (its top at
  12 against the rim's 11). Corrected for that, 7.5-8.6.
- Heights are whole steps (8 px), so the entry is **7**. A throwaway build
  at 8 was rendered beside it; the user chose 7.

**Checked:**
- Both render invariants (240 `66e13ab2`, anchor-off 284 `9054c456`,
  centre-240 0/160); EN's faithful frame unchanged.
- With perspective and the lighting on (AO 0.5, Side Sun, torchlight), at
  rest and with `KOL_PERSP_LOOK=1,1`: B_rictor, CI, BK, EI, EJ, EK and EN
  with `KOL_PERSP_NO_DRAWN_HEIGHTS=1` give the old binary's picture byte for
  byte. Runs in parallel, or with `KOL_PERSP_HASH`, can come out a few
  pixels off for either binary (the Mac software renderer's
  nondeterminism, see the present pipeline); every CPU-side hash matched,
  and unloaded reruns matched 3 of 3.
- `KOL_PASS_CACHE_CHECK=1` on EN, at rest and with the stick: 360 checked
  frames, 0 mismatched.
- `KOL_PERSP_HOLES=1` on EN first showed a new 13 px hairline gap (row 148,
  across the back-right inner wall near its tip) beside an older 12 px one
  at row 100. Neither is in the mesh: dumped and rasterised in float, it has
  no interior hole. Both were SDL's software renderer (the Mac only) drawing

  (gbarecomp ENHANCEMENTS.md, "SDL's software renderer dropped mesh
  triangles"); fixed there. Now EN has no gap with the stick and none inside

The cursor keeps the game's place: on a pit cell it would sit at the
game's 11, over the drawn water (not looked at; in EN it is on the statue).

## Perspective: lifted props, what they hid (2026-10-02, experimental)

Asked: the camera deforming the picture as it moves is acceptable, but where
what lies behind is known, mostly behind layer BG1, it should be shown
there.

The warp is one sheet: where a near surface meets a far one they share the
corners on the line, and a camera move stretches whatever lies there. Where
BG1 covers BG0 the game drew both, so the hidden part exists. Options >
Lifted Props (off by default; `lift_props` in enhancements.cfg,
`KOL_PERSP_LIFT_PROPS=1` on the desktop) does for BG1 props (the cut-outs and
the trees' rule) what was done for units:
- the compositor records what lies behind each BG1 pixel (gbarecomp
  `g_ppu_scene_under_bg1`, ENHANCEMENTS.md §6);
- the scene keeps the terrain pass's own place under each prop pixel (taken
  before the props claim theirs) and the lighting there (the props' "own
  colour" reset is skipped for those pixels);
- `lift_prop_pixels` cuts each prop (grouped by its place) into 32-px atlas
  squares, marked as props; the warp draws them as upright cards at the
  prop's place, sorted in depth just past their cell's front corner (not
  after the whole map as units are), and puts the colour behind BG1 at the
  scene's pixels there;
- a lifted pixel loses every shared corner to a pixel that is not lifted,
  and is a run of its own sorted before its prop's card: by row place the
  ground behind the castle's statue (the pool's back wall, 548 against the
  card's 544) took the vase's corners and drew over the gargoyle's body;
- a prop's square pads its texels a pixel round with their colours.
Only BG1 can be lifted: what an object hides on its own layer was never
drawn, so that keeps the stretch. The statue's vase (BG0) stays in the
sheet at the card's place.

**BG1 terrain too** (the user, the same evening: not only the statues and
trees; other BG1 tiles have tiles behind them too, such as the wall behind
the wall pillars on the statue field, which shows when BG1 is
hidden). On the castle BG1 is the round towers' and
pillars' outer strips, the door frame's edges and stair corners
(`shots/lifted_props/ER_where_bg1_is.png`, 8281 px of the view), with the
wall drawn behind them on BG0. Terrain is a surface, not a card:
- the terrain pass keeps, per pixel, what it showed before a nearer cell
  drew over it (`g_back_*`, in the pass cache and its key while lifting);
- a BG1 pixel with BG0 under it, not a prop's, whose surface behind differs
  from its own (8 units of row place or height) is lifted onto a square of
  the scene's 32-px grid marked `surface`; the scene shows BG0 there at the
  surface behind;
- the warp places such a square's corners from its own pixels' places (the
  nearest touching one, as the scene's corners are placed), draws each pixel
  as a quad of its own sorted by its own depth, and gives its texels the
  terrain's occlusion;
- the blocks' draw order had a cap of 64 (`int order[64]`): a vector now.
On ER (the user's slot 1) 8119 px are lifted; where a pillar's edge smeared
into broad stripes under the stick, the wall behind shows.
Its own switch, asked for: Options > Lifted Walls (`lift_walls`,
`KOL_PERSP_LIFT_WALLS=1`) beside Lifted Props; either turns on the
compositor's colour behind BG1, Walls alone the pass's surface behind. Both
on is byte-identical to the single switch before; each alone lifts only its
part (ER: props 681 px, walls 8119 px).

The Mac's uv truncation (above) needed a second look: a quarter texel on
pushed the far edge of a one-texel quad into the next row (a square's empty
top row, black pixels down the lifted edges); the corners now move a
fiftieth of a texel toward their triangle's middle.

`KOL_PERSP_MESH_DUMP=<path>` writes the 40th present's mesh raw (xy, uv,
indices, scene texels, atlas) to trace a pixel offline to its triangle and
texel; it found both the seams and the corner and order traps above.

Found on the way, Mac only: SDL's software renderer truncates each uv to a
texel and the division put whole texels a hair under, so a square sampled
its neighbour's empty column: black seams (fixed in the host's fallback,
1-3% of the Mac's warped pixels change, KoL's stages hash identical).

Checked: both invariants; with the option off KoL's stages hash identical to
the previous build (EK, BK, EO); with it on `KOL_PASS_CACHE_CHECK=1` 0
mismatched (EK, EN) and the gap view counts no more gaps. Cost on the Mac's
present worker: EK (16 props) 3.1 -> 3.7 ms, EN 4.05 -> 4.37 ms, ER with
the terrain 3.6 -> 4.95 ms (each lifted terrain pixel its own quad: merging
them is the first saving); the compositor's extra candidates on the game
thread and the Thor not measured. Stills `shots/lifted_props/` (off / on, three stick positions;
EK zoomed, the statue zoomed). `KOL_PERSP_NO_DRAWN_HEIGHTS=1` draws the stored
heights. Report protocol for more: slot 1 with the cursor on the tile,
"this should be N steps lower / higher".

**Occlusion under them** (asked for AO under them, then for
both parts). Two parts:
- **Contact occlusion where a lifted prop stands** (`prop_contact_ao`, with
  Lifted Props and Ambient Occl. on), as units have under their feet. The
  ground at the prop's height darkens toward the prop's foot over 12 units,
  at most the occlusion's strength (0.5 at the default) times
  `(1 - d / 12)^0.7`. The foot is not a circle: the snowfield's firs stand
  on the BACK half of their cell (measured: on EK and BK every fir's lowest
  BG1 row is the row just above its cell's centre, and that row spans the
  cell's full width). So the foot is the cell, cut at the lowest row the
  prop's own pixels reach, and `d` is the distance from that foot. The
  ground behind a lifted prop (its `g_under_*` place) takes it too, which
  is where it shows once the camera moves. A prop's own pixels left in
  place (the statue's BG0 vase) do not. `KOL_PROP_AO_LEN` and
  `KOL_PROP_AO_MAX` change the length and strength for mockups.
  **Removed 2026-10-13**, replaced by props casting shadows (the user found the grounding AO on props never
  looked good and asked for shadows on them as on units;
  see "Props cast shadows" below).
- **The wall behind lifted BG1 terrain keeps its own occlusion.** Before,
  the scene at a lifted pillar edge showed BG0's wall with the occlusion
  and shadow the pass had worked out for the pillar in front, so a shaded
  pillar side left a dark band down the wall beside it when the stick moved
  the pillar off it. The pass now keeps the occlusion behind each pixel
  (`g_back_ao`, beside `g_back_*`, in the pass cache). On lifting, the
  scene's AO there becomes the back's, and the lifted texels take the
  front's (`ScenePixels::lift_ao`).
The pass cache's self-check now compares the back arrays too.

**Depth of field on lifted walls** (the user, on the Thor: something
had broken the depth of field). A lifted square's texels took one blur, from
the block's place. That is right for a unit or a prop card. A wall square
has no single place: its block carries its nearest pixel's row place and
height 0, which put every castle wall square at full blur (255 on all of
ET's) whatever the focus. Each texel of a wall square now blurs at its own
pixel's place, as the wall around it does (29-233 on ET). There is no GL
on a headless Mac, so this was checked by printing both values per square.
With the depth of field off nothing changes (ET lifted: identical).

Checked: both invariants (240 `66e13ab2`, anchor-off 284 `9054c456`,
centre-240 0/160). With both switches off the pictures are byte-identical
to the previous build on CI, BK, EI, EJ, EK and ER, at rest and under the
stick. With both on: `KOL_PASS_CACHE_CHECK=1` 0 mismatched (EK, ER, BK),
and the gap view's counts are unchanged (EK 1188 and BK 61, the map's far
edge; ER 0). Cost on the Mac's present worker with both on, stick held:

occlusion is worked out every frame, not cached. Stills

### Props cast shadows (2026-10-13)

Asked with the removal above: props now cast the sun's shadow as units do
(README "Units cast shadows"), with Shadows on, lifted or not
(`cast_prop_shadows`, called from `cast_unit_shadows`; `KOL_NO_PROP_SHADOWS=1`
leaves them out). A prop is the scene's prop pixels (claimed or spread,
upright) that touch and share one place (depth and height); it stands as a
card turned to face the sun at that place, across its pixels' middle column,
its foot the place's ground, its pixels the silhouette. A ground pixel is in
its shadow when the line from it toward the sun meets the card on a prop
pixel, with the units' soft edge (0.06) and the same rules: not on prop
pixels, not on a wall facing away from the sun, not where the terrain's or
an awning's shadow already is. Units' and props' shadows darken a pixel
once, by the stronger. Each prop's shadow is kept while the view, the sun,
the heights and its pixels stay the same.

**And they take the terrain's shadow, as units do** (asked the same night
for terrain shadow to fall on props as on units). Before, a
prop's own pixels kept the full light (EK: firs took the dark band of the
wall behind them), so a bush in the church's shadow stayed bright in it.
Now a prop is a card at its place, as a unit is: its foot at its place's
ground, a row up 2 units higher, and the rows below the terrain shade's
height there (or an awning's) darken by the shadow strength
(`card_shade_row`). Unlifted, per pixel through its light value (the
shade at its own column); lifted, through its atlas block's `shade_row` /
`shade_k`, which units already used (props had them at "never"), at the
block's middle column. Occlusion and torchlight still stay off props.
`KOL_NO_PROP_SHADE=1` keeps their full light. Checked on GJ: the bush in the
church's shadow darkens with the ground around it, those in the sun are
unchanged, lifted or not; DF byte-identical with both prop switches off;
both invariants hold.

**And they shade their own foot** (2026-10-14, asked for a darker
spot at the bottom of props, as if they shaded
themselves, then for it to reach a bit above where they touch the
ground). A prop's own pixels are `dark` darker from below the foot's row
(the prop's place's ground, `xz / 4 - y / 2` on the scene) up to `raise`
rows over it (4), then ease out (squared) to nothing `rows` rows higher
(`ScenePixels::prop_base_light`). (The first version left the rows at and
below the foot undarkened, against its own comment.) With Ambient Occl. on, in proportion to
its strength: defaults 10 rows and 0.5 at the default strength. Unlifted
through the pixels' light value (with the terrain's shadow), lifted
through the block's `foot_row` / `base_rows` / `base_dark` where
kol_perspective copies the prop's texels. `KOL_PROP_BASE_ROWS=<rows>` (0
off), `KOL_PROP_BASE_DARK=<0..1>` and `KOL_PROP_BASE_RAISE=<rows>` try
values. Stills in `shots/prop_base/` (GK at rest and lowered): `GK_rest`,
`GK_low` (off, A 10 rows 50%, B 16 rows 50%, C 10 rows 70%, before the
raise) and `GK_raise_rest`, `GK_raise_low` (raise 0, 4, 8 at A).

Then the user asked that the dark part not stop where the prop meets
the ground but keep fading out across the
tile it stands on. The ground carries the foot's shade: a round spot at
the prop's height, as dark as the prop's foot at its foot point (under its
pixels' middle column, at its place) and easing out (smoothstep) with the
distance from that point, to normal 16 sqrt 2 away (the tile's front
corner for a prop at the cell's middle). The props are found once
(`scene_props`, shared with the shadows). Checked the spot does not
compound on still frames (the terrain pass is cached): a patch in front of
a rock reads the same over 30 frames.

Then (the user, with a Thor crop of a bush: hard edges were left in
the shadows of all props, from the added shadow). Each effect
rendered alone against none of them (GK, `KOL_NO_PROP_SHADOWS=1`,
`KOL_PROP_BASE_ROWS=0`, `KOL_NO_PROP_SHADE=1`, set through `bash -c`: zsh
does not split a variable holding two of them) showed two causes:
- the tile's fade: a first version darkened only the prop's own tile, in

Two wrong turns, recorded: repainting the game's own slate blob under each

First version: props grouped by place alone. Two bushes on one diagonal at

Now touching pixels only.
Then touching pixels of one cell (2026-10-21, JD = the user's slot 3,

two pines side by side on a diagonal at one height (0,11 and 1,10) overlap,

Checked: JD before/after (`KOL_PROP_GROUP_BY_PLACE=1` reproduces the old

### Plants sway with the wind (2026-10-14)

Asked whether vegetation props could move slightly in
the wind. Options > Advanced > Plant Sway (`plant_sway`, on, in
Enhanced). It acts on lifted props only (Perspective + Lifted Props): a
lifted prop is its own card, placed vertex by vertex every frame, so the
sway is a sideways offset per vertex row in `warp_provider`. The foot stays;
a row `up` rows over the foot leans `2 px * min(1.5, up/32)^1.5`, so the
plant bends rather than slides. The wind is a slow swing (3.2 s, 0.65) with
a quicker gust (1.3 s, 0.35), both phased on world X + Z, so a gust reaches
the plants in turn.

Plants are the cells whose terrain record is in `kPlantRecords` (the tree
records and 42, the bushes of map 3 and the snowfield), filled per map in
`build_scene_now` (`g_plant_cell`); the block takes its cell from the
prop's middle column (`Block::plant`, `wind_x`/`wind_z`). Rocks, statues,
pots stay still. Cast shadows stay still too (cached; at 2 px it does not
show).

The strength is the user's pick between previews at 1.5 and 3 px
(`shots/prop_sway/`): 2. `KOL_PROP_SWAY=<px>` overrides it (0 = still).
Checked: BK with the setting on is byte-identical to `KOL_PROP_SWAY=2`,
and with `KOL_SETTINGS_OFF=plant_sway` the plants are still; both
invariants hold. Not measured on the Thor (a few multiplies per lifted
plant vertex).

## Roofs, set in the editor (2026-10-03)

Asked about houses like those on map 95, where some roof mesh
shapes should be triangular but were square, which broke the
lighting. Then, of two ways (measuring each house myself, or a roof tool in
the editor), the user chose the tool.

**Why they were square.** In the grid a house is a flat block (map 95: the
two houses at X 10-13, Z 6-9 and 13-16 stand at 9 everywhere on ground 3;
their cells are record 71, the church's obstacle record, with a strip of
walkable record 64 along the ridge and record 42 in front). Nothing in the
data gives the roof's slope; the old building model (the church) derives
its ridge from heights that step up, and these do not. So the slope comes
from the player.

**The tool** (Debug > Tile Info on, L2 held; `kol_tile_edit.cpp`):
- B marks a roof's first corner (the readout says so and the rectangle so
  far is tinted); B again on another cell makes the roof over the
  rectangle: one gable, its ridge along the longer side, the eave at the
  target's drawn height, the ridge three steps over it.
- On a roof, D-pad left / right picks the field up / down change: the
  cell's height, the eave, the ridge (half steps), the gables (how many
  prisms side by side, 1-8) or the axis (ridges along X or Z). A deletes
  the roof.
- The readout shows the roof (cells, axis, gables, eave, ridge) and the
  field; the roof's cells are tinted lighter, the target as before.
- Saved with the heights in drawn_heights.cfg: `roof map x0 z0 x1 z1 axis
  gables eave ridge` (half steps). A new roof replaces any it overlaps.
- Fixed the same night (the user: no L2 shortcut worked except
  up and down): in the scene viewer the filter hid A, B, Select and Start
  from the game before reading the pad itself, so L2 + B and L2 + A never
  fired (and left / right only act on a roof, which could not be made). The
  pad is read first now.
- **One-way slopes (asked for roof slopes, a lean-to).** A sixth
  field, SHAPE: gable (as before), or one slope per prism from the ridge
  height at one side to the eave at the other, falling toward + or -
  across the ridges' axis (the readout: "SLOPE DOWN TO +X"). Saved as an
  optional tenth number on the `roof` line (0, 1, 2); a line without it is
  a gable. Several prisms with one slope make a sawtooth; the vertical step
  between them is not modelled. Checked on EY: gable, +X and -X slopes in
  the mesh paint and the light; a gable roof identical to before the
  change; no roofs: both invariants, ER and EY identical.
- L2 + left and right did nothing: headless, through the new
  `KOL_TILE_EDIT_SCRIPT=<frame>:<keys>,...` (pad states fed to the
  editor's filter, as the host's poll does), L2 + B twice then L2 + right /
  left step the field (ridge -> gables -> axis; ridge -> eave). Off a roof
  they do nothing by design, and the readout had offered them everywhere:
  its hints now follow where the cursor is ("L2 + B TWICE MAKE A ROOF" off
  a roof, the field and left / right on one).
- **A peak at a corner (asked for a junction shape, a pyramid
  whose top goes to one corner instead of the
  centre).** SHAPE 3-6: the ridge height over one corner of the
  rectangle, falling to the eave along the two far sides (the larger of
  the two fractions of the way across), two slopes meeting on the
  diagonal and vertical sides at the peak: the piece where two ridges
  meet. The readout names the corner as it sits on screen: FRONT +X+Z,
  RIGHT +X-Z, BACK -X-Z, LEFT -X+Z. Gables and axis do not apply. Solved
  per plane on the ray like the gables. Checked on EY: the four corners in
  the mesh paint (the back peak shows both slopes meeting; the front one
  only its walls, both slopes falling away); both invariants.
- **The inverse, a valley (asked for the same inverted and concave,
  to join other parts).** SHAPE 7-10: the eave height at the chosen
  corner, rising to the ridge along the two far sides, the two slopes
  meeting in a concave crease on the diagonal: the inside corner where two
  ridges meet. The readout: LOW AT FRONT / RIGHT / BACK / LEFT. The same
  solver with the planes' sign flipped (base the eave). Checked on EY: the
  four in the mesh paint (low at front shows the V; low at back only its
  walls); both invariants.

**The model** (kol_focus, after the old building model). A house is its
footprint up to the roof; the roof is `gables` prisms side by side, each
falling from its ridge to the eave at its sides. Every map pixel in the
roof's screen box follows its ray (X = 2 row + hx + Y, Z = 2 row - hx + Y,
nearer as Y grows) to the first point inside: a near wall where the ray
enters the footprint at or under the roof there, else the first slope it
meets (solved exactly per half-prism; a slope steeper than the ray faces
away and is not met). That also claims the gable peaks the old block never
reached. The block's own pixels always take it; any other only where the
house is nearer. Slopes are placed as flat (the mesh paint shows their
bands slanting), walls upright. Light: the shadow map reads the roof's
height inside a roof (`roof_y`), so roofs cast gable-shaped shadows; a slope
facing away from the sun is in its own shadow; walls as before.

Checked: on map 95 (EY, in the viewer, a test roof over X 11-13, Z 13-15,
ridges along Z, 2 gables, eave 9, ridge 12) the block becomes two prisms
with triangular gable ends in the mesh paint and the light follows; with no
roofs: both invariants, ER, EK and EY identical with the perspective on and
off. The key handling cannot be driven headless (the replay writes keys
after the host's filter); `KOL_TILE_EDIT_FILE` loads roofs from a file.

**Holes in a roof with Lifted Walls (2026-10-04, FA = the user's slot 1,
map 6, Debug > perspective mesh on).** The roof showed its own art unpainted
in the mesh view, and in the normal view dark dots along its creases. The
house's art is BG1 there, and Lifted Walls lifts any BG1 pixel the terrain
pass drew over another surface (`g_back_*`): the roof's pixels went onto
cards, and the roof under them showed BG0's colour behind the art. A pixel
the roof model places now has no surface behind it, so it stays on the roof.
Cells of a house with no roof yet (FA: x 7-8 z 13, x 7 z 14-15; the other
house's x 4 z 8-10) are still lifted as wall cards, which the mesh view
never paints; in the normal view they are whole, still and at
`KOL_PERSP_LOOK=1,1` and `-1,-1`. Without lifting the picture is
unchanged; both invariants, pass cache check 0.

**Boxes: chimneys and dormers (2026-10-04, asked for the
chimneys, and the same for the roof windows,
FB = the user's slot 1, map 6, the cursor on a dormer).** The art draws a
chimney or a dormer on the roof's layer, so the roof model placed it on the
slope and the perspective sheared it into the roof. In the editor (Tile
Info, L2 held), **Select** puts a box on the target cell: a chimney to start
(3/8 of a cell square, flat, its top a step over the roof's ridge there).
On a cell with a box, Select switches the fields between the box and the
rest (the roof, the height); with the box's: left/right pick TOP, PEAK,
SIZE X, SIZE Z, SHIFT X, SHIFT Z, AXIS, up/down change it, A deletes the
box. Sizes and shifts are in eighths of a cell, heights in half steps; a
PEAK over the TOP puts a gable over the walls, its ridge along the AXIS (a
dormer on map 6's +X slope: ridge along X). Saved as `box map x z top peak
size_x size_z shift_x shift_z axis` lines in drawn_heights.cfg.

flat top or a gable slope (the highest point on the ray at or under the

the box is nearer than what the pixel shows. Lit like the roofs (slope
facing, walls facing, the shadow map); boxes stand in the shadow map (the
higher of roof and box) and their art is never lifted. Measured on FB's

21 4 5 0 -3 X` (fronts at X 280, 5/8 wide, walls to 9.5, gable to 10.5),

behind a dormer stretches where the mesh joins the box's top to the slope.
Without boxes the picture is byte-identical to before (FB, EK); both
invariants; pass cache check 0 with boxes; the present worker 6.6 ms a
frame with the sun moving over FB's roofs and boxes. The editor's keys
checked with `KOL_TILE_EDIT_SCRIPT` (Select adds, Right to PEAK, Up, A
deletes the box and leaves the roof).

**Shadowed wedges on sunlit gable ends (2026-10-04, map 6, seen on the
Thor; FB with the Thor's drawn_heights.cfg on the Mac).** Beside the door at
x 8 z 13, the +X gable ends of the roofs over x 8 z 12 and z 14 showed dark
triangles, on walls facing the sun. Shadows off, they went; boxes off, they
stayed. A roof wall placed on its own cell's pixels kept the terrain pass's
light ("walls as before"), but over the eave the terrain pass knows no wall:
it had drawn the cell's top or the house behind there, and lit the gable as
that surface, in the shadow of the door's block (height 10) or the roofs.
Now a wall of the roof's own cell over the eave is lit by the roof model
like any other roof wall (facing the sun, then the shadow map); up to the
eave nothing changes. On FB every change is a gable triangle (803 pixels:
the sunlit ones lose their wedges, a few on shaded faces move by a shade).
Without roofs the picture is byte-identical; both invariants.

**The chimney stretched the ground behind it (2026-10-04, map 6, the
stick held on the Thor).** Boxes took "nothing behind" like the roofs, so
under the stick the strip a chimney uncovers was the mesh stretched from
its edge to the terrace (a dark band down its right side; the crates left
dark trails). A dump of the under-BG1 buffer on FB showed what the game
keeps there: on this house only the upper roof and the chimney are BG1, and
BG0 under the chimney is the cobbled terrace and cliff behind it. So a box
pixel now records what it showed before the box claimed it (the terrain
pass's surface, its place and light) as the surface behind, as BG1 terrain
does, and Lifted Walls lifts it onto its own patch with BG0 at that surface.
A pixel a roof placed still has nothing behind (the house's own art; the
holes of FA), so dormers and the chimney's foot on the slope keep theirs.
Checked on FB with the Thor's drawn_heights.cfg at `KOL_PERSP_LOOK` 1,1 /
-1,-1 / 1,-1 / -1,1: the band and the trails are gone, the terrace opens
behind; at rest the chimney is nearer the game's flat frame (its right
outline back). Without boxes, or with Lifted Walls off: byte-identical. Pass
cache check 0; both invariants. Trap on the way: the lifted patches added an
atlas row, and the atlas sits under the scene in one texture
(gbarecomp `warp_atlas_h`), so on the Mac's software renderer one texel's
rounding moves all over the frame (~1700 scattered pixels); not the change.

**Then the roof's edge (the same night).** Along a roof's edges over the
ground beyond the house (the gable over the terrace, the back eave over the
grass) the stick drew teeth and navy wedges: the same stretch. FA's holes
came from roof pixels whose surface before the roof was the house itself;
these are not. A roof pixel now keeps what it showed before as its back when
that was ground beyond the house: not one of this roof's cells (`own`), not
another roof's pixel (`g_roofed`), and more than 16 units under the roof on
the pixel's ray. Everything inside the house keeps nothing behind, as
before. A box over such a pixel keeps the roof's back. Checked on FB and FA
at the four looks: the teeth and wedges are gone, the edges meet the
terrace and the grass cleanly, no holes in the roofs (FA's dormers and
creases as before). What opens there is BG0 as the game drew it, which
under map 6's gable edge still holds a few dots of the house's own outline
(seen at 1,-1). Without roofs, or with Lifted Walls off: byte-identical;
pass cache check 0; both invariants.

**Awnings: open roofs, and a pyramid (2026-10-05, asked for map 89's
kiosk to get a 3D element shaped like its awning, for shadows
and the rest, FC = the viewer on map 89, the cursor at X 7 Z 13).** The
kiosk's cloth, its posts, its counter and the fishmonger are all BG1 (with
Debug > hide BG1 they go; BG0 under them is the ground and the wall). Only
the two posts stood (props); the cloth lay on the ground and the wall
behind, and slid down them under the stick. Two additions to the roofs:

- **SHAPE: PYRAMID** (11): the ridge height over the middle of the
  rectangle, the eave on all four sides. Solved on the ray piece by piece
  between the middle lines and the diagonals, as the boxes' gables are.
- **OPEN: YES (AWNING)**, a seventh field (an eleventh number on the
  `roof` line; left out, a roof with walls). An open roof has no walls and
  owns no cell: a ray that comes in under its edge goes on to whatever
  stands under it (except within `kAwningSkirt`, 4 units, under the edge:
  the cloth's hem, upright). It takes only BG1 pixels, and keeps what the
  pixel showed before as the surface behind (as the boxes do), so with
  Lifted Walls the camera opens onto the ground under it, BG0 as the game
  drew it. Its posts cannot take its pixels as theirs (`g_awning`; a
  one-pixel column of cloth over the front post went with the post).
- **The cloth by its colours.** The fishmonger's head is drawn over the
  cloth's hem, on the same layer, inside the awning's outline: no shape
  tells them apart, and the first try lifted the top of the head onto the
  roof. A first pass over the roof's pixels collects the colours of those
  more than `kAwningSure` of the way up its slopes, where only the
  cloth can be; the second takes only pixels wearing one of them. (The
  head's dark outline shares the cloth's: a few of its pixels can still
  go. Without the scene's colours, the depth of field's own call, all are
  taken.)
- **The shadow.** The shadow map is one height per place (under it,
  shaded), which makes anything in it solid to the ground. An awning has
  its own pair per place, `g_canopy_lo` / `g_canopy_hi`: a point is in its
  shadow when its ray toward the sun is under the awning at one step and
  over it at another (it goes through the cloth). So the sun shines in
  under the edges, the shadow lies where the cloth's does (at 45 degrees,
  two cells from the kiosk's foot), units under it are shaded and their own
  shadows are not drawn into it. With an awning on the map every ray of the
  map runs its whole way (the early stop is for the one-height test); the
  map is still worked out only when the heights or the sun change. A point
  on the awning itself is not tested against the pairs (its slopes say
  which face away; tested, the map's 4-unit places striped the cloth).

- **No slope of its own in shadow (the Thor, the same day: a
  shadow on the left of the awning that did not move when
  the sun changed).** As on the roofs, a slope facing away from the sun was
  drawn in shadow. On the cloth that was its whole left half, dark at once
  with a straight edge along the model's ridge (not the fold the art
  draws), and unchanged until the sun passed 34 degrees: not a shadow that
  moves. I first said the art painted that side darker; it does not (with
  the light off the cloth is even; the darker left half in the pictures
  from before was the old light, the cloth lying on the wall behind). An
  awning's own pixels now take only the terrain's shadow.

- **Cut-outs in the awning (the Thor, the same day): a bite out
  of the cloth's lower-left edge under the stick.** I took it for the
  fishmonger's head (no cloth is drawn behind it) and tried twice to fill
  it: his pixels kept as the surface behind with the nearest cloth colour
  (a navy smear: the nearest colour was the outline, and the scene's mesh
  stretched round the island), then the fill in the cloth's own squares,
  drawn just before or after his pixels (painted over by the wall he lies
  on, which is at his depth). Both removed. The bite was the fit: laid
  over the flat frame as a solid mask (`KOL_AWNING_MASK`, not hatched as I
  first drew it), the model left a strip of cloth 2-4 px wide outside it
  along the front-left edge and at the peak, and those pixels stayed on
  the ground. So: an awning reaches `awning_overhang()` (4 units,
  `KOL_AWNING_OVERHANG`) past its cells on every side, as cloth does past
  its posts; the cloth's colours are learned from 0.15 of the way up
  (`kAwningSure`; at 0.35 the hem's own tan was not among them); the
  hanging edge is 4 units, not 8 (dark specks of the counter under it went
  with the cloth); and the kiosk's ridge is 14.

- **Part of the cloth is on BG0 (the Thor, the same day: still a
  cut-out, the stick held low: a triangle of wall in the hem left of the
  front post).** Logged per pixel, that patch of cloth (6 x 4 px beside the
  fishmonger's head) is not BG1: in the tiles where the fishmonger has BG1
  the game draws the cloth on BG0. An awning took BG1 only. Now a third
  pass takes BG0 pixels in a cloth colour that have, along their row within
  8 px, the cloth on one side and the cloth or a refused BG1 pixel (the
  fishmonger) on the other; without that test the wall under the hem, which
  wears the same tans, went too. They are lifted with the rest
  (`g_awning` 2; `lift_prop_pixels` takes them though nothing is recorded
  behind a BG0 pixel), the scene behind showing the nearest BG0 pixel that
  is not cloth (`g_under_fix`, laid over the under-BG1 picture in
  `g_under_patched`). Left in the scene's mesh at the awning's height they
  pulled the fishmonger beside them up into a streak. Before finding this I
  went looking for a darkening of the cloth the user described; there was
  none (every cloth pixel of the Thor's capture is the art's own colour):
  what is dark is the kiosk's inside, under the awning's shadow and the
  occlusion together.
- `KOL_AWNING_SKIRT`, `KOL_AWNING_SURE` and `KOL_AWNING_OVERHANG` set the
  three fitting numbers for a run.

Map 89's kiosk: `roof 89 6 15 7 16 X 1 20 28 11 1` (eave 10, ridge 14,
fitted on the flat frame with the mask, `shots/awning/FC_fit_mask*`). In the editor: L2 + B on two opposite corners, SHAPE one step
down from GABLE (PYRAMID), OPEN to YES, then the eave and the ridge.
`KOL_AWNING_MASK=<path>` writes the pixels the awnings took as a PGM, to
lay over the flat frame when fitting one.

Checked: stills at rest and at three looks, before and after
(`shots/awning/`): the tent stands on its posts, the head stays on the
fishmonger. Without an open roof the pictures are byte-identical to the
build before (map 89 with the Thor's 48 roofs and 25 boxes, at rest, under

beam), not the hidden half of the counter; other open shapes (a lean-to
over a shop front: SLOPE + OPEN) run the same code but none has been
