**A map's own sun (2026-10-05, asked to save the sun position set on
the Thor as the sun for the cutscene on map
89).** `kMapSuns` in kol_focus.cpp: a map number, the sun's height in
degrees and the direction toward it along the ground. While Options >
Shadows is on, a map in the table takes its sun from there whatever the
pick (the pick still says whether there are shadows, and their strength);
Debug > L2 Moves Sun moves it from there. Map 89: 18.5 degrees from (2,
-1), the last line the Thor logged (`sun: ... KOL_PERSP_SHADOW_ELEV=18.5
KOL_PERSP_SHADOW_DIR=0.894,-0.447`, 13:49). To add one: move the sun with
the stick, read that line with `adb logcat | grep "sun:"`, add a row.
Checked with `KOL_SHADOWS=<0..4>` (new: the Shadows pick for a desktop
run): map 89 under High Sun is byte-identical to an explicit 18.5 degrees
from (2, -1) and not to High Sun's own; the castle (EM) under High Sun is
unchanged.

**The Thor's edits, in the build (2026-10-05, asked to bring the Thor's
files into the code).** `tools/bake_drawn_heights.py <drawn_heights.cfg>`
writes `src/kol_drawn_baked.inc`, the file's lines (no comments, by map),
and kol_tile_edit loads that text when the device has no
drawn_heights.cfg of its own: a fresh install and every desktop run draw
with the heights, roofs and boxes set so far. First bake: 928 heights, 54
roofs, 51 boxes over maps 6, 89, 91, 92, 95, 97-102, 117, 118, pulled
about 14:00, and again at 14:15 once the user had set the kiosk's ridge
to 14 there (the only line that changed). A device's own file,
once there is one, is all there is: the first edit there saves the baked
lines with it, so a roof deleted in the editor stays deleted, and the
Thor, which has its file, is not changed by a bake. (Heights as
`kDrawnCells` rows, the first plan, would have left roofs and boxes with
no home and baked heights that the editor could not take back.) To bake
again: `adb exec-out "run-as com.koldecomp.game cat
files/drawn_heights.cfg" > f.cfg`, the tool, build.
`KOL_TILE_EDIT_FILE=/dev/null` runs with none; a path to a file runs with
that one. Checked: map 89 from the baked text is byte-identical to the
same run given the Thor's file; with none it differs; from a device with
no file, one edit saves all 1033 lines and the edit; both invariants (the
drawn heights touch only what is drawn at present time). Desktop stills
of those maps taken before this were drawn without the edits.

**A map's cut edge faded to the background (2026-10-05, asked for map
89, and likely other cutscene maps, to fade its border into the
background, the map being narrower than the view).** The straight cut is
where the guest's composed map runs out of tiles: on map 89 the art fills
array columns 35-75 and rows 37-84, and past that the guest draws nothing,
so the backdrop shows. The cut steps: the rows of the town's houses end
two tiles further right than the roofs above them. `map_source_extent`
reports which tiles of the array hold anything on BG0 or BG1 and where
hardware pixel 0 sits in the array; the capture keeps it, and the scene pass shifts it by the picture's own
latched BG0 scroll against the tick's (the frame hook's registers can lead
the presented picture by a frame while the camera moves). Every scene
pixel within `width` hardware pixels of the nearest pixel past the art
(Euclidean: a distance transform over the array's pixels, once per map,
then a lookup per frame) keeps
smoothstep(distance / width) of its colour and takes the rest from the
colour the backdrop shows on its row (the row's first backdrop pixel, or
the nearest row's). Applied after the light, in the warp and in the flat
light: the map's pixels, lifted props and walls (the awning) and units;
not the HUD or the interface. Because it is worked out in the scene, it
stays on the map under the stick.

`kEdgeFadeMaps` in kol_focus.cpp, {map, width}: map 89 at 32 (the user's
pick from 16, 32 and 48, `shots/edge_fade/map89_widths_0_16_32_48.png`).
`KOL_EDGE_FADE=<px>` fades any map for a run (0: none). Another map
(the castle, EM) is byte-identical with it forced off; both invariants.
The first version faded toward the bounding rectangle only, and on the
Thor the shorter rows below the roofs kept a hard edge all the way down.
The second faded each row at its own end and each column at its own:
the band jumped sideways at the step (the junction still looked
off). The distance bends round it
(`shots/edge_fade/map89_junction_distance_fade.png`). Worked out per frame
over the scene it cost 1.8 ms on the Mac at every camera move; in the
array's pixels it is the same picture byte for byte (two views) and is
worked out once. A battle map's
diamond would be faded all round, which is why it is a list of maps and
not a switch for all.

**Map 89's sky at dusk (2026-10-08, asked for the fade to the
background as before, but with a black/grey gradient
instead of blue, then for dusk colours, slightly
desaturated).** The fade still goes to the backdrop's colour on its
row; the backdrop itself is recoloured. The game's sky there is a
gradient by row, 8,66,255 at the top to 90,239,255 at the bottom
(brightness 70 to 187). `recolour_backdrop` (kol_perspective, first thing
in the flat and the warp providers, so the fade and the warp's sky fill
read it) sends every backdrop pixel (low nibble 5, no interface sprite)
through a ramp by its own brightness: the ramp's first colour at 64, its
last at 192, darker toward black below 64 (a screen fade), then pulls it
`desat` toward its own grey. A lookup table per frame. Ramps: grey (black
to 96) and dusk (30,26,58 indigo, 74,58,104, 150,96,120 mauve,
206,128,108 dusty rose, 230,166,120 peach). `kEdgeFadeMaps` rows are
{map, width, sky, desat}; map 89 `{89, 32, kSkyDusk, 0.35}`.
`KOL_SKY=<0 game, 1 grey, 2 dusk>` and `KOL_SKY_DESAT=<0..1>` override it
for a run; with the game's sky the picture is byte-identical to the build
before. Stills on FC at 384x216: grey 0/64/96/128
(`shots/edge_fade/map89_sky_grey_0_64_96_128.png`, 96 picked), then grey
and dusk at desat 0 / 0.35 / 0.6
(`shots/edge_fade/map89_sky_grey_dusk_0_35_60.png`). The ramp shows the
game's own colour steps (its gradient moves in 15-bit steps) as bands.
Only where the flat light or the perspective runs (as the edge fade); the
Original preset shows the game's blue. First I made the fade itself go to
black, then to dark grey, over the blue sky: a misreading, reverted.

**Dialog boxes had a halo (2026-10-05, the user saw what looked like a shadow on dialog
boxes, the intro's dialogue on map 89).** The light
(occlusion, shadows, torchlight) fell only on pixels whose top layer in
the frame was the map, and under a dialog box the frame's top is the box
(BG2/BG3): the map there stayed unlit. The warp draws the box flat and
moves the map against it, so 2-4 rows of that unlit map showed along the
box's bottom and left edges, a band of another brightness hugging the box
wherever the ground around it was shaded. `apply_lighting` now takes the
layer under a HUD layer as the pixel's own. Found by rendering the same
frame with BG2/BG3 hidden: the box changed 1,122 pixels outside itself,
now 0; the scene's data under the band was identical both ways, so it was
the light, not the terrain pass. `shots/dialog_box_halo_before_after.png`.

**Light through the castle's windows (2026-10-06, asked for the windows on
slot 2 to cast godrays following the sun position).**
FL = that slot 2: map 55, the castle, the two arched windows in the long
wall. A window (`kMapWindows`) is an opening in a wall facing +Z: the
wall's plane Z, its X span, sill and top Y, the top rounded; these two
were measured from the scene's world buffers (`KOL_FOCUS_DUMP` now also
writes `.wx/.wz/.y/.face`) on the glass: Z 32, X 327-349, Y 272-386 and
Z 64, X 519-541, Y 269-381. Two parts, both moving with the sun (Debug >
L2 Moves Sun too):

- *The patch:* a point the terrain pass drew whose ray toward the sun passes
  through a window, unblocked (marched every 4 units through the height
  grid), takes the sun back: warm, x(1 + 0.75 a) on the map's pixels.
- *The haze:* the beams on a 4-unit grid of the world, traced from the
  windows outward (rays 2 units apart across each opening and its soft
  edge, each marched away from the sun until the terrain stops it), fading
  over 160 units; the view direction is the same for every pixel (+1, +1,
  +1), so running sums along the grid's diagonals give each pixel's haze in
  one trilinear read; added over everything but the interface.

The user looked at four suns (`shots/godrays/sheet_suns_off_on.png`) and
picked the map's own, Side Sun (2, -1) at 30 degrees, where the light
runs almost along the wall and hugs it, at strength 1.5, haze 0.05: now
the default wherever Options > Shadows is on and the map has windows.
`KOL_GODRAYS=<strength>` (0 off), `_HAZE`, `_FADE`, `_TIME` (timings).
Without the torchlight it keeps the world buffers itself (`world_on`,
`world_dirty`; unchanged when it is off).

Cost (Mac, the present worker): the first mockup recomputed every frame,
46 ms. Now: nothing on a still frame (keyed on the terrain pass's key and
the sun; 3 computations in 300 frames, worker 4.09 ms against 4.10 off);
per frame while the camera moves, patch ~0.8 and haze ~0.7-1.4 ms; while
the sun moves, the beams again, 2.6-9 ms (more lit cells with the sun
behind the wall). Against the mockup: the map's sun the same, smoother
(no streaks); with the sun behind the wall the shafts end where their
rays land on the steps (the mockup's coarse per-cell check let light past
the step edges). Units are drawn after it: a unit in a beam is neither lit
nor veiled. Thor cost not measured.

**Then, from the Thor (same day):** the user set the castle's sun with
L2 and asked to keep it for this map, as for the intro's: `kMapSuns`
{55, 49.5 degrees, (-0.316, -0.949)}, from behind the long wall, read from
the Thor's `sun:` log line (the Low Sun pick's direction raised to 49.5).
Three reports, all fixed:

- *The left window's ray cut off unnaturally:* a straight vertical
  edge down from the window's left side. The beam grid starts at the
  window's own X (light from this sun moves +X), and a wall pixel left of
  it reads its haze from a point outside the grid, so it read nothing
  though its view line enters the beam further on. Such a point now moves
  on along its line by whole cells into the grid (the same diagonals and
  weights, so exact); the haze's left edge slants away as the beam goes
  forward. Found with a probe of the wall pixels along the window's row.
- *The light left units unlit:* the units' own pixels now take it,
  each a point on a card at the unit's place (as a lamp's light,
  `unit_window_light`, every frame, only units within the beams' bounds),
  the sun through a window on it and the haze in front of it, in the
  warp's atlas and in the flat path.
- *A cut-out of the hand pointer in the light* (seen once the stick
  moves the camera): the window light skipped interface pixels, and the
  ground the warp fills in under the floating hand's spot is one; it now
  takes the light as the shadows and occlusion do (`ground_under_iface`).
  A/B on FL with the stick held (`KOL_PERSP_LOOK=0.9,0`, sun 25 degrees):
  the hand-shaped gap in the haze is filled.

Cost: the units' pass every frame, worker mean 3.85 -> 4.21 ms on FL
(godrays off/on, still camera). With godrays off the picture is the same
as before except that map 55 now has its own sun.

**Then tamer and warmer (same day, asked for a little tamer and a little
more yellow/orange):** the user picked C from

for mockups.

**Then the castle's sun turned toward the side (same day, asked for it

**Holes in the light where walls are lifted (same day, FM = the user's
slot 1: cut-outs on the left pillar and on cell x15 z4).** Seen
in an exaggerated red render (`KOL_GODRAYS=3 KOL_GODRAYS_TINT=1,0.1,0.1`):

**After View List, lifting died and a prop blinked (2026-10-06, FN = the
user's slot 1: with the in-battle menu open, View List and back gave
a big stutter, then glitching
graphics).** Reproduced from FN with an input replay (A at +20, B at
+200; `GBARECOMP_INPUT_REPLAY` lines `frame,0xKEYINPUT`, from the state's
own frame, 459201), dumping presents and timing every frame.

- *The glitching:* after the return, every 9 presents a pair of frames
  lost the gargoyle and showed the scene unlifted. Not the godrays, the
  present pipeline or recompiled code (the same with `KOL_GODRAYS=0`,
  `GBARECOMP_PRESENT_PIPELINE=0`, `GBARECOMP_FORCE_INTERP=1`); gone with
  Lifted Props/Walls off. After View List the game keeps WIN1 and the OBJ
  window on (DISPCNT 0xDF40, was 0x1F40) while it darkens sprites 8/16
  for its menu with the effect off in those windows (WININ/WINOUT
  0x1F3F). `build_sprite_atlas` gave up on "brightness with windows" and
  returned before clearing `g_lift`: for the rest of the battle no unit
  came from the atlas and `lift_prop_pixels` ran against last frame's
  marks (0 walls lifted; a prop's sliver every 9 frames). Now `g_lift` is
  cleared first, a frame where the atlas gives up lifts nothing
  (`g_atlas_bailed`), and windows count only if they leave the effect off
  somewhere; then the units' texels (coloured from the palette) take the
  outside region's rule. FN: 422 of 422 frames lift, no bad frame; eight
  states at the Thor's settings byte-identical to before; both invariants.
- *The stutter* is the game's: it holds the faded unit list for 54 frames
  (459411-459464, the same picture every frame) while it rebuilds the map
  inside its VBlank handler, so no frame boundary reaches the host's
  present hook until it is done (207 ms of emulation on the Mac, then the
  pacer's 700 ms to keep time). The same with everything interpreted and
  with the watchdog off (`GBARECOMP_HANG_WATCHDOG=0`).

**A candle that lights the fortune teller and Alphonse (2026-10-05,
asked for a small glow on the candle on the table before the woman in
purple in state 1, lighting her and Alphonse).**
`states/FC_slot1_candle_fortune_teller.state` (map 89, the opening). The
stall (the table, the candle, the woman) is sprites: the torchlight, which
finds its torches among the terrain records, knows nothing of it. So:

place, the distance to the step that set its shadow height
(`g_shadow_dist`): the terrain that casts it. `shade_frac` gives a point's
share in shadow: the blur's radius is the rate x that distance (at most 16
units, half a cell); where the point and four around it at that radius
agree it is that, else a 5 x 5 average. Samples count only on cells as high
as the point's own (across a step one stands inside the block beside it:
the castle pit's lit wall went dark), and on a wall only along it. A mask
of the places near a shadow's edge on the ground (`g_shadow_edge`, built
with the map, grown by the largest blur) skips the sampling elsewhere: the
pass cost +2.1 ms per recompute on the Mac without it (the blur's width
taken from the map's longest distance covered everything), +0.35 ms with
the cap and mask; the pass is cached while the camera and sun are still.
Applied in the main terrain pass (tops and walls) and the round towers;
roofs, boxes and awnings keep the hard edge. The user picked 0.07, then 0.11, from
`shots/soft_shadows/terrain_FH_*` and `terrain_EM_*` (0 / 0.05 / 0.1 /
0.2). `KOL_TERRAIN_SOFT=<rate>`, 0 = hard. Both invariants; pass cache
check 0 with the sun turning. Thor cost not measured.

### Making the perspective cheaper (2026-10-26)

Asked for ways to optimise the perspective, with subagents to argue or
brainstorm allowed. Three read-only reviews (GPU offload,
CPU parallelism and caching, a skeptic on where the frame goes). The
skeptic's finding came first: the guest and the present worker took turns
(gbarecomp ENHANCEMENTS "The worker starts before the draw"), fixed there.
Then, on the Thor panning slot 3 at full wetness, the worker took 20-23 ms
and the music slowed with it: a late picture is now shown again instead of
holding the game (same section). On the worker:
- **The light's steps on the row pool** (`par_px` in kol_perspective: the
  occlusion, the lamps' light, the darkness, the torches' tint, the slime,
  the sun's bumps, the windows, the evening, the sunset; each a pixel at a
  time, split by rows). With `KOL_PERSP_THREADS=0` it is the old order, and
  the pictures are byte-identical to it on JP, JN, GT, FL, HO, BL. Mac:
  0.73 -> 0.34 ms (JP), 1.08 -> 0.50 (JN).
- **The wet pass works out a pixel's light only for a glint or running
  water** (three divisions a pixel); byte-identical.
- Next, from the reviews: the scene build (8-12 ms on the Thor while
  panning, serial: kol_focus never uses the row pool) - the terrain pass and
  the units' sun shadows shifted, not rebuilt, as the camera pans; the
  focus pass on the pool; the pool's wake-up; then the shading on the GPU.

### Map 102's props made cheaper (2026-10-26)

Asked to measure why this scene in particular is slow, suspecting the
many props, then to start with the props. On the Thor (JR = slot
3, map 102 as the rain starts) the worker took 23-25 ms, and 271-303 of
every 600 pictures were shown twice; the props were about 9-10 ms of it,
the reflections 5-6. On the Mac (JR, 2700 frames, `KOL_WORKER_TIME=1`,
the Thor's drawn heights) the props' sections, with sub-timers:

| Part | Before (ms) | After (ms) |
|---|---|---|
| BG1 shapes' flood fill and feet (`bg1.middles`) | 1.33 | 0.38 |
| Prop shadows and units' (`scene.sun_cast`) | 1.14 | 0.70 |
| The cards' texels (`af.blocks` in `warp.atlasfill`) | 0.87 | 0.37 |
| `warp.scene` in all | 5.98 | 4.62 |
| `warp.atlasfill` in all | 2.00 | 1.44 |

About 1.9 ms a picture less on the Mac. Every change leaves the pictures
byte for byte as they were: JR's 600 pictures from 1500 on (`85a910a1`,
the same before any of this), and 60 pictures each of HQ, HR (the flame
and smoke cards), BK, GN, IN and JP against the old switches; both
invariants hold.
- **The BG1 shapes' work cached** (`Bg1Cache`, kol_focus): on a map whose
  BG1 is props (kBg1PropMaps), each shape's flood fill and feet depend on
  the opaque map, the scene's layers, the cells' heights, the camera and
  the sun's way; keyed on all of them, kept once a key comes twice,
  replayed on a hit (the shape pixels' place, cell and shape, the pixels
  past the scene, the plant cells). It hits on a still camera (about half
  of JR's pictures). `KOL_BG1_CACHE=0` off; `KOL_BG1_CACHE_CHECK=1` works
  it out anyway and compares (JR: 1320 checked, 0 different).
- **A prop shadow that falls on nothing is kept too.** The prop shadow
  cache took an empty list for "not worked out", so every prop whose
  shadow lay on nothing (most of them in the rain) was cast again every
  picture: 78,837 casts over the run, 59,714 of them such. Now a
  `taken` flag marks a list handed on; 15,710 casts.
  `KOL_PROP_SHADOW_EMPTY_RECAST=1`: as before.
- **The cards' texels on the row pool**: each card has its own square in
  the atlas, so the light, wet look and shade of each are worked out apart,
  the effects' cards first, one after the other (their cache). Trap paid:
  a `static thread_local` the calling thread filled (the cards' fire
  light) is empty on the pool's threads; it is read through a pointer.
  `KOL_PERSP_THREADS=0`: one after the other, as before.
- Smaller: `scene_props` asks its hash map once per run of one shape's
  pixels (0.74 -> 0.65 ms for its two calls), and the round foot spot
  skips the square root well outside its reach.
- Left, each 0.2-0.4 ms on the Mac: `scene_props` runs twice (the foot
  spot, then the shadows; too much writes the props between them to share
  it safely), `lift_prop_pixels`' grouping, props and walls, the
  outline spread before the cards, the foot spot's loop.

On the Thor (the 16:20 APK, JR, the same stretch of the scene as the run
before): the worker 24.8 -> 19.8 ms a picture, the props 9.5 -> 6.7 ms,
pictures shown twice 271-314 -> 175-272 of 600. Still over 16.7: the wet
look 4-5.5 ms (its rays 3.3), the scene ~5.5, the water 2.9, the mesh 2.5.

### The reflections at 30 a second (2026-10-26)

Asked then about updating the reflections at 30 fps. The rays
(water, ice, the puddles; `block_rays`) now trace every other row a
picture, by its parity; a pixel of the other rows takes the hit its place
had one picture ago, moved with the camera's pan (kx + ox, ky + oy: the
scene moves by whole pixels), its colours copied (`RayKeep`). So every
pixel is at most one picture old and each picture does half the rays,
rather than whole pictures at 30 (one heavy picture, one light). Not kept:
a hit itself kept, one where the surface was not (a puddle grown), one
from before a view size change or a move of the stick's look (the rays'
slant), or more than 4 guest frames old.
- Mac, JR: the puddles' rays 2.16 -> 1.31 ms, the water 1.49 -> 1.03.
- Pictures against every ray every picture: 300 a picture of 83k pixels
  differ, by 2-3 levels, single pixels in the ripples (the water's wobble
  a frame apart); over the narration's pan (presents 110-440, 1 px steps,
  `KOL_REFL_KEEP_LOG=1` prints them) at most 186 pixels, 22 of them by more
  than 24 levels. Nothing shows at 4x.
- `KOL_REFL_EVERY_FRAME=1`: every ray every picture, as before.
- Then from the Thor: no gain at first. The rows' parity came from the
  guest's frame, and two pictures worked out are often two guest frames
  apart there (a late picture is shown again; the Mac never does it), so
  the same rows were traced every time. Now by a count of the pictures
  (`RayKeep::jobs`). Thor, `KOL_REFL_KEEP_LOG=1`: half kept; puddles' rays
  3.0-3.2 -> 2.5 ms, the water 2.9 -> 2.4. With `KOL_PERSP_THREADS=4` in
  the Thor's env.cfg (a run, the Thor cooler): the worker 20.2-20.8 ->
  17.0-17.9 ms in the rain, shown twice 247-262 -> 200-222 of 600.

### What three reviews found, the first batch (2026-10-26)

Asked whether refactoring or code reduction could cut the cost,
looked at with
subagents. Three read-only reviews (the scene build; the warp's effects;
what every picture copies and clears), their claims checked in the code;
then approved the first batch. Each change byte-identical: seven
reference runs (JR's pan presents 110-440 and the rain 1500-1800 with both
cache checks on, GN, BK, HQ, JP, HR) the same as before the batch; both
invariants.
- **The rays' results are no longer cleared** (5.6 MB a call on one thread,
  twice a picture) **nor copied back** in a second pass over every pixel: a
  hit is read only on the surface's own pixels, each written by the pool.
  This was most of what the rays at 30 a second had saved, spent again.
- **The uv grid crosses to the drawing once** (gbarecomp ENHANCEMENTS "The
  uv's fixed part copied and converted once"): with the pipeline's own
  copies every picture copied it (1.6 MB), converted every vertex on the
  guest thread and uploaded all of it. `PresentWarpMesh::uv_gen/uv_fixed`.
- **Map 102's sunset**: the sun steps every 6th frame and each step changed
  the terrain pass's key, the BG1 shapes' and every shadow's. A cache now
  keeps its result at once after a hit (`prev_hit`: steady inputs that
  changed once), not only once the same inputs come twice (each step was
  two whole passes); and the BG1 shapes' key takes the terrain's places
  (`place_key`), not its light. `KOL_CACHE_STORE_TWICE=1`: as before. JR,
  0-2200: the pass cache hits 1560 -> 1860, the BG1 cache 900 -> 1260,
  both checks 0 different.
- **The sun's shadow map on the row pool** (`kol::parallel_rows`, the
  warp's pool lent to the scene build; one run at a time, a lock), 8 rows
  of places a chunk. Trap avoided: `under_roof` is a `static thread_local`
  (read through a pointer).
- Smaller: the rays, the water's and the puddles' pixel passes in 4-row
  chunks (`fine_rows`; a band of water in 16-row chunks kept a few threads
  busy and the rest waiting); a prop's round foot spot searched 17 columns
  either side, not 24 (it reaches 16); the interface-prop list kept between
  pictures.

Mac, JR (2 threads, the worker's sections per picture, before -> after):
0.3-1.5 ms less a picture, the most over the sunset and pan (13.6 -> 12.1,
14.4 -> 12.8); the terrain pass while panning ~0.6 ms less, the BG1 shapes
up to 0.4, the puddles' rays 1.32 -> 1.01, the water 1.04 -> 0.85. Not in
these numbers: the uv copy (gbarecomp) and the guest thread's conversion.
Left for a second batch: rays skipping 8x8 tiles that cannot stop them, the
terrain pass on the pool, units' shadows moved with a pan (as props'),
the warp's serial passes on the pool.

### What the roofs cost, and their cache (2026-10-26)

On the Thor's slot 3 (states/JP_slot3_wet_floor: map 6, the rain battle,
52-54 fps) the present worker's sections (`KOL_WORKER_TIME=1` through
`files/env.cfg`, read in logcat; sum the `warp.*` sections only, the
`scene.*` / `light.*` / `wet.*` ones are inside them) were 12.5-14 ms a
picture with the camera still and 16-17 moving; the GPU 16% busy and the
guest thread 63% of a core. "scene.glow" was 3 ms on a map with no glow
(the user found that odd, the scene having no glow): that
section ran on to the next lap, over the windows, the editor's roofs and
boxes, the map's model and the props' bases. Split now (`scene.windows`,
`scene.roofs`, `scene.boxes`, `scene.model`, `scene.propbase`). On the Mac
with the Thor's drawn_heights.cfg, the roofs: 1.85 ms (map 6: 36 roofs and
19 boxes; each ray-solves every pixel of its screen box, each picture,
after the terrain pass and outside its PassCache).

**Their cache** (`RoofCache`, approved by the user): the arrays the roofs and boxes
write (16 of them, and the under-fix list), kept by a key of the terrain
pass's key, the roofs and boxes, and what their pass reads of the frame
over each one's screen box: the layer it takes each pixel for and, of the
colours, only whether a pixel passes the roofs' outline test (an awning's
box, grown by 18, reads the colours whole). Four results, by last use; a
result is taken once its key was seen in the last 8 pictures (one result
and "the same key twice running" threw it away every other picture).
`KOL_ROOF_CACHE=0` off; `KOL_ROOF_CACHE_CHECK=1` builds anyway and counts
differences: 0 in 300 checked; 120 pictures byte-identical on and off.
On JP it hits 48% of pictures: Alphonse stands in front of a house, inside
its box, and as he animates the layer under some of his pixels goes from a
sprite (his shadow's or the cursor's pieces) to the ground: the roofs'
pass does read that. Mac: 1.81 -> 1.23 ms (two runs each); where no unit
stands in a roof's box it should hit nearly every still picture. Moving
the camera, the roofs are built each picture as before.

**Merging the roofs, tried and dropped** (asked to merge contiguous roof
parts set up one by one): roofs a cell each that continue
each other along the ridge with the same section (gable or single slope)
and heights are the same shape as one; map 6 went from 36 to 26. It saved
0.10 ms (1.80 -> 1.70, cache off): the work is per pixel of each roof's
screen box, and neighbouring roofs' boxes hardly overlap, so the merged
ones cover the same pixels. And the cell that owns a pixel on a seam
(clamped to its roof's cells) changed, which moved 150 pixels of a bush
beside one. Not kept.

## The editor on the second screen (2026-10-04)

Asked to use the bottom screen to place and delete things, the design
left open. While Debug > Tile Info is on, the second screen's
page (`src/kol_edit_panel.cpp`) takes the sheet's place:

- **The map**, the top 112 rows: the battlefield's cells from above on the
  game's diagonal (a cell a 10 x 5 diamond), around Tile Info's target,
  coloured by drawn height (dark blue low, sand high; off the field near
  black, not walkable darker), roofs tinted red, a box a dark block, an
  edited height a white dot, the target's edge yellow. It moves only when
  the target nears its edge, so a tap does not slide it under the finger.
  **A tap on a cell makes it the target**: on a battle map until the game's
  cursor moves (`tile_edit_pick` / `tile_edit_resolve_target`; the game's
  cursor can only be sent to units), in a story scene's viewer its tile
  cursor goes there and the camera follows. **In ROOF, a drag across cells
  makes a roof** over the rectangle (its eave the first cell's height, the
  ridge three steps over), as L2 + B twice does.
- **The controls**, three rows of the game's windows in its font
  (`menu_draw_window` / `menu_draw_text`, exported from kol_menu):
  HEIGHT / ROOF / BOX (what the fields edit; the gamepad's L2 + Select and
  left/right move the same state), the target's X, Z and drawn height;
  `<  FIELD VALUE  >  -  +` (a tap on the field steps it too); the mode's
  actions: RESET (the height), DELETE (the roof, the box), ADD BOX. Greyed
  where they would do nothing (no roof, no box, nothing edited).

Edits go through the same code as the pad's and save at once to
drawn_heights.cfg. The grid comes from kol_focus each frame Tile Info is on
(`tile_edit_publish`: map, drawn heights, walkable / off-field, target).
Java (`StatsView.drawEdit`, `SecondScreen.pushEditPanel` / `editTouch`)
only shows the picture and passes touches in canvas pixels; the zone and
the options menu keep theirs. Checked headless on FB with
`KOL_EDIT_PANEL_PPM=<path with %lu>[,frame]` and
`KOL_EDIT_PANEL_TOUCH=<frame>:<0 down|1 move|2 up>:<x>:<y>,...`: the tabs,
a tap moving the target (the main screen's readout follows), + on the
height, a drag making a roof, ADD BOX; the saved lines checked. Both
invariants. With Tile Info on, the second screen shows the editor, not the
unit's sheet.

Every map with a saved state has a sky, map 55's castle included, and

**Map 51 lit by its blue fire pots (2026-10-14).** Asked for the map to be

shadowless, then darker with more reach. The fire

## A map editor for the space past a map (2026-10-08)

Asked for a Mac map editor to draw the map further out, only
to extend the view with less sky at higher resolutions; map 89 (the
opening's town) as the test, as a web page.

**What the game shows past a map.** Map 89's art fills columns 35-75 and
rows 37-84 of the guest's composed map (`[0x02026CA8]`, 128 x 96 entries a
layer; README "The composed map is in EWRAM"). A wide view's margins are
drawn from that array (`map_source_entry`), so past the art they show the
backdrop. Its header points at the placeholder graphics 33 scene maps share
(`+0x14 0xC1B0`, `+0x18 0x15400`); the scene brings its own tiles (578 of
them, ids 7-662, 8 palette banks; townspeople, barrels and goods are tiles,
not sprites). Where in the ROM they come from is not found.

**The extension** (`kol_map_source.cpp`, "Map extensions"): `map_ext.cfg`,
one cell a line, `map layer row col entry` (entry in hex, array coordinates),
beside enhancements.cfg (the Thor: `files/map_ext.cfg`; the desktop: the
working directory, or `KOL_MAP_EXT_FILE=<path>`). `map_source_entry` answers
the extension's entry for a cell the guest left empty on BOTH layers, and
`map_source_extent` counts its cells as art, so the edge fade (kEdgeFadeMaps)
moves out to where the painted scenery ends. Only the margins see it; the
game, the height grid and the units do not. The file is re-read when its
mtime or size changes (checked every 30 ticks), so a running game follows
the editor's saves. `KOL_NO_MAP_EXT=1` turns it off. The tiles are the ones
in VRAM, so animated tiles animate and fades apply.

**The editor** (`tools/map_editor/`): `export_map.py <state>` runs the game
headless from a state and writes `maps/map<N>.json` (char blocks 0-1, the BG
palette, both composed layers; gitignored, it is the cartridge's art);
`serve.py` serves `index.html` on http://localhost:8089 and reads/writes
map_ext.cfg in the repo root (only the posted map's lines are replaced;
"Send to Thor" also copies the file to `files/` with `adb shell run-as … cat
>`, nothing else). The page: Stamp (Shift+drag copies a block of the map or
of the tile sheet; a click paints it, a drag repeats it a stamp apart; X
mirrors it), snapped by default to the iso grid relative to where it was
copied (a move of 2k columns and j rows with j ≡ k mod 2 keeps the 32x16
diamonds); Pencil (one entry on BG0 or BG1, palette bank and flips), Erase
(a rectangle), Pick; undo/redo, a 384x216 / 480x270 frame around the
cursor, the game art's edge in yellow. Only cells empty on both layers can
be painted, the same rule the game side applies. The tile sheet is laid out
32 tiles a row, VRAM's own layout, where art pieces are whole.

### Override: repainting the game's own art (2026-10-14)

Asked (state GL, map 6): the bush at 6,8 is half BG0 under the house's
corner, so lifting can only stand its BG1 half up (the user asked to edit that part
into BG1 in the map editor). The editor paints over the game's
own tiles now: **Override art** (O). Over game art the pencil sets a tile on
the active layer (right-click: no tile), a stamp writes as usual, Erase
gives a cell back to the game; overridden cells are tinted magenta. Saved as
`ov map layer row col entry orig` lines in map_ext.cfg (the server keeps
them per map with the cells).

Game side (`kol_map_source.cpp`): an override is served only while the
guest's entry there is still `orig`, the one painted over, so the game's own
tile changes (the move range's highlight) show through. Through the margins
(`map_source_entry`) and inside the native screen through a new gbarecomp
seam, `g_ws_tilemap_override_provider` (any entry, asked per tile under the
margin provider's x-phase promise, before the fill provider, only for the
layers in `g_ws_tilemap_override_layers`, which KoL sets each frame to the
current map's override layers and is 0 otherwise). Not at 240x160 (the
native renderer never asks).

To lift a BG0 object: copy a whole copy of it with BG1 only (map 6's other
bush, at 8,5, is all BG1; the bushes sit on the same 8x8 grid), stamp it on
BG1 only with Override on, then pencil the wall or ground behind it on BG0.

native screen (GL, 480x270); the editor in headless Chrome (pencil refused
without Override, painted with it, saved as two `ov` lines with their
originals, map 89's lines kept, erase, undo, reload); both invariants hold.
gbarecomp's `ppu_smoke_tests` fails ("extended-view clamp mismatch") with
and without this change.

**The stones by their shape, and relief shadows (2026-10-15).** Asked on
HB (the user's slot 2, map 51): alternatives to the bump mapping, parallax

angle (only the right stick tilts it), shifts of 1-2 px swim on pixel art,

stone shapes, C shapes + relief shadows; `shots/bump_alternatives/`): the
user took C at a lower strength. Now on the wet floor:

  (`KOL_SLIME_BUMP`; the mockup's B and C were 0.8).
- **Relief shadows.** Each pixel is marched up to 10 px toward its flame;
  a stone higher than the ray climbing 20 px over the distance to the flame
  shades it, x 0.8 (`KOL_RELIEF`; the mockup 1.2). Far from a pot the ray
  is low, so the shadows grow away from it.
`KOL_BUMP_SHAPE=0 KOL_RELIEF=0`: the brightness bump of before;
`KOL_BUMP_DEBUG=<pgm>` writes the heights. The glints keep the sharp
brightness bumps. Kept per view like the rest; worked out only over the

invariants (no dark map in them).

**Then measured on the Thor** (HB, the user still ~10 s then panning ~20
s, per-second `simpleperf` + SurfaceFlinger frame times, today's bump by
`files/env.cfg` `KOL_BUMP_SHAPE=0` / `KOL_RELIEF=0`): still 59.8 / 59.7
fps either way; panning **55.4 fps with today's bump, 49.8 with C** (frames
over 20 ms 148 -> 345, over 34 ms 14 -> 42). Even today's bump drops
while panning there.

**So the stones slide with the camera.** A pan moves the scene's art by
whole pixels, the change of (kx + ox, ky + oy) (`glow_fx` is
`(x - z) / 2 + ox + kx`), and the pots with it. The kept heights and terms
are moved by that, and only 16 px blocks whose art, pool or flame (to 0.5
px, relative to the pixel) changed are worked out again: heights over them
and one block round (8 px of context), terms two blocks round (the relief
looks 10 px). A kept height near the band's edge stays only if it stands
as far from each edge (to 8 px) as it did, since the edge clamps the 5x5
mean. Three fixes the self-check found: the frame's edge rows and columns
are zeroed after the move (the whole pass never lights them); the relief's
step is rounded on its own (`x + round(ux t)`, not `round(x + ux t)`), or
a slid pixel sampled one over; and a first rule that redid everything
within 8 px of the band's edge kept the top and bottom block rows dirty
every frame (no faster than before). `KOL_BUMP_SLIDE=0`: everything every
time; `KOL_BUMP_SLIDE_CHECK=1` works it out from scratch after each slide
and logs any difference. Checked: 506 recomputes over two pans
(perspective on, HB) exact, heights and terms; 300 presents of a flat pan
byte-identical to `KOL_BUMP_SLIDE=0`; both invariants. Typically 25-60 of
250-420 blocks are dirty a panning frame (sprites and art changing).
Mac, the same 600-frame pan: worker job today's bump 8.75, C worked out
every time 9.55, C sliding 8.20 ms, and on the Thor 55.2 fps panning --
**both wrong**: see the next paragraph.

**A slip, committed in c038c5d and fixed after.** Taking my temporary
counters out before that timing also took out the one line that marks a
block dirty (`if (bad) db = 1;`, it carried a "TMP" note): the committed
build only moved what it kept and never worked anything out while the
camera moved (the strip that came into view had no bump until a whole
rebuild), and the 8.20 ms and 55.2 fps measured that. Found when the same
self-check failed on another map. Lesson: run the self-check again on the
build that is measured, after any cleanup. With the line back: 289 + 217
recomputes over two pans of HB exact; Mac, the same 600-frame pan: worker
job today's bump 8.85, C worked out every time 9.64, **C sliding 9.2 ms**
(lighting 1.72 / 2.60 / 2.14): about half of C's extra cost gone. Thor not
measured again.

unit_lamp_glow places a unit's pixels for kMapLamps): by its distance to
each pot, by how squarely the pot faces the card (half from behind), with
the flicker, and hidden where the terrain stands between it and the flame
(the ground's own `lamp_hidden` test). Passed as `ScenePixels::unit_lamp`; the warp's atlas uses it for
units in place of the foot's light. `KOL_UNIT_LAMP_FEET=1`: the old light.

behind him, faintly (light 18-21 of 255), fading out by row 15; his legs
stay dark. With `KOL_POT_REACH=3` the line shows plainly
(`shots/unit_card_light/`, feet left, card right). GR's unit is in full
light either way (150, past the gain's cap): identical. Cost 0.02 ms a
job (KOL_WORKER_TIME, scene.unit_ao+glow+win). Both invariants; maps that
are not dark return before any of it.

**The edge (the user found the cutoff harsh).** The first build

### Black ovals on the ship's deck: whose blob, whose parts (2026-10-15)

Reported on the Thor (state GY = the user's slot 3, the opening's harbour
scene, 384x216): shadows misbehaved as the screen faded out. Not the
fade: in those seconds two units walk down the gangplank past two sailors
sitting on the deck, and three things in `claim_unit_sprites` went wrong
(presents 322-348):

- A walker's blob pair (8x8 tiles 0x14B/0x14C) drawn on the deck below its
  frame went to a sailor whose frame it fit, or half of it to no unit: a
  black oval, since only a unit's own blob gives way under Unit Shadows.
  Now a blob part goes first to the unit it lies under: the game centres
  the pair one column right of the feet, its bottom row 2 above to 12 below.
- The sailors are 24x24 sprites ending 5 rows under their feet, past the
  frame's 2-row slack: their lower parts went to a passing walker, which was
  then too tall for a 32 slot and drawn flat. The frame now reaches 6 rows
  under the feet (`KOL_FRAME_FEET_SLACK=2` is the old frame).
- A walker 5 px from a sailor: the OAM-order rule carried on from the
  walker's blob into the sailor's parts. The blob pair is the last of a
  unit's parts in OAM: after it, that unit takes no more (`closed`), and
  the parts just before it are its unit's while they fit its frame and a
  32x32 slot. The part-join's slot bound leaves blob parts out (they are
  split off when out of the frame), so the walker's head 3 rows above its
  frame joins it.

`KOL_NO_BLOB_FEET=1 KOL_FRAME_FEET_SLACK=2` restores the old ownership.

byte-identical old/new at 384x216 present 60 on BO, CJ, CF, CQ, CP, CL,
CH, CK, CB, BL, EM, B_rictor, DE, CN, BW, DM, AB, FE, FF, FC, FD; both
invariants.

### Torchlight at 480x270 on map 51: the worker's cost cut (2026-10-14)

Reported: at 480x270 this map ran very slowly with torchlight on.
Measured on the Mac (GR, 480x270, `GBARECOMP_FRAME_PHASE` gives the
present worker's mean job; the old build kept as a second binary and the
two run alternately, since this Mac's absolute numbers drift by a few ms
between rounds): torchlight on, the worker's job was 12.7 ms still and
14.1 ms with the cursor held down (the camera moving), against 6.3 / 7.1
off. The Thor runs this worker about twice as slow (10-01: Mac 4.2 ms, Thor
22 M cycles), so that was well past a frame there.

Where it went, by section (`KOL_WORKER_TIME=1`, new: the worker's time by
section, means printed every 300 jobs; `warp.scene` encloses the `scene.*`
sections and `warp.lighting` the `light.*` ones, so the total double-counts
them): the pots' lean. With it, every pixel of the scene re-read its lamp's
pool at a shifted spot, a square root and four reads each, and that ran
twice a frame, once for the darkness and once for the tint (about 4 ms);
the units' shadows from the pots were recomputed every frame (0.5 ms); the
darkness pass rounded three floats a pixel.

Now: the lamps' light is read once a pixel (`lamp_light`, kept in a buffer
for both passes), 0 where the pool is 0 (it fades to nothing at its reach),
the slide's ramp near the flame by the distance squared (no root), the sway
by a dot product, the four-tap read plain (the pool holds every lamp's light
summed, so a neighbour's is the same light whichever lamp it is mostly
from); the units' shadows from the lamps are cached as the sun's are
(`LampCast`, keyed on the unit, the lamp at rest, the view, the heights),
each applied at its lamp's strength on the unit with the flicker each
frame (the lean's shift of the flame, 0.36 units at 0.06, is a fifth of a
pixel: dropped from the shadows); the darkness pass in 8.8 fixed point.
Also found: the heights the cast shadows bound their regions by
(`g_cast_heights`) were only refreshed with the sun on, so indoors they
were stale; refreshed with lamps too.

Measured after (old vs new, alternating, three pairs each): still 12.7 ->
7.4 ms, moving 14.1 -> 8.5. By section, torchlight's share is now about
1.3 ms: the lamp read 0.51, the tint 0.41, the darkness 0.34, the pools
0.05 (0.27 moving), the shadows 0.02; the rest of the job (the mesh 1.3,
the atlas fill 1.2, the props' claims and lifting 1.0) is not torchlight's.
Checked: both invariants; BK, EI, BN, GM, CA, EJ, S_move_highlight
byte-identical to the old binary (no dark map: nothing there changed);
GR differs at the pools' and shadows' edges only (the slide's read, mean
0.28 a pixel, and lifted wall pieces now take the lean too). Not measured
on the Thor.

### The worker on the Thor: what each option costs, and two cuts (2026-10-14, night)

Asked where workload could be saved, then to start with
the profile. Measured on the Thor with
EM (map 55) loaded through slot 1 (the user's slot put back after), 480x270,
camera still: `simpleperf stat --per-thread` for 10 s (game = the first
`Thread-4`, worker = `present` plus the two later `Thread-4` row-pool
threads) and SurfaceFlinger's fps over the same window.

All options on: game 32.9 M cycles a frame, worker 39.0 M, 59.3-59.8 fps.
On 10-01 the worker was ~22 M at the same size, and on 10-06 the game was
32.0 M: everything added since went to the worker. The user switched options
off one at a time (each step keeping the earlier ones off):

| Option | Worker | Game |
|---|---|---|
| Perspective itself (all else off) | 23.7 M | 6.5 M |
| Shadows (with map 55's godrays) | 6.7 M | |
| Lifted Walls | 4.2 M | 3.2 M (the compositor's under-BG1 record) |
| Depth of field | 1.1 M | 2.5 M (plus the GPU) |
| Lifted Props (map 55 has few) | 1.7 M | |
| Ambient occlusion | 1.2 M | |
| Torchlight | ~0.9 M | |
| Water, Bump Map, Unit Shadows, Tile Info | under the noise (~0.7 M) | |

The game thread drifts 28.5-32.9 M between readings with nothing changed:
read under 1 M there as noise. The worker profile (384x216, then 480x270):
the warp mesh about half, then lighting, lifted props, the scene build, the
focus map.

Two cuts, both byte-identical by construction:
- **`range_mask` with no range** (`kol_highlight.cpp`):
  `highlight_world_lit` handed out the composed map's lit masks on every
  battle frame, all zeros when no range is up, so the capture copied ~200 KB
  of zeros a frame and the worker tested every scene pixel against them
  (1.9% of the process at 384x216). It now counts the lit cells as they are
  written and hands out nothing at zero.
- **The zip's rescans** (`warp_provider`, the index build): each step of a
  run's zip looked for the next kept corner on BOTH edges and advanced one,
  so the edge that stayed was scanned again from the same corner, a long
  scan where merging left few corners. The hottest line of the Thor profile
  (2.2%). Each edge's next corner is now found again only when it advances.

Checked against a build of the commit before: both invariants; lit present
dumps (perspective, lifted props and walls, torchlight, water, shadows, AO,
480x270) of S_move_highlight, CO_target_in_range and EM byte-identical, and
`KOL_RANGE_LIGHT=0` changes all of the first two (the range path does run
there); `KOL_PERSP_HASH` pass4 (the index list) identical on 120 frames of
EM and 300 each of BL (camera panning) and CK (stick look). Mac worker job
on BL 7.31 -> 6.99 ms (three alternating pairs). Thor, EM fresh load, all
on: worker 40.0-40.2 M (range cut alone) -> 37.2-37.7 M (both).

Then three more, byte-identical (both invariants; lit dumps of EM, EP, ER,
BK, S_move_highlight, CO still and with the stick look, 60 of 60;
`KOL_GODRAYS=0` changes EM, so the window pass runs there): the window
light skips pixels with no sun and no haze before classifying them
(window_light changes nothing there), and `lift_prop_pixels` keeps its two
scene-sized buffers (`prop_of`, `want`) between frames instead of mapping
fresh ones every frame. Mac worker on EM 7.94 -> 7.56 ms; Thor 37.4 ->
37.0 M (at the edge of the noise).

Why the mesh is not cached on a still camera (tried 09-28): on EM the
mesh's inputs (kind, xz, y) change only 8-9 times in 120 frames (unit
animation), but every corner moves every frame, because `yref` eases 5% a
frame toward the scene's mean height and never settles, and unit animation
moves that mean. Settling it (terrain-only target, snap when close) would
change the picture by sub-pixels while easing: the user's call.

## The ship on map 97, a 3D model (2026-10-13)

Asked (state `GF` = the user's slot 3, map 97, a story scene at the quay):
asked for lighting on the boat, its sails and the rest, perhaps through
a 3D model of the boat. The user's own height edits for the map were
scrapped at their word (removed from the Thor's `drawn_heights.cfg`, backup
kept off the project, and from `kol_drawn_baked.inc`).

**Why the grid could not do it.** The scene's grid is 19 x 19 walkable
cells: the quay at 3, the deck at 1, a gangplank step at 2, and a line of
cells stored at 31 across the quay's edge and the deck (x 14, z 12-18 and
three by the bow): a wall to the sky. The hull, the stern castle, the mast,
the yard and the sails are art the grid knows nothing of; nearly all of it
is BG0 (the yard, the furled sail and the rigging are BG1; the banners and
crates are sprites, placed by the game's own object list). So the terrain
pass laid the mast and sails on the cells behind them: the mast bent, the
castle folded, and the 31 wall cast long shadow strips over the deck.

**The model** (`tools/models/ship97.py`, kit `tools/models/model.py`;
writes `src/kol_model_map97.inc`, 902 vertices, 952 triangles). Measured on
the flat frame of GF with outlines drawn over it (`ship97.py fit FLAT INFO
OUT`, the `.info` from `KOL_FOCUS_DUMP`: projection, units, grid). The ship
lies along X, bow at +X, the quay on its -Z side; units stand on the deck
at 16 and the quay at 48, which pins the projection.
- Keel line Z 565 (the mast's foot and the yard's middle agree); rails at
  56 over the waist, far bulwark's inner face Z 484, near rail Z ~645.
- Stern castle: deck 80, front wall X 467 (its top edge measured along two
  points: X 467 both), its rail rising from 90 at the front to 112 round a
  rounded stern (back X 358). The art draws the stern's top rail flat across
  the screen and its near post upright: no single shape is that; a rounding
  of 30 lands within a few pixels of both. Its hull tucks in toward the
  water (the counter: 0.45 a unit of height).
- Bow: no hull pixel lies right of x 292, so the sides close on a stem at
  X 733 (the far rail meets it at X 674, Z 510). Bowsprit from (715, 80) on
  the keel line, rising ~20 degrees.
- Mast at (507, 565), radius 5; yard along Z at 218 (it crosses the mast at
  row 51), Z 439-685; the furled sail a cloth sheet hanging 30 under it.
- Rigging: the near shrouds are five lines meeting over the mast at row
  ~-20 (a masthead at 360). They are not traced: two "rigging sheets" (a fan
  from the masthead to the castle's near rail, and the mast's own plane)
  give a place to BG1 pixels that no other BG1 part takes. The ropes' lower
  runs are painted into the castle on BG0 and go with it.
- `kDrawnCells` puts the 31 cells back: the quay's at 3, the deck's at 1.

**In kol_focus** (after the roofs and boxes, before the props;
`kModels`, `ModelView`, `ModelShadow`):
- Each pixel's ray meets the model's triangles (rasterised, the nearest
  point wins). The art's layer decides which parts may take it: a BG0
  pixel only a BG0 part (hull, decks, castle, mast); a BG1 pixel a BG1 part
  first (yard, sail), then the rigging's sheets, then a BG0 part. So a pixel
  of quay seen between the sail's swags is never put on the sail. The
  terrain keeps a pixel only where it is clearly nearer (24 units).
- Light: the terrain's shadow map and the model's own shadows decide. The
  model's shadows are a depth map seen from the sun (one unit a texel,
  3 x 3 samples), built when the sun moves; it also darkens what the model
  shades around it (the deck the grid has, the quay, the water). Nothing
  is lit by Lambert: the art has its own shading, as everywhere else.
  (Corrected 2026-10-13: a point facing away from the sun WAS put in
  shade, as the terrain's walls are; see "The far bulwark's dark band"
  below for why the model no longer does that.)
- Lifted Walls: a BG1 model pixel opens onto the BG0 part behind it, or the
  terrain. Model pixels own no cell (not water, not a building's).
- The art's dark outline a pixel past the model's edge joins it (as the
  roofs' outline), from a precomputed ring just outside the silhouette.
- Cost. What the model shows does not depend on the camera (it moves it by
  whole pixels), so the raster and each point's light are worked out once
  in the model's own frame, and again only when the sun or the map's
  heights change; the shadow it casts on the terrain is kept per terrain
  pass key. Mac worker: 2.6 ms a frame at first, 0.32 ms now (assign 0.26,
  outline 0.02, shadow 0.01), byte-identical through each step but the
  ring (which stopped quay cobbles in the rigging's area being claimed as
  the ship's outline). Thor not measured.

**Checked.** Both invariants (66e13ab2 / 9054c456). `BN_water_focus` and
`EM_slot1_slower` lit at 384x216 are byte-identical with and without the
model (`KOL_NO_MODELS=1`): it only runs on map 97. Stills, before and
after, flat light and four camera looks: `shots/ship97/GF_before_after.png`.
Not seen on the Thor.

**Switches.** `KOL_NO_MODELS=1` (the map as the grid draws it). To add a
map: a script like `ship97.py` writing its `.inc`, one line in `kModels`.

- Every strip's normal was inverted (the kit's corner normal was (rows)
  x (columns)): the hull's near side faced the quay, so "facing away from
  the sun is shade" happened to leave it bright, while the bow's front
  faced inward and went dark, and the far bulwark's inner face faced the
  sun, passing the facing test only to be shaded by its own outer skin
  through the depth map (6 units of wall; the top 13 units cleared the
  rail and stayed lit: the band). Fixed in `model.py` (normals outward
  for skins, inward for the inner faces).
- With the normals right the facing test would have darkened the whole
  near side of the hull and the whole inner face, which the art draws as
  lit wood. So a point facing away from the sun is taken to be in the
  ship's own lee, which the art has drawn: it is left as drawn, never
  shaded by the model (the ray from it toward the sun runs through the
  hull: its own wall, deck, roof and far side would all "shade" it; a
  first try with a thickness allowance of 16 units left the inner face's
  foot dark and put the near hull in the deck's shadow). A point facing
  the sun takes the model's shadows as before: the bulwark's strip on the
  deck, the mast's across the castle, the yard's on the sail.
- And the terrain's shadow map is no longer consulted for model points.
  It had kept the inner face's foot dark after both fixes: the grid's
  quay cells (48 high, z 9-14) run right up to the gangplank's and the
  deck's (z 15, 16) where the art has a strip of water between the quay's
  wall and the far rail, so the quay's edge "shaded" the ship's far side
  up to 32 high and the deck's edge. The grid is walkability, not shape,
  and the model's own depth map covers everything that can shade the ship
  here. (If a model ever stands under a real wall, give it the terrain's
  shadow back for blockers above its rail.)
- Found in the same numbers: the castle's deck was shaded over its whole
  width (100 at row 110). The rigging's sheets, which exist only to give
  rope pixels a place, were in the depth map as full triangles, so the
  shroud fan cast a triangular shadow over the castle. Rope sheets cast
  no shadow now.
After: the inner face, the near hull, the cabin's near wall and the prow
read 255; the deck's strip beside the bulwark stays (the bulwark's own
shadow, 30-100, soft). The sun on this scene is the battle default, 60
degrees toward (0.585, -0.811): from the quay's side, so the far bulwark
does shade the deck beside it and the hull shades the water on the near
side.

*Traps.* Judging a tint by eye at 4x misled me three times today (the
sail looked blue, the balustrade looked uncovered, the bow looked to take
water); the `.model` dump answered each in one query. Read the mask's
numbers (part per pixel, the leftmost modeled column per row) before
changing geometry. And measure the art's edges on an UNLIT frame: the
lit one carries the model's own shadow on the water, which a hue test
takes for hull. When the user draws the line, follow the line: both of
my "measured" yards were ropes.

### The two people on the quay, and the flags, there from the start (2026-10-16)

The user, on the boat scene, asked for two sprites at the bottom right
that appear after the seagulls pass to be there from the
start. They are actors 0x05 and 0x75 at cells 15,10 and 14,10, which the
scene's script creates only after the gulls have flown. At 240 they stand
just off the game's screen, so the game never shows them arriving; the
wide view does.

*The scene script* (states/HL = the user's slot 1 just before the scene,
script at ROM 0x0876F78C; interpreter decoded with a subagent): a step
routine 0x0811A248(ctx) runs a thread's ops until one waits (ctx +0 s16
offset, +2 the wait timer, +0x10 the script; op table 0x0816501C, 8 bytes:
s8 length, handler; a handler returning 0x110 continues in the same step,
any other value becomes the thread's state in the task loop at
0x081207A9). Contexts live at 0x02028ED0, stride 0x3C. The main thread:
`50 60` (sleep 96 frames under the narration) | `00 12 00`, `00 14 00`,
`00 17 00`, `00 1b 00` (spawn the fade and gull 1 threads at the relative
offsets) | `01 01 21 00` (spawn thread id 1: `50 1c`, `19 69 ...` gull 2's
flight, `09 69` delete it, `02` end) | `04 01` (join thread 1) | `6d 26 00`
(a relative jump) | `06 05 0f 0a 0a`, `06 75 0e 0a 02` (create the two
people: id, cell x, z, direction/mode) | `50 01` | the crew ... Op 06
creates the actor's record in the 8 "other side" unit slots at
0x02001760 (or the party's at 0x02001420 after `6e 12 11`); 09 deletes an
actor at once (the wait is the preceding action's); 02 ends a thread.

After the people the script goes on, a `50 01` between each block: `06 76
12 12 0e`, `06 77 0f 10 0e`, `11 77 00 e0 00` (the two blue pennants on the
deck), then three blocks of `6e 12 11`, `06 71/72/73 ..`, `0b`, `11`, `13`
.. (the banners hanging from the yard, lifted 120-150 high at once), then
the crew (`06 6f`, `06 70`, who walk and animate). With the gulls' longer
flight all of it came ~330 frames in (the user asked for the same on
the flags on the boat).

*The fix* (`src/kol_gulls.cpp`, a declining `[[mod_function_hook]]` on the
step routine): the main thread's step that starts at 0x7E (the sleep over,
nothing spawned yet) starts at 0xB9 instead and runs the people's,
pennants' and banners' blocks (a step each, their `50 01`s between); the
step after the last block (at 0x13F, the crew) goes back to 0x7E, where it
spawns the gulls' threads and joins them as before; and its step after the
join (at 0x90) skips to 0x13D, past the jump and those blocks. One more
thing was needed: op 06 makes the actor's record in the 8 "other side"
unit slots at 0x02001760, or the party's at 0x02001420 when game flag
0x112 is set (`6e 12 11`; byte 0x020011EE bit 2; one-shot, the 06 that
reads it clears it). Early, the other side has 3 free slots (the fade's
actor and the gulls are deleted only later), one short for the people and
pennants: with none free, 06 goes on without a record and the sprite setup
traps in 0x0801355A (that was the subagent's finding, and the first
pennant run proved it). The hook sets the flag before the pennants' step:
76 goes to the party's side and 77 takes the last free slot; the banners
and the crew take the party's with the script's own flags. Checked on HL:
people and pennant stand there from the first lit frame; the gulls fly as
before; the records after the scene hold each actor once (party 02 76 71
72 73 6f 70, other 4a 32 05 75 77); late in the scene (the deck shown,
frame 1060 from HL) both orders show the same pennants, banner, crew and
people, the early one running two frames behind (its five extra steps),
which is where the remaining pixel differences lie (the pan's edges, the
water); a state saved mid-scene (HJ, the main thread already in its join)
plays the game's order. In the wide view the second gull's flight is
drawn out ~225 frames (kol_gulls), so the game's own creations came ~950
frames after HL loads (at 240, ~800). `KOL_NO_QUAY_EARLY=1` leaves them to the game. Both
invariants hold.

*Two dead ends.* (1) Running the creations in gull 2's child thread hung
the game in 0x0801355A, a `b .` trap at the end of a sprite table search
(0x08013540, 16-byte entries sorted by a u16 key) for a garbage key: the
creation reads context the child thread does not carry. (2) A 600-frame
headless run from HL looked like a stall at the narration with the hook
merely declared; the narration simply lasts longer than that (the scene's
first step is ~470 frames after HL loads). Measure before blaming a build.

### The street soldier walks to the edge and fades out (2026-10-17)

The user asked for the character heading up-right to keep walking until
off-screen, then, offered a fade, chose the fade. During the gulls a
soldier (actor 0x31) walks up the upper street: the script op `16 31 2a`
walks him along route (0x2a & 0x1f) - 1 = 9 of the scene's route table
([[0x02029AC4] + 0x18], 36-byte records: 16 cells as x, z bytes, then a u32
count; a game task 0x08122D28 hands it to the walker, 0x0806D5A8(obj,
route, count), and polls 0x0806D5B8 until he arrives), then `09 31` deletes
him. Route 9 is cells 5,8 to 5,3; at 240 he is off the game's screen when
he goes, in the wide view he vanished mid-street.

- *Further* (`src/kol_gulls.cpp`, the step hook): just before that op runs,
  route 9 gets 5,2, 5,1 and 5,0 (the street is height 7 to the map's edge);
  the deletion waits for the walk and nothing waits for that thread. Row 0
  is the map's last: the walker reads cells as unsigned bytes, so there is
  no cell past it. At 384x216 his feet still showed at the edge; at 480x270
  all of him.
- *Fade* over his last cell and a half (Z 64 to 16), by the game's own
  blending, as the deployment ghost (kol_ghost.cpp): object flag 0x100
  (+0x78) makes every part of his sprite OBJ mode 1, and the game's BLDCNT/
  BLDALPHA copies (0x03000E1A/E1C) get BG0-3 and the backdrop as second
  targets and weights 16/0 down to 0/16; only while the game blends nothing
  itself; put back when he is deleted (`gulls_frame`, every frame).
- *His shadow blob* stayed solid, and his boots over it did not fade: our
  PPU blends a sprite with the layer under it only when that is not another
  sprite. The blob (a subagent traced it): the draw list 0x0805A77C registers
  a node for callback 0x080598DC(node, object), which emits descriptor
  0x0860EFBC (tiles 0x14B/0x14C) through 0x03005759; no per-object flag
  turns it off (+0x6E bit 0 does, but is a terrain result rewritten each
  step and read by gameplay). A declining `[[mod_function_hook]]` on the
  callback returns at once for him while he fades.
- *Our shading*: in the perspective view his card kept the contact
  occlusion and cast shadow at full strength (a dark silhouette when he was
  nearly gone). A semi-transparent unit now casts its shadow and contact
  occlusion at BLDALPHA's EVA / 16 (`BlockCaster::strength`). The deployment
  ghost (8/8) therefore casts half a shadow now.

Checked on HL at 384x216 and 480x270, perspective and flat: he walks on,
fades to nothing with no blob or silhouette left, and the script deletes
him; HJ (saved mid-walk) plays the game's way; both invariants hold.
`KOL_NO_LONG_WALK=1` leaves the walk, the fade and the blob to the game.

### The same ship on map 58 (2026-10-17)

Asked: make map 58 editable in the map editor, then whether map 97's boat
model could go to map 58, then agreed.

**Editable.** No state is on map 58, so it was exported from the New Game
viewer: EV + `KOL_DEBUG_MAP=58 KOL_VIEWER_CELL=center`, A at 1324,
`KOL_MEM_DUMP=2400,<file>` (the dump frame is the ABSOLUTE frame count:
EV loads at ~1314, so a run-relative 1100 fired at the load), then
`export_map.py --dump <file>`. The editor lists every `maps/*.json`.

**The same drawing.** Map 58's ship (a night palette, at a rock instead of
a quay) is map 97's tile for tile: 156 tiles unique to both maps' BG1
agree at one shift of the composed array, 12 columns and 16 rows. The
hull's split between BG0 and BG1 differs, so BG0 does not match by tile;
the pixels do.

**Where it sits.** On the flat frames (viewer, perspective off, unlit)
the mast and its top match at a screen shift of (-32, +16) between map
97 at cell 13,12 and map 58 at cell 0,2. A screen shift fixes the place
only up to the line of sight, (t, t, t). The grid settles it: map 58's
deck cells are stored at 3 where map 97's are at 1, so Y + 32, which
gives X - 416, Z - 256 (13 cells, 2 steps, 8 cells). `tools/models/ship58.py`
builds ship97.py's model in map 97's world and moves it by that. Its
overlay on map 58's frame lands the mast, the top, the yard, the sail,

### The boat's flag and door on map 58 (2026-10-17)

The user, on slot 2 (states/HM_slot2_map58_flag: the night scene on map
58, rain): the flag should be blurred, its shadow fell wrongly as if
at the wrong height, and the door twitched
with the rain.

**Both are units 32 x 40.** The flag hanging from the yard (unit at 80,
168, 356: its tip; the yard is at 255, and the flag's top at ~248) and the
castle's door (48, 48, 336, its anchor at the door's right edge) are scene
actors, and both sprites are 8 rows taller than a unit's frame and slot (32
x 32). `KOL_OAM_DEBUG=1`:

- *The flag:* its top 16 x 16 (OAM 18) fits no frame; the part join refused
  it (the unit with it would not fit a slot), and the run pass then gave it
  to the interface: drawn flat, never blurred (its blur was 0 where the rest
  is 140-190), and left out of the card that casts the shadow.
- *The door:* its anchor at its right edge, its left parts fit no frame;
  only 0x2B7 and 0x2BB were the unit's (a card of 16 x 32), the rest stayed
  in the scene. And 0x2B7 (2 rows above the frame) came and went: on the
  frames a raindrop fell inside the door's frame (OAM 9-17, x 45-50) the
  drop took the door as owner until the run pass gave it back to the
  interface, and in between the part join counted it, the door was 34 wide,
  and 0x2B7 was refused. The door's right half jumped between a card and
  the castle's wall with the rain.

**Now:**

- The part join counts only the unit's parts drawn with it: the stretch of
  OAM round the part it joins that holds no other unit's part (the rain is
  drawn elsewhere). `KOL_PART_JOIN_ANY=1` counts every part, as before.
- It allows up to `kTallCard` (48) rows at most a slot wide, and runs again
  until nothing joins (the door's parts join one through another).
- `build_sprite_atlas` makes a unit taller than a slot two cards, its top
  rows then the slot over its feet, both at its place (the mesh places a card
  from the unit's feet, so they stack exactly). A caster has `upper` (its
  shadow's texels reach `2 x (feet_hy - hy0)` up) and the contact shade runs
  once a unit. The flag and the door are each one unit in every frame.
- *Hanging units:* over `kHangRise` (96) above the cell under them, not in
  the sky, with no blob of their own: no contact shade at their feet (there
  is nothing there; it darkened the deck art beside the flag's tip, which
  stood at the flag's height). And with the perspective, the art the scene
  shows behind a hanging unit's lifted card keeps the ground's place
  (`g_under_*`), not the unit's: the deck and castle behind the flag stood
  at 168, took its shadow and would move with it under the stick.

The flag's shadow is now its whole shape. With the flag 120 over the deck
and the sun at 60 degrees, it falls ~69 units down and to the left, past
the near rail onto the water: where a flag that high casts it.

**Hung at the depth of what it hangs from.** Whole as a card, a flag moved
with the game's place for it, which fixes it on the screen only up to the
line of sight: map 97's flag at 166 (states/HJ, present 320, at the view's
bottom) has its top 23 over the yard it touches (223), and under the
perspective it came off the yard by a few pixels (before, its top piece
stayed flat on the yard and the card below it moved: torn). A hanging
unit's cards, its shadow's caster and its pixels now slide along the line
of sight until its top row is at the height of the model's pixels just over
it (their median; the flat picture is unchanged). Map 58's flag moves by
~7 (its top at 248 under the yard's 255). `KOL_NO_HANG_ANCHOR=1`: off.

**Checked against the build before:** byte-identical on BO, CJ, CF, CQ,
CP, CL, CH, CK, CB, EM, B_rictor, DE, CN, BW, DM, AB, FC, FD (2 presents
each), BL/CL/CP at 150 and FE (40 presents), with `KOL_YREF_HOLD=0`. Only
the boat scenes differ (GY, HJ, HM: their flags and the door). Both
invariants (240 `66e13ab2`, anchor-off 284 `9054c456`).

**The door's last twitch was the reference height.** With the parts fixed,
the door's left half still moved a pixel now and then, and its bottom row
(4 rows over its anchor, on a pixel's edge) came and went with the rain.
`yref`, the height the perspective scales about, eases toward the mean
height of the scene's pixels; rain hides and shows scene pixels and moved
that mean ~0.02 a frame, and an ease that never stopped moved every point
far from its anchor by a hair. Now `yref` holds within `kYrefHold` (0.5) of
its target (`KOL_YREF_HOLD=0`: always eased). Measured over 60 frames
settled, the door changes only where a raindrop crosses it, as in the flat
frame. (Tried first: unit shadows off, terrain shadows off, occlusion off,
torchlight off: none changed it; lifted walls and props off did, which
pointed at the card against the wall, then at the scale.)

### The town's archers walk in from beyond the edge (2026-10-17)

The user, on a new slot 2 (states/HP_slot2_town_archers, the end of the
boat scene fading into the town, map 98): the soldiers seemed to
appear out of thin air and should come from farther off before
they shoot their arrows.

*The script* (same script, 0x0876F78C, from 0x234; decoded by a subagent,
the table below is the part that matters). The three archers 0x75, 0x76,
0x77 and the soldier 0x78 are made hidden (`6e 13 11`, then `06`) on the
map's west edge: cells 0,14, 0,15, 0,15, 0,16. Nothing on the grid lies
west of column 0 (x 0..22, z 0..23 here). After the 80-frame fade-in, five
threads; each shows its actor as its walk starts:

| Offset | Ops | |
|---|---|---|
| 0x2CA | `2c 75 00 01`, `17 75 01 02 10 02`, `1a 75 00` | T+0: 0x75 walks 0,14 -> 6,14 -> 6,12 |
| 0x2D8 | `50 28`, `2c 76 00 01`, `17 76 03 04 0f 02` | T+40: 0x76, 0,15 -> 6,15 -> 6,17 |
| 0x2E8 | `50 5a`, `2c 77 00 01`, `16 77 45` | T+90: 0x77, 0,15 -> 5,15 |
| 0x2F2 | `50 82`, `2c 78 00 01`, `11 78 00 f6 00`, `0b 78 02 10`, `10 78 60 00 02` | T+130: 0x78 glides 96 px in |

Then (after all five and 18 frames) `0a 7x fa 13`, the shooting, and the
arrows 0x69-0x6B made on the archers' cells and flown east (`19`). At 240
the edge column is on the game's screen too; in the wide view it is in
plain sight, well inside.

*Why not routes:* op 15 packs a route's cells in 5 bits and the walker
reads cells as unsigned bytes: no cell west of column 0. But op 10
(`10 id dx dz speed`) moves an actor by signed pixels: at once with speed
0 (the handler adds to its X and Z only, its cell is kept), or as a glide
(0x08124EC0, a task at 2 px a frame; 0x78's own entrance).

*Now* (`src/kol_gulls.cpp`, the scene step hook): at each of the four
show ops the thread runs ops of ours instead, written to the end of EWRAM
(0x0203F000, 0x80 a thread: that area is zero in all 230 saved states and
written only by one clear at a scene load, a write watch over HL and HP).
The context's script pointer (+0x10) points there and its offset is 0

#### Their bodies vanished on the last stretch off the grid (2026-10-19)

*The archers coming in to shoot fire arrows sometimes lost their bodies
while walking the path.* (HP, 384x216, the Thor's
settings: object 4, the archer second from the top left, presents
~355-375.)
Only the head and shoulders were drawn; the legs showed the ground.

It was the game, not the perspective: OAM had the unit's lower half at
**priority 3** (behind the terrain) and the upper half at 1, exactly while
its X was -22..-1. The PPU composed the scene without those legs, so
kol_focus counted the card's texels "hidden by priority" (150 of 278).
The writer: the unit's slot routine stores four quarter priorities at
object +0x8C (0x0805A368) from 0x03005DE0 (IWRAM, the copy of ROM
0x087D58F8, called through the pointer at 0x0860FC5C). That routine takes
the place the move started from (object +0x16, -112 during our glide) and,
west of column 0, gives the ground height -255: the unit stands in a pit,
and the edge column's terrain covers its lower quarters once they reach
it. The same "no ground off the grid" as the blob (`on_blob`).

Fix (src/kol_gulls.cpp `on_occlusion`, `[[mod_function_hook]]` on
0x03005DE0 in game.toml, regenerate `generated/`): on map 98 with the
walk-in on, a call whose X (or Z) is off the grid is made again with it on
the grid's edge (0), the cell the walk goes on from; every other call is
declined. Prio 3 on any sprite over HP's 362 frames: 33 before, 0 after;
the archer whole on every frame. Both invariants hold (66e13ab2,
9054c456). `KOL_NO_ARCHER_WALK_IN=1` turns it off with the walk-in.

Found by elimination, recorded so it is not repeated: lifted walls/props,
depth of field, special effects, torchlight, the overlay bucket, the
mesh's per-vertex alpha, the flat HUD pass, the spell card and the present
pipeline all changed nothing; the mesh and atlas the present drew were
complete (rasterised offline); the card I first chased (unit 3) was not
the vanishing one. The present dumps are 240 wide while the view is 384
(no `--view-width`), so their x is the frame's x times 0.625: map a
dump's pixel to the frame before picking the unit.

The frame comes to the warp already whitened, and the occlusion, shadows
and the rest of the light were laid over it: grey shapes on white. Now the
light goes under the whitening (kol_perspective `under_white`;
ScenePixels::scene_white = BLDY / 16 when BG0 and BG1 are first targets of a
brightness increase): the frame's c = c0 + (1 - c0) y, light laid on c0 is
y + (c - y) L, which is c - (c - y) (c - lit) / c from the lit pixel, on the
scene (warp and flat shading) and on every card texel. At y = 1 it is the
frame (white). A/B present 1094/1100 with `KOL_NO_UNDER_WHITE=1`: the old
build kept the shadows and occlusion grey on the white map, the new one is

**The flash in perspective.** The field (BG3 white) was on top of every

### The town's flames stand up (maps 98 and 99, 2026-10-16)

Asked on states/HK (the user's slot 2, the intro's town under the archers'
fire arrows) for the fire not to look stuck to the walls.
The flames are not sprites (OAM holds only the arrows): the game writes
each one into its composed map as a block of BG1 tiles in palette 15, 4x4
(32x32 px) once grown, smaller while it grows upward from the same bottom
row, animated by rewriting the entries. The terrain pass laid those pixels
on whatever was behind them (a roof, a wall face, the street), so the
perspective and the right stick bent and smeared them with it.

Now (`flame_cards`, kol_focus) each flame is a prop of its own: an upright
card, lifted like the bushes (the BG0 behind shows through when the stick
moves), lit by itself (no terrain shade, no torchlight, no shadow cast, no
shaded foot, no sway). Its place:
- Which pixels: a BG1 pixel over a composed-map BG1 entry in palette 15,
  on maps 98 and 99 only (`kFlameMaps`). On those maps BG1 holds nothing
  else (98: 80 entries, five flames; 99, the town burning: 576). Palette 15
  is ordinary BG1 art on maps 2, 3, 8, 9, 29, 32, 40, 50 and 89 (a scan of
  the saved states' composed maps), hence the list. `kol::MapExtent` now
  carries the guest's BG1 entries (`bg1[]`) for this.
- Which block: the tile numbers do not give a tile's place in its block (the
  grown flames' sheet is 22 wide at 0x240, the growing ones' rows step 20
  then 22), and map 99's 54 blocks overlap. But every block stands on the
  cell grid: the lowest flame tile left over goes to the cell-aligned 4x4
  block over it that holds the most flame tiles left over.
- Where it stands: the block's anchor is its middle column, 8 rows over its
  bottom. On map 98 that is exactly a cell's top middle at the game's own
  height (all three of HK's: cells 12,10 h7; 13,10 h3; 12,14 h3); the card
  stands there. On map 99 many stand off the middles (on the cells' corners,
  8 rows off): there, the terrain point drawn at the anchor pixel.
- Measured on HK: map 98's three blocks and map 99's 40 keep one place each
  for the whole run (the first try took each flame's lowest pixel, which
  moved as it grew: one foot jumped from the street to the roof in front).
  The frame of the cut to map 99, where the map leads the picture by the
  camera's jump, is skipped (lead over 16 px: the flames stay on the
  terrain for that frame).
- So a flame the game put on the street behind a house stands there: under
  a lean the house in front covers its foot, as it would a unit's.
- Left: on map 99 some blocks lose tiles to the one drawn over them, and a
  card of the leftovers can show a straight cut edge.

`KOL_NO_FLAME_CARDS=1` leaves them on the terrain; `KOL_FLAME_TRACE=1` lists
each block and where it stands.

**The smoke stands too (map 100, 2026-10-17).** The user asked for
the smoke to come off the wall texture, as the fires had. The smoke
scene after the burning town (states/HR, saved inside it) has BG1 holding
only smoke: 282 composed-map entries, palette 15 (the flames' too), as
columns two tiles wide and up to twelve tall, each rising from a cell; the
game blends it over BG0 and the sprites (BLDCNT 1142, BLDALPHA 0B08: 8/16 of
the smoke plus 11/16 of what is behind). Now (`kSmokeMaps`, flame_cards'
column mode) each column is one card standing at its bottom: on a cell's top
middle when its middle column is a cell's (exact, as 9,18), else on the
ground drawn at its foot (8 px off, on the cells' corners). Self-lit, as the
flames. But a card is opaque, and a smoke pixel already holds 11/16 of the
wall behind it: the first build carried the wall's texture up the column
and was opaque, and standard alpha cannot match weights summing over one
(8/19 left a quarter of the wall in the card). So the card is drawn
see-through, premultiplied (gbarecomp `PresentWarpMesh::alpha`, new): its
texels the frame's colour less 11/16 of the ground the game blended in (the
compositor's scene behind BG1, `under_rgb`), its corners at alpha 1 - 11/16.
Over its own ground that is the game's pixel again; over another (the stick,
the perspective) it is the smoke on that one. `KOL_NO_SMOKE_CARDS=1` leaves
it on the terrain. Stills: `shots/smoke/HR_smoke_before_now.png` (before /
now, at rest and the stick left, up, down). The columns are the game's art,
smoke across the tiles' 16 px (rebuilt colours: almost all the palette's
four light ones), so standing up under a strong tilt their straight edges
show. HK (map 98) byte-identical; both invariants hold. On the Thor the
first APK drew the smoke scene all black: the alpha attribute took GL slot 6,
which on GLES2 is the mesh's position (desktop GL's is 0, so the Mac never
saw it); every corner moved. It is slot 5 now. The Mac cannot run the GL
alpha path; judge it on the Thor.

to 0x08000000), but only together with HLE SWIs (`--bios-hle`), a different
machine. New in gbarecomp: `--skip-bios-intro` / `[bios].skip_intro` /
`GBARECOMP_SKIP_BIOS_INTRO`, the skip alone with the recompiled BIOS's SWIs;
never when resuming a savestate. `android/app/jni/main_android.cpp` passes
it; the desktop build is unchanged (the flag by hand). Headless: frame 60 is
the game's "Licensed by Nintendo", frame 200 without it still the BIOS logo.
Both invariants hold (states never boot).
