live palette is that one darkened (nine entries in ten no brighter in any
channel; full from 0.95 up). On map 101 and on battle maps 0x0202D90C is
not the live palette (map 101: rows 4-8 match, the map's rows 0-3 and
12-13 are another scene's; B_rictor: 48 of 255 no brighter), so only BLDY
counts there. The haze is multiplied by it. Both invariants hold.

**Fire light, and the burning town at night (maps 98, 99, 2026-10-17).**
The user asked for these arrows (not those in battles) and the fires to
give orange light, then for a glowing blob round the arrows, then
for the town to look as if burning at night, with no sunlight,
only the fires. Not the torchlight's lamps (their visibility volumes
rebuild whenever one moves, every frame for a flying arrow): each source is
a soft pool, power x (1 - d / reach)^2 by the 3D distance from a pixel's
world place (so it hugs the walls and roofs), worked out in a box about it,
no shadows (`ScenePixels::fire_lights`, kol_focus; `fire_light_pools`,
`fire_light_scene`, kol_perspective). Sources: the placed flames
(`g_flame_at`, their foot from their tiles, 16 up) and the archers' fire
arrows, actors 0x69-0x6D on map 98 (the object list; record +0x17's
bit is 0 for every object in this scene, so no "drawn" test: a landed arrow
glows on until the script deletes it). An arrow also has a halo, a soft
orange bloom about it on screen. Cards (units, props) take the light at
their foot; a flame's or the smoke's card (`SpriteBlock::fire`) none. With
Options > Torchlight. Mockups `shots/sunset/HK_fire_light_mockups.png`; the
user picked A for arrows and B for fires: flames 1.1 / 72, arrows 0.9 / 48 and a
10 px halo (`KOL_FIRE_GLOW=` five numbers, mockups).

Map 99 at night: an indoor map (kIndoorMaps: no sun, no sun shadows, no
evening) and a dark map (kDarkMaps {99, 0.2, 3, 1}): the battlefield down to
0.2 where no light reaches, the fire light bringing it back up as a lamp's
glow does (the darkness pass takes max(lamp, pool)), then its warmth at
half on top. The flames' cards stay as bright as they are (a flame is its
own light), and the warp's backdrop, copied before the light, is darkened
by the map's darkness (the sky at night). Mockups
`shots/night/HQ_night_mockups.png` (0.3 / 0.2 x reach 72 / 100); the
user's pick: 0.2, 72. `HQ_night_built.png`. Left: the first frame or two of
the fade-in, before the camera is known, show the game's own sky. Both
invariants hold.

*The fire map slowed the game down.* Measured on HQ's fire scene
(the Mac's worker, mean per job, the Thor's settings): 8.0 ms without the
fire light, 10.0 with it, 14.8 with Special Effects too (the Thor about
twice). Now 9.5 with everything:
- the effects: no noise where the shape is already empty, worked out once
  a corner (a texel the mean of its four), two octaves of noise, not three,
  and at 30 a second: a square made from the same part of the same flame
  (its place relative to the flame, not on screen, as the camera pans)
  takes the texels made a frame before (`g_fx_cache`);
- the pools: a box of 0.71 x 0.61 of the reach (what a sphere covers on
  screen), not the whole reach, a squared-distance test, and kept while the
  lights and the view hold;
- a card's fire light worked out once a card, not once a texel;
- on map 99, the burning town (its BG1 is its flames), Lifted Walls lifts
  nothing and Lifted Props only the flames (`fire_map_now`; the user
  had lifted props and walls ignored on this one; walls alone were 0.8 ms; then
  kept them on the archer map: 99 only).
  `KOL_FIRE_MAP_LIFT=1`: as elsewhere.

**Options > Special Effects: fire and smoke drawn anew (2026-10-17,
experimental).** The user asked for a switch turning on special effects that
replace the fire and smoke with shaders, these
two for now. Advanced Settings > Special Effects (`special_effects`, off, in no
preset; needs Perspective and Lifted Props, the cards' own needs). With it
on, a flame or smoke prop (flame_cards, maps 98, 99, 100) is no longer the
game's texels: kol_focus makes its squares a whole slot wide about its
middle column, starting 12 (fire) or 8 (smoke) rows over the game's top and,
for fire, 5 under its foot, every texel opaque; the game's pixels are lifted
as before, so the scene shows what lies behind them. kol_perspective's
`effect_texel` draws them a texel (and a corner) at a time, from the time:
fire as tongues (the shape narrowing up, eaten by two layers of value noise
rolling up, swaying, flickering) on a ramp dark red - orange - yellow -
pale core, its base ragged and lower in the middle (the user found the fire's
base too straight); smoke as a plume widening and drifting as it rises,
wisps of stretched noise thinned by a threshold, a warm grey. Both are drawn
see-through, premultiplied, each corner at its own alpha
(PresentWarpMesh::alpha; gbarecomp's SDL emulation now darkens by each
corner's alpha, runs split only opaque / see-through). Lit by themselves.
Stills: `shots/special_effects/` (off / on). Not measured on the Thor; off
by default, both invariants hold.

**In the presets since 2026-11-16** (Enhanced is to be the default, so special
effects are on by default): it was in no preset, so a fresh install (which starts
on Enhanced) had it off. Now Enhanced turns it on and Original off, and Enhanced counts as
the current preset only with it on (`Preset::special_effects`). A saved enhancements.cfg
keeps its own value: a device set up before this shows Custom until Enhanced is picked
again.

Then, from the Thor:
- *The fire and smoke did not fade in the transitions.* The scenes
  fade by the palette, not BLDY (their `5e` op): PAL RAM and the palette
  buffer at 0x02002400 both go dark, from the scene's full palette at
  0x0202D90C (found by searching EWRAM mid-fade for the full colours). The
  effects take BG 15's brightness against that one (`ScenePixels::fx_dark`
  / `fx_white`, with BLDY's effect on BG1 besides).
- *One fire was not converted.* Props group by place and
  cell, and six of map 99's flames on one diagonal at one height had the same
  place and no cell: one prop 192 px wide, of which the effect drew the
  middle 32. Each flame's pixels now carry their own (negative) prop cell,
  -2 - its index; the flame cards without the switch are byte-identical.
- *The smoke moved oddly left and right.* Its middle followed the
  bounds of the game's own pixels, which wander across the column as the
  game animates its wisps, and the plume swung as a whole. Each effect now
  stands at its tiles' middle and top (`g_flame_cx` / `g_flame_top`), and
  the smoke's only drift is slow turbulence carried up with it.

**Deeper holes in the burnt houses (map 100, 2026-10-17).** The user asked for
the holes in the houses to look deeper, perhaps with AO blobs.
Mockups first (`shots/holes/`): on the flat frame, then, asked,
lit with the perspective, shadows and AO (`HR_holes_mockup_lit.png`: A the
far rim's shadow inside, B darker toward the middle, C B with a ring around,
D A and B). The user chose D, stronger. The holes (broken roofs, doorways) are
drawn in two dark blue greys, (57, 66, 82) and (33, 49, 66), which also draw
the roofs' outlines and the walls' mortar shadows: a hole pixel is one of
them with 4/5 of its 5x5 around them too, grown 2 px over them; the colours
are read under the sprites and the smoke (the compositor's scene without
them), so the scouts and the drifting smoke leave the mask as it is. In the
light, on a copy of the occlusion (a cached scene keeps its own), each hole
pixel darkens by the far rim's shadow (its run from above, fading over 3
rows) and toward its middle (full at 4 px in), each at 0.75 (`kHoleMaps`,
`hole_depth`, kol_focus). The mask is worked out again only when it
changes (the camera holds still here): +0.2 ms a job on the Mac's worker
(0.6-0.9 before the cache). Only with the occlusion or shadows on.
`KOL_NO_HOLE_DEPTH=1` off. `HR_holes_built.png`: before / now. Both
invariants hold.

**The faint square in the burning town (2026-10-17).** The user, on
states/HQ (slot 2, map 98 fading into map 99 on fire): a strange,
barely visible square mid-screen at higher resolution,
more noticeable when the screen moves. The cards were made
only inside the native 240x160 (the reasoning: the margins are the
composed map's entries, the animation the guest's VRAM). So a flame in
the margins stayed painted on the wall behind it, shaded with it, and a
flame crossing the native window's edge changed look there: under the
perspective, a trapezoid (the native rect, warped) that stood still while
the scene moved. Found on the user's Thor recording, not by eye: the mean
of each frame's fine detail (frame minus a box blur) over the clip; what
moves averages out, the edge stayed. The same mean over the desktop's
present dumps showed it too, and switching effects off one at a time
(only `KOL_NO_FLAME_CARDS=1` removed it) named the flames. Now the cards
cover the whole scene: the margins are drawn from the same composed-map
entries the blocks are found from. `KOL_FLAME_NATIVE_ONLY=1`: as before.
Checked: the mean over HQ's fire shows no edge; HK (map 98) byte-identical
over 20 sampled frames; the pass cache self-check clean; both invariants. Both invariants hold (66e13ab2, 9054c456).
Stills: `shots/flames/HK_map98_old_new.png` (old left, new right; at rest and
three leans) and `HK_map99_old_new.png` (rest, down, sideways).

## Water: ripples, shore foam, reflections (2026-10-09)

Asked for a shader to make the water a bit more interesting. Mockups
first (`shots/water/`, made offline from present dumps): A now, B a 1-px
ripple + shore foam, C B + reflections, D a strong mirror. The user picked
**C with the reflection at 0.4** (the mockup's C was 0.6).
`shots/water/BN_built_0.4.webp` is the built one, 90 presents of BN.

- **The game animates its water already**, by cycling 4-5 colours (BN
  82,189,206 / 33,148,181 / 132,222,231 / 8,107,148, sparkles near white).
  The effect sits on top and keeps it: the game's sparkles keep three
  quarters of their colour under a reflection.
- **What is water: the game's own terrain class.** The terrain table's first
  byte (`0x0861CA5C + 0x20 * record`) is a class: 0 ground, 1 obstacle, **2
  water** (records 10, 11, 12; BN's pool and DQ's streams are 12, BK's
  channels 11), 4, 8, 0x0C, 0x10 (not identified). CK's ice is class 0 and
  is left alone. `kol_focus` `water_mask()`: a pixel is water's surface when
  the cell that drew it (`g_cell_owner`) is class 2, it is a flat top, and
  its layer is BG0/BG1 (no sprite, no lifted piece); anything else the
  terrain pass placed is shore. `ScenePixels::water` (1 surface, 2 shore).
- **The effect** (`kol_perspective` `water_effect()`, after the light, in
  both the warp and the flat light): each water pixel takes the colour a
  pixel to its side in slow bands; mirrors its column about the top of its
  run of water (past the art's 1-px shore line), wobbling, tinted
  0.72/0.86/0.98, at 0.4 fading out over 60 rows; the water darkens to
  0.82; foam (235,250,250, up to 0.7) breaks in and out on the pixels
  touching the shore, fainter one in. Time from the guest's frame serial.
- **Options > Advanced Settings > Water**, on in the Enhanced preset and by
  default (`water=` in enhancements.cfg). It only acts where the scene is
  composed (the perspective or the light), so not at Original size.
  `KOL_WATER_REFL=<strength>` overrides 0.4; `KOL_SETTINGS_OFF=water` (new,
  any default-on key) turns it off for a desktop run.
- **Cost:** 0.25 ms a frame on the Mac worker for BN's pool (7,600 water
  pixels), only while water is in view. Thor not measured.
- **Verified:** both render invariants unchanged (240 `66e13ab2`, anchor-off
  284 `9054c456`). On against off: BN, DQ and BK change 7,672 / 3,068 /
  6,919 px (the step writes only water-surface pixels); CK (ice) is
  identical. With the
  setting off there is no mask, and the step does nothing.

**The waves ride on the water, and the foam is a soft band (2026-10-12).**
Reported: the water effect looked wrong along the Z axis, the waves making
unnatural small white dots on the shore as the camera moved. The ripple, the
reflection's wobble and the foam were phased on the scene's pixels, and the
scene is the screen (a column is `(X - Z) / 2 + kx`, `kx` following the
guest's scroll), so a scroll slid the water under a pattern standing still.
- **Phased on the world now:** on the water's flat top `X + Z` is the
  scene's depth (`ScenePixels::xz`) and `X - Z = 2 (x - kx)`. The ripple is
  two slow waves crossing, along X (22 units) and along Z (30), shifting a
  pixel only where both crest; the wobble follows the depth.
- **The foam:** 0.45 at the shore (was 0.7), a paler grey-cyan
  (215,232,235; was 235,250,250), fading over three pixels in (1, 0.5, 0.2;
  orthogonal neighbours only, the diagonals made speckle), swelling and
  ebbing over long stretches of shore (90 / 140 units).
- **Seen:** `shots/water/BN_pan_before_now.webp` (the same D-pad pan of BN,
  input replay from frame 37960, before / now),
  `shots/water/BN_shore_before_now_zoom.png` (2x, the shore's dots gone).
  The pale flecks across the open water are the game's own sparkles.
  Both invariants unchanged.

**Not as in the mockup, on purpose:**
- **Foam where the screen cuts the water.** The scene goes on past the view,
  so the near shore just below the screen edge foams into the last rows
  (BN, bottom middle). The mockup had nothing past the frame.
- **Units cast no reflection under the perspective.** The warp draws them
  from their own sprites, not from the scene. With the flat light they are
  in the scene, so they do.
- **Water falling down a step** (BK's channels) is upright: it is shore, so
  the foam lines the top of each step.

**Water tags, for maps with no terrain (2026-10-09, asked whether water on map
89 could count, then for a way to tag it as water).** Map 89 is a story
scene's map: every cell's record is 0 (no class), and its harbour lies on no
cell at all (off the field, height 0, and past the 28 x 28 the game uses),
so nothing said water. Its colours do not either: the cycling ones are the
roofs' and walls' too.
- **The WATER tab** on the second screen's editor (Tile Info on): a drag
  across cells paints the brush over the rectangle, PAINT the target cell;
  the brush (< > or - +) is WATER, DRY (not water, whatever the game says),
  ICE (2026-10-27: ice, not water) or AUTO (the tag cleared). On its map the water is blue: a tag deep, the
  game's own paler, a dry tag brown. The tabs got narrower to fit it, and
  the readout reads `x,z Hn`.
- **Saved** as `water map x z water|dry` lines in drawn_heights.cfg
  (`kol_tile_edit` `tile_edit_water` / `tile_edit_paint_water`);
  `tools/bake_drawn_heights.py` bakes them with the rest.
- **kol_focus** `water_cells()`: the game's class 2, then the tags over it,
  for the mask and for the editor's map (`kTileWater`). A water-tagged cell
  the pass would not place (off the field, or past the grid) is placed flat
  at 0, with Water on only: off, the picture is byte-identical with or
  without tags (checked on EU). Placed, the harbour takes the light like any
  ground: the quay's shadow falls on it (dark at map 89's low sun).
- `shots/water/map89_tagged_before_after.png` (EU, before / after) used
  tags picked by colour for the test (cells whose flat pixels are mostly the
  harbour's purple, 122 cells); a first rectangle took in the quay past the
  grid as well, and it rippled. Tag by eye; DRY puts a cell back.
  `shots/water/panel_water_tab.png` is the tab, driven headlessly
  (`KOL_EDIT_PANEL_TOUCH`).
- The pad's L2 editor has no water field: the tab only.

**First tries that failed:**
- **"The pixels the terrain pass leaves undrawn are the water"** (as an
  older comment in kol_focus says). It is true on some map, but on BN, DQ,
  EM, CK and BK the pass places the water like any cell, so that mask
  caught nothing but a few tree tips. The terrain class was the answer.
- **The reflection blended over the water's own colour** read as a pale haze
  in the mockup (the shore's yellow over cyan). Keeping the reflection's
  contrast and darkening the water under it is what shows it.


**Ice (2026-10-20).** JB (the user's slot 3, map 17): asked for an effect to make
the map's ice look more realistic. The ice is record
22 (the striped blue; map 12's too), terrain class 0, so not the water's
class 2: `ice_cells` (kol_focus, `kIceRecords`) and `ice_mask` (the cells'
flat tops, face 0, not lifted, not interface) give `ScenePixels::ice`.
`ice_effect` (kol_perspective, after `water_effect` in both the flat light
and the warp): a whiter, colder base and broad diagonal glossy streaks
phased on the world (they slide as the camera turns), a faint pale mirror of
what stands over each run of ice (the column above its top, blurred a pixel
either side, 0.35, fading over 40 px), and sparse glints (one world point in
~180 on a 2-unit grid) that twinkle. Mockups `shots/ice/JB_ice_mockups.png`
(now / A sheen / B + reflection / C + glints, level and stick down); the
user's pick: C, all three. Under Options > Water (off: byte-identical, JB
checked). `KOL_ICE=<sheen>,<reflection>,<glints>` (1,1,1). Map 12 (IX):
`shots/ice/IX_map12_off_on.png`. Both invariants; Thor cost unmeasured.
Then, asked for more reflection: the mirror 0.6 over 60 px (was 0.35 over 40;
`shots/ice/more_reflective.png`, before / after on JB and IX); then asked to
bring it back to 0.35: 0.35, the 60 px reach kept.

*The mirror as a reflected ray.* Reported: a plant near a patch of ice
reflected as a chevron, which is not how reflections work: each column
was mirrored about the top of its run of ice, and along the ice's diagonal
edges that bent whatever stood there into a V. In this projection a row is
(X + Z) / 4 - Y / 2, so a ray off the ice goes straight up its column, a
height unit and 2 X + Z back for each pixel. The ice now walks that ray up
to 120 px and shows the first thing standing at or in front of it (its
depth, `sp.xz`, at least the ray's): each thing mirrored about its own foot.
Flat ground behind the ice is on its plane and reflects nothing; the sky
stops the ray; a lifted prop's colour comes from its atlas square (the
scene holds the ground under it) and its depth from its card. The fade goes
by the distance below the thing's foot (half the ray's steps), 0.35 over 60
px as before. Probed on IX: a wall behind the ice is met at the step its
depth gives (wall 260, ray 262). `shots/ice/ray_reflection_exaggerated.png`
(old column mirror / ray, both at 0.6) and `ray_reflection_wall_zoom.png`.
Both invariants; Thor cost unmeasured (at most 120 steps a pixel of ice).

*With the camera.* Asked to try updating the reflection with the camera:
the ray's slope now follows the warp's camera. Its rows are base + (dref +
(d - dref) s pitch) / 4 - (yref + (y - yref) s) / 2, s = K / (K + dref - d),
so along a line of sight the depth a height unit costs is k = (s / 2) / (s
pitch / 4 + (s^2 / K)((d - dref) pitch / 4 - (y - yref) / 2)): 2 in the
game's own view, measured about 1.3 with the stick up, 1.9 level and 3.3 to
3.9 with it down (IX). The ray climbs 1 / (k / 4 + 1/2) a pixel and goes
back k times that (`IceCam`, from warp_provider; the flat light keeps k =
2); the fade still goes by the depth gap / 4 over 60. With the camera low
each pixel of ice sees lower down what stands in front of it and farther
back, as a grazing reflection does. `shots/ice/camera_reflection.png`
(fixed view / with the camera, stick up, level, down; reflection
exaggerated). `KOL_ICE_FIXED_VIEW=1`: the game's view always. Both
invariants; cost unmeasured.

Then, judged right up and down but wrong side to side: the warp draws a scene
column x at depth d at cxp + (x - cxp) s(d), so a line of sight drifts
across the scene's columns with depth, the more as the stick turns the
camera aside (cxp, the perspective's centre, moves off the view's); the
mirror stayed in the ice's own column and slid off what it mirrors. The ray
now samples column cxp + (x - cxp) s(ice) / s(u) at its depth u (`IceCam::
cxp`; the atlas lookup of lifted props too). `shots/ice/camera_side.png`
(game view / with the camera, stick left and right, exaggerated); judged in
motion on the Thor.

*The sky in the ice.* Asked to improve the ice by replacing the blue
streak texture with a darker reflection of the background
fade. The reflected ray now also tells where it leaves into the sky: the
backdrop's pixel it meets, or, off the top or out of reach, the fade's
colour on the last row it reached (a table of the backdrop's colour per row,
from its own pixels; a row without takes the nearest). The ice's base is
that colour x `darkness`, plus `detail` x the art's own light against 150,
under the things' reflections, the sheen and the glints (the cold tint goes
with the art). Where the ray meets a thing, the sky at its row is the base
under its reflection (first left out: the art's streaks stayed under the
rock and the step). Mockups `shots/ice/sky_JB_mockups.png` (map 17's
night) and `sky_IX_mockups.png` (map 12's blue sky): A 0.55 / 0.25, B 0.4 /
0.15, C 0.7 / 0.35; the user picked C, lighter still: 0.85, 0.35
(`sky_built.png`). Then asked for a bluer tint and lighter, judging the
darkening a mistake: the sky at 1.1, tinted
(0.88, 1.0, 1.18) (`sky_blue_lighter.png`). `KOL_ICE_SKY=<amount>,
<brightness>,<detail>` (1,1.1,0.35; 0 none). Both invariants; cost
unmeasured. Then asked where the colour streaks in the reflection came from:
not the reflection. The ray and the sky table took any pixel the terrain
pass left unplaced (kSceneNone) for the sky, and map 17's dirt faces and
map 12's dark undersides are those too: the ice copied their brown and dark
blue in vertical bands, even with everything else off. The sky is now the
backdrop by the scene's own layer code (5, `ScenePixels::scene_codes`); what
streaks remain is the 0.35 of the art's own stripes and the sheen
(`shots/ice/sky_streaks_fixed.png`, sky only / all, before and now).

*Snow as spots.* Asked for snow to reflect as spots, not streaks: a
ray goes straight up its column, so every ice pixel under a flake met it,
and in view mode (no unit: the flakes not interface) a flake was a thing
standing there: a streak down the ice. The ray now passes through the
weather (`ScenePixels::weather`: `g_weather_px`, built whenever there is
ice, the renderer's margin copies included: one native screen away each
way, the sides 80 rows up / down, outside the native 240 x 160). And each
flake reflects as itself (`ScenePixels::flakes`, `weather_reflections`):
the game moves its particles in screen space only, so a flake's height is
a guess, its ground set the first time it falls within 56 rows over ice in
its column (that ice and 0 to 8 rows more, kept for the rest of its fall;
set when it appeared, the mirror almost never fell on the ice). Its pixels
are mirrored about that row, a spot where they land on ice at 0.6, fading
as it is higher; it rises to meet the flake as it falls
(`shots/ice/flake_spot.png`). `KOL_ICE_NO_FLAKES=1`: no spots. Both
invariants.

*A vivid sky calmed.* Judged nearly right on one map but too saturated
on the other: map 12's sky is near-pure cyan
(saturation 0.9-1.0; map 17's night 0.28-0.34), and the ice's 1.1 and blue
tint pushed it further. Past a saturation of 0.4 the sky's colour now goes
toward its own grey, up to 0.6 of the way by 0.9, before the tint
(`shots/ice/sky_desat_map12.png`); map 17 moves by at most 4 levels.
Then, still slightly too much: 0.75 (`sky_desat_075.png`).
`KOL_ICE_SKY_DESAT=<0..1>` (0.75). Both invariants.

**The water's reflection as a ray too (2026-10-21).** Asked whether the new
reflection (the chevron fix and the camera movement) could be applied to
water too. The ice's walk is now `reflect_ray`
(kol_perspective), shared: from a surface pixel up its column at the
camera's slope and drift, through the weather, the first thing at or in
front of the ray (lifted props from their squares) or the sky (by its layer
code). The ice uses it unchanged (byte-identical, IX level and stick down).
The water's reflection was its column mirrored about the run's top row;
it now takes the ray, its column moved by the ripple's wobble, a thing
fading by its foot's distance up and the sky by the pixel's distance below
the water's edge (as the mirror did), tinted and with the sparkles' quarter
as before; the warp passes it the camera. Where the ray now passes flat
ground and reaches the sky, DQ's vivid blue showed in its stream: the
sky is calmed as the ice's (`calm_sky`, shared). `shots/water/`
(`ray_vs_column_BN_DQ.png`, `DQ_sky_calmed.png`).
`KOL_WATER_COLUMN_MIRROR=1`: the column mirror. Both invariants; cost
unmeasured.

**Units in the ice: no streaks (2026-10-21).** Reported (JF = the user's
slot 3, map 40, an Angel Knight flying in over the ice 2-3 s after the
load): its reflection made streaks. Three causes in `reflect_ray`, found
with a per-pixel map of what each ice ray met (`shots/ice_units/
JF_ray_hits_map.png`):
- A flying unit's card stands at its place on the ground (its shadow), its
  sprite high over it. Its square's empty texels (the scene holds the ground
  there) blocked rays at the card's depth and mirrored the ice; and any ray
  past the card's depth still met it. Now an empty texel is judged by the
  ground under it (`under_xz`, the sky where none), and a unit's card is
  met only where the ray crosses its depth (within a step). The angel is
  mirrored under its shadow, at its height, faint.
- The ray stopped at any interface pixel, and the ice under the angel's
  blob shadow (interface) took the sky of the shadow's own low row, the
  light fade by the horizon, as a cyan column down the ice. Interface is
  now judged as the ground the scene holds under it.
- A ray that met a unit took the sky at the unit's row, light low down:
  the mirror was a pale cyan ghost. It now takes the sky it would have
  reached behind the unit. Terrain and props keep their row's sky (their
  look, approved on maps 12 and 17; JC is byte-identical but for one pixel
  under the cursor's corner).
`shots/ice_units/` (`JF_before_after_flyby.png`, `_later.png`: the units'

## The light without the perspective (2026-10-03)

Asked for shadows and AO to be available with the perspective
option off, so the map aligns 1:1 with the original but with
dynamic shadows and AO.

With the perspective off and any of Ambient Occl., Shadows or Torchlight on
(`kol::lighting_on`), the same present-time provider runs in a flat mode
(`flat_provider`, `perspective_set_flat`): the HUD-free scene is composed and
built as for the perspective, lit the same way (`apply_lighting`, moved out
of the warp unchanged: its pictures are byte-identical), and drawn back onto
itself pixel for pixel, the HUD on top from the frame as the warp has it.
Units keep their own pixels: with Unit Shadows the game's blob under them
gives way to the ground the game drew there (as the warp draws units from
their squares without it), they cast their shadows, and a unit in the
terrain's shadow is shaded as its square would be. Nothing is lifted, there
is no overscan and no look. Tile Info works in it too.

- The identity is a quad a pixel, built once per picture size. One quad
  over the whole picture drifted on SDL's software renderer (texture
  coordinates stepped with too little precision over a long triangle:
  46,682 pixels of EK off by one toward the far corner), and so did squares
  of 8; per pixel, with the light almost off, only the bobbing hand differs
  (the providers present a frame behind).
- Not at Original (240x160): gbarecomp composes the HUD-free scene only for
  an expanded view (`view_expanded()` in gba_ppu.cpp), and the native
  path is the 240 invariant's. The menu's help says so.
- Cost on the Mac's present worker (EK): 0.80 ms a frame, the perspective
  3.18 ms. `KOL_NO_FLAT_LIGHT=1` leaves it off; `KOL_FLAT_GRID=<px>` sets
  the squares.
- Checked: ER and EK lit without the perspective, aligned with the plain
  picture; the perspective's pictures identical to the previous build (ER,
  EK); both invariants (the light is off in them).
- Debug > Perspective Mesh paints in it too (asked for the Mesh to
  still apply): `paint_mesh_kind`, shared with the warp. Units keep their
  colours, as the warp's squares do, and the ground freed of a unit's blob
  is painted as the ground it is. The perspective's paint is unchanged.

## Debug: any battle map, through Training (2026-10-03)

Asked for a debug menu to view every map in the game in View Mode, wrong
starting spots acceptable, so that every map in the game could be
corrected.

Options > Debug > **Battle Map**: Game's (off), or a map number 1-119 (the
count is the u16 at `0x085C55C4`, the header table's head). Left/right step
one, L/R ten, a tap one; saved as `debug_map=`, `KOL_DEBUG_MAP=<n>` for
headless runs. Then start a Training battle from the world map's main menu
(or meet a random battle): it is fought on that map, and L in its
preparation is View Mode.

- **How the game picks.** A world map script's battle op (`0x0801FA78`, op
  0x93) takes the map from `0x08118B4C(place, n)`, a table of 12 map numbers
  a place at `0x08768BCC` (255 none, n + 6 under a story flag), and writes it
  to `0x02029D40` (at `0x0801FAF8`); the header parser `0x08021B68` then
  takes every pointer from the header. That routine has one caller (scanned
  the ROM for BLs), so the hook cannot start a battle the game would not; it
  only answers the map (a `[[mod_function_hook]]`, `src/kol_actions.cpp`).
  Found with a write watch on `0x02029D40` while Training from EB.
- **What loads.** A survey (Training from EB, then L, one frame each;
  `shots/battle_maps/`): maps **1, 3-56 and 104-115** load whole (67).
  **2, 57-103 and 116-119** come up with the terrain's shape in the wrong
  tiles (black/white/grey-blue: no terrain palette or tiles) or nothing at
  all. Their headers are read the same way (a read watch over map 60's and
  map 55's headers: the same fields at the same PCs); the difference is the
  data: 60, 64, 100 and 119 share the same graphics offsets (`+0x14
  0xC1B0`, `+0x18 0x15400`, `+0x1C 0x0A00`), and most have `0x00FF` at
  `+0x34` where loading maps have a small number. They seem to take their
  graphics from whatever uses them (story scenes, probably); not found yet.
- The units' starting places stay the battle's, wherever they land.
- Checked: both invariants (240 `66e13ab2`, anchor-off 284 `9054c456`);
  with Game's, Training picks its own map (3 at Solea) and the hook declines.
  The Training path's 6 dispatch misses (`0x08007698`, `0x080079D0`,
  `0x080124BC`, `0x08076524`, IWRAM `0x030012D0`, `0x03001550`) are the
  battle misses already open, the same with the hook declining.

**The other maps, through a story scene (2026-10-03, later the same night).**
The user pointed out story sequences that are not battles (EU = their slot
1, a scene in a town: map 89), then said to press New Game on slot 1 (EV).
- **Why Training could not show them.** Training loads their data right: on
  map 89 the composed map, the height grid and every header pointer match
  the scene's, and the palettes differ only in entry 1 of each terrain bank
  (Training's deployment highlight, `0x7C42`). What breaks is VRAM: 42 of
  the 52 have the scene layout (header +0x00/+0x02 `1416 1213`: layers at
  screen blocks 0x16/0x14/0x13/0x12, terrain tiles up to 0x7FFF; map 89 uses
  tile 662), where the battle interface writes its own maps (0x5000-0x5FFF)
  and graphics (from 0x8000). A battle cannot hold them; a scene does.
- **How a scene loads its map.** New Game's opening loads map 89 through
  `0x0811C77C` (called from `0x08120B0A` and `0x081275D0`), which hands
  `0x02029D40` to the header parser and sets the layers up. Nothing from
  0x0811C77C to 0x0811CBA0 was in the static build: it is an `[[extra_func]]`
  now, with a hook that, with Battle Map set, writes the chosen number first
  and lets the loader run.
- **The scene script.** Its 122 ops (table `0x08165020`, {routine, argument
  count}) were all missing from the static build: every story scene ran
  interpreted (New Game's opening: 232 dispatch misses, now 5-6; on Android,
  where nothing self-heals, always). All 122 are `[[extra_func]]` now (110
  start with push, 12 are leaf routines after a return or a literal pool).
  Op 23, `0x0811978C`, walks an actor along routes joined from the scene's
  route records and hangs on purpose (`b .` at `0x081197D2`) past 16 steps;
  routes found on a map the scene was not written for overflow it, on every
  map tried. With Battle Map set it answers its own "no such actor" result
  (`0x110`): the actor stays put, the script goes on.
- **The camera.** The map engine's camera is EWRAM `0x02026C78/7A` (x, y; the
  scroll is it less a constant), a copy at +4, and at +8 the point it eases
  to. Moving the camera alone is undone the next frame; moving that point
  (4 px a frame while the D-pad is held, `debug_scene_camera_tick`) lets the
  game ease there and copy the map in as it goes. Only after the scene hook
  ran in this run of the state; in Training's battle the D-pad stays the
  game's.
- **To view a map:** Options > Debug > Battle Map, the number; then New Game
  (or any story scene); the D-pad looks around, A moves the dialogue on.
  Characters stand where the scene puts them.
- Checked with the opening scene: maps 55, 64, 86 and 100 come up whole (the
  castle, the snow forest, the snowy castle, the desert ruins); 2, 57 and
  119 too, out of the opening camera's view until panned. Off: New Game's
  opening byte-identical at +700 and +1500 frames to the build before; both
  invariants; EU and ER under the perspective identical.
- **Tile Info, and the two lists (asked to show the target and the
  tiles' heights for adjustments, and to list the maps Training can show
  apart from the others).** Debug now has **Battle Map** (the 67
  Training can show: 1, 3-56, 104-115, `debug_map_in_training`), **Scene
  Map** (the other 52, through New Game) and **Tile Info**. They share one
  setting; each row steps through its own list and reads "Game's" when the
  map is the other row's. Training takes only a Battle Map one. Tile Info
  (`debug_tile_info`, off) tints the target cell yellow in the scene, so it
  warps with the map, and writes at the view's top left (the warp's flat
  overlay, a 3x5 font): map, cell X/Z, the stored height and the drawn one
  ("TABLE" when a drawn-height entry sets it), the map's byte and the game's
  record, walkable or not, terrain / tree prop / cut-out prop, rounded. The
  target is the game's cursor cell in a battle, and in a story scene the
  cell a third of the way down the middle of the view (the dialogue boxes
  sit lower), which the D-pad moves. Off: both invariants, ER, EK and CM
  (the floating hand shares the overlay) identical.
  Report format that follows from it: "map 55, cell X 6 Z 6 should be drawn N".
- **Live editing (asked for).** With Tile Info
  on, hold **L2**: D-pad **up / down** raise / lower the target cell's drawn
  height one step (repeating after 350 ms, every 120 ms), **A** puts it back
  to the game's. The game sees neither the D-pad nor A while L2 is held (a
  key filter chained after the options menu's, `kol_tile_edit.cpp`), so the
  cursor and the dialogue stay. Each change is written at once to
  `drawn_heights.cfg` beside enhancements.cfg ("map x z height" lines; on
  the Thor `files/drawn_heights.cfg`), read back at launch, and applied by
  the terrain pass over the built-in table (`kDrawnCells`), so the next
  frame is drawn with it (the pass cache's key has the drawn heights). The
  readout marks such a cell "(EDITED)". The file is the hand-over: pulled
  from the Thor, its lines become `kDrawnCells` entries.
  A rounded cell (`kDrawnRounds`) keeps its top at the stored height; an edit
  there moves its foot only.
  Headless: the input replay writes the game's keys after the host's filter,
  so it cannot drive the editor; `KOL_TILE_EDIT_FILE=<path>` loads an edits
  file where there is no settings directory (the desktop), and
  `KOL_TILE_EDIT_HOLD=1` counts L2 as held. Checked: `55 6 6 18` reads
  "DRAWN 18 (EDITED)" and draws the cell at 18; no edits: both invariants,
  ER and EK identical.
- **The scene as a viewer (asked to stop the cutscene from playing
  and give control at once).** Once a story scene has loaded the
  chosen map (`debug_scene_viewer_active`: Battle/Scene Map set, the scene
  hook ran in this run of the state), the scene is held at its first line:
  A, B, Select and Start never reach the game (in `kol_tile_edit`'s key
  filter; the D-pad still does, it moves the camera), and BG2 (the
  dialogue's text), BG3 (its box) and the sprites (its portrait, and the
  scene's characters, out of place on a foreign map) are hidden over the
  Debug > Hide switches, switched only when the viewer turns on or off.
  What is left is the map, the D-pad camera, Tile Info and the editor.
  Loading a state ends it (the state epoch). Off: both invariants, EU, ER, CM
  and New Game's opening identical. The scene is not stopped, only held: the
  script and its interpreter (not found: the ops are reached in a way the
  entry hook does not see) run until the first line and wait there.
- **Broken on most maps once control was given (EX = the user's slot 2,
  map 100).** Two causes, both mine:
  - The D-pad moved only the point the camera eases to. The game eases at
    about half a pixel a frame, so held, the point ran hundreds of pixels
    ahead; the easing's difference wrapped and the camera went the other way
    (EX: camera 101, point 536), and the scene's own camera moves (its
    script pans to 568,672 about 420 frames in) fought it. Now the camera
    and the point move together (not the copy at +4: the game scrolls and
    copies the map in by the camera's step from it), and in the viewer the
    scene's easing is cancelled every frame (its frame count `0x02026C88`
    and rate `0x02026C8C` zeroed, the point pinned to the camera).
  - The widened view's margins come from the composed map
    (`kol_map_source`), which finds the layer's 256-row ring by matching the
    game's drawn cells. Panned near a map edge, too little is drawn to
    match, and it fell back to the raw ring: the map's edge repeated at the
    other side, stale tiles. In the viewer the camera is known, so the
    offset from it to the window's map position is learned on verified
    frames and used when there is nothing to match.
  Checked: the game's frames along pans left, up, right and down show the
  map's real edges against the sky, with no repeats; off: both invariants,
  AS, BR (the margins' own repros), EU and ER identical. Left: a few stale
  tiles of the game's map buffer outside the map's area can show, which the
  game never displays itself. Loading a state ends the viewer (New Game
  again).
- **The D-pad steps a tile, as the game's cursor does (asked for a
  D-pad tap to move one tile whatever its height, as in
  the game).** The viewer keeps a tile cursor (`kol_actions`): a tap moves
  it one cell, held it repeats after 14 frames and then every 6, in the
  game's own directions (measured on ER's cursor: up Z-1, down Z+1, right
  X+1, left X-1). It starts at the cell under the view's middle. Tile Info
  reads that cell. `kol_focus` works out the camera that puts the cell's
  centre, at its drawn height, at the middle of the game's window (hardware
  120, 80): the scroll follows the camera one for one, so kx = A - camera
  and the goal is kx + camera - (120 - (X - Z) / 2), likewise y. The camera
  eases there (a quarter of the way a frame, 1-12 px), moved with its ease
  point. Checked on map 100: three taps right 16 -> 19, two down 13 -> 15,
  the start cell tinted at the view's middle; viewer off: both invariants,
  EU and ER (Tile Info on) identical.
  **The camera shook**: the goal was kx + camera taken every frame, and
  kx (from the sprite slots) trails the camera a frame while it moves, so
  the goal moved with the camera and it chased it. kx + camera is now
  learned once per viewer session, on a frame the camera stood still, and
  the goal changes only when the cell does (logged: goal changes = taps,
  one reversal per axis where the direction changed).
- **Off the field (asked to widen the field's range, remapping
  the outside tiles, byte FF).** A cell off the
  field (not walkable, height 0: byte FF on the maps seen) was never drawn
  (`raw_cell` -1), so the art the game draws around a field (walls, roofs,
  cliffs) had no shape. Given a height (the editor, or `kDrawnCells`), such
  a cell now stands as terrain at it. The viewer's tile cursor reaches every
  cell of the 32 x 32 grid; Tile Info marks these "OFF FIELD". Checked: on
  ER, `55 4 15 12` and `55 5 15 12` stand as a block at the view's bottom
  left in the mesh paint; no edits: both invariants, EU, ER, EK identical.
- **Past the grid, 32 cells on every side (2026-10-05, asked to extend
  the field into negative coordinates too,
  then for a bit more than 16).** The field is now X and Z from -32
  to 63 (`kTileMargin` in `kol_tile_edit.h`, `kTileSide` 96;
  `tile_cell` / `tile_x` / `tile_z` convert). A cell outside the game's
  32 x 32 has no byte, record or flags: it exists only where the editor (or
  `kDrawnCells`) gives it a height, and then stands as terrain like an
  off-field cell. Heights, roofs and boxes save negative cells as written
  (`89 -1 17 3`); the viewer's cursor walks into the margin and Tile Info
  reads "OFF FIELD ... RECORD -1" there.
  - In kol_focus the per-cell arrays (drawn, rounds, heights, the shadow
    casters' heights) are `kGridSide` = 96 across, indexed by `gi(x, z)`;
    everything the game owns (records, props, torches, buildings, the pass
    key) still loops over the game's 32 x 32 only.
  - The field's bounds are the game's grid widened by any margin cell with a
    height. The shadow map covers those bounds only (`g_shadow_x0/z0/w/h`,
    in the shadow key), and shadow rays stop at them, so a map with no
    margin edits builds the same map at the same cost.
  - **Cost, two traps.** The first build was +0.25 ms on the Mac's present
    worker (EM, shadows on); `kTileMargin` 0 against 32 in the same tree
    isolated it, section timers found it. (1) A unit shadow's reach scan
    counted every margin cell it crossed as ground at 0 (no height reads as
    a hole), stretching each unit's shadow region toward the field's edge:
    0.30 -> 0.52 ms, though no extra pixel was shaded. A cell beyond the
    game's grid now counts only if it has a height. (2) The buildings' 36 KB
    component array was allocated per frame (+0.05 ms): kept per thread now.
    The profiler (`sample`) named data symbols for this code and was no use.
  - Verified: 39 renders (13 states x {all effects, Tile Info, the flat
    light}) byte-identical to the build before; both invariants; pass cache
    check 0 on EM and on map 89 with margin cells; worker 6.19 against
    6.16 ms with the sun turning, 6.12 against 6.08 still (noise is about
    0.05 ms).
- `KOL_SAVE_STATE_AT=<frame>[,slot]` (headless, `--window` with dummy video):
  one save state at that frame. The TCP rig cannot stand in: KoL's hooks are
  installed from the frame hook, which does not run under `--tcp`.

### Units' hidden parts lit up when the stick moved the camera (2026-10-15)

Reported on GX (slot 3, map 55): moving the camera with the right stick
showed sprites lit up where other sprites covered them.

part another unit hides in the frame is drawn too, and the stick slides it
into view. The atlas's light loop (kol_perspective) skipped every texel not
the block's own in the frame (`lift[k] != bi + 1`), so those parts kept

skips them); `KOL_PERSP_HIDDEN_UNLIT=1` = old. The light those texels read
is now the card's own: `g_unit_lamp` (lamps on units, dark maps) and the
window light on units (`g_unit_win_patch_a`/`_haze_a`) are kept per atlas
texel, hidden ones included, instead of per screen pixel where a hidden
texel read the front unit's value or none.

both invariants. Mac worker on GX leaned: 5.78 -> 5.81 ms (noise).

### Units above the view flashing at the bottom: the Y byte's other reading (2026-10-15)

Reported from slot 3 three times: a sprite flickering in the bottom-left
corner (GU), a sprite flashing at the bottom while holding right (GW),
and once more on the Thor after two fixes, caught in a screen recording.
All one cause: OAM Y is a byte, so a unit standing above the view (its head
at -108) is byte 148, which also reads as +148. `kol_obj_cull`'s Y provider
picks the reading from the guest's slot list (README "Units did not appear
in the margins"), and three things made it pick wrong for a frame:

- **The slot was gone** (GU): slots go by call order, not by unit, and on
  some frames the slot that recorded unit 4 held another unit while OAM
  still carried unit 4's sprites, unchanged. The lookup found nothing and
  fell back to the hardware reading (+148): the head at the bottom left,
  every animation step (with the perspective on: the overscan rows show the
  margin, and the unclaimed sprite went to interface). Now each OAM entry
  keeps the row it was last resolved to while its three attributes stay
  exactly the same, forgotten when the entry changes and on a state load
  (`KOL_OBJY_NO_STICKY=1`). A first version kept rows across loads and
  changes; a stray piece then stayed on screen until the app restarted (GV).
- **The cursor's slot made it ambiguous** (GW, the mage at frame 72 of the
  scroll): the grid cursor's slot sat on the byte-wrapped row of a unit
  256 rows above it, so the near search found two answers and declined. The
  cursor's slot is no unit's (its sprites never match it): left out of the
  table (`KOL_OBJY_CURSOR_SLOT=1` = old).
- **Continuity**, for what was left (the Thor recording, frame 107: the
  mage's head at the bottom edge while scrolling; not reproduced on the
  Mac): a sprite cannot move 256 rows in a frame. When an entry's row is
  over 64 from the same sprite's last frame (same tile and palette, x within
  16) and the other reading is within 64, the other reading is taken. Frame
  to frame only, reset on a state load (`KOL_OBJY_NO_CONTINUITY=1`). On its
  own it removes every case above. It may override the lookup two frames
  running at most: every case it fixed lasted one frame, and a sprite that
  truly jumps ~200 rows (the camera snapping) was otherwise held at the
  wrong reading, each frame compared with the last frame's wrong row.

Checked: both invariants; the fixes on vs off identical over AQ, AR, AS,
BV, CH, CJ, CK, CL, CM, CP, S_move_highlight, BL, B_rictor, EM (perspective
on and off, 40 frames each); GU no blip in 300 frames; GW's scroll changes
only the flash frames. `g_declined_high` (KOL_OBJY_STATS) counts only raw
bytes >= 160, so it never saw these (byte 148): count where the lookup
gives up, whatever the byte.

How these were found: present dumps and a one-frame blip test (a frame
unlike both neighbours that match each other); while scrolling, which that
test cannot see, a per-frame log of what the Y provider answered; on the
Thor, `adb shell screenrecord` (mp4; the raw-frames mode hangs) decoded on
the Mac by a Swift AVAssetReader script (no ffmpeg here), the neighbours
aligned by a shift search before the same test. Not fixed (the user judged
it minor): the first frame after a load is the native 240x160
on the desktop's `--load-state` path; on the Thor a load shows the camera
easing for 3-4 frames and the cursor's hand missing for 3.

**Then a green scrap stuck in the bottom-right corner** (the Thor, after
these fixes: the stray sprite part was back, reappearing just from
scrolling around with the left stick; HA = slot 3, where it was already
gone on load). It sat at the same screen place whatever the camera did,
crisp and unlit, at 384x216 game (248, 168). That is where the guest
**parks** every OAM entry it does not use, as an 8x8 (`a0=00A8`,
`a1=00F8`, tile 0): off its 240x160, but inside the widened view's
bottom-right margin, hidden only because the hardware reads byte 168 as
-88. Reproduced on the Mac with `KOL_STICK_TEST` (HA, the stick swept in 16
directions at 384x216, 847 presents in): a unit's lower half stood exactly
at (248, 168) for two frames, its slot's prediction matched every parked
entry exactly, and the kept row (the GU fix) then held them all at 168 for
as long as they stayed parked, which in a battle is for good. With the
perspective off it was in the game frame too, so this was the Y provider,
not the warp. The Thor trace said nothing because it left the parked
entries out. Now an 8x8 at the park spot always keeps the hardware's
reading (the slot list predicts 16x16 unit halves only, so it is never a
recorded sprite), and continuity leaves it alone
(`KOL_OBJY_PARKED_OLD=1` = old). Checked: the scrap gone in all 1700
presents of that sweep (old: from 847 to the end); GU byte-identical
old/new over 300 presents; both invariants. One wrong guess on the way: a
unit 224 px off the left drawn at +288 by the X fallback. The trace's
units at `a1=4120` were real, at their recorded X.

## Making the return from View List quick (2026-10-06)

Asked to investigate the stutter and make the transition smooth and
quick (FN = the user's slot 1: the castle battle, the
command menu on View List; A, then B to come back: a 0.9 s hold on the
faded list before the map fades back in).

**What the 54 frames were.** This game runs its logic from the VBlank
handler: in normal play half the cycles sit at IRQ nesting depth 1, and the
main loop (depth 0) only idles. A handler step longer than a frame never
yields, so no present reaches the host until it is done: the picture holds
and the sound driver runs in nested handlers (depth 2) meanwhile. Found with
a cycle-weighted PC histogram over the stall (gbarecomp DEBUG.md "Where a
long guest stall goes"; `KOL_PC_HIST=<lo>,<hi>,<path>` with
`GBARECOMP_INSN_TRACE=1`), and the function-entry log beside it
(`.entries`: pc, depth, sp, cycles), which gave the steps:

| frames | step |
|---|---|
| 16.5 | BIOS HuffUnComp (`0x1014`), the tileset, bit by bit |
| 1.7 | BIOS LZ77UnComp (`0x10FC`) |
| 5.5 | three A7 archive entries (`0x08004990`, the reader `0x08004E2C`) |
| 3.6 | `0x08002F92`, a byte-at-a-time memset, 47 and 53 KB |
| 16.3 | `0x080221B4`, a per-cell table over the map's diamond |
| 2.8 | `0x0802714C`, the height grid and the map-source arrays |
| 4.1 | `0x0805D6E4`, a table from the units |
| ~4 | the rest (the handler's own entries, a short step at +20) |

(The IWRAM loop at `0x03003800` that first looked like the composer is the
MP2K sound mixer: it runs every frame, at depth 2 during the stall.)

**Fast Loading** (Options > Advanced; in the Enhanced preset, off in
Original and by default; `src/kol_fast_load.cpp`). Each step with an
exact native equivalent runs natively, the same bytes landing in the same
places and the guest clock not moving, so the game takes the next step in
the same frame:

- *The BIOS decompressors*, through the runtime's opt-in `g_bios_hle_hook`
  for SWIs 0x11-0x13 only (gbarecomp `bios_hle_service_decompress`; its
  Huffman now declines a width it cannot do instead of reporting it done).
  Turning HLE mode on for everything was not an option: Div/Sqrt/affine/
  MidiKey2Freq would go through host float math.
- *The A7 decoder*, through a hook on `0x08004990` and the transcription in
  `kol_a7.cpp`: bytes to `[0x030029F4] + [0x030029F0]` while the count + 1
  is under `[0x030029F8]`, the count updated, 1 returned, the bytes decoded
  to `*r2` when set; a stream the transcription declines is left to the game.
- *memset8* (`0x08002F92`: strb, r0++, r1--, while r1 > 0 signed), only for
  4096 bytes and up: the small clears every frame (32 to 968 bytes) stay the
  game's, because sped up they moved the game's own mid-frame writes and one
  frame of FN showed a band of rows changed.
- *Three pure steps memoised.* The runtime's read/write-set recorder showed
  `0x080221B4`, `0x0802714C` and `0x0805D6E4` read EWRAM (and a little IWRAM
  and ROM), write EWRAM and their own stack frame, and touch no I/O, VRAM or
  DMA. A run is recorded: the bytes it reads before writing them (its
  inputs, with their values at entry) and the bytes it writes (at return),
  r0-r3 and the flags. A later call with the same r0-r3 whose input bytes
  all hold their recorded values would take the same path: the outputs are
  written and the call returns at once; else it runs and is recorded. The
  call sites are the rebuild (`0x080485xx`), the battle's first build
  (`0x080481xx`, `0x08047Dxx`) and the deployment's unit changes
  (`0x0805FE3A`); each site's next instruction is a function entry of its
  own, hooked, where a recording ends; a call from elsewhere runs as the
  game's. The memo is kept on disk (`files/fast_load_memo.bin`, up to 64
  entries, ~25 KB each; the desktop `KOL_FAST_LOAD_MEMO=<path>`), so a map
  recorded once serves every later session, the first return included.
  Results under 2 KB are not kept; the file is written a few seconds after
  a recording, not at each.

**Result** (FN, the Mac): the hold 54 -> 26 frames with the decoders and the
memset, -> **6 frames** once the three steps hit (the first return in a
session with no memo file records them: 26). 0.9 s -> 0.1 s. The second
return of the same session, and the first of the next, hit.

**Verified.** `KOL_FAST_LOAD_CHECK=1` (with `GBARECOMP_INSN_TRACE=1`): each
hook works out its result, declines, and the bytes are compared the moment
the routine returns (a PC watch on its LR; compared from the frame hook
instead, a present between two blocks of a routine at depth 0 saw a
half-written A7 entry and said MISMATCH). All 169 states at 900 frames, the
FN replay and New Game's opening to the name entry: 16 decompressions,
~2,500 A7 entries, 35 big memsets, 0 mismatches; a memo hit in check mode
runs the routine anyway and compares. Memory after the return, the game's
own run against a memo-hit run (`KOL_MEM_DUMP=<frame>,<path>`): the BG
tileset, every tilemap, the palette, the composed map, the height grid and
the three routines' outputs byte-identical; only the units' sprite frames,
an animated tile and the sound state differ (the fast run is 34 task-frames
ahead). With the setting off: 300 of 300 FN presents identical to before,
both invariants, EM 3.95 ms a frame against 3.92 (the recorder's idle
branch on every bus access).

**Measured on the Thor** (2026-10-06, 15:19, the user's own play, three
View List round trips each way, 384x216 with the Enhanced effects). Every
hold of more than 3 frames is logged, setting on or off: `hold: N frames
(a..b), M ms, fast loading on|off` in logcat (`fast_load_present()`; the
present is gbarecomp's `g_runtime_presented_frame`, because the frame hook
runs at every guest frame, held or not):

| Fast Loading | back from View List | into View List |
|---|---|---|
| off | 53, 52, 53 frames: 883, 866, 883 ms | 4 frames, 67 ms |
| on (memo hit) | 5, 5, 6 frames: 78, 78, 100 ms | none |

About 0.8 s less on each return, ~10x. The Thor holds exactly 16.7 ms a
held frame either way: it emulates the load faster than real time and the
pacer waits out the rest, so the wait is the game's frame count alone and
cutting frames is the only lever. The memo file the user's first try saved
(3 entries) hit on every return.

**The sound through the hold** is fine as it was: windowed play hands audio
to SDL's queue as the guest makes it, so the queue grows while the host
emulates the hold faster than real time and drains during the pacer's wait;
the music never skipped. (On the Thor that holds as long as the device
emulates the hold faster than real time: `GBARECOMP_AUDIO_PROBE=1` in
`files/env.cfg` logs underruns.)

**Not done:** the game's own fade-out and fade-in around the hold (its ~15
frames each) are left as they are; the remaining 6 frames are the handler's
own steps.

## The pauses on every battle action (2026-10-19)

Reported: on Thor slot 2, every action slowed everything
down (HX = the user's slot 2, map 2 in the rain, an enemy phase about to
run). Measured first, on the Mac at 480x270 with the frame-phase CSV and
on the Thor from its own `hold:` lines in logcat:

- Between actions the game runs at 60 fps with room to spare (Mac guest
  7.4 ms a frame, worker 3.7 ms). Nothing is slow.
- Each action step is a **hold**: the game's VBlank handler runs one
  routine for 4-8 frames without returning, so no frame is presented and
  the picture freezes for 67-125 ms. Nine of them in the 280 frames after
  the load, 49 frames in all. The Mac and the Thor hold the SAME frames
  for the same counts, and the Thor's wall time is exactly 16.7 ms a frame:
  it is the game's own work, paced faithfully, not emulator slowness.
  Fast Loading on or off changes one hold by one frame (its memset).
- What the holds are (cycle histogram + entry log, `KOL_PC_HIST` with
  `GBARECOMP_INSN_TRACE=1`, spans by stack pointer): five routines, each
  walking the map's 1024-cell table at `0x02010440` (24 bytes a cell,
  the height grid `0x02016440` right after it; `KOL_RW_FN` read sets):

  | routine | frames | reads | writes |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `0x0804C5D8` (under `0x0804DB8C`) | 5.6 | height grid, 11 map objects' 13 bytes | a 16 KB table at `0x020387C4`: a reach/flood map |
  | `0x08024CA0` | 2.6 | the cell table | BG0/BG1 mirror rows `0x02008858`.. in a diamond: a tile redraw |
  | `0x0802411C` (under `0x0805B380`) | 3.2 | the cell table | small |
  | `0x0808CDE8` | 5.4 | the cell table + grid | 5 KB |
  | `0x080867BC` | 4.0 | the cell table + grid | 4 KB |

  Their inner "functions" (`0x08024CBA`, `0x080250D0`, `0x080254E8`,
  `0x0802415C`, `0x080246E4`...) are loop labels of the same routines,
  entered 6144 and 24576 times a call.
- The GBA pauses here too: the recompiled code charges one cycle an
  instruction plus data waits, which is no harsher than the hardware's
  ROM fetches, so the cartridge holds at least as long.

**Dead ends, so they are not re-proposed.**
- Today's pacing commit (gbarecomp 41ca6b7, frames inside a handler paced
  one by one) did not lengthen them: before it the next present paced all
  N frames in one wait (`kMaxCatchFrames` is 120). Same total.
- Running the held frames unpaced (the pause shrinks to compute time,
  ~40%) is the behaviour before 2026-09-29: the music rushed and crackled
  whenever things happened on screen, and the user had it fixed.
- The Fast Loading memo (results keyed on the inputs) would rarely hit:
  the inputs are the unit positions, which change every action.

**Fast Actions** (asked to remove the holds through this lever; Options >
Advanced > Fast Actions, `fast_actions=`, in the Enhanced preset, off in
Original and by default; `src/kol_fast_actions.cpp`). No transcription:
the game's own recompiled code does the work and the **guest clock is held
while it runs**. gbarecomp's `g_runtime_clock_frozen` (ENHANCEMENTS.md "A
guest clock that does not move") makes `runtime_tick` only count the
cycles: no device is pumped, no IRQ delivered, no scanline moves. The bytes
the routine leaves are its own by construction; only the time it took is
gone, so the handler finishes its step in the same frame and the next
frame is presented on time. The runtime's function-entry hook (chained
after the terrain probe's and the strike camera's) starts a run at a listed
routine's entry, keeping its stack pointer, and ends it at the first entry
at or above that pointer (the routine has returned: its caller's next call,
or a return further up). Every listed routine begins with a push, so no
entry inside it is at its own level. A cap of 60 frames lets time run again
should a run never end (a wait on VCOUNT or DMA inside it; none has one),
counted and logged.

The list (the table above, plus the enemy's turn): `0x0804C5D8`,
`0x08024CA0`, `0x0802411C`, `0x0808CDE8`, `0x080867BC`, and `0x0809B5AC`
(BL, the enemy choosing: 2.8-3.0 frames, reached through `0x0809E71C` and
`0x0809CE80` / `0x0809C224`). Admission rules, checked with `KOL_RW_FN`
and the check mode: no I/O but IME (three of them write IME 0 and 1 around
a critical section; with the clock held no interrupt is pending anyway),
and **a routine that is called only for the long work**: listing the
enclosing step `0x0809E71C` instead held the clock 207 times in one enemy
turn, 0.06 frame each (it is the AI's every-frame step; the reach map is
called from inside it), a timing change where no pause was. Count a
candidate's calls and their lengths (the entry log) before listing it.

**Verified.**
- HX, 420 frames, Fast Actions on: the nine holds are gone (no `hold:`
  line; before, 49 frames in nine holds). Each run logged
  (`KOL_FAST_ACTIONS_LOG=1`; `KOL_FAST_ACTIONS_CHECK=1` records its reads
  and writes and reports I/O): reach map 4.4 frames skipped in 12 ms of
  host time on the Mac, tile redraw 1.9-2.1 in 4-5 ms, the cell passes
  2.4-3.8 in 5-10 ms; none tripped the cap.
- A sweep with it on: BL (enemy turn, reach map 9.6 frames there, 24 ms),
  GC (enemy hits Alphonse), BV / S / GD with A pressed every 100 frames
  (an attack confirmed, a move range, a spell): no hold left. GN, EM, HT
  idle: no run (nothing happens); HT's one 14-frame hold is a scene load
  (the memoised grid `0x0802714C` and a map build under the IRQ: Fast
  Loading's domain, not an action).
- Both render invariants unchanged (240 `66e13ab2`, anchor-off 284
  `9054c456`); off, nothing runs but a compare per function entry.

**What it changes besides the pause:** the game counts fewer frames
through an action (its frame counter and anything timed by it, the RNG if
it steps per frame), as Fast Loading already does for loads. On the Thor
the host still computes the routine (about twice the Mac's time: the
reach map on BL would be ~50 ms, two or three late frames instead of ten
frozen); the game's own code speed is the limit now.

## Fast walking and quick enemy turns (2026-10-19)

Asked for a faster enemy turn, then specifically for quicker enemy
movement and decisions rather than a fast forward (FF mutes everything),
and for fast walking for every team. Options > Advanced > **Fast Walking** (`fast_walk`) and **Quick
Enemy Turns** (`quick_enemy`), both in the Enhanced preset, off in Original
and by default.

**Where an enemy's turn went** (BL, a per-frame log headless: camera, the
acting object `[0x0202A5F0]`, the phase byte `0x0202A82E`, which objects
moved; no pictures), per enemy: the camera pans to it (10-33 frames), it
stands still in phase 0x02 about 100-130 frames, then twice about 45
(its range shown, the cursor taken to where it goes, with two 17-frame
0x1A stretches), then walks (phase 0x15: 2 world units a frame, 16 frames
a cell, 10-frame stops between straight runs), then attacks.

**What runs then.** The battle's phase task `0x0202A5B0` is stepped once a
frame by `0x0806B640`, which switches on its mode byte (table `0x0806B75C`)
to one of eight handlers, each `adds r0, r2, #0; bl handler; b exit`:
case 4 `0x0806AA44` is the enemy AI (the first ~100 still frames: it runs
once a frame, about a tenth of a frame of work each, so the decision is
spread over frames, not a timer); case 6 `0x08065B20` is the action
executor (the ~45-frame waits, and the walk: down through `0x08065888`,
`0x0805EB4C`, `0x0805D390`, `0x0805BEA8` to the mover `0x0805CC64`, which
writes the object's X and hop, `0x0805C8F0` its Z).

**The lever** (`src/kol_fast_actions.cpp`; game.toml hooks on the resume
entries after the two bl's, `0x0806B7A2` and `0x0806B7B2`): the hook
declines, or in the right phase sends R15 back to the case's own `adds`
(`0x0806B79C`, `0x0806B7AC`) with r2 = the task, so the game itself calls
the handler again in the same frame (a real bl, returning to the hook the
normal way; no hand-made return address, see the hook-tail-call trap). The
guest clock is held over the repeats, so the frame keeps its length and
everything else (the camera, the other tasks, the sprites' animation, the
sound driver) still runs once a frame: the music and the effects keep
their speed and pitch. Per frame:
- walking (phase 0x15), any unit: 2 calls (`KOL_FAST_WALK_X`);
- the enemy AI deciding (case 4, phase 0x02): 8 calls (`KOL_QUICK_ENEMY_X`);
- the executor's waits in phase 0x02 while a unit not on the player's side
  acts (record +0x5D bit 7: enemies and guests): 4 calls
  (`KOL_QUICK_SHOW_X`), so the range and the cursor are still seen.
The hook ends a Fast Actions run that its handler started (the resume
entry's hook runs before the entry hook that would end it), and Fast
Actions starts no run while the clock is already held.

**Measured** (BL, headless, Fast Loading and Fast Actions on in both):
| | off | on |
|---|---|---|
| the enemy phase | 4039 frames (67 s) | 2552 frames (43 s) |
| frames walking | 665 | 326 |
| a player unit's one-cell walk (S_move_highlight) | 16 | 8 |
No cap trip; FULLY_STATIC; both render invariants unchanged (240
`66e13ab2`, anchor-off 284 `9054c456`); with the options off BL's enemy
phase is frame for frame the build's before.

**The battle does not replay as on the cartridge.** The game steps its
random number generator (`0x0813B0CC`, an LCG at `0x02028E24`) once every
frame from its main loop (caller `0x08000732`; 100 writes in 100 frames on
BL), so any change in the number of frames (Fast Loading, Fast Actions, and
this) changes the draws after it: on BL the enemies acted in another order.
Every choice is still the game's own, as when a player presses a button a
frame later.


## Fast attacks (2026-10-26)

Asked for a Fast Attacks switch to go with Fast Walking. Options > Gameplay > **Fast Attacks** (`fast_attack`, in the Enhanced
preset). An attack's strike (the combat camera, phase byte `0x0202A82E` =
0x10; BV: 300 frames, the hit, the number, GUARD and the counter) is stepped
once a frame by the battle task's step `0x08060870` (`bl 0x08088E58` with the
battle entries and the striker's index), but repeating that step as Fast
Walking does the walk left it 300 frames: the step waits on the actors'
animation players (`0x0805E318` per actor), which run elsewhere once a frame.
The user's pick of three ways: the strike's own frames at 2x, its sound
kept.

While the strike's step runs (seen at its entry), the game runs two frames
to a presented one: gbarecomp `g_runtime_guest_speed` (fast-forward's render
skip and fresh-latch presenting, paced as one frame). Over every second
frame the sound stands still: the sound hardware is paused
(`GbaAudio::set_paused`: no samples, no FIFO pops) and the MP2K driver's two
per-frame routines are skipped, SoundVSync (`0x0815BE18`, from the VBlank
handler, decides the frame: hooked in `kol_fast_actions.cpp`) and SoundMain
(`0x0815B838`, the mix, already hooked for the options menu). The sound then
lives one frame per presented frame: the music and the effects keep their
tempo and pitch and the HD render its ticks.

The first build ran every tick and left the other frames' samples out
(`GbaAudio::set_output_muted`, removed); the user on the Thor reported odd
audio during attack animations. Which samples came from the driver's stale
buffer did not line up with the frames: the loudness pulsed every third
frame and HD covered ~56% of the strike. Paused, on BV's strike (HD): the
frame-to-frame loudness roughness 0.118 (off: 0.128), sharp jumps 0.14 per
1000 samples (off: 0.15), HD covered 98.8% as off, nothing degraded. BV's
strike: 300 guest frames in 150 presents. Off (the default, the Original
preset), nothing changes; the 240 invariant holds.

As with Fast Walking, the game's random numbers are stepped once a frame,
so later draws differ from the cartridge's.

## Fast spells (2026-11-02)

Asked for spells to be sped up like attacks and movement, with a Fast
Spells option. Options > Gameplay >
**Fast Spells** (`fast_spells`, in the Enhanced preset, off in Original),
after Fast Attacks.

**What a cast is.** A per-frame trace of the phase byte (`0x0202A82E`, the
phase task's mode) and the two spell routines the spell camera already
watches. In game frames from the load of GD (Ice Javelin; A on Cast at 12):

| Frames | Mode | |
|---|---|---|
| 36-163 | 0x1D | the spell's name box ("Ice Javelin"), 128 frames |
| 172-240 | 0x24 | the camera to the caster |
| 241-294 | 0x24 | the charge (`0x080AC5C8` once a frame) |
| 296-646 | 0x24 | the effect (`0x080AC608` once a frame) |
| 647-680 | 0x24 | the way back |
| 687-827 | 0x3C | "1 EXP earned.", as after an attack |

Mode 0x24 is the spell's animation, as 0x10 is an attack's strike. The same
on IF (Crag Crush: its effect alone 786 frames), ID, IB (a heal) and JQ (a
spell that brings rain: a second stretch of 0x24, 315 frames, is its storm
rolling in). An item's use is the same mode (states/thor/0069, the item
"CURE": 366 frames), so Fast Spells takes items' uses too.

**How.** Fast Attacks' way (above): while the mode is 0x24, the game runs
two frames to a presented one, and over every second frame the sound
hardware stands still and the MP2K driver is skipped, so the music and the
effects keep their tempo and pitch. The byte is read only on a frame where
the phase task's dispatcher `0x0806B640` ran (off the battle map that
EWRAM is not the task's). The name box and the EXP box keep their pace, as
an attack's do. Ice Javelin's 508 frames take 254 presents (picture 330 on
is picture 488 off). A dispatcher frame missed inside a cast (IB, JQ) plays
that one frame at normal speed. `KOL_FAST_ACTIONS_LOG=1` logs "spell at 2x
for N frames". Off: the 52 check renders and both invariants unchanged.

Not seen: an enemy's spell (no state with one); the enemy's attacks go
through the same task, so it should be the same mode. As with Fast Attacks,
later random draws differ from the cartridge's.

### A spell's numbers and sprites vanished on its card (2026-11-02)

Reported: after a heal, the number over the head vanished much too
quickly, with Fast Spells on or off (states/thor/0081, an item's heal,
A at the load + 20). The game keeps the number up 84 frames (its object at
`[0x0202AFCC]`, from 401 to 484 after the load), and the 240x160 picture
and the wide one without the perspective show "50" all along; with the
perspective it was never drawn while the spell camera was on, only in its
last frames, once the camera let go. The cause: during the spell camera,
every interface pixel goes onto the spell's card (`ScenePixels::
spell_card`, moved and scaled onto its target), and gbarecomp drew a card
pixel only where the frame differs from the scene the mesh draws. That is
right for the effect's BG2/BG3 (the scene leaves them out) and wrong for a
sprite, which the scene holds too: every interface sprite on the card was
dropped. Crag Crush's rocks and dust and its damage number too (IF,
pictures 500 and 700), so any spell's damage number shown under its
camera.

Now a sprite's card pixel is 2, drawn from the frame whatever the scene
shows (gbarecomp ENHANCEMENTS "The card's sprite pixels"): the heal's "50"
rises at picture 404 and stays to 486 over the healed unit, moving with
the camera as it eases back; Crag Crush's dust and "46" show on their
target. `KOL_SPELL_CARD_SPRITES_AS_BG=1`: as before (byte-identical to the
old picture). Ice Javelin's effect (BG2) mid-cast is unchanged, the 52
check renders and both invariants too. With Fast Spells the number's 84
frames are at 2x as the rest of the cast, as an attack's number is with
Fast Attacks.

## Our own rain (2026-10-26)

Asked to hide the game's rain effect and make our own.
Options > Graphics > **New Rain** (`own_rain`, in the Enhanced preset, off
in Original). The game draws ten 8x8 drop sprites in screen space (the
particle table before the weather block `0x0202A1C0`); under the
perspective they stayed flat over a picture that moves. Ours live in the
world (`kol_rain.cpp`).

- **Each drop** has a landing place fixed on the map (X - Z, X + Z), tiled
  over a box around the view so it stays put while the camera pans, and
  falls 420 units from the ground there at 22 units a frame (times its own
  0.8..1.15), along a slight slant (3 units along X and 3 back along Z per
  34 up: right on screen). It is placed the way the warp places the world
  (`corner_at` / `row_drawn` in kol_perspective: s = K / (K + dref - d),
  the pitch, the combat camera's zoom), or at scale 1 with the light
  without the perspective (`flat_provider`). A streak is 28 units long,
  alpha 0.38 x s (capped), soft across (a pixel each side), fading to its
  top, colour (214, 222, 234).
- **The ground** under a drop: the highest top face the scene shows in each
  8-unit square of the world (a top face's pixel back in the world by its
  height), else the scene's mean height. **Splashes**: where the landing is
  seen (the flat frame's pixel there is a top face at that height, nothing
  lifted over it), a ring spreading for 6 frames and two droplets thrown up
  for 3.
- **The game's intensity** (block +6, 0..2, while its drops fall:
  `ScenePixels::rain_level`): the user's picks from the mockups, counted
  over the 384x216 view, **0 = 130 drops, 1 = 300, 2 = 600 with 2.2 times
  the slant**. A density in the world, so 480x270 shows more.
- **Drawn** over the warped scene, after the disc depth of field (so the
  drops stay sharp) and under the HUD: gbarecomp `PresentWarpMesh::over_xy`,
  plain coloured triangles with a straight alpha per corner (ENHANCEMENTS
  "Coloured triangles over the warp"). Faded with the scene
  (`scene_bright`).
- **The game's drops are left out** (kol_obj_cull `own_rain_hides`: the
  sprites at the live particles' places, Y off the screen) only while the
  last picture drew ours, so where ours cannot draw (no scene composed, the
  authentic view, a provider that bails out) the game's stay. The flag is
  set once at the end of a picture (`RainFrame`): the game's frame is
  composed while the worker runs, and a flag cleared at the start of each
  picture let the game's drops through on most frames (GN, first build).
  The particles still move and draw their random numbers: only the picture
  changes. Plant sway still reads the rain (`rain_of` needs a live drop in
  the table, which is untouched).

**Mockups first** (`tools/mockup/rain.py` over a GN present dump with
`KOL_RAIN_MOCKUP=1`, no drops at all, and the camera from `KOL_RAIN_CAM=1`;
`tools/mockup/frames_to_mp4.swift` for motion): 1800 drops was slightly too
much rain; 550 then 260 for the low levels still too much; the final
counts above, and a bit more angle for intensity 2. GN is intensity 1.

**Then, from the Thor** (JM = the user's slot 2, the ship at night in the
heaviest rain): the rain was too fast, too uniform in direction and
not random enough. Now 13 units a frame (was 22) times a drop's own
0.7..1.3; every fall of a drop comes down somewhere new (its landing,
slant, length 0.7..1.3 and strength 0.7..1.2 hashed from the drop and the
fall: one landing each drop made a steady pattern), its slant the wind's
times 1 +- 0.4, +- 0.06 per unit up; and the wind gusts over some seconds
(1 + 0.45 sin + 0.25 sin, the slant's 0.3..1.7).

**Lit by the lights** (asked for the rain's transparency to depend on
light): on a dark map (`ScenePixels::dark` < 1) each streak and splash
takes the light at its place in the world from the frame's lights
(kol_focus `g_scene_lamps` -> `ScenePixels::lamps`: torches, flames, pots,
a map's lamps carried by its units, with their flicker): strength
max(dark, 0.35) + 1.5 x the lamps' sum, up to 1.3, a lamp reaching 1.75
times its ground reach, and up to 0.6 of the lamps' colour (orange, blue,

every drop. Day maps unchanged; `KOL_RAIN_LIGHT=0` off. The user's pick of

**The old rain at first after a load** (the user, loading JM): the weather

**A portrait hung under its frame** (JN = the user's slot 3, map 58's
