## 56 fps on a battle map (2026-11-02)

The user, after the snow's measurement, asked to find what was
holding back performance. Map 34 held 56 fps on the Thor with neither the
guest thread (~25 M cycles a frame, ~9 ms at 2.8 GHz) nor the present
workers busy (the pipeline's `[present-pipeline]` line: 0 late pictures in
every 600), the GPU at 16% (550 of 680 MHz), the big cores capped only to
2.71 of 2.80 GHz at 70-83 C. The same as GN's 56.5 in the 10-19 backlog.

- **The display runs at 120 Hz** (mode 2). SurfaceFlinger's present times
  for the game's layer: 107 of 126 intervals two refreshes, but 7 of four or
  five (33-42 ms), sometimes followed by a one: stalls in bursts, in whole
  frames.
- **An 8 s `atrace`** (sched, freq, gfx, view; parsed on the Mac): in a long
  gap the guest thread (Thread-4) slept ~21-24 ms (a normal gap: 8, mostly
  inside `eglSwapBuffers`, which blocks ~7.5 ms a frame on the 120 Hz vsync),
  woken by its timer: the frame pacer waiting out two frames for one present.
- **Two frames for one present, yet no lag:** a count in gbarecomp (removed
  after) found on the Mac, from 0097 with no input, 13-29 of every 600
  presents covering two frames, every one a yield after the frame's end,
  while no VBlank went without a yield. The present-in-place hook presented
  when the PPU's frame counter had moved; the counter turns at line 228, the
  yield comes after line 160 once the game is out of its VBlank handler.
  When that handler runs past the end of VBlank (~5% of frames here), the
  present counted two frames and the next VBlank's was skipped.

Fixed in gbarecomp (ENHANCEMENTS "One present a VBlank, counted by the
VBlank"): a present for each VBlank yielded at. **Thor, same view: 59.6 fps**
(was 56.2), no gaps of four or five refreshes, 0 two-frame presents in
every 600, cycles per frame unchanged (guest 24.2 M, workers 24.8 M). The
game was never lagging: it was our runner dropping a picture. Desktop: with
no effects on, the same pictures plus the skipped ones (0097: 3 in 120); our
per-picture effects (the rain's drops, the snow, the camera's easing) now
step on every frame. Both invariants unchanged.
`GBARECOMP_PRESENT_BY_FRAME=1`: as before. Tools: `atrace -z -b 32768 -t 8
sched freq gfx view audio dalvik -a com.koldecomp.game` on the device,
zlib after the `TRACE:` header, a parser of `sched_switch` /
`sched_waking` / `tracing_mark_write` for the guest thread's states and
wakers between `eglSwapBuffers`.

### Options > Graphics > Smooth Pacing (2026-11-02)

Reported: watching the snow, frames seemed to drop at times,
after the fix above. SurfaceFlinger's times over 12 s: 59.72 fps, but 697 of
727 intervals two refreshes, 19 three, 11 one. The Thor's panel runs at 120
Hz: the GBA's 59.7275 Hz frames drift across its refreshes, so one frame
stays a refresh longer every ~1.6 s, and while their times sit near a
refresh, frames land on either side of it (3, 1, 3, 1). Offered: present at
the display's 60 Hz (smooth; the game 0.46% faster), or keep the GBA's rate
and only steady the jitter. The user: as an option. Built:

- **Smooth Pacing** (`smooth_pacing`, on in Enhanced and by default, off in
  Original): gbarecomp `runtime_set_frame_rate(60)`, else the GBA's. The
  audio bridge follows the rate: the music 0.46% faster and 8 cents higher
  (keeping the pitch exact would need a time-stretch; not done).
- In gbarecomp, either way: each frame goes to the display with the time it
  is due (`eglPresentationTimeANDROID`), and with Smooth Pacing the pacer's
  period is two of the panel's own refreshes, read from Android's
  Choreographer, the time on the middle of a refresh interval at least 7 ms
  ahead (gbarecomp ENHANCEMENTS "A game-set frame rate, locked to the
  display's refreshes").

On the Thor: present times and an exact 60 Hz first, 723 of 733 two
refreshes and five 3-1 pairs (the panel ~0.05% fast against the clock: the
frames crept across its refreshes, and the five came only 0.5-0.8 ms before
their time); then locked to the panel, **733 of 733 two refreshes**. Still
not fully smooth to the user: the next section.

### The snow stood still a picture, then jumped (2026-11-02)

With every picture two refreshes, the flakes still hitched. What they step by
is the capture's serial (`Capture::serial`, the frame hook's count, kol_focus

12 of 0, in pairs (2, 0). The frame hook counts at a frame's start (line
228); a present the game yields to late, in the next frame's visible lines
(its VBlank handler ran past VBlank, the case of the section above), read

### Map 62: light through the window, and its shadows (2026-10-29)

Asked for most of the light to come in from the open windows, without
shading the room too much. The
castles' window light (godrays, kMapWindows) was put on map 62 first as it
is: the two windows of the back wall (its inner face Z 32, from a focus
dump of the model: the left X 51-90, Y 33-70, its shutters open; the right
X 183-233, slats drawn), the room dark at 0.75 (kDarkMaps). The user
found it box-shaped and asked for a wide cone spreading from the left
window, with only faint light from the right one; then drew the rays
(`shots/attic62`, from the window down to the rug), asking for something
like the godrays; the cone's tip too narrow, to cover the whole window;
units to cast shadows (they still had their blob); realigned and widened a
little to reach the left wall; and the aim: more shadow and light for some
dynamism, light through the railing, the shelf shadowing the tight corner,
units casting shadows; then slightly softer shadow edges.

A window with a `spread` (MapWindow::spread, gain; map 62's only) lets its
light in as a cone (kol_focus):
- On surfaces (window_sun_at, window_aperture): the opening grown by
  spread x t with rounded corners and an edge kConeSoft x that soft, strong
  kConeGain, fading over kConeFade. Each point is tested toward five spots
  of the opening, kConeSoftR apart (lit by the share clear: soft-edged
  shadows, softer the further they fall); toward the opening, not along the
  sun's way (the window's wall, with no hole in the model, stood in the way
  of all but the window's own projection, and the cone never spread); the
  window's own wall (kWindowWallDepth) is not tested.
- In the air: kConeShaftCount shafts from across the whole opening, fanning
  within the cone to the floor (ConeShaft, cone_shafts_at): godrays; they
  end at the first wall or furniture or where they leave the room's floor
  (they lit the air outside the open front), fading over their way to the
  floor all the same (cut short, they faded twice as fast). They lay a
  little light where they pass (cone_shafts_on). The beams' grid only adds
  a faint fill (kConeVolume), sampled every kConeStep units (2 took ~0.4 s
  a sun).
- The room's model stops the light (model_occluder, map 62 too); the
  railing's faces carry kModelLightPass (tools/models/model.py LIGHTPASS):
  they stop the light that lands (its posts' stripes on the floor) but not
  the beams in the air (solid_hard_at).
- Units cast shadows from it (cast_window_shadows: their card shadows
  along the light, a little softer than the sun's, 0.09, taken out of the
  window's light) and lose the game's blob (units_cast_from_windows), with
  Unit Shadows on; out of the light they have only their contact shade.
- The map's own sun stays as set (sun_degrees_base): sunk by the battle
  before it, the light came in low and the beams' grid took seconds.

Map 62's values, the user's picks from the mockups: sun straight in (0,
-1) at 24 degrees (kMapSuns), dark 0.6, both windows spread 0.6, the right
one at 0.25; kConeSoft 0.6, kConeGain 2.5, kConeFade 250, shafts 1.0 in the
air and 0.3 on surfaces, unit shadows 0.09. Map 62 joins kIndoorMaps (it
was only `indoor` in the Thor's file). `shots/attic62/window_light_final.png`.
Maps 55, 101, 58, 97 and a battle (FL, GX, HS, JM, GF, BL) render as before
byte for byte; both invariants unchanged. Mac: the beams' grid ~100 ms once
a sun, the surface light ~16 ms and the haze ~12 ms each time the camera

### Smooth pans in story scenes (2026-10-28)

The user found the panning less smooth than it could be. Not
our pacing: the game's camera. `KOL_CAM_LOG=1` (kol_widescreen) prints the
scene camera (0x02026C78/7A), its ease target and BG0's scroll every frame.
In map 3's church scene (states/thor/0013, replay s13/aa.rep) the pans
across the church and straight down step 1 px every frame, but the
diagonal pan to the shore (frames 60389-60772, ~6 s) goes, every 4 frames:
nowhere, 1 down, 1 sideways, 1 down. Never both axes at once, so the
picture stopped 15 times a second and zig-zagged. The presented pictures
followed the game's camera exactly (a patch match per present): we add
nothing to it, and the cartridge does the same at 240 x 160.

Now (kol_perspective `pan_smooth`, both providers): in a story event
(`ScenePixels::story`) the scene is drawn where the average of its last 4
pictures' BG0 scrolls (`ScenePixels::bg0_h/v`, the latched scroll each
picture was composed with) would put it: the mesh's destination moves by
the scroll minus that average, units' cards with it; the HUD, the moved
interface and the backdrop are drawn apart and stay. A staircase that
repeats every 4 frames becomes a straight line at its own speed, any pan
eases in and out over 4 pictures, at most ~1.5 px behind the game (0.75
here). A step over 6 px (a cut), a new map or a map load starts the
average again; battle maps are left alone (the cursor's hand is drawn
flat and would leave its cell mid-pan). The flat provider moves a copy of
its grid, its edge squares stretched over what the move leaves.
`KOL_NO_PAN_SMOOTH=1`: as before.

Measured on the shore pan: the scroll shown steps exactly 0.25 px
sideways and 0.5 down every picture (`pan:` lines with KOL_CAM_LOG). At
--scale 4 (the mesh drawn at output size, as on the Thor) the ground moves
(1, -2) output px every frame; without it (0, 0), (0, -4), (4, 0), (0,
-4). No view edge left uncovered (44 presents). BL_enemy_turn and thor
state 12 (battle maps) identical on and off; both invariants unchanged.

**A shake is not a pan (2026-11-11).** Map 86 (states/thor/0216, from ~260
frames after the load): the game shakes the ground by stepping the camera
back and forth, X +-1 every 2 frames with a jump of a few pixels now and
then. That repeats every 4 frames, exactly the average's length, so the
ground was held still (and eased slowly through the jumps) while the
characters shook: the user saw, in Enhanced, a slow move and then the
characters shaking instead of the environment. Now
`pan_smooth` notes each axis's last direction; when either turned back
within the last 12 pictures (`kShakeHold`) the scene is drawn where the
game put it, on both axes. `pan:` lines on 0216: moved 0,0 on every
picture after the first three; two shake phases are the same picture one
pixel apart. A pan that turns round loses its smoothing for 12 pictures.
`KOL_PAN_SMOOTH_SHAKES=1`: as before.

### Numbered save states (2026-10-28)

Asked for a proper save state manager: a debug option for sequential save
states on L3+R, with L3+L loading the latest; a bottom-screen submenu
listing every state with its screenshot and Alphonse's level at the time,
a tap loading one; and a command syncing the saves into this project.

- **Options > Debug > Numbered States** (`debug_numbered_states`, off).
  On, the pad's state combos (gbarecomp: L3 + R1 saves slot 1, L3 + L1
  loads it; L3 keeps the shoulders from the game) keep a numbered list
  instead: L3 + R saves the next number, L3 + L loads the highest. Slot
  1's F1 key goes the same way while it is on; slots 2-9 are untouched.
  The game's confirm sound plays on a save.
- Each state is three files in the app's `files/states/` (desktop:
  `KOL_STATES_DIR`): `NNNN.state`, `NNNN.png` (the frame as the game drew
  it, latched at the saved moment, before our effects: no perspective or
  light) and `NNNN.txt` (`level`, `name` and `map` from Alphonse's roster
  record 0x02001420 +0x52 / +0x30 and 0x02029D40, `time`, `frame`).
  The PNG is written uncompressed (deflate's stored blocks, ~115 KB at
  240 x 160, ~250 KB at 384 x 216) so the menu reads it back without zlib.
- **Options > Debug > Save States**: the whole second screen, newest first,
  three across: each state's picture in a 72 x 40 box, its number and
  Alphonse's level under it (no level before the roster exists: the title
  screen reads 0). Drag to scroll; a tap loads that state and closes the
  menu (through slot 90, which the path hook answers with the picked
  file). D-pad moves, A loads, B or a tap on the title goes back.
  **L3 + R3** (both sticks pressed, either first) opens the menu straight
  on this page, or closes it when it is up; Back still leads to Debug
  (kol_actions `on_pad_button` -> `menu_open_states`; the desktop menu
  check takes a `states` step: `KOL_MENU_PPM=out.ppm,states;k2`). It works
  with Numbered States off too (the list is there either way).
- **Deleting** (asked next, for a way to delete states): two
  steps, so a stray tap loses nothing. Hold a state (450 ms) and it turns
  red, darkened, "Delete N?"; a tap on it deletes its three files, any
  other tap only unmarks it. On the pad Select marks the selected one, A
  deletes it, B unmarks. A number is never given again: `files/states/next`
  keeps one past the highest ever saved, so a synced copy of a deleted
  state cannot be taken for a new one.
- **Sync:** `tools/thor_states.sh` (VS Code task "Sync Thor states")
  mirrors `files/states/` into `states/thor/` (gitignored; a state deleted
  on the Thor goes from there too, nothing else is touched) and lists them
  (number, level, map, time). It only reads the device. Then "Thor state
  12" is `states/thor/0012.state`, with its picture next to it.

gbarecomp: `g_runtime_state_path_hook` / `g_runtime_state_saved_hook`
(ENHANCEMENTS "A game's own state files"). Checked on the Mac:
`KOL_STATES_TEST="s20,s90,s160,l200,p1@230"` (desktop only: the combos'
save/load at those frames, `pN@f` loads state N) saved 0001-0003, the load
took 0003 and the pick 0001; a battle state's note reads `level=1
name=Alphonse map=2`; `KOL_MENU_PPM` (now with `KOL_MENU_PPM_WAIT=n`)
drew the page with the five pictures. Deleting: 1-3 saved, 3 marked
(Select) and deleted (A), the next save was 0004 and `next` read 5; a tap
elsewhere unmarked (nothing deleted), a tap on the marked one deleted it.
On the Thor: the device's tar
through run-as checked; the combos and the page not tried yet. Both
invariants unchanged (off by default; nothing changes with it off).

**Scrolling like the army's cards (2026-11-05).** Asked for the state selection screen to scroll
as fluidly as the world map's character cards. The page was redrawn in native on every finger move,
in whole canvas pixels (5 device pixels on the Thor), with no glide. Now `menu_render` draws only the

wetness started over only with a new map NUMBER (or a jump in the frame

A button in the second screen's bottom-right corner (the game's System icon,
from the R-bar icon archive `0x086DA2E4`, icon 16) opens an OPTION window
drawn like the game's own (R on an empty tile > System > Option). Code:
`src/kol_menu.{h,cpp}`; Java in `StatsView` (`drawMenu`, `onTouchEvent`).

**Art, all from the ROM:**
- window and tab tiles: archives `0x086B75B4` and `0x086BBB2C`;
- the hand `0x086D7F61` and the scroll arrow `0x086D7FC2` (raw; the arrow is
  stored pointing up, flipped for down);
- palettes: BG `0x0861DF68` (banks 4 and 12), OBJ `0x0861E288` bank 0;
- font `0x0815DEC4`, widths `0x0815DE6C`;
- the game's option names, values and HELP texts, parsed from the ROM.

**The game's twelve options are editable.**
- They live at EWRAM `0x0200132C`, eight bytes:
  - bytes 0-2 are options 0-2;
  - byte 3, bits 0-4, is options 3-7 (a set bit is ON);
  - bytes 4-6 are options 8-10;
  - option 11, "Default", is an action.
- Defaults: `00 01 00 FF 00 01 00`.
- The game's own menu copies them to `[0x02028950]+0x1194` while it is open.
  The game reads the bits live (`0x0808B426`, `0x08076338`).
- Writes are queued and applied inside the game by a reviewed
  `[[mod_function_hook]]` on SoundMain (`0x0815B838`, runs every frame).
  They are never applied from outside guest execution or during an
  excursion.

**Rows:**
- the 12 game options;
- "- Enhancements -": View Size ("Original" for 240x160), Perspective,
  Depth of Field (OFF / Subtle / Medium / Strong / Very strong: one list,
  the strength and the switch together), Clear Move Range, Wide Weather,
  Shoulder Units;
- a **Sound** page: Sound, Music Volume, Effects Volume, Placed Effects,
  Soft Tones;
- a **Debug** page: Perspective Mesh, R3 Wins Battle (later No Random
  Battles, L2 Moves Sun, Layers).

**Touch and pad:**
- Drag to scroll (it snaps to whole rows). Tap a name to see its HELP; tap a
  value to change it.
- The pad works through gbarecomp's `g_host_keyinput_filter`: up and down
  repeat (300 ms, then every 80 ms), left and right step, A changes or opens
  a page, B leaves a page or closes the menu. The game sees nothing pressed.
- A button held while the menu is open stays hidden from the game until
  released, so the B that closes the menu does not also press B in the game.

**Headless checks:** `KOL_MENU_PPM=path[,taps]` writes the menu after 8
frames. Taps are `x:y`, `dragN` or `k<hexbits>` (a pad press; `k40` is Up,
`k10` Right, `k1` A, `k2` B). `KOL_MENU_DUMP_TEXT=1` dumps the parsed texts.
`KOL_NO_MENU_OPTIONS=1` turns the menu off.

**The main screen dims while the menu is open (2026-09-30).** The game keeps
running; its picture darkens (to 70% at first, now 50%) over about 8 frames, then back when the
menu closes. It is gbarecomp's new `g_present_dim` (runtime.h): black at
that opacity over the whole window at present time, under the touch
controls, so frames and hashes are untouched. KoL eases it in the frame hook
from `kol::menu_is_open()`. **50% since 2026-10-01** (the user asked for
darker, about 50%): the picture goes to half brightness.

**The menu reopens where it was closed (2026-10-01).** Reported: in the
Debug page, closing the menu with the button and opening it again left the
hand elsewhere. `menu_toggle` reset the page to the main one on opening but
kept the row, so Debug's row number landed on a main-page row. It now keeps
the page (Debug, Sound, Layers too), the row and the scroll; B in a page
still goes back as before.

## The EMBLEM page, and tapping for HELP (2026-09-30)

**The page.** A horizontal swipe on the sheet's lower card flips it between
EQUIP./TALENT and EMBLEM. The card follows the finger and snaps on release:
past a third of the width, or on a flick, it goes to the other page;
otherwise it springs back. It stays on that page for every unit until the
next swipe. It never applies to the two-card sheet.

**Where the emblems are:**
- The set is the u32 at record `+0x08`: bit i is slot i (row i/8, column
  i%8). It is ANDed with a mask from the class table, as the window's
  `0x0803C01C` does (control block `+0x6198`):
  - the mask is word `+0x04` of class record `0x08615228 + id*0x58`,
    inherited through `+0x09` like the other class fields (`0x0813FA44`);
  - the id comes from `0x086148A0 + (+0x4E)*20 + 2` when `+0x4E > 1` and
    that byte is not 0, else from `+0x4F` with `+0x50` as the fallback.
- Pictures: A7 archive `0x086D6B7C`, 35 pictures of two entries each.
  Each tile's bank is a nibble in the table at `0x086D6B34` (header at
  `0x086D6B30`).
  - Slots 0-10 are pictures 0-10, and slots 12-30 are pictures 13-31.
  - Slot 11 is picture 11 (Vixen's Whisper) for a woman (`+0x5E == 2`),
    else picture 12 (Broken Heart).
  - Slot 31 is 32 / 33 / 34 (Relix's, Ripple's, Grozz Nuy's) for
    `+0x5E` 1 / 2 / 0.
  - These follow the loader at `0x0803C0C6`.
- Layout, measured from the game's window:
  - The plates are at columns 3, 6, 9, 12 and 16, 19, 22, 25.
  - The empty plate is tiles `0x158-0x15B`.
  - The tab is `0x15F-0x163` in bank 12.
  - The game's page is the right half of its 512-wide BG0/BG1 maps
    (HOFS 240).
- HELP text: kind-10 rows (`0x0802ADB6`). An emblem not earned is `0x298`.
  Otherwise the text is `0x149 +` its picture, except slot 31: `0x17F`,
  `0x169` or `0x16A` for `+0x5E` 0 / 1 / 2.

**Taps.** A tap on a slot shows its HELP at the top of the sheet, with the
slot left lit under the dimmed rest. Tap it again, or anywhere else, to
close it. This covers:
- the four EQUIP. rows: the item's help, the same as SELECT;
- the four TALENT rows: the talent's `+0x06`;
- the 32 emblems.

The card ends above the lit slot. A text too tall for that room closes up,
the same way a text taller than the sheet does: the paragraph gap goes
first, then the line pitch. The top row starts at y 100, which leaves the
card 96 px. Philosopher's Stone (slot 7) ends at a 15 px pitch. Kaukown's
six lines (the first EQUIP. row) are the tightest, at 12 px.

An empty row shows nothing. The game's own EMBLEM page with SELECT now gets
its text on the second screen too.

**Another unit closes it (2026-11-02).** The user expected a
description box opened by a tap on the bottom screen (a medal, a spell, an
item) to close on moving to another unit. It stayed, showing the new unit's item in the same
slot (AZ, Kaukown tapped, next unit: Oracion's text). The tapped slot now
belongs to the unit it was tapped on: when the sheet shows a unit with
another record (the shoulders, a tap in the list, the game's own cursor),
the card closes and no slot stays lit. Checked headless on AZ
(`KOL_UNIT_DUMP=1 KOL_SHEET_DUMP KOL_SHEET_TAP=20:106 KOL_NEXT_UNIT_AT=60`):
the tapped sheet is byte-identical, the next unit's has no card;
`KOL_SHEET_TAP_KEEPS=1` gives the old sheet byte for byte. Both invariants
hold.

**The HELP card reflows.**
- The game's line ends join.
- A page end starts a new paragraph (4 px gap) only where the page ends with
  a period; otherwise the text flows on.
- Text wraps by word to the card's 216 px.
- A line break after a hyphen joins without a space. That happens in one
  text only, `0x1EE` ("blood-", "iron-").

**The swipe's other page.** While a finger is down, the second-screen
thread also renders the other page (`compose_other_page`, JNI
`sheetPeek`). Java freezes it at the release. Without that freeze the page
flip made the thread send the page being left as "the other", and the snap
flickered.

**One card while looking around.** During a unit's turn the sheet showed
the actor above and the unit under the cursor below, even with the cursor
out only to look around. The move task's state byte `0x0202A82E` gives the
phase:

| Value | Phase | States |
|---|---|---|
| `0x02` | command menu | CL, CP |
| `0x05` | looking around | CK, CM, DD |
| `0x0B` | move choice | CT |
| `0x07` / `0x09` | target choice | CN, CO / CS |
| `0x07` / `0x17` | Attack/Cancel confirmation | BV, BW |

At `0x05` (`kol::cursor_browsing`) the sheet is the plain one of the unit
looked at. Repro: `states/DD_two_cards_idle.state`.

**Headless checks:**
- `KOL_UNIT_DUMP=1 KOL_SHEET_DUMP=<ppm>` writes the sheet.
- `KOL_SHEET_EMBLEMS=1` starts on the EMBLEM page.
- `KOL_SHEET_TAP=x:y` taps the sheet.
- The emblem repro is `states/DC_alphonse_emblems.state` (Alphonse's window
  on its EMBLEM page).

## The unit list on the second screen (2026-09-30)

**What it does.** While the player browses the battle map, the second screen
shows the battle's units, modelled on the game's own "View List"
(`states/DE_battle_unit_list.state`):
- the player's side is on the left and the others on the right, two cells a
  row each;
- within a side, units go by the game's NO., and units whose turn is done go
  last (still by NO.);
- a done unit wears the game's END plate over its head; the space under its
  box stays empty for now, by the user's choice;
- the list takes the status sheet's window (184 lines, rows 44 apart where
  the game's are 48, so four rows, eight a side, fit exactly), at the top of
  the second screen like the sheet and the menu, so the black band below is
  the same on every page. A longer list scrolls inside that window.

A tap on a unit selects it on the battlefield: the map cursor glides to it,
any side, done or not. With the cursor on a unit, that unit's card slides up
from the bottom over the list. Dragging the card down (past a quarter, or a
flick) puts it away until the cursor moves to another unit. The card's
horizontal swipe (EQUIP./TALENT and EMBLEM) still works; only a mostly
vertical downward drag moves the card.

**Where it comes from** (`src/kol_unit_list.cpp`):
- The units: the 26 map objects (u32 at `0x0202A238`, stride `0xD0`) with a
  record on the map (`+0x4E` and HP nonzero).
- NO.: record `+0x51` (the players' 1, 2, 4, 3, 5, 7, 9, 14 in record order
  in DE; the game's list shows them in record order, two a row).
- Done: object `+0x78` bit 1, set as a unit's turn ends and cleared for its
  side when that side's turn begins. The other side's bits are left over
  from its last turn, so it counts only for the side whose turn it is: the
  acting unit's (`0x0202A5F0`), or the player's while the cursor browses (no
  acting unit then).
  - **Trap:** the bit also blinks on for exactly one frame on one unit at a
    time, every unit that can still act taking its turn every 10-17 frames
    (DG). It counts only when it was up at the previous look as well.
  - `+0x7A` (FF, 0x1C once done) drops out too; `0x0202A508` counts END
    plates on screen. Neither is the source.
- The sprite: each unit's current frame, as the game draws it on the map
  and in its own list (both use the same OBJ tiles):
  - actor = object `+0x08`, part 0 at `+0x14`;
  - the frame record at part `+0xBC` (ROM: u16 count, then attr0/1/2 per
    piece; a person is 16x32 at (-8,-32), a monster 32x32 at (-16,-32));
  - the tiles at part `+0x28` (OBJ VRAM address);
  - part `+0xC4`: attr1 bits OR-ed in, `0x1000` = flipped;
  - the palette bank at object `+0x65` (Alphonse 2, Ivanna and several
    enemies 1). It is the byte the L-mode blink borrows.
- END: the game paints its plate (archive `0x086D80C4` tiles 24-25, OBJ bank
  0; 28-29 are it pre-mirrored) into rows 1-7 of the unit's first two tiles,
  over whatever was there. So the sprite carries it with no work here.
  **Corrected 2026-10-20** (the user's slot 2,
  `states/II_slot2_list_order_end.state`: three Lefts changed the units'
  order, and enough of them took Alphonse's END
  tag off): only while the game keeps the unit's sprite. Scrolling a unit out
  and back reloads its frames into its slot without the plate, and the
  sprite pool's VRAM callback `0x08059000` sets object `+0x78` bit 1 (and
  `+0x7A` = 0xFFFF) as it does. So `+0x78` bit 1 was never "done": it is the
  pool's, and the blink seen on DG was its reloads. II after twelve Lefts:
  every player unit `0x42`, so all read done, the order fell back to NO.
  (Alphonse first), and his reloaded tiles had no plate.
  - **Done is the battle entry's `+0x0C`** (`0x02001AA0` + record index *
    `0x1C`): 1 on Alphonse in II, Euphaire in DG, both in DH, Flauros and
    Deneb in CN, Rictor in his army's phase (HX); 0 on every unit still to
    act, and unmoved by scrolling. Counted for the acting side only, as
    before; no blink, so no debounce.
  - **The list paints the plate itself** for a done unit: rows 1-7 of its
    first two tiles, transparent pixels too, tiles 24-25, or 28-29 when it
    faces the other way (the game's own choice: DH, DG and CN's flipped done
    units hold 28 then 29; II's unflipped Alphonse 24 then 25, byte for
    byte).
  Checked: II with twelve Lefts, one order all along (Alphonse last, END on);
  DG, DH as before. Both invariants.
- Cell art, measured from the game's list:
  - the box: sheet tiles 33/34 (top and bottom rows) and 35/36, mirrored,
    bank 4 for the player, 7 otherwise;
  - the HP bar: archive `0x086BCA6C` tile 25 the cap (flipped below), then
    four segments from the bottom, 30 empty, 26/27/28 three, five and seven
    pixels, 29 full, bank 12. The game composes its bar tile at run time;
    the step per segment is ours;
  - LEADER: sheet tiles 242-245, bank 12, on the player's NO. 1 while not
    done;
  - the field: sheet tiles 5-8, shifting by two a row.

**When it shows.** The cursor is out (IWRAM `0x03000FD5`: 1 under the pad,
4 while it glides) and either no unit acts or the turn's cursor only looks
around (move task `+0x27E` = 0x05, DF). Not in battle preparation, menus,
move or target choice, or the enemy's turn. "On a unit" compares the
cursor's cell (`kol::map_cursor_cell`) with each object's `+0x10`/`+0x14`
>> 5, and is never true mid-glide. The game's highlighted-unit pointer can't
answer that: it keeps the last unit passed.

**The unit under the cursor is lit** as the game's list marks its cursor
(DE): brightness decrease 8/16 (BLDCNT `0x0FD3`, BLDY 8) on everything
except a window around that cell. The window runs from 2 px left of the bar
to 1 px right of the box, and from 2 px above the box to 1 px under the
label row, with its corner pixels cut (WIN1 plus the OBJ-window strips,
tiles `0x3F5`/`0x3F6`). The card covers the list while the cursor is on a
unit, so this shows when the card is swiped away (and under it as it
slides). With the cursor on empty ground, nothing is dimmed. Still:
`shots/unit_list/highlight_DJ.png` (which also shows partial HP bars).

**The band under the page.** Every page (sheet, list, menu) sits at the
top of the second screen in the sheet's 184-line window. The band left below
it is a zone in the frame of the game's windows: the SUPPLY menu's
(`states/DI_supply_menu.state`), sheet tiles 0x11-0x18 around the weave, bank
4, as kol_menu's `window()` draws them. It is as tall as the band, with the
bottom edge pinned to the bottom. The menu button (the same 3x3 window with
the System icon) sits inside it at the right, vertically centred
(`kol::menu_zone_render`, JNI `menuZone`). A card sliding down passes under
the zone. If the band is shorter than the button, the old corner button
comes back. Desktop still: `KOL_ZONE_PPM=path,h`; stills are in
`shots/unit_list/*_zone.png`.

**Selecting.** `kol::action_cursor_to_object` asks the Next-unit hook
(`0x080745A4`, README "Next unit, from a button"), which, in the machine's
ordinary state with the cursor free, does what the game's selection does at
`0x080744BA`: the cell (world >> 5, `0x08058D5C`) into cursor `+0x3C`/`+0x40`
(`0x03000FDC`/`0FE0`) and 4 into `+0x35`. The camera follows the glide. The
D-pad and A work afterwards (checked with an input replay from DF).

**Checks:**
- `KOL_LIST_DUMP=<ppm, %d = frame>` writes the list whenever it changes;
  `KOL_LIST_TAP="n:x:y,..."` taps it n frames after it first shows. Both log
  the height, the unit under the cursor and the order.
- DF (cursor on empty ground): tap (150,25), and the cursor glides to
  Eunomos. The list keeps its picture through the glide.
- `KOL_LIST_TRACE=1` logs each frame's cursor mode, target cell, sprite
  cell, the unit under it and the game's highlighted unit. In DJ (taps on
  Thompson, then Lechies) the cursor lands in one frame, with no unit
  crossed, and the highlighted unit follows a frame later.
- The card stutter the user saw (DJ, a card swiped away, then another unit
  tapped) was the Java state: the tap cleared "put away" while the cursor
  was still on the old unit, so its card started up, then went down to wait
  for the new one, then up again. Now a tap only brings back the card put
  away when it is that unit's (the tap returns its record). Going straight
  from one unit to another with the card up keeps the card and swaps its
  sheet. Native sends the list before the sheet, and Java handles both on
  the UI thread in that order.
- DG, DH (Euphaire, then Alphonse too, done): both sort last with END, and
  the order holds for 300 frames.
- The mockup is `tools/mockup/unit_list.py`, with `shots/unit_list/`.
- Render invariants unchanged: 240 `66e13ab2`, anchor-off 284 `9054c456`.

**Not seen yet:** the enemy's done units (the list is not up on its turn).

### The enemy's leader wears LEADER too (2026-10-29)

Asked for the enemy leader to get a LEADER tag like ours.
The tag went to the player's NO. 1 only. The battle entry (0x02001AA0 +
record index * 0x1C) has the leader at +0x17 bit 0 on either side: the
player's NO. 1 reads 0x41, the enemy's leader 0xC1 (map 7, 0030; map 2,
0012, HX, B_rictor), the rest 0x40 / 0xC0, a guest 0x42 (bit 1; map 2's
allied army, map 7's NO. 8). Training and random battles' enemies have no
leader (BL, FK: all 0xC0), and get no tag. The list now tags any unit with
the bit (a record outside the battle's 16 keeps the old rule). Checked with

### Persuasion's chance on the second screen (2026-10-29)

Asked, about to persuade an enemy unit, for the success percentage on the
bottom screen between the two middle cards, taken from the yellow text the
top screen shows on the left after A (25% in that state) (states/thor/0036: Allos on Sandy, 73/148 HP).

The confirm box after A ("-- pt / 25 % HIT") is BG text: its digits are
written by 0x0806EE46 for the box builder 0x08070770, which takes the
chance from 0x0813E30C(actor, actor entry, target, target entry) and shows
"--" for the damage. That routine is transcribed (`gauge::persuade_chance`
in kol_unit_data.cpp; the class fields by the existing `class_field` walk):
0 for a leader (entry +0x17 bit 0), a unit off the field (+0x4E > 1), a
class without +0x18 bit 1, an entry with +0x0C bits 3-7, or a battle of type
0x30/0x31 (0x020013BC); else 0 / 80 / 50 / 5 as the actor class's +0x1C /
+0x1A / +0x1B matches the target class's +0x1D, +30 for the actor's +0x08
bit 10, -50 for bit 1 against a class kind 6 and for bit 2 against kind 5,
clamped, then times the target's lost HP over its max (50 x 75 / 148 = 25).

Persuasion is the move task (0x0202A5B0) in state 0x2E (its jump table at
0x08060E84 sends 0x2E to the persuade task 0x080893DC, block at task
+0x1A0, +0 the actor's {record, entry}). While it is, the two-card sheet
draws the chance on the lower card's unit, centred on the cards' seam, in
the box's own glyphs: tiles 34-43 ('0'-'9') and 69 ('%') of archive
0x086B904C (its VRAM tiles 0x11C-0x125, 0x13F), BG bank 12 (0x0861E0E8).
Not on a unit of the actor's side (the game refuses those, message 0x3B).
Checked: 0036 reads 25%, as the game's box; BV (an attack) shows nothing.

#### A unit in the doorway, cut by the wall as the camera moves (2026-10-29)

States/thor/0051 (map 65, someone in the doorway, reported cut in half): the game
cuts a sprite by priority. The door's frame and the wall beside it are on
BG1, which the game puts over the unit's sprites (priority 2); the PPU
draws BG1 over them wherever it has pixels (layer codes 1 over 4 there),
and the dark doorway (BG0) under them. As a card the unit lost those
texels (`build_sprite_atlas`: "hidden by priority"), so the cut stayed
where it was in the frame: with the camera low he was drawn whole over the
wall, leaning right the cut stayed while the jamb moved.

Now (kol_focus `g_over_sprite`, `grow_over_sprite`; ScenePixels::over_sprite;
kol_perspective `kOverSpriteSlot`): the card keeps those texels, and the
pixels that covered them are drawn again after the cards, a quad each from
their own corners (a pixel on a lifted wall's or prop's card from that
card). Then grown over what they belong to, so other pixels of it coming
over the unit as the camera moves cover him too: across any connected
pixel nearer than the unit (X + Z) and more than 4 over the ground it
stands on (its Y; nothing under his feet hides him from a camera over
them), at its own place (a wall's or prop's card keeps it; under the unit's
own card, the ground under it), within 64 of its card, not where another
sprite is on top. Each unit's are drawn right after its own card, so nearer
cards still go over them. The covering pixels themselves always (mark 1);
what grew from them (3), and where the unit itself is on top at rest (2),
only with the camera off its rest (look or combat camera), so the picture
at rest is the game's. States/thor/0048: with the camera down it did not
work as expected, and the whole roof should cover Alphonse: a house's
roof edge (BG1, Y 128, exactly 48 along Alphonse's line of sight) covers
his feet at rest; the roof is lifted as many wall cards and drawn under
him on BG0. Grown along one surface, then within one card, a strip of it
came over his legs while the rest stayed behind him; now the whole roof
covers him with the camera down (`shots/room65/roof_over_alphonse_0048.png`),
and state 48 at rest is byte-identical. (GC: the front of the ledge a unit
stood on, under his feet, had come over them too; hence "over the ground".)
Leaning right the wall and its sconce now slide over him; with the camera
low the nearer wall moves out further and he shows in the opening
(`shots/room65/doorway_cut_follows.png`). At rest the redrawn pixels land
within a fraction of a pixel of the strips they redraw: scattered edge
pixels differ where the game covers a unit (state 51: 91, below him, with
his shadow, now cast from his whole sprite). The units' cast shadows now take their whole sprite.
`KOL_UNIT_PRIORITY_CUT=1`: as before. Both invariants unchanged.

16): Ivanna at 7,7 stands behind the reed at 8,8, and another unit behind

Ivanna's legs and the other unit's feet are now behind their reeds with the

#### And a roof in front of a unit: walls and terrain too (2026-11-02)

Reported as a regression: on the latest state with the camera down, a
sprite was drawn over the house (`states/thor/0096`,
map 13). A unit on the upper street behind the front house (world 336, 80,
208: X+Z 544, standing at 80) is above the roof's ridge at rest; with the

- **terrain no card lifted**, by the same test, within 64 of his card and no

with the camera moved the room lay down like a rug. The walls are a model
(tools/models/room71.py -> src/kol_model_map71.inc), fitted on the flat
scene with its overlay: the right wall along X to its cut end at X 256
(screen x 298-305: 16 thick), the left wall along Z to its cut end at Z
220, both 16 thick, their tops at Y 138. Their inner faces at 32 (X and Z):
the user's pick of the overlays at 24, 32 and 40 (`shots/shed71/
faces_24_32_40.png`: the middle one; I had built 24, by the
right wall's foot, with the left wall 10 thick). `shots/shed71/walls.png`.
The boat, the cloth, the crates and barrels still lie on the floor or, where
they overlapped a wall, on it: the next step if the user wants it.


### The shed's objects (an agent workflow)

Asked for one agent to analyse the image and find each object's 3-D
position, another to review it, and one to place them on the field and
verify: a workflow ran one round. The analyst (on the clean flat
scene: sprites, HUD hidden) solved 14 objects; the reviewer corrected the
post's top (132), the beams (7 tall), the crate stack, the hull's bow (off
the pitchfork handle on the wall), the plank under it, and the cloth's
outline; the placer built them into tools/models/room71.py and rendered
four looks against the walls-only baseline: post, beam (to the left wall
and to the back wall), bucket, small crate, lid, the crate stack, two
barrels, two balls, the hull (a plan extruded 32 tall, the bow a block),
the plank under it all stand. The cloth, a sheet on X 136, stood as a
stiff pale board turned right (its top under the art's drape): left out
(R71_CLOTH=1 puts it back). The pitchfork rack, the shelf and the window
are flat on the walls (the window's glass on Z 32: X 190-196, Y 65-101,
for lighting). Unseen sides of the crates and barrels streak as the camera
turns (never painted). Stopped after round 1 (credits).
`shots/shed71/objects.png` (top walls only, bottom with the objects: rest,
low, low turned left and right), `objects_fit.png` (the overlay).

## Maps 90 and 117: one boat, two scenes (2026-11-03)

Asked to treat maps 90 and 117, which look very similar, the way earlier maps were changed and
reviewed. Done unattended, the way of
the four rooms below: a reader per map, then a fresh reviewer per map with the
game's pictures, the fixes, and the same reviewer's check of them.

**They are one drawing.** A small one-masted boat at a plank pier: 90 with its
sail furled on the yard, over the sea; 117 with its sail set, sky behind. The
hull, mast, yard and fixed ropes are pixel-identical, and the pier is too (6626
of 6628 pixels, at another place). In the world 117's boat is 90's moved by
(0, 32, 320), so `tools/models/boat90.py` has `build_boat(m, at, hang, body,
skip_ropes)` and `tools/models/boat117.py` calls it. The depths are the game's:
90's grid has the deck at Y 48 and the pier at Y 64 with the sea at Y 0, and the
user's drawn deck on 117 (Y 80) agrees exactly at that move. Layers: on 90 BG0 is
the sea (with the pier's shadow painted on it) and the hull and deck, BG1 the
pier, mast, yard, furled sail, ropes and tile-stepped bits of hull; on 117 BG0 is
the whole boat, BG1 the pier.

**The models.** Hull (flared, the rail stepping up in tiers to a near-flat
transom, far and near rails paired along screen lines for the beam), rail cap,
bulwark, deck, bow post, mast, parrel, yard, nine ropes. 90: four sail swags,
the gangplank, the pier with a trestle bent every 128 in Z and four mooring posts.
117: the set sail, one strip (bellying toward the bow, its concave side to the
camera, the cream strip past a fold its convex side), two sheets, the same pier,
ripples on the water plane. The first reviews found the depth overspent on 117:
BELLY 30 -> 10, the foot no longer level (`foot_y`, 30 lower toward the near clew,
15 higher by the mast), the two stern ropes pinned where they leave the sky. Not
a pixel moves at rest; the stretch with the camera moved fell by a third to a half
(the reviewer's figures, within 2% of what it predicted).

**What the game needed.** None of it touches another map: 52 renders and both
invariants unchanged.
- A pixel off every cell has no place, so a rope or yard over it could not lift
  and the sea stood up in walls behind it. `kDrawnCells` {90, -1, -12, -20, 30,
  22, 0} lays the art's whole footprint at height 0, past the grid too, which
  also takes down the grid's walk routes (row z 0 and the pier's cells raised the
  water beside them).
- `kMapTerrainRecords` {90, 50}: that row's record is the stones', so as cut-outs
  they took 537 pixels of the far rail and ropes and stood them up at the cells'
  depth (Tile Info: BYTE 06, RECORD 50).
- **`kModelOver`** (kit `OVER`): a hanging part in front of the model's solids.
  Lifted on BG1 it opens onto the solid behind it, not the terrain. Where the solid's
  own art is on BG1 in that tile (the hull's stepped bits), BG0 under it is water:
  it opens onto the ground. `KOL_MODEL_OVER_OFF=1`: none of it. (Ropes: below.)
- On 90 the hanging parts are also `BG1ART`: 24 water pixels stood in the air
  (rope_stay's 19). On 117 they cannot be: its boat is BG0 against the sky.
- **`kModelAsDrawn`** (kit `ASDRAWN`): takes no shadow, still casts. The sail (the
  art lights its far half; its own shadow darkened 23% of it in a hard diagonal)
  and every rope (a line that thin in shadow reads as a dark scratch or a break).
- **Model AO outdoors, two bugs.** Every earlier `model_ao` map is indoors. The
  terrain's `g_wx` / `g_wz` are filled for the lamps' maps; here the sea read (0, 0)
  and took its occlusion in stripes, so a kModelOver model's pixels get their place
  from the projection. And the deck read its own cubes as a wall all round, the
  whole deck at 70%: flat faces stop nothing on 90 and 117, as on the ships.
  `g_back_ao` takes the model's shadow too (the water under the pier stayed lit, a
  bright stripe).
- 117: the model always wins over the grid (`kTerrainNearer` 1e9, its outline too:
  79 outline pixels stayed on the user's blocks). `kSkyOverCellsMaps` {117}: the grid
  covers the whole map at height 1 and the art there is sky, so sky pixels stood on
  those cells and on the user's blocks; the warp pulled the rail's corners out to
  them (wedges at the far stern) and warped the sky as a pale plane. The sky is no
  surface there now. `KOL_SKY_ON_CELLS=1`: as before.

**The ropes, in the air to their ends.** The user, from the Thor, asked for the ropes
to touch the boat model only at their ends. The first version left a rope's
pixels painted on BG0 on the surface behind them (lifted, BG0 has nothing under them
and the camera pulled a curtain of deck up to the rope), so a rope landed early. Now
every rope is one straight line from its top to its foot, and:
- A rope's pixel is lifted off whatever part it passes in front of, on either layer
  (`g_rope_air`; the model's view keeps a fourth hit, the nearest part that is no
  rope). Only the rope's art: its colours are bluish or pale, the wood's yellow (blue
  under 0.8 of red, a ratio so it holds through the scene's fades). Its dark outline
  a pixel past the cylinder goes with it, or it stays behind as dark specks.
- What it uncovers where the art has nothing behind it: the nearest pixel of that
  surface, never an outline (`g_rope_under_fix`, on the path the awnings' BG0 cloth
  takes). If that surface is not beside it (the far rail only just reaches behind
  the rope), the nearest thing beside it is what it opens onto.
- Over a part itself lifted on BG1 (90's yard) it opens onto what that part opens
  onto: at the part's depth it stood in the sea's mesh, a streak.
- Over the sky (117) it is lifted too: left in the mesh beside the sail, the row
  between them stretched into a bar. Its hole takes its row's sky (`warp_backdrop`;
  copied as it was it showed black, then as faint marks, as the backdrop's own steps
  skip that layer), and is no art to place (`g_cand`).
- In the warp the surface behind a rope is an ordinary pixel of it, not a prop's
  ground (`ScenePixels::rope_air`): a prop's ground gives its corners up to what is
  beside it, and a speck of rail stretched out over the sea.
- The unit priority cut's redraw (`over_sprite`: nearer pixels drawn again after a
  unit's card) goes far to near on these maps and takes the ropes passing in front of
  a part. In row order the deck came over the nearer rail, and the ropes lay under
  whatever was redrawn: they stopped short of their feet in the lean views. (A draw
  bias changed nothing; painting the ropes' texels magenta and logging their quads
  found it: placed right, painted over.) A rope over the sky joins it only if nearer
  than the part beside it on its row, so 117's forestay stays behind the sail.
- Gone with it: the pins of the two stern ropes on 117 and the gap at the mast.
  `SHEET_FAR`'s foot is 4 over the deck (at the deck it ran along the wall for 12 rows).
  `KOL_ROPES_ON_SOLIDS=1`, or without Lifted Walls: a rope painted on a part stays on it.
- **Blue streaks along the ropes over the deck (2026-11-11, Thor state 221, ending
  scene 2 on map 90).** The user saw blue lines through the boat, then asked
  for a fill in the boat's colour, perhaps from the adjacent pixels. That fill
  was already there (`g_rope_under_fix`, all 401 rope pixels over the deck code 2),
  but only in the under picture: the scene codes still said backdrop under those
  BG0 pixels, and the warp gives a lifted pixel over the backdrop its row's sky
  (16, 89, 255). Now the rope fixes mark the under layer as the kModelWallBehindMaps
  flame fixes do (`kol_focus_present`), so the deck colour shows. Not mesh holes
  (`KOL_PERSP_HOLES=1` left them blue), not Smooth Sky (off: 0 px changed).
  221: 205 streak pixels -> 1, 322 px changed in all. `KOL_ROPE_FILL_SKY=1` old.
  Both invariants hold.
- **The mast's foot lifted too (2026-11-11, same state).** The user asked to lift the
  mast as the ropes were lifted, rather than see the
  stretching. The mast's lower half is painted on the deck's BG0 (hide BG1
  and it is still there); kModelOver with the deck behind kept those pixels at the
  mast's depth with nothing behind them, so the deck stretched up to them, a smear
  beside the mast with the stick moved. Now `kLiftFillParts` ({map, part, dx, dy};
  map 90's mast, part 5) lifts them as a rope's BG0 pixels (g_rope_air 2), opening
  onto the deck (l[1]). Three things differ from a rope:
  - The fill never takes the part's own pixels (the mast's BG1 above), and looks
    along the deck's planks first (with the keel, along Z: screen (-2, +1)), then
    the row. One colour a row across the mast's 12 pixels read as bands.
  - The deck behind takes no shadow from the mast's pixels (`shadow_list`'s back
    pass for kModelOver): that was the mast's own shaded side, a dark patch.
  - Leaning right, the plank line from the gap reaches the coil's pale art, so a
    piece of coil shows there. Left as is.
  At rest: the mast's foot a pixel crisper, and 1-px sampling shifts in the water and
  pier (the mesh's row cuts move with the lifted pixels), 1211 px in all,
  deterministic. `KOL_MAST_ON_DECK=1` old (byte-identical to the rope fix's picture).
  Both invariants hold.

**Left.**
- Hull streaks on the water behind the far side in the lean views: true parallax,
  BG0 has no sea behind the hull.
- On 117 the bands between mast, sail and bulwark: what lies behind was never
  drawn. 90's art has the same deck clear of the sail, so a patch could in principle
  be borrowed from it; not tried.
- A small band of sail across the mast on 117 at full stick lean (coordinate trace:
  sail pixels at x 134, rows 118-122, flat coordinates, over the mast). The mask and

  or `KOL_PERSP_NO_KEEP_SPREAD`: it is in the mesh's corner logic. Not chased: the

- The user's 48 drawn heights on 117 no longer matter to the picture and can go.
- Six dark pixels of the sail's head outline stay with 117's forestay (a dash at 196-201,

- The figure sometimes seen near the yard in the viewer is the scene's character on

**Tried and dropped.** A grid of world cells to skip model AO's search on open sea:
it changed 117's picture (high flat pixels on the sail lost their search) and saved

The user, states/thor/0113: the right pillar is a sprite, and should behave exactly like

  (`g_model_actor_px` in `lift_wall_surfaces`); what the lift uncovers is the compositor's
  picture without sprites.

stood out round the effect's flame and slid against it with the camera. Model flag `FXART`

**Still a darker outline around the flames (2026-11-08, the Thor):** the fix above did
almost nothing. Three reasons, found by painting each art-flame pixel by why it was skipped

  the wall behind is taken all the same (`kol_focus_models.cpp`).

shadows yet. Not yet: the shutters swinging, the lightning.
Then, not a godray like that but much
wider: a cone (spread 0.9, past map 62's 0.6); at gain 1 it washed the shed
white, so 0.35. That lit the room's front evenly with a straight back edge
(the sill's shadow); the user asked why only the bottom half was lit, as
the light should spread in a cone. Mockups `shots/shed71/
cone_variants.png`; the user's pick C (spread 0.3, the sun 22 degrees)
with less intense light: gain 0.5 (C's 0.8). Then, only while the right stick moved
did the light take its right orientation: with the camera low and close the shaft became a
column beside the post (Thor screenshots, the user: the diagonal shaft is
right). I first blamed the haze being painted on surfaces and turned it
off (a map whose haze in kMapWindowTints is 0 has none, the cones' shafts
too: window_haze_at; kept). The user disliked it and asked for the
true culprit. The culprit: map 71 was not in model_occluder, so
its window light was worked out before the model pass, on the flat art's
places (the back wall's pixels as floor). Now model_occluder takes map 71
(no model floors: its crates' and barrels' tops are no cell's floor), the
light is worked out after the model, the haze is back (0.05), and the
crates and barrels stop the light. With the camera low the shaft stays
diagonal (`shots/shed71/window_light.png`, rest and low).
`shots/shed71/window_light.png` (rest, camera low).
Then the cone's tip shaped like the window, as asked: a cone's haze is
nine shafts that started as thin lines across the window's width, meeting
near it in a point. On kConeWindowTipMaps (71) they start on a 3 x 3 grid
over the opening, each half its share of the opening's larger side thick,
so at the window they fill its rectangle and fan out from there. (Drawing
the haze from the cone's volume alone, whole and unbanded, was tried: a
wash through the whole room, no cone.) `shots/shed71/cone_tip.png` (rest,
camera low; the dialogue hidden).
Then a faked light bounce: a steady cool ceiling lamp over the shed's middle
(kCeilingLamps {71, 144, 110, 128, reach 280, 0.25, hue 3, steady, ring
80}), as maps 65's and 68's; `shots/shed71/bounce.png` (none, 0.12, 0.25).
Then asked for the light to follow the window panel's
movement: the shutter is a panel hinged at the window's left edge that the
game swings among four positions by swapping BG tiles (no sprite; ~25
frames each, at irregular moments). Each picture the scene's pixels over
the wall around the window (Z 32, X 140-200, Y 60-106, placed by the
camera) are hashed (read_shutter); a known hash gives the window's light
strength (kShutter71): open, flat against the wall 1.0; half open 0.6;
nearly shut 0.25; mostly closed 0.35 (the user pointed out the second
mostly closed position). An unknown hash (the lightning's flash, a fade, a unit
in front) keeps the last. KOL_SHUTTER_LOG=1 prints the hashes. The first
mapping was wrong (picked by the log's frame counter, not the picture's):
checked against each position's frame with the light off.
`shots/shed71/shutter_light.png`. Not checked on the Thor: if its pictures
hash differently (another view size should not matter: the rectangle is in
the world), the light stays at 1.0.
Then asked for a smaller cone and dimmer light when it is closed, and
perhaps a short transition between positions: the position's value is eased, 0.12 of the way a picture (about
half a second, g_shutter_shown); the light's strength follows it, and the
cone's spread is 0.4 + 0.6 x it of map 71's (window_cone_spread), in steps
of 1/20 (g_shutter_spread) so the window light (beams, shafts, the patch)
is rebuilt only when a step changes, keyed on it. The log prints open,
shown and spread. Then a faster ease, also driving the
bounce light's brightness: 0.3 of the way a picture (most of it in
~6 pictures), and map 71's bounce lamp (kCeilingLamps) is scaled by the
same eased value, through its flicker (applied each picture, so the cached
lamp light is not rebuilt). Shut, the room away from the patch averages
39 against 49 before. Then faster still, about 4 frames: 0.6 of the
way a picture, 97% there after 4. Then the brightest rays were too bright: every
step a bit dimmer, the brightest most: the window light
goes through shutter_light, open 1.0 -> 0.7, half 0.6 -> 0.5, mostly
closed 0.35 -> 0.3, nearly shut 0.25 -> 0.21 (eased values in between
along those points); the cone's width and the bounce keep the openness.
Then the user's own values: open 0.5, half 0.38, mostly closed 0.28,
nearly shut 0.2.

Then asked for lightning strikes to be very bright, the bounce light too
(the user noted the flash is BG1 tiles laid over). The rectangle read_shutter
hashes has no BG1 pixel except in a flash: 612, 529 of them bright
(scene_top = 1; state 50: a double flash ~every 400 pictures, 2-3 then
8-12 pictures; the hash is unknown then, so the shutter keeps its value).
More than 100 bright BG1 pixels sets g_lightning to 1, halving each picture
after; the window light gains 1.5 x it (open is 0.5) and the bounce lamp's

acf1af88 (mean 84, darker than any position, ~25 pictures at serial 610)

Then asked to find what made it so slow and fix it.
On the Mac (state 50, KOL_WORKER_TIME, KOL_GODRAYS_TIME), the present
worker took 15.7 ms a picture, two thirds of it the window light: built
75 times in 300 pictures, 38 of them with the grid (~45 ms each), every
build with patch and haze (~15 ms). Two causes: the cone's eased width,
each 1/20 step a new grid; and the terrain pass's key, which flips with
world_dirty (the torchlight's view key, its backdrop codes changing with
the shutter's tiles) on each position change, so patch and haze were
worked out again even with the width unchanged. Then the user suggested
dropping the easing to cache the 4 shadow states. The width now
snaps to the position (the strength still eases, and the lightning: both
per picture, free), and the window light's last 8 builds are kept whole
(beams, shafts, patch, haze, glow, haze k), keyed as before; a hit
restores them. 10 builds in 600 pictures; the worker 15.7 -> 7.2 ms a
picture. Byte-identical with KOL_WIN_CACHE=0 (state 50 at presents 300,
520, 763 the flash; state 53, map 67). Thor not measured. Then, asked to lock
the camera on this map: map 71 joins kNoLookMaps (as 89);
the right stick does not move the camera there.

and someone appears at the bottom; asked for a little light from that
spot, as from an unseen door, not necessarily godrays and with no

#### His blue flame, and the summoning circle (2026-11-11)

states/thor/0232 (A through the talk; he summons his knights). The user: Shaher's blue
flame was darkened by the AO and should be bright and give light; and his spell
that spawns enemies, with a red circle on the floor, should look good.

- **The flame.** As a prop card his flame took the prop's foot shade (it is his lowest part),
  the card's shade and the light; with the camera moved it went nearly black. New map flag
  `glow_flame` (57): on that map's props, texels that are blue flame (green and blue well
  over red: `glow_flame_px`; his 20b0f8 / 48f0f8 and their steps, not the wings' purples)
  keep the game's colour x 1.12 over all the light (`KOL_FLAME_GLOW=<gain>`). A blue lamp
  at (16, 40, 16) (kCeilingLamps, a fire's flicker, reach 160, 1.2) lights the board round
  him; it is lit only while 40 or more blue-flame BG1 pixels are in the frame
  (`Capture::bg1_flame`): the map's earlier scenes have BG1 on and no Shaher (0201 is
  byte-identical to Torchlight off).
- **The circle.** The game draws it on BG2 in screen space, blended as the first target:
  a black circle fading in (EVA 1 -> 16 against EVB 16 -> 10: the floor darkened under it),
  then a red pulse added (EVB 12: the floor under its lines at 3/4). It went through
  `hud_glow` as light on a HUD layer: flat on the screen, so off the floor once the camera
  moved, and faint over the lit floor. New map flag `magic_circle` (57): `circle_capture`
  reads BG2's whole 256 x 256 tilemap from VRAM (the circle is all there, more than the
  GBA's 160 rows show), finds where frame pixels show it (frame x + BG2 scroll - the native
  origin, checked on the frame's BG2 pixels: 678/678 on 0232; one period of the wrap, the
  one the frame shows) and its colour. **The colour from the frame, not the palette:** the
  latched entry (bank 0, index 1) reads black all through while the frame is pink-red; the
  game changes it during the frame. So the frame's less the scene's at EVB, over EVA, as
  hud_glow does (166,49,43 at the pulse's top). Its pixels leave hud_glow; kol_perspective
  `magic_circle` draws it on the scene after the light, each scene pixel by its place in the
  game's picture, so the warp lays it on the floor and it stays there under the stick:
  floor under the lines dimmed (2 x the game's 1 - EVB / 16), lines x 1.4 its colour plus
  0.5 of its peak in white, a halo (box blur 4, twice, cached by the mask) at 0.5, a faint
  ember while it is still black. Pick E of five (shots/map57_circle/circle_variants.png;
  A-D brighter, pinker or muddier); `KOL_CIRCLE=<lines,white,halo,dim,ember>`. Its light: a
  spell light of its colour from 24 over its middle, as wide as it, 0.4 x the pulse
  (`KOL_CIRCLE_LIGHT`). `KOL_NO_MAGIC_CIRCLE=1`: as before; `KOL_CIRCLE_LOG=1`.

Before/after: shots/map57_circle/before_after.png (presents 1000 and 1500 of 0232 with A
taps, and 1500 with the stick at -1, 0.5). Both invariants hold. Not seen on the Thor;
cost unmeasured (map 57 only: a 64 K mask a captured frame, a pass over the circle's box).

### Map 94's clouds, rearranged without seams (2026-11-12)

The clouds past the game's 240 columns (painted in the map editor) met the
game's own at seams: a vertical one where the horizon jumped 18 rows (frame x
328, the array's column 33), one at x 72, and pasted blocks. A blur and new

clouds). Asked instead for the best tile matches for a continuous background,
free to override the art, the central art too, not only the sides and top.

`tools/cloud_tiles.py --map 94 --apply` re-chooses every cloud cell of layer 0
among the tiles the game itself uses for its clouds, from within 3 rows of where
the game uses them: the least colour jump along its four edges, plus a cost for
leaving one of the game's own tiles (3000), for repeating a neighbour's (4000;
not for plain sky) and per row away (500); sweeps until nothing changes. Cells
with rock and cells of pure sky stay; empty cells in the columns the camera can
show (-16..47) are filled down to the art's last row (92). Result: 109 of the
game's cells changed (`ov` lines), the extension's cells rewritten (1973 lines in
all). It writes map_ext.cfg (the user's file, not committed) after saving the
map's lines as they were to `shots/map94_clouds/map_ext_before.cfg`; `--revert`
puts them back (checked byte for byte). `--preview <png>` draws before/after
from the editor's export. Reload the map editor's page before painting map 94
again (it writes back the lines it holds); "Send to Thor" copies the file to the
device.

states/thor/0209, the scene after the beams. The user asked to run the
animation until text appears, on Original and Enhanced, and for Enhanced

**What the game does** (frames after the load; the registers read line by
line, a temporary log in gbarecomp's render_line):

  field, kol::ui_field). WIN1 is on and empty (WIN1H 0xF5FA), WINOUT 0x33
  hides BG2: nothing shows yet.
- 60-301: 0x7D40, WIN0 and WIN1 on. An HBlank DMA rewrites WIN0H and WIN1H
  every line: two circles about (120.5, 84), WIN1 the outer, WIN0 the inner.
  WININ 0x3F3B (inside WIN0: no BG2; inside WIN1: everything), WINOUT 0x33
  (no BG2, no BG3): BG2 shows between the circles, a white ring; BG3, a soft
  glow, inside the outer one. Radii 24 -> 48 and 0 -> 31 over 60-70, held past
  260, then (by 280) both grow to 79.5 / 78.5 at 301: the ring thins to a pixel and
  is gone at 302. It never reaches the game's own edges (4 rows at the
  bottom apart).
- 302-303: 0x1940, no window, the glow alone.
- 304-439: 0x3D40, WIN0 alone, radius 31, WINOUT 0x37: BG2 everywhere but
  inside it, its palette rising from black to white (added: the picture
  goes grey, then white); the glow inside WIN0 only.
- 440-533: 0x1D40, BLDCNT 0x00BF, BLDY 16: all white. 534-1013: 0x1F40,
  BLDCNT 0x00BB (BG2 exempt): the text, black on white. 1014-1144: 0x00BF,
  BLDY 16 -> 0 with BG2 one black tile: white to black. 1154: map 86.
  1164: 0x00FF BLDY 16 (black); 1314: 0x00FB, the white text on black.

**Causes.** The compositor's wide frame was right (windows and all, in the
game's columns). The warp was not: (1) a field is blended over every pixel
of the moved picture (field_all, the thunder's flash), whatever the windows
say: white everywhere from frame 50, when the game still hides it; (2)
hud_glow took the ring's pixels as beams and carried them on scaled; (3)
the field's colour ignored a fade it is a target of: the black BG2 of
1014-1144 was laid over the game's white-to-black fade, black at once.

**Now** (ScenePixels::window_light; kol_focus capture, kol_perspective
window_light_runs / light_anchor; KOL_NO_WINDOW_LIGHT=1 old): with the
field an alpha blend's first target and WIN0 or WIN1 on (no OBJ window),
and the field not shown alike in every part, the field is drawn over the
moved picture only where the windows show it, from each line's window
registers (gbarecomp GbaPpu::latched_line_windows, new). A window whose
lines fit a circle (least squares on the lines that reach neither side,
every line within 1.5 px) is a disc; any other keeps its lines' spans. With
EVB 16 the light is ADDED, as the game adds it (gbarecomp
PresentWarpMesh::over_add_from, new), the BG3 glow with it (its colour where
the blend ran into white: the nearest colour seen whole, not under the glow
beside it); else laid over at 1 - EVB/16. hud_glow leaves the field's
pixels alone and does not carry anything on while the windows' light is up.
**Chosen, flat interface or light:** light. The frame's pixels hold the
blend with the picture as it was flat; drawn flat over the warp they would
show the unmoved floor and units inside the glow and, in 304-439, over the
whole view.
**About the unit:** the light is about a disc's centre: the point of the
picture under it (over the ground first seen at or below it, so a unit's
middle stays over its feet), placed through the warp as the rain's points
are; the discs, the spans and the glow move and scale with it. At rest it
is where the game has it within a pixel; with the camera turned the ring
stays round the unit, at the unit's size. KOL_WINDOW_LIGHT_FIXED=1: where
the frame has it.
**Past the game's 240x160:** a disc goes on as the circle it is (rows and
columns the game never draws: the same centre and radius); "outside both"
is the whole rest of the view (304-439: grey to white to every edge). A
window of plain spans ends at the game's area.
**The fade:** a field that is a target of BLDCNT's brighten or darken takes
BLDY in its colour (kol_focus_present; KOL_FIELD_NO_FADE=1 old).
Checked against the Original at the same guest frames (presents and frames
part ways here: see below): the ring's edges within 1 px at 480x270 in
perspective, pixel for pixel with the light without the perspective (4419
white pixels, 0 apart, frame 148); the glow, the grey, the white-out, both
texts and the fade alike. 384x216 and look 0.6,0.5 seen. 0208 at presents
70, 100, 130 and at look 0.6,0.5, and 0204 at 150: byte-identical to before.
Both invariants hold.
**Presents are not frames here** (both modes alike, not changed): from
frame ~100 to ~464 the game's frame handler runs long, gbarecomp's
present-in-place unwinds ("call-depth unwind", 136 times) and the outer
loop presents the same frame a second time: 1500 presents are 1401 frames.
A windowed 240x160 run has the same 140 doubles. Compare pictures by the
`[present-dump] ... guest frame` line, not by present number. Whether each
double costs a paced frame on the device (the scene ~2.3 s longer) was not
measured.
Left: over the bright floor the glow's colour where the game's blend
saturates is an estimate (alike here to the eye); the rising grey of
304-439 is a palette step ahead (frame 397: 189 against the game's 181;
the field's colour is read by the frame hook, a frame on); the ring is
1 px larger each side at rest (the unit is drawn ~2% larger there); the ring's centre sits up
to ~8 px off the unit at look 0.6,0.5 (the unit's card and the ground point
are placed by different rules); sprites are taken as under the field
everywhere (they are, here).

## RetroAchievements, softcore (2026-11-16)

Options > Achievements logs in to RetroAchievements and lists the game's set
(game 5029; our ROM's MD5 `5d4f385e4e1cfa4a057d0ac828993906` is on its list).

- **rcheevos 12.5.0** vendored in `third_party/rcheevos` (MIT; rc_client, rapi,
  the runtime, md5 only: no hashing, the MD5 is fixed), built by
  `third_party/rcheevos.cmake` into both builds.
- **`src/kol_cheevos.{h,cpp}`**: the rc_client, softcore only. Memory map:
  RA 0x00000-0x07FFF = IWRAM, 0x08000-0x47FFF = EWRAM, 0x48000-0x57FFF (save
  RAM) read as zeros. `cheevos_frame` runs every guest frame from
  `kol_extended_view_frame` (never in an excursion); a frame-count jump (a
  state load) calls `rc_client_reset`. Logged out it does nothing.
- **Login**: a password once; only the token is kept, in
  `settings_dir()/retroachievements.cfg` (gitignored). A refused or expired
  token is deleted. Errors are shortened for the menu's two-line help.
- **User agent** `KnightOfLodisRecomp/0.1.0 (Android N|macOS) rcheevos/12.5`.
  The server does not know it: it serves the set with a "Warning: Unknown
  Emulator" entry first and turns any hardcore unlock into a casual one
  (RAWeb `ClientSupportLevel::Unknown`). Raise `kClientVersion` with each
  release; message RAdmin to have it listed as casual-only.
- **Android**: `Cheevos.java` (HttpURLConnection, a toast per unlock, the
  login dialog), bound in `main_android.cpp`; the INTERNET permission.
- **Desktop**: libcurl (`src/kol_cheevos_curl.cpp`); notices on stderr; no
  text entry, so `KOL_RA_USER=... KOL_RA_PASSWORD=...` once, then the token.
- **Badges**: each row starts with its badge at 16x16, the HELP box shows
  the selected one at 32x32; locked ones grey at 60%. Fetched once from the
  media server (rcheevos' URL), kept in `settings_dir()/badges/`, decoded with
  stb_image (`third_party/stb`, public domain), box-filtered.
- **Unlock popup**: the game's window (`menu_cheevo_popup_render`, 28x6
  tiles): badge 32x32, "Achievement Unlocked!" + points, the title; the
  game's confirm sound. Android: `Cheevos.showPopup`, top-right corner,
  3x per 1080 lines, slides in, 4 s, slides out, queued. Badges are
  prefetched when the set loads. Desktop: `KOL_RA_POPUP_PPM=path
  [KOL_RA_POPUP_BADGE=name]` writes a sample.
- **"Warning: Unknown Emulator"** (the server's made-up entry, id 101000001
  and up) is left out of the list and the toasts; rcheevos already leaves it
  out of the counts and never submits it. Unlocks stay casual all the same.
- Checked: the page drawn headlessly (`KOL_MENU_PPM=out.ppm,k80 x17;k1`), a
  login with a made-up account ("Wrong name or password", nothing saved),
  the 240 invariant. Not yet tried with a real account or on the Thor.

## The Thor's misses, six weeks of them, compiled (2026-11-16 night)

The Thor's `files/misses/` (408 launches, 10-06 to 11-16) named 6,651
distinct PCs the interpreter ran: 6,615 in ROM, 35 in IWRAM, 1 in EWRAM.
None were in the build. 434 M instructions interpreted in all; a typical
launch 100 k, the worst 62 M (11-10). The user never noticed a stutter;
done before going public for slower phones.

- **ROM (all covered).** Each PC grouped to its function: the nearest
  `push {.., lr}` at or before it (546 functions, every one after a return,
  a branch, padding or a literal pool; 7 of them held 63% of the work, 50
  held 90%). 541 `[[extra_func]]` (5 were entries already). Then 12 PCs
  left: two switches (`0x0807C024`, 21 cases, `cmp r0, #0x14`, the finder
  walked 18; `0x08156EA8`, 6 cases) and five leaves reached only through
  pointer tables (found as `addr | 1` in ROM data).
- **EWRAM `0x02026CC0` (39 M instructions): not code.** One entry in one
  launch (10-22 21:56): the CPU ran through pointer data there, a runaway
  that evening. Nothing to compile.
- **IWRAM `0x03007C48`..`0x03007E5C`: the flash-save routines,** copied
  onto the stack just before use (the SDK's way: flash cannot be read while
  written; `ldrb r0, [r0]; bx lr` caught by `GBARECOMP_MISS_IWRAM_DUMP` at
  a cold boot). They exist for an instant, at addresses that depend on the
  call depth, and run only while saving, loading or checking the save at
  boot. Left interpreted on purpose: a moment per save, and save code is
  not worth the risk.
- **Checked:** the reference binary against the new one, headless,
  `GBARECOMP_SELFHEAL_RECOMPILE=0`: EX, BL, FF, EM, AF, EV, CI, EU and a cold
  boot at 600 and 1800 frames, 18/18 pictures identical; the 107 Thor states
  from 0200 on at 1800 frames, 107/107 identical, interpreted instructions
  8,605,278 -> 160,136, distinct misses 1,959 -> 6, fully static 87 -> 106
  (left: 0245, a save, and the boot: the flash routines). Both invariants
  unchanged. `generated/` must be regenerated on a fresh tree.
- **Size:** the new entries led the finder into much more code (dispatch
  entries 403,769 -> 531,972; `generated/` 351 -> 444 MB); libmain.so
  94.6 -> 120.3 MB, the APK ~139 -> ~165 MB. (A debug APK built
  incrementally showed 282 MB: Gradle's leftover space, gone when rebuilt
  from scratch.)
- **Desktop launches stall ~74 s** in the self-heal cache (`recomp_cache/`,
  ~4,150 dylibs, Mac only; the Thor never uses it): checks pass
  `GBARECOMP_SELFHEAL_RECOMPILE=0`. Clearing it is the user's call.

## Mods: playing a patched game (Options > Mod, 2026-11-17)

The user added "Lancelot - Somebody To Love" as both a `.ups` and an `.ips`
(not committed: a mod is the player's file). Both turn our ROM (MD5
5d4f385e…) into the same image (MD5 cce2f4af…, SHA-1 f3ff2c1b…): 5,517 bytes
in 991 places, **all data**, none within 64 bytes of a compiled function:
the class table 0x08615228 (2.5 KB), the talent table 0x0861A8F0, the menu
icon table, the terrain panel, the HELP text banks (1 KB) and ~4.8 KB at
0x08769134-0x0876EFC3 (after the place -> battle map table; likely the
battles' setups). Nothing our hooks key on: the harbour script, the world
map event bank and the name strips are untouched.

A second mod, "Tactics Ogre TKoL Re-Rebalanced" (`.ips` + its `.txt` notes:
every class's stats, modifiers and abilities), is smaller: 695 bytes in 241
records, 682 in the class table and 13 in the talent table, SHA-1 bddea926….
Accepted the same way (no code), boot at 300 frames identical to the stock
game's. Our second-screen sheets read both tables from the loaded ROM, so
they show the mod's numbers. One mod at a time: both rewrite the class table.

How it plays (gbarecomp ENHANCEMENTS "A player's mod"): `--rom-patch FILE`
applies an IPS / IPS32 / UPS / BPS patch over the verified stock ROM in memory
and refuses one that changes compiled code. Desktop: pass the flag. Android:
Options > Mod (main page, after Achievements) shows the mod playing; A opens
`Mods.java`'s dialog: Choose a patch (the system picker, through
SetupActivity's `pick_mod` mode; copied to `files/mod/<its name>`, one at a
time), Remove mod, then "Close the game" (it is read only at start). The first
setup screen has "Select a mod (optional)" / "No mod" too. main_android checks
the patch before starting (`rom_patch_load_and_check`): one that does not
apply or touches code goes to `files/mod_refused/`, a message says why, and
the original game starts.

Kept apart per mod (keyed by the patched ROM's SHA-1, first 8): the cartridge
save `totkol-f3ff2c1b.sav`, the slots `totkol-f3ff2c1b.stateN`, the numbered
states `states-f3ff2c1b/`, and the fast-load memo (it keys on RAM, not on the
ROM the routines also read: the mod changes the terrain panel table they
read). A mod starts with no save: the original game's save is not carried
over.

KoL: achievements are off with a mod ("Not available with a mod loaded."; the
set is made for the stock game). The transcribed name strips (`kStripText`)
are dropped for any strip a patch redraws (`strip_text`), so a renamed item
shows its new strip.

Checked (Mac): UPS and IPS give the same SHA-1; boot 300 frames stock / UPS /
IPS identical, same 3 boot misses (flash-save code, as always); three
hand-made IPS patches: one changing an instruction (0x080000C4), one an odd
byte of a THUMB instruction (0x080221B7) and one inside an IWRAM code copy's
ROM source (0x08025FF4) are refused, a HELP-text byte is accepted. Both render
invariants unchanged (66e13ab2 / 9054c456). Not seen on a device yet; the
mod's own changes not played.

### Then: the notice, the setup screen, restarting (2026-11-17)

- **"Mod Loaded"**: a second after start, with a mod, the achievement popup's
  window (top right, slides in) says so with the mod's name
  (`cheevos_mod_notice_frame`, `menu_notice_popup_render`; desktop:
  `KOL_RA_POPUP_PPM` + `KOL_RA_POPUP_MOD=name` writes it).
- **The setup screen** (SetupActivity) is three boxes side by side, ROM / BIOS
  / Mod, each opening the picker: a red "!" for a missing or wrong ROM (or a
  wrong BIOS), a grey "?" for the optional BIOS and mod, a green check when
  loaded; a note that the real BIOS is best and the HLE BIOS is used without
  one; Remove mod and Play. The "Play without a BIOS" checkbox is gone: Play
  writes `files/no_bios` when there is no correct BIOS. No title bar; it
  scrolls; picking the ROM no longer starts the game.
- **Restart, not close**: "Restart the game" after picking or removing a mod
  (`RestartActivity`, its own `:restart` process: ends the game's process,
  starts SetupActivity, which goes on to the game).
- **Debug > Unlink ROM** (dev builds): sets `files/totkol.gba` aside as
  `totkol.gba.unlinked` and restarts on the setup screen; "Use the previous
  ROM" there puts it back. Mods live in `mods/` locally (gitignored).

### Then: everything in the game's own windows (2026-11-17)

- **RetroAchievements notices** (welcome with the account's avatar and the

  drawn in the achievement popup's window on the guest thread
  (`show_notices`); the Android toasts remain only without a popup backend.

  (`rc_client_user_get_image_url(u)`; a made-up `rc_client_user_t` with no

- **Popups size to their text**: 28 x 6 tiles at least, wider up to 40, then

- **Dialogs** (`menu_dialog`): the Mod dialog, "Restart to play …?", "Mod

## A moving camera rebuilt the light every frame (2026-11-17)

Thor state 0309 (map 62's house scene, window light): it felt slow while moving
the camera. Story scenes got a small look on 11-16, and two per-view caches
missed on every frame while the stick moved:

- **The overscan crept with the look** (`perspective_overscan`): the scene's
  size and place changed a pixel a frame, keys of the window light and the
  lamps/AO. It now grows at once in 16-px steps and shrinks after 60 frames of
  needing less (`KOL_OVERSCAN_EXACT=1` old). Map 62 on the Mac, worker mean:
  still 6.2, moving 27.7 -> 6.7 ms. Still picture byte-identical; moving, 26
  one-pixel edges (warp rounding from the moved origin).
- **The lamp light's backdrop key hashed the margins** (map 56, state 0302):
  the side margins are composed only on the rows the tilt needs, the rest left
  as backdrop. Now hashed inside the view only (`KOL_GLOW_KEY_WHOLE=1` old):
  moving 15.1 -> 9.8 ms (still 8.1), pictures byte-identical still and moving.

`KOL_PERSP_STICK_SWEEP=<frames a turn>` turns the stick in a circle for
headless cost runs. A sweep over one Thor state per map (71 maps) found no
other map where moving costs more than ~3 ms over still (the mesh rebuilt per
view); maps 75, 73 and 84 are heavy even still (15-19 ms on the Mac).
