## Rewind on L2 (2026-11-17)

L2 was gbarecomp's default Rewind binding already, but KoL kept no history.
Now `RunOptions::rewind_history_seconds = 20` (desktop and Android): a state
every 15 frames (~80 kept, ~50 MB), each L2 press back a second, held it
repeats every half second. While Debug > Tile Info (the L2 height editor) or
Debug > L2 Moves Sun is on, KoL sets gbarecomp's new
`g_runtime_rewind_blocked` each frame and L2 stays theirs. Cost on the Mac: a
capture is ~0.16 ms in the input pump, every 15th frame. Both invariants
unchanged. Desktop: the Rewind key (1).

## On-screen controls when no controller is connected (2026-11-17)

gbarecomp's touch controls were always off on Android (`GBARECOMP_TOUCH_CONTROLS=0`,
for the Thor). New gbarecomp mode `GBARECOMP_TOUCH_CONTROLS=auto`, now the
Android default: shown while no SDL game controller is open, hidden as soon
as one is (USB, Bluetooth, or a handheld's own pad: the Thor's opens at
start), following SDL's controller added/removed events
(`update_auto_touch`). Pixel 6, no controller: D-pad, A, B, L, R, Select,
Start beside the 16:9 picture (log `touch_controls=1`; its one joystick is
not a game controller). Not on screen: Rewind (L2), the unit buttons (X/Y),
L3+R3.

Then (the user): the picture keeps the whole height, the buttons over it, all
grey and more see-through, Nintendo's layout (A east, B south, Y west, X
north), and Rewind and Fast-forward buttons. gbarecomp `touch_layout` (Android):
sized by the drawable's height, so round on any phone; a 5x7 pixel font for
A, B, X, Y, L, R, SELECT, START; Rewind/Fast-forward as double triangles
under L and R. X and Y reach the game as the controller's own buttons
(`g_host_pad_button_hook`: KoL's unit buttons), Rewind and Fast-forward feed
the host's assist inputs. The desktop layout is unchanged.

Then: the hold's blue progress bar is drawn only in builds with gbarecomp's
runtime menu (KoL has none, so the hold did nothing but show it). And with no
controller, a finger that goes down on no button drags the camera: it sets
`g_host_pad_right_stick` (a full push at 15% of the screen's height from
where it went down; centred on release), so the perspective's look moves and
springs back as with the stick; it presses nothing it slides over.

**The first rewind crashed (Pixel 6, 2026-11-17):** `rewind_loaded`, then a
jump to 0xFF00 read from the game's task table. gbarecomp loaded the rewind
point inside the present hook, so under present-in-place the guest's old call
chain resumed on the restored memory; and its points were recorded there
too. Now, as the save-state slots: a rewind asked for in the hook is pending
and applied at a dispatch boundary outside any exception handler, and points
are recorded only there (the hook asks the guest out when one is due, and the
boundary clears that unwind first: left set, the guest stops). Headless
(`GBARECOMP_ASSIST_SCRIPT="400:rewind;430:rewind;460:rewind;700:rewind"` on
Thor state 0309): four rewinds, each ~45-60 frames back, fully static, no
crash; guest time per frame unchanged (6.99 vs 6.89 ms); invariants hold.

And with the menu open on one screen (BACK): the overlay is only as wide as
the page (248 k, centred, SecondScreen.showOverlay), so the strips beside it
are the game's surface: the on-screen controls show there over the held
game and drive the menu (its input is still read while held). Checked on the
Pixel 6: D-pad down moved the menu's hand.

Then: **Cheats > Rewind** (`rewind`, off by default). Off, KoL sets
`g_runtime_rewind_blocked`: L2 does not rewind, gbarecomp keeps no history
(and drops what it had), and the on-screen Rewind button is not drawn nor
pressable. **Save States** is a main-page row below Cheats (page 7); its Back
returns to the page it was opened from (Debug's row, else the main page;
L3+R3 counts as the main page).

Then: the Save States page has a **save button** at its title's right end
(the bottom bar's button: its frame, the world map's save icon, pushed in
while touched; R on the pad): it does what L3+R does (`kol::states_save_new`,
slot 1 through the path hook). For it to save at once on one screen, where
the game is held while the menu is open, gbarecomp's hold loop now steps out
to the dispatch boundary when a save, load or rewind is pending, and holds
again at the next present (it used to wait for the menu to close). Pixel 6:
the D-pad and A on the on-screen controls to the page, the button tapped:
`state_drain: applying save=1` 22 ms later, state 1 listed with its picture.

## Pixel 6 performance (2026-11-17)

Measured with SurfaceFlinger timestats and per-thread CPU (states copied from
the Thor; the phone warm, its big core at 1.4 of 2.8 GHz):
- **45 Hz cap:** the Pixel rendered the app at `renderFrameRate 45` (adaptive
  refresh guessing from what we present). MainActivity now says
  `Surface.setFrameRate(60, FIXED_SOURCE)` (API 30+): map 62's house scene
  ~44 -> 60 fps.
- **Profile** (simpleperf `--app`, no system change; map 9 battle): present
  threads 50% (reflect_ray 14%, warp mesh ~28%), game thread 37.5%
  (compositor 20%, should_yield + tick 19%), audio 8% (the stall search; see
  gbarecomp ENHANCEMENTS "Audio bridge"). After that fix: audio 2%, map 9
  ~38-40 -> ~55 fps.

## Steam Deck (started 2026-11-18, branch `steam-deck`)

Asked: a Steam Deck build. The Deck is a Linux x86-64 computer with one
1280x800 screen and a controller, so it is the desktop build plus everything
the Android app does around the game. This section is the port's state.

**Built so far, checked on the Mac only** (headless, `SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy
SDL_RENDER_DRIVER=software`, present dumps):

- **The options menu over the game** (`src/kol_desktop.{h,cpp}`). kol_menu's
  canvas, which Android shows on the second screen, is a present-time overlay
  here: centred, at the largest whole scale that fits (4 on 1280x800), the
  black around its windows see-through (a fill from the canvas's edge), the
  game dimmed behind it as on Android (`g_present_dim`). **F10** or a **click
  of the right stick** (down and up within 400 ms, L3 not held: L3 + R3 stays
  the Save States page) opens and closes it; the pad drives it through
  kol_menu's key filter, as on Android. gbarecomp: `g_present_overlay_provider`
  and `g_host_key_hook` (ENHANCEMENTS "A game's own pictures over the window").
- **Player mode** (`kol::desktop_prepare`, first thing in `main`): with
  `--data-dir <dir>` or `KOL_DATA_DIR`, or by default in a public build
  (`KOL_DEV_TOOLS=OFF`: `$XDG_DATA_HOME/KnightOfLodisRecomp`, else
  `~/.local/share/KnightOfLodisRecomp`; `~/Library/Application Support/...` on
  a Mac), the game's files live in one directory under Android's names
  (`totkol.gba`, optional `gba_bios.bin`, `totkol.sav`, `enhancements.cfg`,
  `states/`), `kol::settings_init` reads and saves the settings there (a fresh
  directory starts on Enhanced), the BIOS is used when present and `--no-bios`
  otherwise, the Game Boy logo is skipped, and the self-heal compiler is off.
  Without it a run is the developer's, exactly as before (no settings file).
  No ROM in the directory: a message box says where to put it, and the game
  does not start (the setup screen's place).
- **A view size chosen at run time drew enlarged on the desktop** (found by
  the first player-mode dump: a 384x216 battle filled the window with a

    shift. `KOL_PASS_SHIFT=0` off; `KOL_PASS_SHIFT_CHECK=1` draws the whole
    pass too and compares; `KOL_PASS_SHIFT_LOG=1` says why a pass was not
    shifted.

### Lifted props and walls: the work a moving camera repeated (2026-11-19)

Asked: lifting (what BG1 hid, seen as the camera moves) for less. Measured
with the camera moving (`KOL_PERSP_STICK_SWEEP`): the camera does not change
its cost; about two thirds was scene work done again identically every frame.
Trap: KOL_WORKER_TIME's "total" sums nested sections (warp.scene holds
scene.*, scene.lift holds lift.*); the job's real time is the
`[present-pipeline] jobs=N compute mean` line (GBARECOMP_FRAME_PHASE), and
the section table held 48 (now 64: mesh.* were dropped).

- **The window light behind lifted pixels** (`lift_window_light`) is kept per
  world point: a pixel reuses the last picture's value at its place shifted
  by the pan, when that place shows the same world point and height and the
  key (the world, heights and sun without the view: `pass_still_key`; the
  sun's height, window masks, shutter, beams, shafts, haze, map) is the same.
  `KOL_LIFT_WIN_MEMO=0` off, `KOL_LIFT_WIN_MEMO_CHECK=1` compares every reuse.
- **Wall lifting** (kol_focus_atlas): cells with no prop and no layer skip
  the per-pixel tests first; step 3's box counts from prefix sums (per
  thread, per group) instead of re-counting each box.
- **Card runs** (kol_perspective `warp_card_runs`): a corner is tested only
  between its rows' own first and last pixels (every corner of a 33 x 33
  square was tested for a few pixels).
- Byte-identical: the `KOL_PERSP_HASH` fingerprints through a pan with the
  camera turning, `KOL_LIFT_PAR_CHECK` (601 checks), the memo check.
- Deck (EM, Enhanced): lifting's cost +3.45 -> +2.55 ms a frame. Left: walls
  0.72 (want, inlay, pieces, fill), window light 0.22, props 0.12, atlas fill
  +0.38, card runs +0.34. Next idea: walls per tile, reused (the inlay's
  flood fill needs a per-component recompute).

### RetroAchievements on the desktop: the login form, HTTPS, the popups (2026-11-19/20)

From the Deck: the Achievements page's Log In opened nothing (the desktop
printed how to use KOL_RA_USER), then "No answer from the server", then no
welcome.

- **A login form in the menu** (`MenuPlatform::login_in_menu`; kol_menu
  `login_*`): the game's window over the dimmed page, Username and Password
  (stars), a message line, Log In and Cancel. The pad moves, A presses,
  Start logs in, B cancels; the keyboard types (gbarecomp
  `g_host_text_input` / `g_host_text_hook`: while it is up the keyboard
  presses nothing for the game and SDL_TEXTINPUT comes to the form). On
  SteamOS the line says "Steam + X: on-screen keyboard." The password is
  wiped once sent and never kept. Android keeps its own dialog.
- **Enter**: on Username it goes to Password, on Password it logs in, also
  with a controller attached (the Deck: Steam's keyboard types Enter). On the
  buttons it stays the pad's A: Desktop Mode types Enter from A too.
- **Characters the font lacks** (`# $ ; @ \ ^ ` { | } ~`) are drawn from a
  one-pixel stand-in font (kol_menu `kStandIns`, codes 0xE0+; the user: "even
  if it looks weird"); `[ ]` and `"` take the font's own 0x53, 0x54, 0x51
  (`"` was 0x52, the font's ellipsis). The sheet's encoder gets spaces.
- **HTTPS from the AppImage**: its libcurl and OpenSSL come from the
  freedesktop SDK, whose OpenSSL looks under /etc/pki/tls; SteamOS keeps
  certificates in /etc/ssl/certs, so every request failed (curl 35, "TLS
  connect error ... No such file or directory"). kol_cheevos_curl now gives
  libcurl the first certificate bundle found in the distributions' usual
  places (SSL_CERT_FILE wins). Checked on the Deck: a made-up login got the
  server's "Invalid user/password combination".
- **Popups** (kol_desktop `desktop_popup`, `cheevos_set_popup`): the welcome,
  unlocks and the mod notice, as Android's: top right, slide in 250 ms, held
  4 s, out 250 ms, one at a time, x round(height x 3 / 1080). Before, the
  desktop only logged them. `KOL_DESKTOP_POPUP_AT=<n>` (dev) shows a sample.
- Seen working by the user on the Mac (11-20). On the Deck: the login and the
  welcome not yet confirmed after the certificate fix.

### Windows: cross-compiled on the Mac (2026-11-20)

`tools/package_windows.sh` -> `build/release/KnightOfLodisRecomp-<version>-windows-x64.zip`:
a folder with KnightOfLodisRecomp.exe (SDL2 and the C++ runtime linked in, no
DLL but Windows' own: the script checks the import table), the HD bank beside
it, licenses.txt and a README.txt. Built on this Mac with Homebrew's MinGW-w64
(`brew install mingw-w64`, GCC 16.2; toolchain `tools/mingw-w64-x86_64.cmake`)
and SDL2 2.30.9 built from its release source (the Flatpak's pinned version
and SHA-256) as a static library in build-windows-deps/. gbarecomp's
GBARECOMP_STATIC_RELEASE does the static link, with its prefix pointed there.

- Achievements over WinHTTP (`src/kol_cheevos_winhttp.cpp`; Windows has no
  libcurl): the system's certificates and proxy, TLS 1.2/1.3.
- The setup screen's ROM / BIOS / mod through the system's Open dialog
  (`src/kol_setup_win.cpp`, as the Mac's panel).
- `src/kol_windows.rc`: the icon (the Android launcher icon's PNGs in an .ico)
  and a manifest with UTF-8 as the code page (Windows 10 1903 on), so a user
  folder with accents opens through the game's UTF-8 paths.
- Portability: the badge folder made with std::filesystem (POSIX mkdir), no
  nanosecond mtime from MinGW's stat, and `SceneBuild::rounds` defined in
  kol_focus.cpp: as an inline thread_local with a constructor in the header,
  MinGW's GCC gave each file its own TLS init function and the link refused.
- A relative `--data-dir` is made absolute: a public build moves into
  <dir>/logs before the runtime opens the ROM, and on Windows the runtime's
  own Open dialog then came up for the ROM it could not find.
- Wine 11 on this Mac (a private prefix, display driver null, SDL dummy):
  600 frames, HD sound verified, a made-up login answered by the server over
  WinHTTP. Not run on a real Windows PC. Unsigned: SmartScreen asks once.

### Options > Licenses on the desktop, and the notices of what each package carries (2026-11-20)

The desktop's Licenses row opened a dialog naming a file in the source tree.
Now a page over the whole window (`setup_text_page` in kol_setup.cpp: the
setup screen's Roboto rasterised on the CPU with stb_truetype, sized to the
window, h / 800 as its unit), shown by kol_desktop as a present overlay over
the menu. The pad through the menu (`MenuPlatform::page_up / page_scroll /
page_close`, in menu_filter_keys with its press and repeat rules: up/down two
lines, L/R or left/right a page, B or A back), Escape, Page Up/Down,
Home/End and the wheel (an SDL event watch). `KOL_DESKTOP_LICENSES_AT=<n>[,first]`
(dev) opens it at a present.

The text: `tools/make_licenses.py` now writes two files. Android's as before
(the Roboto and stb_truetype sections, desktop-only, hand-added there, are
gone). `third_party/NOTICES-desktop.txt` adds the setup screen's typeface and
renderer and the libraries the packages carry: the AppImage's (libcurl,
OpenSSL, nghttp2, libpsl, libidn2 and libunistring under the LGPLv3, zlib,
libffi, libdecor, the GCC runtime), the Windows .exe's (MinGW-w64 runtime,
winpthreads), the Mac app's (SDL3, sdl2-compat), then the Apache 2.0, LGPLv3
and GPLv3 texts in full. ASCII (the page draws ASCII). The licence texts are
in `third_party/licenses/`, fetched 2026-11-20 at the packages' versions
(curl 8.11.1, nghttp2 1.65.0, libpsl 0.21.5, zlib 1.3.1, libidn2 2.3.7,
libffi 3.4.6 and libdecor 0.2.2 (their SDK versions not read; the texts are
the same), mingw-w64 14.0.0, GCC 14.2's runtime
exception) or taken from Homebrew's kegs (OpenSSL, libunistring, SDL3,
sdl2-compat, mingw-w64). CMake bakes the desktop file; every package script
puts it beside the game as licenses.txt.

Also: the desktop's Options > Mod said "Start the game with --rom-patch
FILE"; it now says a mod is chosen on the setup window and how to get it
back (delete totkol.gba, or --setup).

Then, before 1.1 went out: the APK's `libc++_shared.so` (the NDK's C++
runtime, there since 1.0) had no notice. Android's text now ends with
libc++'s and libc++abi's, verbatim from NDK r27's toolchain NOTICE
(`third_party/licenses/libcxx*-ndk27.txt`). The Mac zip is packed without
the `__MACOSX/._*` sidecars (`ditto --norsrc --noextattr`; the signature
verifies after unzipping).

## 1.1.1: two slow scenes, the Deck's music, Options > Display (2026-11-20)

### Map 102's sunset and map 58 at night, faster

Thor states 0311 (map 102: narration, rain, the sun setting) and 0312 (map
58, the ship at night) were slow on the Thor and the Deck. Every change below
is byte-identical (`KOL_PERSP_HASH=1`, line by line; the first frame after a
state load varies run to run on both states, so it is left out of every
comparison) except the prop-shadow spread, which is a timing change.

- **What the mean hid.** On 0311 five pictures in six took ~8.2 ms of worker
  time on the Mac and every sixth ~14.8 ms: the sunset moves the sun every
  6th frame, and the terrain pass, the prop shadows, the shadow map and its
  edge were all redone for it. The 300-job means did not show it; per-job
  times did (`KOL_WORKER_SLOW=1` sections per job, gbarecomp
  `GBARECOMP_JOB_LOG=1` each job's time, and the job-spread line at exit
  with `GBARECOMP_FRAME_PHASE`).
- **The terrain pass in row bands** on the row pool: the clear on the caller,
  then one band of rows per thread, each walking every cell and drawing only
  its own rows, so each pixel is still the last cell drawn over it.
  `KOL_PASS_SERIAL=1` old, `KOL_PASS_PAR_CHECK=1` draws it again serially and
  compares.
- **Prop shadows in three steps** (keys, matching, casts), the keys and the
  casts on the pool, keys kept while the props, the sun and the camera are
  the same. `KOL_PROP_SHADOW_SERIAL=1` old.
- **Kept across pictures:** lamp sight grids of lamps that did not move
  (`KOL_LAMP_VIS_KEEP=0`, `_CHECK=1`), the ship model's rope sums while its
  patch is unchanged, `scene_props` by identity, the BG1 opaque map (an
  8-slot cache), the warp mesh. The model pass walks one flag byte per
  pixel; the prop-under-interface walk starts only beside interface sprites
  (`KOL_PROP_FRONT_ALL=1` old).
- **The next sunset step's shadow map built ahead** on its own thread: the
  next step's sun height is known exactly (`t_sun_ahead_steps`), so it is
  built during the quiet pictures and taken at the step only on an exact key
  over every input and the whole height and roof data. Roof and box lookups
  became free functions over a `RoofSet` so the thread works on its own copy
  (map 102 has two boxes). Posting it on the step picture slowed that
  picture's terrain pass (1.4 -> 2.3 ms): it is posted a picture later.
  `KOL_SHADOW_AHEAD=0` off, `_CHECK=1`, `_LOG=1`. 119 of 120 steps took it.
- **Prop shadows spread over three pictures** when only the sun moved: a
  third of the props recast per picture, the rest keep the last step's
  shadow until their turn. Not byte-identical: three pictures per step
  differ, at most a few pixels of shadow one step behind.
  `KOL_PROP_SHADOW_SPREAD=1` puts back all at once (byte-identical to the
  build before), `_LOG=1`.

Mac worker time: 0311 mean 11.8 -> ~8.2 ms, the step pictures 14.8 -> ~9.8
(quiet ones ~8.1); 0312 10.4 -> ~9.5. Tried and removed: a tighter bound on
the shadow map's rays (same output, same time).

### The banded terrain pass crashed on maps with rounded cells

Found on the Deck the same evening (its state 0302, map 56, and others):
a segfault in the terrain pass on a row-pool helper. `SceneBuild::rounds`
(the rounded towers and boxes) is a static `thread_local`, so a helper saw
an empty list while `round_of` pointed into the caller's. Maps 102 and 58
have no rounded cells, which is why the checks there never met it. Each
helper now takes the caller's list for its band. Checked with
`KOL_PASS_PAR_CHECK=1` on 0302, EM panning (61 passes), FS and EP: the same.
Pool work must be checked on a map with rounds too.

### The music on the Deck: a late picture no longer holds the game

On Android a picture the present worker has not finished 3 ms into the
present is skipped (the last one shown again) and the game goes on
(gbarecomp `GBARECOMP_PRESENT_SKIP_LATE`, since 2026-10-26). gbarecomp left
it off on the desktop for its picture tests, so on the Deck every late
worker held the guest, and the music with it. The desktop's player mode now
turns it on, except with the dummy video driver or a present dump (every
headless test).

### Options > Display (desktop)

Players on Windows reported Alt+Enter doing nothing: with a controller
connected, the desktop key hook took every key but F1-F12. Alt+Enter now
goes to the host's toggle. And a Display page above Graphics: **Display**
(Window / Full Screen) and **Window Size**, the window's own size, apart
from the game's view size (the picture is fitted into the window). The
sizes are common 16:9 and 16:10 ones that fit the display's usable area,
of the display's own shape (the Deck's 1280x800 is 16:10; its taskbar left
no 16:10 size at first, only 16:9 ones). Window Size is greyed and skipped
in full screen. Saved in `display.cfg` (mode=, window=WxH), read before the
window opens, over the launcher's `--fullscreen`; Alt+Enter's switch is
saved too. gbarecomp: `g_host_window_mode_request` /
`g_host_window_size_request`, `g_host_window_*_now`,
`g_host_display_usable` / `_size`, applied once a frame on the window's
thread (`HostWindow::apply_display_requests`). Greyed text is lightened, not
darkened: the menu's text is dark on a light window.

### Lifted Props and Walls back in Enhanced

Taken out for 1.1 for the Deck's sake, put back. Settings are saved key by
key, not by preset, so a player who never changed anything had them saved
off. `settings_version=2` is now written; a file without it whose settings
are exactly 1.1's Enhanced is moved to today's Enhanced once. Checked: 1.1's
Enhanced file -> on; with one other change -> untouched; version 2 with
them off -> stays off.

## Options > Display > Ratio: the picture's shape (2026-11-21)

Asked: a Ratio row in the Display page, 1:1, 4:3, 3:2, 16:10 or 16:9, the
one that suits the top (or only) screen chosen by itself, on Android and the
desktop; the desktop's window sizes to follow it. Until now the view sizes
were 16:9 everywhere (asked 2026-11-17), 16:10 only on a 16:10 computer (the
Deck): a 4:3 tablet showed a 16:9 picture with an eighth of the screen black
above and below.

- **kol_settings** `kRatios`: each shape's sizes, the authentic 240x160 first
  in every list. 1:1 240x240 256x256 270x270 280x280; 4:3 256x192 288x216
  320x240 360x270; 3:2 270x180 300x200 324x216 360x240 420x280; 16:10
  256x160 320x200 384x240 432x270; 16:9 284x160 320x180 384x216 480x270. The
  renderer's range is 240..480 wide, 160..280 tall (GbaPpu kMaxRender*), so
  4:3 and 1:1 grow taller, not wider. 240x240 is the only size at the game's
  own width (margins above and below only); 240x240, 256x192 and 280x280
  were rendered on B_rictor before the lists were made: whole, margins filled.
- **The screen's shape** (`ratio_for_panel`): nearest by the log of the
  ratio. 1920x1080 and 20:9 phones 16:9, the Deck 16:10, 1024x768 4:3,
  2160x1440 3:2, 720x720 1:1 (KOL_PANEL runs). On a Mac the notch is taken off
  the screen first (`mac_main_screen_top_inset`, NSScreen safeAreaInsets):
  full screen sits below it, so a notched MacBook's 1512x982 (nearest 3:2)
  plays as 1512x945, 16:10. Not seen on a notched Mac; this one has no notch.
- **Saved** as `ratio=4:3` only once picked; otherwise the screen decides at
  every start. A size is now known by width AND height (320 is 320x180,
  320x200 or 320x240; 240 is Original or 1:1's 240x240). A saved size not on
  the shape's list becomes the list's nearest in height, except that a
  preset's own size (as many lines: Enhanced 216, Original 160) with the
  rest of the settings that preset's becomes the preset's size for the
  shape, so the Preset row stays on it. Presets name lines now, not a width:
  Enhanced is the size nearest 216 lines (384x216, 288x216, 324x216, 320x200,
  240x240), on a computer the widest whole-pixel size when that one is
  uneven, as before.
- **Changing the ratio** (`ratio_choice_set`) rebuilds the list and keeps a
  preset's size (or the nearest one); Original stays Original.
- **Menu:** the Display page is on Android too (Ratio only); on a computer
  Display, Ratio, Window Size.
- **Desktop window sizes** (`kWindowSizes`): common sizes of each shape
  (1:1 720..2160, 4:3 800x600..2880x2160, 3:2 720x480..3240x2160, 16:10,
  16:9); Window Size offers the chosen shape's that fit the usable area. A
  change of ratio puts the window at the new shape's size nearest its height
  (at once in Window mode; for going back to a window in full screen);
  a window already of that shape stays.

Checked (Mac, player mode, KOL_PANEL): the lists and picks above; a 16:9
Enhanced file on a 4:3 screen -> 256x192 (288x216 is 3.56x at 768) with the
Preset row on Enhanced; a hand-picked 480x270 on 4:3 -> 360x270; ratio=4:3
on a 1080p screen kept; the menu's Ratio stepped from 16:9 to 16:10 ->
432x270 (Enhanced's whole size at 1080), ratio=16:10 saved, the window
960x600; the Display page and its HELP rendered (KOL_MENU_PPM). Both render
invariants (66e13ab2 / 9054c456). Not tried on a device.

### The options menu in two pages (2026-11-21)

Asked the same day: the game's options on a page of their own, the
enhancements on another, Save States and Achievements staying on the first
level. The main page is now **Game Options** (page 10: the cartridge's
twelve), **Enhancement Options** (page 11: Preset, Display, Graphics,
Audio, Gameplay, Cheats, Mod, Licenses), Save States, Achievements, then
Quit Game on a computer and Debug in a dev build. Quit Game stays on the
first level (my call, said to the user): it is how a computer with only a
controller leaves the game. The "- Enhancements -" heading is gone.

- Back goes to the page's parent (`parent_page`: Enhancement Options' five
  pages to it, Layers to Debug, Save States where it was opened from), the
  hand on the row that opened the page; `g_return_sel` is gone.
- The game's own OPTION command (its system menu) opens the menu on Game
  Options, first option, and Back/B there closes it, back to the game's
  menu, as its own window did (`g_game_option`).

Checked (KOL_MENU_PPM): the main page, Enhancement Options, Game Options
(the cartridge's names and HELP), B from Graphics -> Enhancement Options on
Graphics' row; DZ (the system menu on Option): A opens Game Options, B
closes it and the game's menu is back (present dump). Not tried on a device.


### Never 480 wide by itself (2026-11-21)

The user, on the Mac: a change of ratio went to 480 wide, which the maps are
not made for (experimental). Their 16:10 Enhanced (384x240) -> 16:9 took
Enhanced's size, 384x216, uneven on a 1440x900 screen, so the desktop's
widest-whole-pixel rule picked 480x270 (3x). Now nothing picks a 480-wide
size for the player (`auto_pickable`): not a preset, the whole-pixel rule, a
change of ratio, or a size saved under another shape. 480x270 stays in View
Size, to be chosen by hand; a saved 480x270 of the same shape is kept as the
player's own choice. Checked: 16:10 384x240 -> 16:9 gives 384x216 at
1440x900, 1280x800 and 1680x1050 (menu, KOL_MENU_PPM).
